name: Regal Private Credit Opportunities Fund
management_company_description: Regal Funds Management was founded in 2004 by the King family and has pioneered the development of the hedge fund and alternatives industry in Australia over the last 20+ years. As a subsidiary of ASX-listed Regal Partners Limited (ASX:RPL), Regal sits alongside investment managers PM Capital, Merricks Capital, Taurus Funds, VGI Partners, Argyle Group, Kilter Rural, and Attunga Capital, which manage capital across a diverse range of alternative investment strategies covering long / short equities, private markets, real & natural assets, and credit & royalties. Together, the Group employs approximately 190 staff, including more than 90 investment professionals, located in offices across Australia and offshore, managing investments for a broad number of institutions, family offices, charities and wealth advisory groups across Australia, the America’s, Europe and Asia.
strategy_description:
The Fund has been established to focus on investments in private credit opportunities, targeting bilaterally originated and negotiated loans to small and middle market companies, to corporates owned by financial sponsors, loans secured by pools of financial or real assets, as well as other idiosyncratic loans and opportunities predominantly in Australia and New Zealand.

The Fund may gain exposure to investments via a variety of credit instruments when pursuing the Investment Objective, including directly originated loans, secured floating and fixed rate syndicated loans, subordinated and mezzanine loans, asset backed securities and other types of credit and credit-like instruments. Its portfolio may also contain warrants, equities, debentures, convertible notes, preferred equity and other types of securities.

The Fund may use leverage to enhance returns, fund liquidity and bridge investments.
region_exposure_description: The Fund will be focused primarily on investing in businesses whose operations are predominantly in Australia and New Zealand. This is intended to enable the Fund to capitalise on the depth and breadth of Regal’s network in these areas to assist with the origination of opportunities and engagement with borrowers.

name: OrbiMed Genesis Fund
management_company_description: As one of the largest healthcare-dedicated investment firms globally, OrbiMed boasts a strong investment platform with $20.2 billion in assets under management and a team of 151 professionals with deep expertise in science, medicine, and finance.  By virtue of OrbiMed’s sizable venture capital activities, the Firm can access a range of distinctive later-stage private investments, PIPE (private investment in public entity) opportunities, and other special situations.
strategy_description:
The Genesis Fund takes advantage of OrbiMed's powerful platform to invest in an overlooked market niche: later-stage private opportunities that may be unsuitable for typical venture capital funds as well as less-liquid public equities and special situations that may be passed over by many public market participants.  The fund invests in emerging life sciences companies through "crossover" positions in private companies, initial public offerings, "cornerstone" investments, PIPE transactions, and opportunities in catalyst-driven smaller cap public companies. Investments focus on life sciences companies engaged in the discovery and development of novel products and services that OrbiMed believes will address significant unmet medical needs. 

Genesis Fund investments are subject to a thorough due diligence process and validation by proprietary internal research.  Sources for idea generation include scientific data from industry publications, medical conferences, industry contacts, and rigorous financial reviews of companies across healthcare subsectors. OrbiMed prefers to invest in companies with specific catalysts that could trigger value realization, such as attaining a clinical development or regulatory milestone for a potential blockbuster new drug.

name: Greenwoods Golden China Fund
management_company_description: Greenwoods is one of the largest and earliest China managers, with a long track record in Greater China & domestic China equities, and a team with strong local experience in China. Greenwoods manages both long/short and long only strategies. Greenwoods adheres to a fundamental value investment approach, focusing on stock picking and high conviction portfolios. The investment team seeks to do in-depth on-the ground research on target companies following a 360 degree due diligence system similar to private equity investing. Greenwoods' public equity team consists of 4 senior PMs and 31 analysts (as of June 2022). Greenwoods has offices in Shanghai, Hong Kong and Singapore, and a private equity arm.
strategy_description:
Golden China Fund is a long biased long/short fund primarily investing in Greater China equities including A shares, H shares, ADRs etc.  The Fund adopts bottom-up long term fundamental stock picking with a top down overlay and primarily aims to invest in companies which (a) it considers exhibit good historical performance with sound financial position, outstanding management, competitive advantage and good growth potential; and (b) are trading at attractive or reasonable valuations. For short positions the Fund targets companies which are over valued, exhibit financial weakness or other risks, poor business models, weak compeitive position and poor industry structures.

The Fund is managed by Jinzhi Jiang (George), Founder and CIO of Greenwoods.

name: Forada - Enhanced 2x Strategy
management_company_description:
Forada was founded in London, UK, in 2017 by Jon Ridgway. 
The firm is managing over US$ 2bn across the Forada Fund and pari-passu managed accounts.
strategy_description:
Forada is a catalyst-driven discretionary macro manager based in London, set up by CIO, Jon Ridgway in 2017. It seeks uncorrelated returns, with low drawdowns and convex upside. Forada focuses on highly liquid macro instruments with emphasis on developed market interest rates, particularly in Europe, US, Japan and the UK. It also adds portfolio diversification using equity indices, foreign exchange and commodities.

Founded in 2017, Forada runs a portfolio via the commingled Forada Master Fund and managed accounts.
Forada's commingled fund launched in May 2021. 
Forada launched an Enhanced  2X levered share class of the existing strategy in January 2026.

Appendix: Enhanced Strategy Backtest Methodology   
Calculations for Enhanced Strategy
Monthly gross returns originate from the i) historical trading returns of the Ixworth SMA (November 2016 - May 2017), Forada SMA (October 2017 – April 2021) and Forada Fund (May 2021 – August 2025) and ii) money market returns (May 2021 – December 2025).
i) Trading returns: the Enhanced share class doubles the risk of existing strategy. For example, if an existing position is 1,000 bund futures, to double the risk the corresponding position is 2,000 bund futures. The historical monthly trading returns or losses are therefore double those of the existing share classes.  
ii) Money market returns: Forada Master Fund holds unencumbered cash in money market funds. The Enhanced share class consumes twice as much encumbered cash, which reduces cash available to earn a money market return. The historical monthly money market returns have been reduced to account for the imputed additional cash usage of the Enhanced share class. Prior to May 2021’s launch of the commingled fund the strategy ran SMAs which did not receive any money market return that a commingled fund may have earned, so no money market return adjustment has been made during that period.  
The doubled trading returns and adjusted money market returns are combined to form the gross returns. 
Fund expenses, 1% management fee and 25% performance fee are applied to calculate the historical net track record.

FOR EXAMPLE, THE ABILITY TO WITHSTAND LOSSES OR TO ADHERE TO A PARTICULAR TRADING PROGRAM IN SPITE OF TRADING LOSSES ARE MATERIAL POINTS WHICH CAN ALSO ADVERSELY AFFECT ACTUAL TRADING RESULTS. THERE ARE NUMEROUS OTHER FACTORS RELATED TO THE MARKETS IN GENERAL OR TO THE IMPLEMENTATION OF ANY SPECIFIC TRADING PROGRAM WHICH CANNOT BE FULLY ACCOUNTED FOR IN THE PREPARATION OF HYPOTHETICAL PERFORMANCE RESULTS AND ALL OF WHICH CAN ADVERSELY AFFECT ACTUAL TRADING RESULTS.

Appendix: Enhanced Strategy Backtest Methodology   
Calculations for Enhanced Strategy
Monthly gross returns originate from the i) historical trading returns of the Ixworth SMA (November 2016 - May 2017), Forada SMA (October 2017 – April 2021) and Forada Fund (May 2021 – August 2025) and ii) money market returns (May 2021 – December 2025).
i) Trading returns: the Enhanced share class doubles the risk of existing strategy. For example, if an existing position is 1,000 bund futures, to double the risk the corresponding position is 2,000 bund futures. The historical monthly trading returns or losses are therefore double those of the existing share classes.  
ii) Money market returns: Forada Master Fund holds unencumbered cash in money market funds. The Enhanced share class consumes twice as much encumbered cash, which reduces cash available to earn a money market return. The historical monthly money market returns have been reduced to account for the imputed additional cash usage of the Enhanced share class. Prior to May 2021’s launch of the commingled fund the strategy ran SMAs which did not receive any money market return that a commingled fund may have earned, so no money market return adjustment has been made during that period.  
The doubled trading returns and adjusted money market returns are combined to form the gross returns. 
Fund expenses, 1% management fee and 25% performance fee are applied to calculate the historical net track record.

Castlebar runs a European-focused Event Driven strategy, investing in announced M&A (equity risk-arbitrage) and event-driven Credit. strategy_description:

Castlebar seeks to build a high conviction portfolio around 30-40 core positions.  Individual position sizing is managed to optimize risk adjusted returns and is under constant review translating to active trading of the portfolio.  Beta exposure is controlled within -10% to 20% of NAV with dynamic asset allocation across strategies and asset classes in an effort to reflect the prevailing opportunity set.  When evaluated across the cycle, expected strategy exposures will be 2/3 equity, 1/3 credit, which reflects a 50:50 split on a risk adjusted basis.   
 
An integrated active risk management approach utilises individual position and portfolio hedging techniques which seek to isolate alpha and hedge residual beta / protect against event gamma.

management_company_description:

Our expertise includes Global Macro, Emerging Local Markets and External Debt, and Private Credit, including both asset-backed and direct lending capabilities. Decades of investment experience and a disciplined risk management approach make Kirkoswald a partner of choice to capital allocators globally.
Kirkoswald combines decades of professional experience in macro and emerging markets investing with institutional knowledge, a rigorous research and risk management process, and experience weathering economic headwinds and market cycles. The firm deploys a range of strategies across various investment products, primarily focused on emerging markets.
Kirkoswald is committed to excellence first and foremost and builds connections with investors to help them diversify their strategy and grow their assets.



Abbeville Partners LLP was formed in 2013 and changed its name to Kirkoswald Capital Partners LLP on 30 January 2018.
strategy_description:
Kirkoswald Capital Partners LLP launched a discretionary global macro fund with an emerging market bias, namely the Kirkoswald Global Macro UCITS Fund (“Fund”), on the Investcorp-Tages UCITS platform in January 2022. The investment objective of the Fund is to seek positive returns for investors by investing in global emerging and developed markets. The Fund seeks to achieve the investment objective by executing a discretionary global macro strategy investing across various asset classes, with a primary focus on fixed income securities, currencies and foreign exchange, and to a lesser extent equities.

The investment strategy relies on the analysis of top-down macroeconomic economic drivers and bottom-up technical factors to identify investment opportunities that we believe will generate a return for the Fund by taking long and short exposure to the asset classes. Top-down macro-economic views are formed by assessing a wide range of inputs including fundamental data (e.g., economic statistics, central bank actions), market trading flows and technicals (e.g., price and volume movement), monitoring political events (e.g., referenda and elections) and reviewing research and strategy reports produced by external economists. Bottom-up technical factors may include relative pricing of the securities and the asset flows between various interest rate market participants.

exact_name: TCW Sepulveda Focused Value Fund, LP
management_company_description:
Founded in 1971 and based in Los Angeles, TCW manages a broad range of innovative, actively managed investment products that strive to enhance and protect clients’ wealth. TCW’s clients include many of the largest corporate and public pension plans, financial institutions, insurance companies, endowments and foundations in the United States, as well as a substantial number of international entities including central banks, sovereign wealth funds and private banks.

In 2001, TCW was acquired by Société Générale (SG), one of the largest global banking franchises with a presence in 85 countries. SG worked with TCW to grow and expand its global footprint for a dozen years. The partnership was very productive, including in early 2010, TCW’s acquisition of Metropolitan West Asset Management, LLC (MetWest), a top-ranked fixed income asset manager. As a result, key employees of MetWest assumed primary responsibility for the oversight of TCW’s fixed income mandates. Since that time, MetWest has operated as a subsidiary of The TCW Group, Inc. 

In February 2013, TCW’s management effected a management led buy-out of SG in partnership with The Carlyle Group. Following the buyout, The Carlyle Group held an approximately 60% stake in the firm, with TCW management and employees owning the balance of approximately 40%, on a fully diluted basis. TCW management negotiated strong governance provisions to ensure that TCW’s managerial autonomy would be preserved. Equity for the transaction came from TCW management and two Carlyle investment funds – Carlyle Global Financial Services Partners, a $1.1 billion financial services fund, and Carlyle Partners V, a $13.7 billion U.S. buyout fund. The Carlyle transaction facilitated a management initiative to increase employee ownership.  Prior to 2010, TCW employees did not have significant equity interests in the firm. Since the 2010 acquisition of MetWest by TCW, employee ownership has continued to increase.

On December 27, 2017, Nippon Life completed its acquisition of a 24.75% minority stake in TCW from Carlyle. As a result of this transaction, ownership in TCW by TCW management and employees increased to 44.07%, and Carlyle maintains a 31.18% interest in the firm through a purchase by its long duration private equity fund, Carlyle Global Partners.

There is a high level of employee ownership of the company, including most of TCW’s key decision-making investment and other professionals. TCW believes strongly that employee equity ownership aligns the interests of the decision-making employees with the interests of the firm and the firm’s clients, and creates a cohesive “ownership culture.”

Nippon and Carlyle have agreed to continue the existing strong governance protections for TCW management, which help to ensure that TCW’s current management and investment teams are primarily responsible for personnel and compensation decisions, and solely responsible for the management of investment portfolios.

management_company_description: Tidan Capital is a Stockholm-based, independent investment management company established in 2020 by Brummer & Partners alumni with several decades of investment experience across the capital structure. Our flagship strategy, a market-neutral credit relative value approach, is built on a foundation of deep fundamental analysis and a disciplined investment process. With a presence in Europe and expanding globally, Tidan Capital operates under rigorous regulatory standards and an organisation relying on premier service providers ensuring a scalable and governance-focused investment platform for our clients.
strategy_description:
Themis is Tidan Capital’s dedicated equity market neutral strategy, built on a carve-out from the flagship Tidan program. The strategy seeks to generate consistent alpha by exploiting value creation and dilution across single stocks—through long and short positions—with limited reliance on index or factor hedging. Themis applies a deep fundamental approach, underpinned by credit analysis, to identify companies undergoing structural or financial transitions that are not yet fully reflected in equity valuations.

The investment process focuses on isolating idiosyncratic opportunities, particularly in companies where credit dynamics signal upcoming equity repricing. Typical candidates include those facing refinancing challenges, structural threats, or inflection points in cash flow generation. The strategy maintains a balanced portfolio with a targeted gross exposure of 150% and deploys capital across US and European markets, focusing on companies with a market capitalization above USD 1 billion.

Themis has been live as a stand-alone carve-out since July 2024 and is designed to be a self-sustaining market neutral strategy, aiming for attractive risk-adjusted returns with low correlation to traditional equity markets.

General Description. Verition Multi-Strategy Fund LLC and Verition International Multi-Strategy Fund, Ltd. (collectively, the “Fund”) have offered various classes of securities over the years. The net performance returns presented herein were calculated, for certain periods, by adjusting the combined gross profit and loss of the Fund to provide a more direct comparison of the net performance that could have been achieved by the interests currently offered by the Fund (the “Modified Class”).  
In each period, these adjustments reflect: (i) a management fee payable monthly (the “Management Fee”); (ii) an annual incentive allocation/performance fee (subject to a high-water mark) (the “Incentive Allocation”); and (iii) the trading, administrative, operating and Specialty Strategy costs allocated to the Modified Class (“Operating Expenses”).  The Management Fee, Incentive Allocation and Operating Expenses are referred to as the “Modified Class Expenses”.  The rate at which the Management Fee and Incentive Allocation was charged or allocated, as applicable, by the Fund has differed over time.  The Fund has used a consistent Management Fee rate and Incentive Allocation rate to present the pro forma returns for each relevant class, utilizing the current rates for each such class.  The Modified Class Expenses do not include Pass-Through Costs allocated to the Fund’s Initial Class, which are not borne by the Modified Class.  (For a description of “Pass-Through Costs” and the “Initial Class” please refer to the Fund’s offering memoranda.)
March 2008-September 2008. This period presents gross returns of NM Capital LLC (Mr. Maounis’ proprietary account and predecessor to the Fund) (the “Predecessor Account”) adjusted to reflect Modified Class Expenses.  The Predecessor Account was established in January 2008 and only engaged in testing trades prior to March 2008.  Operating Expenses were not borne by the Predecessor Account and Verition does not have specific records showing the actual expenses borne by the Predecessor Account.  The returns reflect an assumed Operating Expenses adjustment based on an assumed expense ratio of 1.43%.  This assumed expense ratio is equal to the actual Operating Expense ratio of the Fund during the period from October 2008-December 2009 and has been included because Verition has determined it represents a reasonable approximation of the Operating Expense ratio that would have been borne by the Predecessor Account during this period given the net asset value of the Predecessor Account and the size of Verition’s operations during this period.  
October 2008-December 2013. This period presents gross returns of the Fund, adjusted on a pro forma basis to reflect Modified Class Expenses.  The Operating Expense adjustment reflects Operating Expenses actually borne by the Fund during this period, including all categories of Operating Expenses currently borne by the Fund.  The Modified Class did not exist during this period, so the Operating Expenses incorporated have been adjusted to remove the impact of Pass-Through Costs allocated to the Initial Class.  
January 2014-April 2020. This period presents gross returns of the Fund, adjusted to reflect Modified Class Expenses.  The Operating Expense adjustment reflects Operating Expenses actually borne by the Funds during this period, which did not include all categories of Operating Expenses currently borne by the Fund. May 2020-Current. This period presents gross returns of the Fund, adjusted to reflect actual expenses borne by the Modified Interests, including Operating Expenses that are the same as those Operating Expenses currently borne by the Fund.
Specialty Strategies.  Returns prior to November 2014 include the performance of two strategies that were subsequently designated as Specialty Strategies. name: Whale Rock Long Opportunities Fund
management_company_description: Founded by Alex Sacerdote in 2006, Whale Rock Capital Management LLC ("Whale Rock") is a Boston-based global long/short equity manager focused on the Technology, Media and Telecom ("TMT") sectors.  Alex and a team of six analysts bring a combined 90+ years of experience in these sectors.  Whale Rock is a growth-oriented manager seeking to benefit from the innovation and disruption inherent in the TMT space. We invest in companies of all capitalization ranges and most subsectors including internet, software, hardware, services and social media. We look across the globe seeking to identify the most attractive opportunities on the long and short side. The firm utilizes a distinctive S-Curve based investment approach.  Our approach is underpinned by intensive and rigorous fundamental research. In a typical year, our team conducts over one thousand face to face meetings with TMT companies in the United States, Asia and Europe. In addition to financial modeling and analysis, the team meets private companies, venture capitalists, customers, competitors and suppliers to gain an in-depth understanding of market dynamics.

strategy_description:
The Mariner Cicero CMBS Opportunities Fund (the “Fund’) is a fixed-income strategy that seeks to outperform the broader fixed income markets on a risk-adjusted basis while carefully managing risk. The Fund invests in commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) and other structured commercial real estate (CRE) opportunities, leveraging the investment team’s extensive experience in analyzing property-level asset valuation and credit quality. The team’s comprehensive research process has been developed over 21 years of investing through various CMBS cycles and security types. We believe the team’s experience across real estate and fixed income is not common to CMBS investors and provides the Fund with a competitive advantage. Additionally, we believe the inefficiency of the CMBS universe provides an opportunity for an experienced team such as the Mariner Cicero Team to capture structural alpha in a risk-controlled fashion. The primary drivers of the Fund’s return include higher-yielding event-driven bonds that require property-level analysis which seeks to reduce risk as well as a mixture of investment-grade and non-investment grade CMBS securities.

*The Fund Description is prospective and reflects the Mariner Cicero Team’s views and opinions at the time of this presentation. There is no guarantee the Team will be successful in their efforts to implement strategies that take advantage of such perceived opportunities.

management_company_description:
Holocene Advisors, LP ("Holocene" or the "Firm") is an investment management firm registered with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. Holocene pursues two strategies: (a) a sector-diversified, beta-neutral long/short equity strategy limited to investments in public companies and (b) a concentrated, long-only, long term-focused equity strategy, which primarily invests in public companies (with a limited ability to invest in private companies, in which participation is optional for investors). 

Holocene seeks to deeply understand its portfolio companies' operations and the sectors in which they operate. The Firm invests in companies that it believes will outperform based on idiosyncratic, fundamental drivers. Potential investments are evaluated on many factors, including a company's competitive positioning, drivers of growth, quality of management team, returns on capital, cash flow generation and capital allocation. Deep research is conducted, including proprietary financial modeling and an expected value analysis. Investments are in global equities, primarily in the U.S. mid- and large capitalization space. 

For each strategy, Holocene employs a coverage model, in which our sizeable research team is organized by sectors, which enables our portfolio managers and analysts to develop industry and company knowledge across the globe. Analysts maintain current research on the companies in their respective coverage universe whether we are invested at a given time or not. We believe our research across 1000+ companies, industry knowledge and culture of collaboration across our investment team gives us a unique ability to identify investment opportunities for both strategies. 

Holocene strives to be a diverse firm comprised of intellectually curious and intellectually honest individuals. We believe the investment business is humbling; therefore, we aim to be flexible in our thinking and challenge each other's ideas, which leads us, hopefully, to more thorough and creative research, with better outcomes. We are highly process-oriented and utilize technology throughout our investment process and business operations in an effort to make us more efficient. Honesty and respect are imperatives in every aspect of how we conduct business with colleagues, management teams, counterparties and investors. 

Holocene operates from its office located in Manhattan. The Firm provides investment management services to private investment funds in which pension plans, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, foundations, financial institutions and high net worth individuals invest.
strategy_description:
The Holocene Children's Fund (the "Children's Fund") is a concentrated, long-only, long term-focused equity fund that launched on February 1, 2022. The Children's Fund is managed by Holocene Advisors, LP ("Holocene"), an investment adviser registered with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission that has managed an equity long/short, beta-neutral fund since 2017 (the "Beta-Neutral Fund"). 

The Children’s Fund seeks to invest in a concentrated, long-only portfolio of companies that we believe have unique business models and whose shares we believe have the potential to compound at high returns over many years. 

The Children's Fund investment program leverages Holocene’s team, infrastructure, collaborative culture, and creative thinking, and the Children's Fund research process is highly integrated and synergistic with the research process that Holocene utilizes in managing the Beta-Neutral Fund. Holocene organizes its sizable investment team by sector/sub-sector coverage, which enables our portfolio managers and analysts to develop deep industry and company knowledge on a global basis. Analysts maintain current research on the companies in their respective coverage universe whether one of Holocene’s strategies is invested at a given time or not. 

As our investment team continually evaluates all companies under our coverage, we come across a small number of companies that do very well in each of the following four areas and are accordingly identified as candidates for inclusion in the Children's Fund portfolio. These four areas are:

(i)	Business Model – the company has a durable, sustainable competitive advantage that we believe will persist and will allow it to earn higher-than-average returns on invested capital over many years; 
(ii)	Capital Allocation and Growth - management is strategic in thinking about capital allocation, and the company should have the ability to grow sustainably at attractive rates and invest its capital at compelling rates of return; 
(iii)	Quality of Management - managers have exceptional skill, motivation, integrity and alignment with shareholders; and 
(iv)	Valuation - we are able to buy the stock at a reasonable price with the potential to generate strong risk-adjusted returns over many years.

In the Children's Fund, we construct a concentrated, long-only, long-term, low-turnover portfolio composed of approximately 20-40 stocks, with the goal of generating strong returns over many years. The Children’s Fund invests predominantly in public mid-cap and large-cap equities on a global basis. We are sector-agnostic in our stock selection given the scarcity of suitable candidates. The Investment Manager generally expects the Children’s Fund to have gross exposure of approximately 100%. 

The Investment Manager also may invest very selectively and opportunistically in private companies. Though we do not hold such investments currently, we offer opt-in and opt-out classes for private investments to accommodate potential investors who do not have the ability to invest in private companies.

The Children's Fund is a limited partnership organized in Delaware, U.S.A., and is available to U.S. taxable, U.S. tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors.

strategy_description:
The Holocene Advisors Funds (the "HAF") employ a fundamental, global, equity long/short beta-neutral investment strategy that launched in April 2017. The HAF is managed by Holocene Advisors, LP (the "IM"), an investment adviser registered with the SEC. The IM focuses on alpha generation through disciplined stock selection based on fundamental research conducted by sector-focused investment teams, coupled with analytical, risk-focused portfolio construction to isolate alpha and minimize systematic risk. The Master Fund ("MF") seeks to invest in publicly-traded equities and equity-related instruments across all market capitalizations, though predominantly in U.S.-listed mid and large cap companies.

The IM's sector-focused approach to investing is a defining trait of its investment process. The IM believes that sector specialization is critical to the early identification of investment ideas and can lead to recognition of important nuances, enhance analysts' views on company and industry expectations and timing, and drive idea generation velocity within the Firm.

The IM's investment team is designed to capitalize on its sector-specific research skills while managing risk through portfolio construction. The portfolio of the MF is a single book composed of multiple portfolios of investments as follows:

(1) the "Holocene Book" over which Brandon Haley, Holocene's CIO has full discretion, though certain senior investment team members ("Holocene Book PMs") have a limited ability to make investment decisions on the portions of the portfolio on which they focus; 

(2)(a) dedicated sector-specific portfolios over which certain senior investment team members (each, a "Sector Head") exercise discretion and risk management responsibilities (each, a "Sector Portfolio") and (b) a number of smaller, dedicated sub-sector portfolios over which a select group of analysts (each, an "Epoch PM") exercise discretion and risk management responsibilities (each, an "Epoch Portfolio"); and 

(3) a Capital Markets Portfolio. 

Each portfolio is subject to the oversight of Holocene's CIO and Chief Risk Officer. Sectors covered generally include Consumer, TMT, Industrials, Energy, Healthcare and Financials. The IM's team structure, process and culture encourages collaboration and debate across and within the Holocene Book and Sector Portfolio teams.

The IM strives to maintain strict adherence to a process-oriented, repeatable research process. The goal is to conduct deep, differentiated fundamental research and generate alpha through disciplined stock selection. The IM conducts several stages of due diligence on investment ideas and industry trends including:

Sector-Specific Coverage Model: Each team maintains detailed company-specific models and forecasts on the majority of companies in its sector universe regardless of whether or not the MF is presently active in a name. 

Generation and Refinement of Investment Ideas: Once an idea is identified, the IM initiates a research process that typically includes formal and informal team discussion and debate, exploring cross-sector implications and consequences, seeking to identify potential trends impacting companies and sectors, and unearthing the best way to express the idea (including timing) and the implications for other companies in the sector. 

Due Diligence and Financial Modeling: Thorough research and development of financial models for each company, including, but not limited to, expected value analysis and scenario analysis, various forms of company valuation, and stock multiple upside and downside cases, will be utilized to identify risks and opportunities. 

Position Sizing and Monitoring: Position sizing is a function of the expected return-to-risk ratio of and level of conviction in an investment, and the expected return-to-risk characteristics of the overall portfolio. The investment team generally will analyze 'expected value', portfolio risk, liquidity and short interest, among other considerations, as part of the position sizing process. The IM imposes position size limits across each portfolio and at the MF level. Once a position is initiated, the IM employs a rigorous monitoring process that includes tracking fundamental metrics to monitor the thesis. 

Risk Management: The IM utilizes its internally developed proprietary risk management system. Much of the data that drives risk measurement is built on risk models created by companies such as Barra, while other applications are developed within the IM. Risk management is further served by establishing limits on various sources of risk, thereby allowing for a robust process-driven approach to portfolio construction.

name: Magnetar Relative Value Fund Ltd
management_company_description:
Founded in 2005, Magnetar Financial LLC (“Magnetar”) is a multi-strategy and multi-product alternative investment manager that seeks to achieve stable risk-adjusted returns by opportunistically employing a wide range of alternative credit & fixed income, fundamental, quantitative, and venture investment strategies. Currently run by two managing partners – Ross Laser and Dave Snyderman – Magnetar is registered with the SEC as an Investment Adviser. Headquartered in Evanston, Illinois, Magnetar and its affiliates employ a team of approximately 221 professionals as of December 31, 2025 and maintain three satellite offices in the US (New York, Menlo Park, Austin), and the UK (London).

Disclaimer: Assets Under Management (AUM) reflects approximate investor capital managed by Magnetar and its affiliated investment managers, on a discretionary and non-discretionary basis, including designated investments in side pockets and unfunded commitments (money committed to any fund managed by Magnetar and its affiliated investment managers as of the report date, but not yet transferred by the investors).
strategy_description:
The Magnetar Relative Value Fund Ltd (the “Fund”) provides investors with access to two mainstream hedge fund strategies: Systematic Risk Arbitrage (SRA) and Systematic Convertible Arbitrage (SCA). These strategies are designed to deliver differentiated, complementary sources of return that are rooted in intuitive, persistent market dynamics and historically well-understood risk premia.

Magnetar brings a distinctive edge to these strategies through decades of investment experience, robust institutional infrastructure, and a proprietary data platform. We believe these advantages support the development and execution of systematic, rules-based approaches that aim to capture the core return drivers of each strategy in a disciplined and repeatable manner.

SRA and SCA are combined in a 50/50 strategic allocation, with the mix rebalanced monthly. Each strategy independently adjusts its exposure and long market value (LMV) leverage based on market opportunity. This dynamic construction allows the Fund to scale into periods of higher activity – such as increased merger announcements or new convertible issuance – while maintaining a diversified profile. The combination of two lowly correlated strategies is intended to enhance risk-adjusted returns and reduce directional market exposure.

To improve capital efficiency, the Fund applies a leverage multiplier to the combined strategy allocation. Total Fund LMV – including both underlying strategy leverage and the Fund multiplier – is generally managed to remain below 3.75x, though it may vary over time. If the combined LMV exceeds that level, the multiplier is adjusted downward during monthly rebalancing.

In the SRA strategy, the Fund invests in the equity securities of companies involved in announced mergers to capture the risk arbitrage premium. The portfolio is intended to be reasonably diversified, with positions dynamically scaled based on deal size, timing, and capital availability. The strategy’s rule set governs deal selection, sizing, leverage, and exit criteria – enabling consistent risk management and exposure scaling as the number of eligible deals expands.

The SCA strategy seeks to profit from relative mispricings between convertible bonds and their underlying equities by going long the convertible and shorting a portion of the equity. The strategy may also hedge portfolio-level interest rate risk. Exposure is determined by a rules-based filtering process that evaluates liquidity, balance, credit risk, and valuation. Risk is tightly controlled through systematic position sizing, portfolio construction, and rebalancing protocols.
region_exposure_description: The primary geographic focus of the Fund is North America, with additional exposure to Europe and Asia-Pacific.

strategy_description:
The Magnetar Systematic Multi-Strategy Fund LLC (the “Fund”) provides access to a diversified portfolio of systematic hedge fund strategies, including Systematic Risk Arbitrage (SRA), Systematic Convertible Arbitrage (SCA), Equity Statistical Arbitrage (ESA), and Tail Hedging. Each strategy is rooted in historically persistent risk premia and executed through disciplined, rules-based approaches.

Magnetar leverages its practitioner-led investment philosophy, proprietary data platform, and institutional infrastructure to systematically extract alpha across strategies. The Fund’s design aims to deliver attractive, risk-adjusted returns with low correlation to traditional markets.

Portfolio construction is guided by Magnetar’s Systematic Investing Investment Committee, which combines quantitative asset allocation methods with qualitative insights. Strategy weights are actively managed and intended to adapt over time as opportunity sets evolve. Each strategy manages its own exposures and leverage, while overall Fund LMV leverage is governed at the portfolio level using a mix of cash and derivative instruments.

SRA targets announced M&A deals by investing in the equities of target companies. The strategy applies a systematic framework to assess deal quality, size positions, and manage risk, allowing the Fund to scale exposure based on deal flow.

SCA seeks to capture mispricings between convertible bonds and underlying equities. The Fund goes long convertibles and shorts a portion of the related equity, while selectively hedging interest rate exposure. Position sizing and selection follow a rules-based process emphasizing liquidity, credit quality, and relative value.

ESA focuses on short-term, mean-reverting price dislocations not explained by fundamentals. The strategy aims to monetize temporary inefficiencies across a diversified equity universe, with systematic sizing and rebalancing.

Tail Hedging provides downside protection in extreme market events through options strategies designed to capture exposure to skew and vega. Positions are delta-hedged to maintain pure tail risk exposure, and strategy-specific hedges may be used where appropriate.

The combination of lowly correlated strategies, dynamic risk allocation, and systematic implementation seeks to deliver stable performance across market environments. The Fund is intended to serve as a differentiated return source and a diversifying complement to traditional and alternative portfolios.

strategy_description:
The Magnetar Alternative Credit & Fixed Income group’s investment approach is designed to identify and capture alpha across different economic and market environments. We aim to add alpha at three fundamental points in the process – quantitative analysis, fundamental analysis, and sourcing.  While we will pursue market inefficiencies that continue to exist in traditional areas, our efforts are also focused on areas that are overlooked or avoided by today’s market participants. These “white space” opportunities often arise at the intersection of different markets, where we can identify meaningful dislocations. We believe that the best investment ideas arise from true collaboration and deploying expert resources in the sourcing, structuring, and risk management of trades. Combining internal sourcing with a non-siloed investment process allows us to pursue cross-pillar themes and investment opportunities, leveraging Magnetar’s investment teams and expertise. Through this approach, we expand the opportunity set of high-quality transactions and identify traditional opportunities with attractive risk-reward profiles.

The Magnetar Constellation Fund Ltd (“Constellation Fund”) seeks to achieve consistently attractive risk-adjusted returns by investing in corporate, consumer, and real estate credit products across multiple markets. Magnetar employs strategies based on its quantitative analysis and portfolio management techniques, complemented by in-depth fundamental credit analysis. The goal is to create an opportunistic portfolio that benefits from volatility and dislocations in the underlying markets. Investments span corporate, real estate, energy, and consumer credit-driven strategies, targeting both primary and secondary markets. The Constellation Fund may also engage in relative-value trading of tranches in structured products or between securities, loans, and equities of a given company or asset type, aiming to identify value dislocations and/or hedging opportunities.

We believe the Constellation Fund’s strategy stands out due to the combination of internal sourcing of investment ideas, superior fundamental analysis, differentiated structuring capabilities, and expert risk management. These elements work together to create an optimized portfolio. Additionally, we consider the opportunity to structure an investment organization with an innovative approach to be a significant advantage. Magnetar actively works to minimize organizational inefficiencies, which can hinder others from adapting to today’s changing landscape. Our senior portfolio managers are deeply involved in the market, staying close to the details and making investment decisions. This hands-on approach, combined with robust infrastructure, allows us to execute and optimize our investment processes on a scalable and repeatable basis, giving our strategies a competitive edge.

The investment approach targets opportunities where market inefficiencies, capital structure complexity, or operational and financial dislocation create mispricing that can be addressed through rigorous fundamental analysis and active, hands-on engagement. The strategy is positioned to be opportunistic and value-oriented, emphasizing downside protection and a disciplined hedging framework designed to mitigate exogenous risks, isolate idiosyncratic sources of return, and drive attractive outcomes across market cycles.

The Special Situations Fund is led by Austin Camporin, who spent more than 15 years at Elliott Management prior to joining Magnetar. We believe the Fund is distinctive due to its ability to uncover and act on complex opportunities in areas of the market that are often overlooked – particularly among small- and mid-cap capital structures where inefficiencies are typically more pronounced. Our approach is built on disciplined sourcing and rigorous selection, driven by internal idea generation from a highly experienced team, supported by custom screens and best-in-class tools. 

We screen approximately 1,300 companies using Magnetar Labs' proprietary analytics and market networks, with fewer than 1% of ideas progressing to funded positions. Each investment targets specific catalysts – refinancings, restructurings, governance changes, or operational improvements – with contingency paths and multiple avenues to value creation. Where appropriate, we engage proactively across financial, operational, strategic, and governance dimensions seeking to align stakeholders and drive outcomes. We maintain flexibility to invest across the capital structure, from senior secured debt to junior credit and equity.

We believe the current market environment – characterized by a large pipeline of upcoming maturities, elevated distress levels, and fragmented capital availability – creates a timely and scalable opportunity set. Magnetar’s flat organizational model, cross-functional team, and institutional infrastructure enable us to pursue high-conviction investments with creativity, precision, and speed, which we believe provides a competitive advantage.

management_company_description:
Complus Asset Management (“Complus”) is a global asset management firm founded in 2011. With offices in Hong Kong, Singapore, and London, Complus specializes in providing discretionary investment solutions tailored to international institutional investors. Our focus is on delivering stable long-term returns while adhering to a prudent risk management framework.

The firm was founded by Chester Kam (Founder and Group CIO). Prior to founding Complus, Chester held various key roles in investment management and trading at Alphadyne Asset Management and JP Morgan. Rajeev Leekha is a Partner of Complus.
strategy_description:
The Complus Asia Macro Fund aims to produce superior risk-adjusted returns through a diversified portfolio in liquid interest rate and currency markets. We employ fundamental as well as market dynamic analysis in order to construct a balanced portfolio in directional and relative value opportunities focusing on Asia and G10 markets. The Complus Asia Macro Fund targets high single digit returns with a mid-single digit volatility.

The Complus investment team believes that there continues to be structural inefficiencies in the interest rate and FX markets. The 13 Asian countries as well as G10 markets we trade offer a diversified set of opportunities as the countries widely differ in their economic development, their demographics and the resulting monetary and fiscal policies. While we have a top-down global macro view, we apply fundamental as well as technical analysis to identify opportunities across geographies taking into account the local micro factors. As such we do not aim to construct a global risk on / risk off portfolio, but rather focus on having a diversified portfolio of idiosyncratic opportunities following local underlying fundamentals. 

While we take into account market technicals and trends, the strategy is discretionary. We mainly trade instruments such as FX forwards, FX options, Interest Rate Swaps, Interest Rate Futures, Swaptions, Cross Currency Swaps and Government Bonds.

name: Obion Capital (Fund)
strategy_description:
Obion Capital employs an opportunistic equity strategy focused predominately in mid-to-large cap businesses in the consumer, real estate, and industrial sectors.  The strategy aims to own long positions in businesses that have strong competitive advantages, the ability to add meaningful value to customers, a long runway of new business opportunities, and a management team capable and incentivized to drive value.  This value creation is the ultimate driver of long-term investment results and when coupled with the disciplined valuation analysis Obion employs, creates a highly durable framework for investing in public equities.  

Our research process consists of two distinct parts.  The first part of our research is oriented around developing a high conviction view of a business’s ability to create value over time. Here, we focus on how the company adds value to customers and whether the competitive advantages are likely to strengthen or weaken, which we believe are the most important factors for accurately forecasting businesses over extended periods. Importantly, the way we look at the value a company is creating is not limited only to a company’s financials; we’re looking at the total ecosystem and what the company is providing above and beyond the cost of its products or services. The second step is then to translate this research into a financial model built to develop a view on the company’s intrinsic value. We believe stocks are priced based on the market’s expectations of future cash flows, which requires a differentiated view to earn an above market rate of return. Our process is built around developing this differentiation through the intersection of value creation and valuation.

We expect our research approach and time horizon to create a natural alignment with the management teams running the companies in which we invest.  Obion strives to build a relationship, if one does not already exist, with management teams of portfolio companies, as a key to helping unlock potential embedded value in these companies.  Obion believes a value add to the strategy is the ability to suggest to executives decisions that can optimize the relationship between business operations and long term share price performance.  These suggestions come from Obion’s wider lens of studying varying business models, industries, capital structures, and strategic decisions over time.  This type of “suggestivism” and partnership has helped David add value to both public and private companies in the past and will continue to be a part of Obion’s strategy when appropriate.  

David has dedicated a large portion of his professional career to shorting stocks and views shorting as a productive way to generate returns when the right opportunity arises.  Obion’s approach towards shorting will be highly focused, in line with the overall firm strategy.  Short positions will be directed to companies where we see a permanent impairment of value relative to the current share price and the long-term risk / reward on the investment is comparable to our longs. 

The portfolio will typically consist of 10-15 long investments. Shorts will be opportunistic in nature, with no requirement to ever have shorts in the portfolio.  Investments will be concentrated in the consumer, industrial, real estate and adjacent sectors.  Gross exposure will typically range between 60-110%.  Net exposure will range from 50-100%.  Long positions can be sized 5-15% of equity capital based on conviction, with no positions sized over 20% at market (15% at cost).  Shorts will be sized at 1-5% of equity capital.  The strategy will have a bias towards holding stocks for long periods of time (3-5 years+).  The strategy may hold cash when our research indicates that returns of our portfolio do not warrant being fully invested.

management_company_description:
Perseverance Asset Management (“Perseverance”, “Firm” or “Company”) is a China-based equity hedge fund manager specializing in investing in Greater China Equities, including but not limited to stocks of Chinese companies listed in mainland China, Hong Kong and United States. Perseverance follows a fundamental research driven bottom-up and long oriented equity investment strategy. The Firm’s senior portfolio managers have an average of 20+ years of industry experience in China equities. Perseverance launched its first fund in Feb, 2015, and has since then grown to be one of China’s largest equity hedge fund managers. Its client base includes some of China’s and the world’s most prominent institutional investors such as sovereign funds, pension funds, insurance companies, banks, university endowments and family offices, as well as high net worth individuals. Perseverance is headquartered in Shenzhen, China with offices in Beijing, Shanghai and Singapore. The firm is the sole winner of “Best of the Best Awards” from Asia Asset Management in “Greater China Equity (3 Years)” consecutively in Year 2023 and 2024, and the sole winner of “Best Domestic Private Fund Manager (China)” in Year 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2025, and the sole winner of “Best Equity Manager (China)” in Year 2024 and 2026.

strategy_description:
Fund Investment Objective & Strategy
Perseverance China All Shares Long Only Fund L.P. (the "Fund" or "Master Fund") is a long only fund that invests mainly in publicly listed equities of Chinese companies. The fund strives to generate consistent and high excess return over the selected benchmark - MSCI China All Shares Index.

Investment Strategy: 
The fund capital is managed by three Portfolio Managers of Perseverance Asset Management. All three Portfolio Managers follow a bottom-up fundamental and discretionary equity investment strategy. The investment styles of each Portfolio Manager are summarized below: 

Mr. Qiu Guolu: Deep Value - emphasizes on buying quality company at cheap price with sufficient margin of safety and prefers consolidated competition landscape and focuses on clear sector leaders with dominant positions. 
Mr. Deng Xiaofeng: Balanced and Contrarian - exploiting market inefficacies with independent thinking and contrarian investment approach and a well-diversified and balanced portfolio across sectors and value/growth spectrum. 
Mr. Zhuo Liwei: Quality Growth - identifies quality growth opportunities that create sustainable value by examining a company from five dimensions: business model, people, organization quality, environment, and valuation.
Mr. Wu Renhao (Richard): Global Perspective - generating long-term risk adjusted return by selecting high quality businesses with the potential to sustain fundamental driven earnings growth, then constructing a portfolio of well diversified opportunities at reasonable valuation levels.

management_company_description:
TPG Angelo Gordon is a diversified credit and real estate investing platform within TPG, a leading global alternative asset management firm. TPG Angelo Gordon manages approximately $86 billion* across a broad range of credit and real estate strategies and we have been investing on behalf of pension funds, corporations, endowments, foundations, sovereign wealth funds and individuals for 35 years.

Angelo Gordon was founded in November 1988 by John Angelo and Michael Gordon to focus on global alternative investments with an absolute return orientation.
In May 2023, TPG Inc. announced that the companies entered into a definitive agreement under which TPG will acquire Angelo Gordon. The transaction􀆟on closed on November 1, 2023.

The platform manages capital across four investment categories: (i) corporate credit, (ii) direct lending, (iii) securitized products, and (iv) real estate. In each discipline, the firm seeks to generate absolute returns, in all market environments and with less volatility than the overall markets, by exploiting market inefficiencies and capitalizing on situations that are not in the mainstream of investment opportunities. The Firm is an SEC registered investment adviser.

*Note, prior to January 1, 2023, AUM was cited on a net basis.
strategy_description:
TPG Dynamic Credit Income Fund (DCIF) is TPG Credit's flagship alternative multi-asset credit hedge fund. It addresses the growing investor need for a liquid, diversified, uncorrelated exposure by providing a single solution access point to the breadth and depth of the $93bn TPG Credit Platform. 

TPG DCIF seeks to generate returns through a combination of high current income, trading gains and capital appreciation from a portfolio of long and short positions with an emphasis on liquidity and downside protection. DCIF would expect to capture the upside in a rising market while, importantly, protecting capital in a declining market through diversification and combination of uncorrelated return streams. 

Asset Allocation is a combination of a top-down and bottoms-up approach. The top-down approach consists of the PM, Dan Pound, evaluating the relative risk and return opportunities across the available strategies and allocating up to 75% of available capital down to the five core sub-strategies: Opportunistic Corporates; Arbitrage Strategies; Residential and Consumer ABS, Commercial Real Estate Debt, and Diversified Credit. Once the capital is allocated to the underlying expert investment team, the deep bench of analysts and underlying PMs take a bottoms-up approach to credit picking and make all of the day-to-day trading decisions with the capital allocated to them by the Fund's PM. In addition, up to 25% of capital can be retained by the PM in an "alpha sleeve", where the PM can upsize individual trades or themes from the individual strategies as a "best ideas portfolio". Allocations to strategies are dynamically rotated, with formal allocation meetings at least monthly but can happen at any point throughout a month. In the background, the Fund has a bespoke systematic hedging program that seeks to materially protect the fund from significant broader market sell-offs.

The fund fully hedges FX exposure and maintains a low interest rate duration (through the combination of floating rate assets and hedging).

Fund Profile:

Inception Date: March 1993*
Net return target of 8-12% (net)
Target Current Yield: ~8%
Exposure: Long bias, select alpha shorts and beta hedges.
Primarily US and Western Europe.
Position Size" 1%-4% of NAV
Quarterly Distribution of Income: Optional at LP's request

*In mid-2020, following the retirement of Michael Gordon, Dan Pound was elevated to Portfolio Manager and oversaw the implementation of a meaningful shift in the fund's investment philosophy and approach to multi-asset credit investing. Along with a robust set of portfolio and risk management process and protocols, the primary change was moving from a truly bespoke best ideas portfolio of TPG AG credit to one of an allocator model as previously described.

strategy_description:
The investment talent and expertise of Eric Bendahan and his team is applied to a bottom-up stock picking approach, which is active in nature and conviction-based in its stock selection. ELEVA Absolute Return Europe is aimed at investors with a medium-term horizon.
 	Bottom-up approach: stock-picking is central to the approach and is expected to be the main source of alpha generation over time. This approach is supported by a solid macro view especially during more challenging periods.
 	Great consideration is given to direct and regular contact with companies through on-site company visits and meetings with management.
 	Conviction-based, active stock-picking: the investment strategy is totally active with investment decisions founded on strong convictions. As such, allocations are mostly the result of stock-picking and can deviate meaningfully from the benchmark. However, the Fund Manager is “risk conscious” and tries to maintain a balanced portfolio in terms of risk/reward profile.
 	Style-agnostic: The Sub-Fund is style-agnostic in the sense that investments can be done according to value and/or growth criteria depending on market cycle, visibility, and the manager’s assessment of the relative opportunity set.
 	All cap-approach: The Sub-Fund invests in all market capitalization segments providing sufficient liquidity.
 	Time horizon: When selecting individual stocks, the Fund manager has an 18-24 month investment horizon, over which the target price is set.
 	ESG integration: The strategy is active from an ESG standpoint with the application of exclusions, of ESG analysis and selectivity in the long book, and of active ownership.
ELEVA Absolute Return Europe follows a disciplined investment process leveraging ELEVA Capital’s skills and expertise in European Equities with a natural extension of the current successful approach with ELEVA European Selection, our long only Sub-Fund.

strategy_description:
The Canyon ESG Credit Fund (“C-ESG” or “The Fund”) is an extension of Canyon’s involvement in the Corporate and Structured Credit space. The Fund strives to combine the investment discipline and multi-decade credit experience of Canyon with analyses of environmental, social and governance (“ESG”) considerations in order to create a portfolio that provides capital appreciation and current income, with assets that are consistent with the ESG criteria for the Fund.  The Fund will primarily invest in debt and debt-related investments.  Equity securities (net of short positions and hedges, and exclusive of risk arbitrage equities and equities received due to a reorganization or other restructuring) are not expected to exceed 10% of the Fund’s net asset value at any given time. The Fund is structured as a Master Feeder and has both an onshore and an offshore access point. 

CESG combines Canyon’s investment discipline and multi decade credit experience with analyses of environmental, social and governance (“ESG") considerations.
The Fund will also generally avoid investment in issuers who fall within the following GICS Classifications Energy: (Sector 10 Casinos Gaming (Sub Industry 25301010); Tobacco (Industry 302030); Brewers (Sub Industry 30201010) and Distillers Vintners (Sub Industry 30201020). Further, the Fund will generally avoid issuers that it determines to be principally engaged in (e.g. derives more than 10 of its gross revenues from) the production of cluster munitions or anti personnel mines.

management_company_description:
AQR is a global investment management firm built at the intersection of financial theory and practical application. We strive to deliver superior, long-term results for our clients by seeking to filter out market noise to identify and isolate what matters most, and to develop ideas that stand up to rigorous testing. Our focus on practical insights and analysis has made us leaders in alternative and traditional strategies since 1998. 

AQR takes a systematic, research-driven approach, applying quantitative tools to process fundamental information and manage risk. Our clients include institutional investors, such as pension funds, defined contribution plans, insurance companies, endowments, foundations, family offices and sovereign wealth funds, as well as RIAs, private banks and financial advisors. 

Investment decisions across all funds are made using a series of global asset allocation, arbitrage, and security selection models, and are implemented using proprietary trading and risk-management systems. Both the traditional benchmark and market-neutral strategies are managed by the same portfolio teams and driven by the same underlying research. The research of AQR's principals and portfolio teams is internationally recognized and has resulted in numerous published papers in a variety of professional journals since 1991. 

The Firm has 32 principals and more than 500 employees; nearly half of employees hold advanced degrees. We are based in Greenwich, Connecticut, with offices in Bangalore, Frankfurt, Hong Kong, London, and Sydney. * AUM is approximate as of 9/30/2024 and includes assets managed by AQR and its advisory affiliates
strategy_description:
The AQR Tax-Aware Delphi Long-Short Equity Strategy (the “Strategy”) seeks to provide equity-like returns with lower risk using a systematic approach to investing in global developed market equities. The Strategy is a long/short portfolio and targets 50% exposure to market moves (beta). Our investment model ranks and scores stocks based on a number of investment signals that aim to capture the themes listed below. Stocks that score well through the lens of these investment signals tend to be held long, while stocks that score poorly tend to be held short.
The Strategy utilizes proprietary tax aware rebalancing to systematically defer realization of capital gains and accelerate the realization of capital losses. The result is a tax-efficient strategy where realized losses may help to offset gains realized by other investments, to potentially address existing tax inefficiencies in the investor’s overall portfolio.

esg_approach_description:
AQR and the UN PRI co-created a framework for responsible investment in 2019. We include the schematic below; the full paper, entitled Clearing the Air, is available at our ESG webpage, aqr.com/esg. In short, we contend that being a responsible investor mandates both the consideration of ESG issues in the investment process (responsible asset selection) and a commitment to interacting with companies on ESG-related concerns (responsible ownership).

Responsible Asset Selection
We have used “G” signals in our models since the firm’s inception in 1998. We see the inclusion of ESG considerations in our full security selection model as promoting a more holistic approach to understanding a given company’s fundamental value, and have published research on this: for example, our paper mapping the ESG-efficient frontier argues that in general, any optimal allocation includes ESG information, like the signals in our models as standard [link]. However, we would not describe those strategies using these signals as having an explicit ESG-related investment objective.

We have been managing portfolios to clients’ ESG restricted lists for nearly two decades, over which time we naturally expanded into more robust client-customized ESG solutions. Additionally, as of June 30, 2022, we manage ~$20 billion in dedicated ESG solutions. Portfolios managed according to our standard ESG process target significant carbon reductions in long-only and relaxed constraint accounts and net negative carbon exposure in long-short portfolios, avoid companies with the largest ESG risk exposures by imposing static and dynamic exclusions, and target an improvement in portfolio ESG profile. In relaxed constraint and alternatives portfolios, we may actively short the worst ESG offenders. We currently offer this process for equity, multi-strategy absolute return, and total return portfolios.

Responsible Asset Ownership
AQR’s stewardship approach is grounded in a belief in transparency, as well as a desire to create positive long-term value for our clients. Our approach to engagement is three-fold, involving direct – both proactive and reactive – and collaborative initiatives. In 2021, we expanded our engagement efforts by volunteering to lead over 100 engagements on behalf of the CDP signatory group with companies not meeting disclosure requirements and which appear in our largest firmwide holdings. In 2022, we led engagements with twice the number of companies, encouraging them to publicly disclose their climate, forests, and water data. 

Where clients have delegated proxy voting to AQR, we seek to align our voting with long-term value creation, including on ESG issues. Please refer to our Proxy Voting Policy, which is publicly available on our ESG webpage, for further details.

Corporate Social Responsibility
AQR has a number of initiatives to help promote sustainability within its operations – ranging from offsetting 100% of our global carbon footprint internally to promoting an inclusive, diverse workplace – and with respect to its interactions with the community.

In 2019, 2020, 2021 and again in 2022, AQR received a 100% in the Human Rights Campaign’s Corporate Equality Index (CEI) national benchmarking survey (link), making our firm one of the “Best Places to Work for LGBTQ Equality” four years in a row. The recognition reflects our long-standing commitment to diversity, inclusion and equality, and to fostering an environment that ensures every employee has a true sense of belonging and every opportunity to excel in their careers.

We strive to deliver superior, long-term results for our clients by seeking to filter out market noise to identify and isolate what matters most, and to develop ideas that stand up to rigorous testing. Our focus on practical insights and analysis has made us leaders in alternative and traditional strategies since 1998. 

AQR takes a systematic, research-driven approach, applying quantitative tools to process fundamental information and manage risk. Our clients include institutional investors, such as pension funds, defined contribution plans, insurance companies, endowments, foundations, family offices and sovereign wealth funds, as well as RIAs, private banks and financial advisors. 

Investment decisions across all funds are made using a series of global asset allocation, arbitrage, and security selection models, and are implemented using proprietary trading and risk-management systems. Both the traditional benchmark and market-neutral strategies are managed by the same portfolio teams and driven by the same underlying research. The research of AQR's principals and portfolio teams is internationally recognized and has resulted in numerous published papers in a variety of professional journals since 1991. 

The Firm has 32 principals and more than 500 employees; nearly half of employees hold advanced degrees. We are based in Greenwich, Connecticut, with offices in Bangalore, Frankfurt, Hong Kong, London, and Sydney. As of September 30, 2024, AQR had approximately $116 billion* in assets under management. 

* AUM is approximate as of 9/30/2024 and includes assets managed by AQR and its advisory affiliates
strategy_description:
The AQR Delphi Long-Short Equity Strategy (the "Strategy") is a diversified alternative strategy that is systematically focused on stocks with lower risk through the lens of three investment pillars: Low Statistical Risk, Low Fundamental Risk, and Valuation. The Strategy aims to outperform its benchmark (50% MSCI World and 50% risk-free rate) while targeting a beta of 0.5 to the MSCI World Index, and seeks to deliver low correlation to other long-short equity hedge fund strategies.

The three investment pillars underlying the Strategy are grounded in academically evidenced fundamental economic understanding:
- Low Statistical Risk: Lower sensitivity to aggregate market fluctuations
- Low Fundamental Risk: Lower sensitivity to fluctuations in economic activity
- Valuation: Attractive prices relative to fundamentals

esg_approach_description:
AQR and the UN PRI co-created a framework for responsible investment in 2019. We include the schematic below; the full paper, entitled Clearing the Air, is available at our ESG webpage, aqr.com/esg. In short, we contend that being a responsible investor mandates both the consideration of ESG issues in the investment process (responsible asset selection) and a commitment to interacting with companies on ESG-related concerns (responsible ownership).

Responsible Asset Selection
We have used “G” signals in our models since the firm’s inception in 1998. We see the inclusion of ESG considerations in our full security selection model as promoting a more holistic approach to understanding a given company’s fundamental value, and have published research on this: for example, our paper mapping the ESG-efficient frontier argues that in general, any optimal allocation includes ESG information, like the signals in our models as standard [link]. However, we would not describe those strategies using these signals as having an explicit ESG-related investment objective.

We have been managing portfolios to clients’ ESG restricted lists for nearly two decades, over which time we naturally expanded into more robust client-customized ESG solutions. Additionally, as of June 30, 2022, we manage ~$20 billion in dedicated ESG solutions. Portfolios managed according to our standard ESG process target significant carbon reductions in long-only and relaxed constraint accounts and net negative carbon exposure in long-short portfolios, avoid companies with the largest ESG risk exposures by imposing static and dynamic exclusions, and target an improvement in portfolio ESG profile. In relaxed constraint and alternatives portfolios, we may actively short the worst ESG offenders. We currently offer this process for equity, multi-strategy absolute return, and total return portfolios.

Responsible Asset Ownership
AQR’s stewardship approach is grounded in a belief in transparency, as well as a desire to create positive long-term value for our clients. Our approach to engagement is three-fold, involving direct – both proactive and reactive – and collaborative initiatives. In 2021, we expanded our engagement efforts by volunteering to lead over 100 engagements on behalf of the CDP signatory group with companies not meeting disclosure requirements and which appear in our largest firmwide holdings. In 2022, we led engagements with twice the number of companies, encouraging them to publicly disclose their climate, forests, and water data. 

Where clients have delegated proxy voting to AQR, we seek to align our voting with long-term value creation, including on ESG issues. Please refer to our Proxy Voting Policy, which is publicly available on our ESG webpage, for further details.

Corporate Social Responsibility
AQR has a number of initiatives to help promote sustainability within its operations – ranging from offsetting 100% of our global carbon footprint internally to promoting an inclusive, diverse workplace – and with respect to its interactions with the community.

In 2019, 2020, 2021 and again in 2022, AQR received a 100% in the Human Rights Campaign’s Corporate Equality Index (CEI) national benchmarking survey (link), making our firm one of the “Best Places to Work for LGBTQ Equality” four years in a row. The recognition reflects our long-standing commitment to diversity, inclusion and equality, and to fostering an environment that ensures every employee has a true sense of belonging and every opportunity to excel in their careers.

strategy_description: The AQR Global Macro Strategy (the "Strategy") leverages AQR’s full suite of macro capabilities to maximize expected returns and provide a source of alpha that is diversifying to traditional and alternative investments. The Strategy employs a primarily fundamental approach, combining quantitative and qualitative inputs to build views across asset classes and geographies on the premise that markets ultimately respond to and reflect changes in their underlying fundamentals. Opportunities are exploited across equities, fixed income, currencies, commodities, and credit, and across both developed and emerging markets. First, the Strategy builds views based on the systematic evaluation of quantifiable data relevant to the fundamentals of underlying markets. Second, as not all information is quantifiable, a discretionary set of inputs complement those systematic views. Finally, as markets can experience major dislocations relative to their fundamentals at times, the Strategy opportunistically deploys risk to capitalize on those situations. Both relative value and directional sub-strategies are employed, using a diversified set of macro inputs and themes, and are integrated in a systematic portfolio construction and risk management process.

strategy_description:
The Equity Market Neutral Global Value Strategy (the "Strategy") was created in December 2019. The investment objective of the Strategy is to provide capital appreciation. The Strategy pursues its investment objective by holding a portfolio of long and short positions in equity securities, while targeting a beta of 0 to the overall equity market. The Fund utilizes value to take long and short positions in companies it believes to be attractive on a relative basis. 

Stock Selection strategies primarily do not utilize leverage as part of the Strategy’s active investment strategy, and primarily do not use derivatives for leverage. For portfolio management purposes, the Fund may use equity index futures, swaps, and/or currency forwards to equitize flows or for security-specific implementation efficiency to minimize transaction costs. In certain cases, the Strategy may also use derivatives as a tool for implementing country- or currency-specific overlay views. For these portfolios, the currency forwards and country-level equity index futures are implemented with the intention of expressing an active investment strategy. However, for strategies that do not explicitly trade country and currency selection models, derivatives typically represent only a more efficient means of gaining and managing risk exposures
