esg_approach_description:
AQR and the UN PRI co-created a framework for responsible investment in 2019. We include the schematic below; the full paper, entitled Clearing the Air, is available at our ESG webpage, aqr.com/esg. In short, we contend that being a responsible investor mandates both the consideration of ESG issues in the investment process (responsible asset selection) and a commitment to interacting with companies on ESG-related concerns (responsible ownership).

Responsible Asset Selection
We have used “G” signals in our models since the firm’s inception in 1998. We see the inclusion of ESG considerations in our full security selection model as promoting a more holistic approach to understanding a given company’s fundamental value, and have published research on this: for example, our paper mapping the ESG-efficient frontier argues that in general, any optimal allocation includes ESG information, like the signals in our models as standard [link]. However, we would not describe those strategies using these signals as having an explicit ESG-related investment objective.

We have been managing portfolios to clients’ ESG restricted lists for nearly two decades, over which time we naturally expanded into more robust client-customized ESG solutions. Additionally, as of June 30, 2022, we manage ~$20 billion in dedicated ESG solutions. Portfolios managed according to our standard ESG process target significant carbon reductions in long-only and relaxed constraint accounts and net negative carbon exposure in long-short portfolios, avoid companies with the largest ESG risk exposures by imposing static and dynamic exclusions, and target an improvement in portfolio ESG profile. In relaxed constraint and alternatives portfolios, we may actively short the worst ESG offenders. We currently offer this process for equity, multi-strategy absolute return, and total return portfolios.

Responsible Asset Ownership
AQR’s stewardship approach is grounded in a belief in transparency, as well as a desire to create positive long-term value for our clients. Our approach to engagement is three-fold, involving direct – both proactive and reactive – and collaborative initiatives. In 2021, we expanded our engagement efforts by volunteering to lead over 100 engagements on behalf of the CDP signatory group with companies not meeting disclosure requirements and which appear in our largest firmwide holdings. In 2022, we led engagements with twice the number of companies, encouraging them to publicly disclose their climate, forests, and water data. 

Where clients have delegated proxy voting to AQR, we seek to align our voting with long-term value creation, including on ESG issues. Please refer to our Proxy Voting Policy, which is publicly available on our ESG webpage, for further details.

Corporate Social Responsibility
AQR has a number of initiatives to help promote sustainability within its operations – ranging from offsetting 100% of our global carbon footprint internally to promoting an inclusive, diverse workplace – and with respect to its interactions with the community.

In 2019, 2020, 2021 and again in 2022, AQR received a 100% in the Human Rights Campaign’s Corporate Equality Index (CEI) national benchmarking survey (link), making our firm one of the “Best Places to Work for LGBTQ Equality” four years in a row. The recognition reflects our long-standing commitment to diversity, inclusion and equality, and to fostering an environment that ensures every employee has a true sense of belonging and every opportunity to excel in their careers.

management_company_description: Founded in 1999, Coatue Management is a global investment manager, managing assets on behalf of individuals, endowments, foundations and other institutional investors. The firm focuses on technology, internet and media stocks, with offices in New York, Menlo Park, Hong Kong, Los Angeles, and London. Coatue was founded by Philippe Laffont, a graduate of MIT, who worked previously at Tiger Management for Julian Robertson.
strategy_description:
- Coatue Long Biased Fund ("Long Biased" or the "Fund") employs an investment approach primarily based on fundamental research and have an overall long-term investment horizon. The Fund invests globally long only. The Fund invests primarily in the Technology, Media and Telecommunications ("TMT") sectors, and may also invest opportunistically outside the TMT sectors, for example, in the Consumer sector.
- We believe the TMT and Consumer sectors represent large markets underpinned by strong long term growth drivers. Coatue believes the forces of creative destruction and innovation continuously create large new addressable markets in these sectors and that new technology or consumer trends emerge and establish new market opportunities. After an initial horse race, where many companies compete for dominance, often with different technologies, a winner emerges as standards coalesce. Coatue views those winners in the early stages of penetrating a large new market as attractive multi-year investment candidates. Often, such companies tend to be expensive on current earnings, but are typically attractive when valued on future earnings prospects looking out three to five years. Coatue seeks to identify these new markets or trends and to use our technology expertise to determine what we believe will be winning trends and companies. With a longer investment horizon than the often short-term nature of the markets, the Fund often employs a "buy high" approach to enter into positions in these long-term winners given our belief that these companies move up the "S-Curve" and achieve greater market shares and profits.
- Coatue determines which companies we expect to be potential winners by utilizing horizontal and vertical industry analyses to assess which companies may benefit from new technology breakthroughs or standards, or which companies can reinforce their leadership through scale and competition. The emphasis during this step is to: (i) understand the forces at work and the major drivers in each trend to assess the size of the opportunity or total addressable market; (ii) analyze the different companies competing to capture this market and identify the winner; (iii) evaluate the quality of its business model and management team: and (iv) assess where the company is on its S-Curve with respect to market penetration and profit growth.
- Coatue also believes that attractive investment opportunities exist in markets that are already in more mature stages as long as they continue to benefit from secular trends. In particular, we believe that capital allocation and capital return to shareholders can be key value drivers for companies with strong business models but moderate growth.

Current investment themes include the trend toward electrification, the transformative technological innovation including AI infrastructure, and the rapid expansion of renewables (despite political headwinds). It’s anticipated that around 5% of global GDP will be invested in the energy transition annually over the next 30 years.

The investment team employs a thematic investment approach looking for changes in market trends across key industries, technology and regulation to assess how these affect sub-sectors and regions. On a micro level, the team evaluates the company-specific outlook with a focus on competitiveness, management and financial position.

esg_approach_description:
ESG Process
The energy sector is one of the largest contributors to global environmental pollution, including the largest source of carbon emissions and other airborne pollutants and a key contributor to poor land and water use. There are also significant risks and negative externalities associated with nuclear power, uranium and coal mining. The emerging new power system promises to be significantly more sustainable, from both an environmental and an economic perspective and we see ample new investment opportunities in this transformation process. The core of CLEAN’s mandate is to invest in companies that reflect this trend towards sustainability. 

The Firm utilises a proprietary three-step process: 

Step 1 - Exclusion: 
Carbon Underground 200
The Carbon Underground 200 list identifies the 100 largest public coal and 100 largest public Oil & Gas reserve owners based on the potential CO2 emissions of their reported reserves. All of these companies are excluded from the CLEAN investment universe.

Norges Bank Investment Management published Exclusion Lists
As managers for the Norwegian Government Pension Fund Global, Norges produce product and conduct based exclusion lists restricting investments in companies that do not meet certain criteria. CLEAN is committed to not investing in any companies involved in the Production of Coal or Coal-Based Energy product-based exclusion list, or companies listed on any of the conduct-based exclusion lists.

Paris Aligned Benchmark
CLEAN follows the exclusions for the EU Paris-aligned benchmarks as set out in Article 12(1) of the Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/1818 and will not invest in corporate issuers which, in the opinion of Clean Energy Transition LLP:
1.	are involved in any activities related to controversial weapons;
2.	are involved in the cultivation and production of tobacco;
3.	are companies in violation of the UNGC principles or the OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises;
4.	derive 1% or more of their revenues from exploration, mining, extraction, distribution or refining of hard coal and lignite;
5.	derive 10% or more of their revenues from the exploration, extraction, distribution or refining of oil fuels;
6.	derive 50% or more of their revenues from the exploration, extraction, manufacturing or distribution of gaseous fuels;
7.	derive 50% or more of their revenues from electricity generation with a GHG intensity of more than 100g CO2 e/kWh.

Clean Energy Exclusion List
In addition to the Carbon Underground 200 and the Norges Bank Exclusion Lists, the Firm has established a set of internal guidelines to exclude companies that derive more than 1% of net external sales from oil, gas, or coal extraction activities.
The Firm’s ESG Committee meets on a monthly basis to review existing companies in CLEAN’s portfolio, as well as the proposed addition of new companies to the portfolio and/or the exclusion of companies from CLEAN’s universe based on the “Step 1” process summarised above. The Committee is comprised of Eirik Hogner (Portfolio Manager), Per Lekander (Deputy Portfolio Manager and CEO), Benjamin Singh (COO & CCO; Chair of the Committee), Nick Rodgers (Quantitative Analyst & Trader) and Naomi Gill (Client Relations Associate). 

Step 2 - Proprietary rating: 
In the second step, we seek to assess four basic questions. (1) What ESG challenges does the relevant company have? (2) To what extent does the company acknowledge these? (3) Do we see a strategy to tackle these challenges? (4) Do we believe that the company has the financial and human resources to implement that strategy and overcome the relevant challenges?

Examples of such strategic plans range from clear actions to reduce environmental impact; programs aimed at improving the health and safety of employees and contractors, and initiatives geared towards increasing staff empowerment. We believe that these strategic plans should form part of a company’s “tone from the top” working culture, and therefore we seek clear evidence that the relevant company’s management team embraces ESG.

It is essential that the company exhibits a conscious ESG culture, not only internally, but also within the whole supply and distribution chains, including waste.

One could rely on external ratings to assess all the criteria above, or the ESG reports published by many companies these days, but as explained above, we prefer a more personalised approach. We like to discuss these issues directly with the company, and better yet, assess them ourselves through company site visits.

Step 3 - Invest and Monitor: 
The third step includes monitoring ESG news flow at the regulatory, industry, and company levels; company site visits to search for evidence of ESG measures; ongoing dialogue with management; and systematic voting on companies’ resolutions.

It is clear that the selected companies are not immune to disappointments, especially in the case of concealed malicious intentions in some divisions. However, if the culture is right, these cases should be few and far between.

Only constant dialogue with companies, their suppliers and customers, and even ex-employees, through management meetings, attendance at capital market days (which give us opportunities to meet managers at lower levels) and company site visits, can help us develop a true appreciation of the culture.

management_company_description: Tryphon Capital Advisers, Inc., a long/short healthcare investment management firm, conducts leading, fundamentally-based healthcare research.  The analytical effort is led by founder Gerry D. Koumatos, Ph.D., CFA, who has 25 years experience on Wall Street.  Our investment process is tied to the insights we gather through our constant information gathering and analysis of key issues in healthcare.  For example, we attend medical and investor conferences, review medical literature, visit academic and medical centers to interview key thought leaders and attend FDA advisory meetings.  Investment ideas constantly emerge from this information flow.  We refer to our experience to focus on the key issues for each company. Usually, it takes months for us to develop investment strategies surrounding a group of companies, but this long lead time provides many investment ideas because we are examining about 20-30 new companies at any given time to validate and refine our investment strategy.  We cast a wide net by contacting hundreds of companies each year.  Tryphon is always choosing from at least 5-6 “finalists” to displace stocks which have already achieved our return objective. Because we rarely have a shortage of investment ideas, we are levered approximately 2:1. We begin our risk management before a stock enters the portfolio. We perform scenario analyses for each company and institute valuation objectives for each stock, which also serve as price limits for trading. Furthermore, we often use pairs to minimize risk. Also, we maintain a portfolio Beta range of -0.4 to +0.4.  We have made changes over the years to our risk management strategy in light of changes in Fed interest-rate policy. We consider the interest-rate policy now to be normal and have readjusted our risk management strategy accordingly. We have re-instituted tighter net long and beta controls of the portfolio that fall back in line with strategies we had pre-2008. Obviously, we can be wrong in our picks, but we view these moments as unique opportunities to recover money for our investors.  How? Tryphon has preset strategies for periods after surprising news. We use our proprietary database to quickly identify the effects of the surprise to the sector.  This helps explain Tryphon’s rapid drawdown recovery.  Nearly all of our investors have come from referrals within the financial community or our existing clients.

strategy_description:
L1 Capital Global Long Short Fund (GLSF) is a geographically unconstrained, global version of L1 Capital’s flagship Long Short Strategy (which focuses on Australia and invests up to 30% in global developed markets). portfolio_additional_details:
The L1 Capital investment team combines valuation (primarily discounted cash flow) with qualitative considerations (management quality, long-term industry and company structure and business trends) to identify attractive investment opportunities. Given the strict valuation criteria in the process, the portfolio tends to have a slight value and contrarian bias. 

The investment process is based on detailed fundamental stock research by the 12-person Equity Long Short Team. Their comprehensive company visitation programme of between 2,000 and 3,000 company meetings a year includes one-on-one visits with company management, listed and unlisted competitors, customers, suppliers, operational personnel, regulators, consultants, unions and other parties that can help provide a deeper insight. The team have incorporated a bespoke research database and ranking tool which has been instrumental to the firm’s success and consistency. 

Intensive, bottom-up stock selection has been a defining feature of L1 Capital’s approach since inception. This approach enables the investment team to put into context their detailed analysis of annual reports, company announcements, industry publications, broker reports and other relevant material, which, when combined with their financial modelling, allow them to form views on management quality, company structure and business trends. 

Long positions reflect the stocks with the highest combined valuation and qualitative rankings from L1 Capital’s proprietary research, overlaid with consideration of asymmetry of likely returns, liquidity characteristics, individual stock contribution to risk and correlation between positions. Short positions typically are the lowest ranked stocks, reflecting being overvalued and exhibiting weak management, industry structure and operating trends. Importantly, any short position must have a clear catalyst for a share price fall. Shorts are held at a lower weight in the portfolio than longs to provide a buffer in case the shares rally before the catalyst is realised. The Co-CIOs use Bloomberg Risk Services and MSCI Barra to monitor a variety of risk factors, including portfolio beta, correlations, VAR, stock contribution to risk, liquidity, etc.

strategy_description:
L1 Capital Long Short Fund is an absolute return strategy launched in 2014 that offers investors a that offers investors a highly diversified portfolio of long and short positions based on L1 Capital’s fundamental bottom-up research process.

The Fund’s objective is to deliver a net return of at least 10% p.a. to investors with considerably less market risk (on average) and invests primarily in Australian equities with up to 30% in international shares. 

The portfolio typically comprises 50-100 positions across a wide range of sectors. The investment team, led by L1 Capital Co-Founders/Co-CIOs, Mark Landau and Rafi Lamm, combines valuation (primarily discounted cash flow) with qualitative considerations (management quality, long-term industry and company structure and business trends) to identify attractive investment opportunities. The team conducts extensive independent company and industry research, including meetings with a wide variety of company and industry players.

The Fund has three enduring advantages over many other Australian competitors:
1.	Market exposure: Ability and willingness to adjust the portfolio net long to reflect the risk-reward of the market.
2.	Shorting: Allows the portfolio to profit from both rising and falling share prices.
3.	International exposure: Scope to exploit research insights offshore, not just domestically, broadening the opportunity set beyond the Australian market.

Together, these three levers, which the L1 Capital Long Short Equities Investment Team uses actively and with conviction, are tools for generating returns from all of the team’s investment and market insights.

portfolio_additional_details:
The L1 Capital investment team combines valuation (primarily discounted cash flow) with qualitative considerations (management quality, long-term industry and company structure and business trends) to identify attractive investment opportunities. Given the strict valuation criteria in the process, the portfolio tends to have a slight value and contrarian bias. 

The investment process is based on detailed fundamental stock research by the 12-person Long Short Equities Team. Their comprehensive company visitation programme of between 2,000 and 3,000 company meetings a year includes one-on-one visits with company management, listed and unlisted competitors, customers, suppliers, operational personnel, regulators, consultants, unions and other parties that can help provide a deeper insight. The team have incorporated a bespoke research database and ranking tool which has been instrumental to the firm’s success and consistency. 

Intensive, bottom-up stock selection has been a defining feature of L1 Capital’s approach since inception. This approach enables the investment team to put into context their detailed analysis of annual reports, company announcements, industry publications, broker reports and other relevant material, which, when combined with their financial modelling, allow them to form views on management quality, company structure and business trends.

Long positions reflect the stocks with the highest combined valuation and qualitative rankings from L1 Capital’s proprietary research, overlaid with consideration of asymmetry of likely returns, liquidity characteristics, individual stock contribution to risk and correlation between positions. Short positions typically are the lowest ranked stocks, reflecting being overvalued and exhibiting weak management, industry structure and operating trends. Importantly, any short position must have a clear catalyst for a share price fall. 

Shorts are held at a lower weight in the portfolio than longs to provide a buffer in case the shares rally before the catalyst is realised. The Co-CIOs use Bloomberg Risk Services and MSCI Barra to monitor a variety of risk factors, including portfolio beta, correlations, VAR, stock contribution to risk, liquidity, etc.

management_company_description:
A Singapore-based hedge fund boutique cofounded in 2011 by Ranodeb (Ronnie) Roy (CIO) and Vickram Mangalgiri (COO). The firm comprises of 38 individuals, and the CIO leads an investment team of 14 professionals with support from two deputy CIOs for the macro and credit strategies.
 
The investment team architecture and compensation mechanism are key to implementing the investment process and encourages alpha generation through collaborative teamwork. The investment process follows a research driven and value-oriented approach to form macro themes, which typically have an investment time horizon of 6 to 12 months. Risk management is integrated within the investment and portfolio construction process, and adopts rules-based monitoring, which ensures volatility control and limits drawdowns. To enable this, the risk management function is independent, consists of 5 team members and is led by a seasoned professional with over 25-years of experience.
 
Currently, RV Capital manages over US$1bn in assets across three Asia focused strategies (i) macro, (ii) liquid public credit, and (iii) a stand-alone India private credit specialty.
 
Asia Macro
A discretionary macro strategy that employs a research-driven approach to generate alpha through long, short and relative value investments in Rates, FX and Credit in Asian Markets. Launched in January 2012 in a Cayman structure and in September 2016 in UCITS, the macro strategy is distinctly different in that it focuses entirely on Asian markets and seeks to implement medium to long-term views (6 to 12 months). This has resulted in consistently positive returns with low volatility. In 2022, using greater leverage, a higher volatility version of the macro strategy was launched.
 
Asia Credit
A carve-out of the macro strategy using a research driven, long and short approach to generate alpha in publicly traded, liquid, single-name credits in Asia. A stand-alone fund using the same team, research and investment process was launched in March 2022.
 
India Private Credit
A standalone strategy that opportunistically invests in performing private credit and high yielding price dislocated bonds in secondary markets. The first fund launched in February 2023 in a close-ended structure and has an investment team led by Shyamal Karmakar (CIO).

name: Fidelity Convertible Arbitrage Fund LP
management_company_description:
Since Fidelity’s founding in 1946, the firm has been known for its professional money management and comprehensive client services. Fidelity Investments is one of the world’s largest providers of financial services with assets under administration of $17.97 trillion, including total discretionary assets of $7.1 trillion as of December 31, 2025. In 1977, Edward C. Johnson 3d became Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of FMR, succeeding his father, Edward C. Johnson 2d. In 2014, Abigail P. Johnson, daughter of Edward 3d, was named Chief Executive Officer of FMR. In 2016, Edward C. Johnson 3d retired as Chairman of FMR LLC, Fidelity’s parent company. Abigail P. Johnson, Chief Executive Officer of Fidelity, assumed the role of Chairman of FMR LLC, with responsibility for the management of all FMR LLC businesses, including Fidelity Financial Services and Fidelity’s other diversified businesses and investments.
Fidelity is a privately held company, with its stock entirely owned by employees and members of the Johnson family. Each stockholder not only has an interest in the company's success but also has an ability to contribute to that achievement.
Headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, Fidelity employs more than 80,000-plus associates with a global presence spanning nine other countries across North America, Europe, Asia, and Australia.
Fidelity Diversifying Solutions LLC (FDS) is an investment management firm primarily providing discretionary advisory and sub-advisory services. FDS has been in business since 2022. FDS is a Fidelity Investments company and is wholly owned by FMR LLC. FDS is part of the Fidelity Asset Management Solutions (FAMS) business unit which, together with its affiliates, FIAM LLC and Fidelity Institutional Asset Management Trust Company, provides a broad array of investment solutions with its Global Institutional Solutions (GIS), Global Asset Allocation (GAA), and institutional equity, fixed income, high income, and alternative asset management teams.
FDS employs a broad range of investment strategies across various asset classes and also offers customized investment strategies and solutions. FDS offers advice on a diverse set of investable assets, including a variety of investment securities and asset types. In addition, FDS or its affiliates provides the management and administrative services necessary for the operation of investment funds and institutional client accounts. FDS is registered with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission as a commodity trading advisor and commodity pool operator. FDS is also a member of the National Futures Association. 
FDS leverages the resources of the entire Fidelity organization (“Fidelity Investments” or “Fidelity”) in managing the Fund.
strategy_description:
The goal of the Fund’s investment process is to construct a portfolio that aims to take advantage of market inefficiencies and the complexities of convertible securities to generate alpha.

The Fund’s strategy involves gaining exposure to a portfolio of convertible securities (typically debt securities or preferred stocks that can be exchanged for, or converted automatically to, common stock), and seeking to hedge the equity risk inherent to these securities by selling short the common stock into which the securities may be converted. By using a diverse set of trade constructions and underlying instruments, the Fund seeks to generate attractive absolute returns while maintaining a “market-neutral” stance.

The investment team generally aims to create a portfolio of long bond/short stock positions that are delta neutral, long equity volatility and long credit of the issuer. This is known as classic convertible arbitrage. In addition to classic convertible arbitrage, the Fund intends to utilize other investment constructs including, but not limited to: (i) convertible yield - long out-of-the money convertible bond with a strong or improving credit profile, short duration; (ii) synthetic put – long deep-in-the money convertible bond, short equity; (iii) credit defensive – long out-of-the money convertible bond, short equity; (iv) event driven – corporate repurchases, exchange offering; and/or (v) Vega defensive – long in-the-money convertible bond with a short call option trading at inflated implied volatility. It is anticipated that the most common trades in the portfolio will be classical convertible arbitrage, synthetic put, and convertible yield.  

The strategy is typically implemented using convertible bonds, equity, straight bonds, and options, but may be invested, directly or indirectly, on margin or otherwise, in securities and other financial instruments issued by U.S. or non-U.S. entities. This includes bonds, notes, debentures, currencies, forwards, futures contracts, options, swaps, swaptions, warrants, and other derivatives. The Fund may also employ the use of passive ETFs. 

While the portfolio will be primarily invested in liquid positions at most times, the team may elect to invest in securities or other instruments that have limited liquidity, such as certain privately negotiated convertible bond offerings, if it deems such opportunities to be compelling. The team expects that illiquid positions will not exceed ten percent of the net asset value of the Fund.

management_company_description:
Founded in 2001 and part of BNY since 2008, ARX Investimentos is a Brazilian asset‑management firm recognized for its independent investment philosophy and strong long‑term track record. With deep expertise across equities, macro, and fixed income, the firm combines the agility of an independent manager while operating autonomously under BNY’s global asset‑management umbrella.
As a specialist in Brazilian markets, ARX focuses on delivering high‑quality investment solutions to both local and international investors. Its experienced team applies rigorous stock selection, macro analysis, and multi‑strategy approaches to capture opportunities within Brazil’s dynamic economic environment, consistently emphasizing excellence and disciplined execution.
Currently, ARX manages approximately USD 10 billion across five strategies—Brazilian equities, corporate debt, REITs, macro, and cash—supported by strong internal processes and a commitment to ethical values, high‑performing teams, and long‑term client partnerships. strategy_description:
The philosophy is based on a discretionary investment management. ARX Value follows a combination of fundamental analysis and bottom-up stock selection in the approach to portfolio construction. In addition, macroeconomic and business sector conditions are evaluated.   
It is important to highlight that, during the investment process of the fund, a quantitative screening is used in the initial phase in order to identify prospective buy candidates, according to some parameters, such as: earnings estimates, growth, price, dividend yield estimates, liquidity etc. Once this is done, the universe of stocks is further analyzed by incorporating fundamental analysis with macroeconomic scenarios, industry and sector trends and risk.
The portfolio will usually be composed of a large percentage of high-quality businesses with sound cash flow generation and a smaller percentage of companies that have exceptional long-term perspectives, but may be going through challenging times in the short term.

management_company_description: III Capital Management (“III”) is a registered investment adviser that has been managing investor capital since 1982. The firm currently advises investment funds and accounts with over $5 billion in capital across four primary strategies: fixed income relative value, long only credit, long/short credit, and asymmetric portfolios. strategy_description:
The III Multi-Strategy Fund (the "Fund") seeks to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns with low correlation to equity markets and an emphasis on capital preservation.  To achieve this objective, the Fund will build portfolios primarily comprised of III Capital Management’s three core alpha strategies: Fixed-Income Relative Value, Long/Short Credit, and Convexity. The Fund’s investment approach leverages the firm’s longstanding investment expertise in each individual strategy (40 years in FIRV, 20 years in Credit, and 15 years in Convexity) while incorporating a dynamic capital allocation process designed to tactically and fluidly allocate capital across strategies and regions. The Fund’s three investment strategies tend to be complementary and can provide diversification through their 15+ underlying sub-strategies and various individual trades. The diversification across strategies and the long-volatility bias of III's Convexity strategy are designed to help the Fund moderate drawdowns and potentially outperform during periods of equity market stress.

Strategy AUM is ~$480mm as of March 1, 2026 including a separately managed account launched in July 2025 and the commingled III Multi-Strategy Fund that launched in January 2026.

management_company_description:
Bracebridge Capital, LLC (“Bracebridge” or the “firm”) is a leading alternative asset manager founded in 1994 by Nancy Zimmerman and Gabriel Sunshine. The firm has approximately 175 employees, including about 80 investment and quantitative research professionals. The senior investment team of 8 principals is highly stable, with an average tenure of more than 20 years working together.

The investment objective of Bracebridge is to achieve absolute returns and capital preservation by identifying and capitalizing on inefficiencies in global financial markets. We believe markets are inefficient, and the absolute return funds seek to capture the cheapness or richness created by these inefficiencies while hedging risks related to interest rates, foreign exchange, and credit. By seeking to hedge these macro risks, the funds’ strategy is focused on isolating the source of potential excess returns and creating a portfolio with a return profile that is intended to be largely uncorrelated with systemic factors. 

Bracebridge is selectively open to a small number of new partners to raise $1-2 billion of capital.
strategy_description:
The Bracebridge absolute return strategy seeks to produce consistent, superior risk-adjusted returns by capitalizing on market anomalies across global financial markets.

Historically, fixed income and related derivative markets have provided the most robust arena in which to identify and capitalize on investment opportunities for absolute return investments. We also seek arbitrage opportunities in other liquid capital and currency markets.

We allocate risk capital across four broad areas: Corporate Credit, Structured Products, Developed Market Rates, and Emerging Markets. Representative strategies include corporate capital structure arbitrage and bond/credit default swap (CDS) basis, structured products relative value, sovereign credit and emerging market arbitrages, yield curve and intramarket opportunities, cash/futures arbitrage, and inefficiencies in pricing of debt and derivative instruments that are new to the market.

The firm manages several investment vehicles participating in one overall absolute return investment strategy. We have both Cayman Islands feeder funds and a Delaware limited partnership feeder fund, and we offer share classes in multiple currencies (e.g. EUR and GBP).

An investment in any of the funds managed by Bracebridge is speculative and involves a significant degree of risk. Such risks are described in more detail in the Confidential Offering Memorandum of each fund.

Investment and Trading Risks in General
All investments made by the funds risk the loss of capital.  Bracebridge utilizes such investment techniques as margin transactions, short sales, option transactions and forward and futures contracts, which practices can, in certain circumstances, maximize the adverse impact to which the funds may be subject.  No guarantee or representation is made that a fund’s program will be successful, and investment results may vary substantially over time. The funds have been given very broad investment parameters and maintain a flexible investment program.  The funds are not limited with respect to the types of investment strategies they may employ or the markets or instruments in which they may invest. 

Past Performance Not Indicative of Future Results
There can be no assurance that the funds will achieve their investment objective.  The past investment performance of the funds should not be construed as an indication of the future results of an investment in the funds.  There can be no assurance that Bracebridge’s assessments of the short-term or long-term prospects of investments will prove accurate.

Credit Risk
The funds invest in corporate and government bonds, and until the bonds are sold or paid at maturity, the funds are exposed to credit risk relating to whether the bond issuer will meet its obligations when they come due.  

Arbitrage Trading
Arbitrage transactions involve the risk that transactions will fail to be executed as intended or agreed upon, the risk that the other party to a transaction will fail to pay or otherwise perform as agreed, and credit risk.  Arbitrage investing also involves the risk that the value of a fund’s long positions may decrease while the value of its corresponding short positions may increase over the same period.  

Hedging Transactions Risk
There can be no assurance that the funds will engage in hedging transactions at any given time or from time to time.  There is significant judgment involved in determining which risks to hedge, how to effectively hedge such risks and how much to hedge such risks.  Failure to effectively hedge significant risks in a fund’s portfolio could have a significant adverse impact on the fund.

Risks Associated with the Use of Leverage
The leveraged trading strategy of the funds may increase the volatility of their returns.  A relatively small price movement in an option, futures, or forward contract may result in immediate and substantial losses to the fund.  A fund’s use of leverage may magnify many of the risks discussed herein.

Market Risk
If a fund were required to liquidate all or a portion of its portfolio during a constrained time period as a result of market conditions, investor redemptions, or otherwise, it may realize significantly less value than the value at which it previously recorded investments in such portfolio.  

Counterparty Risk
The funds face the risk that the other parties to transactions entered into by the funds fail to perform as agreed, including the risk that a counterparty will not settle a transaction in accordance with its terms and conditions because of a dispute over the terms of the contract (whether or not bona fide) or because of a credit or liquidity problem, thus causing the funds to suffer a loss.  


Derivatives Risk
The funds’ use of derivative instruments involves risks different from, or possibly greater than, the risks associated with investing directly in securities and other traditional investments.  Derivative products are specialized instruments that require investment techniques and risk analyses different from those associated with equities and fixed income securities.  Derivatives are subject to a number of risks described elsewhere in this section, such as limited liquidity, counterparty and leverage risk.

Illiquid Securities
The funds may not be able to readily dispose of certain investments, and, in some cases, may be contractually prohibited from disposing of such securities for a specified period.  These limitations on liquidity of a fund’s investments could prevent a successful sale thereof, result in delay of any sale, reduce the amount of proceeds that might otherwise be realized, or result in distribution of securities in-kind upon liquidation of the fund.

Trading Restrictions
Bracebridge, including as a result of confidentiality agreements or non-disclosure agreements, may acquire confidential or material non-public information which may restrict the funds in their investment activities.  

Interest Rate Risk
To the extent the funds invest in corporate bonds, notes, mortgage-related or other asset-backed securities, or other securities which are callable, such securities may be prepaid.  Because prepayments generally increase when interest rates fall, the funds are subject to the risk that cash flows from securities will have to be reinvested at lower rates.  Likewise, since prepayments decrease when interest rates rise, these securities have maturities that tend to be longer when that is least desirable.  

Currency Risk
A portion of the funds’ assets is invested in debt and equity securities denominated in various non-U.S. currencies and in other financial instruments, the price of which is determined with reference to such currencies.  The funds will, however, value their investments and other assets in United States dollars.  To the extent unhedged, the value of these assets will fluctuate with United States dollar exchange rates as well as with price changes in various local markets and currencies.  

Prime Broker Risk
For assets other than fully paid securities and excess margin securities, subject to the establishment of reserves, a prime broker generally has the ability to loan, pledge, and rehypothecate the securities in a fund's account, as is typical market practice, and may have insufficient assets to meet all of its obligations to customers in the event of the insolvency of the prime broker or a similar event which restricts the fund’s ability to seek return of the securities in the fund’s account.

Pricing Limits on Futures Contracts
Once the price of a contract for a particular future has increased or decreased by an amount equal to any daily limit imposed by exchange regulations, positions in that contract can neither be taken nor liquidated unless traders are willing to effect trades at or within the limit.  These limits could prevent a fund from promptly liquidating unfavorable positions and subject the fund to substantial losses.

We leverage more than four decades of convertible security research and investing experience. Our portfolio is diversified across sectors and credit quality, with an emphasis on companies possessing higher-quality balance sheets. Our equity research positions us to identify convertibles with attractive upside potential.

name: Helikon Long Short Equity Fund
management_company_description:
Federico Riggio and his team deploy capital across Europe and selected Emerging Markets, with other domiciles of listing (such as US and Asia) justified by underlying economic drivers. The Helikon Long Short Equity Fund aims to deliver absolute returns over the medium term through implementing a concentrated, value-driven long/short investment strategy, with an opportunistic credit exposure. The Fund is currently hard closed and is only accepting subscriptions where there are offsetting redemptions.

The portfolio is usually built on a 2:1 equity long/short ratio. Typical high conviction long equity positions are sized at 10%-12% of NAV (maximum 15%) and typical high conviction short equity positions are sized at 3%-4% of NAV (maximum 7.5%).
Initial position sizes are usually 3% of NAV for the longs and 1% of NAV for the shorts; as conviction grows, positions are scaled-up. Potential catalysts can be an input to sizing decisions. The sum of long positions sized >5% is likely to exceed 80% of NAV at most times. The portfolio is likely to be composed of 15-25 longs and 10-15 shorts (excluding hedges). 

Gross equity exposure range: 100% to 200%. Net equity exposure range: from net short up to 100% net long. 
Typical net equity exposure in the +40% to +70% band. Opportunistic gross credit exposure range: 0% to 50%.

name: Chenavari European Debt Opportunities IV
management_company_description:
Chenavari is an established, credit-focused asset manager with a core expertise in European markets. With expertise across the liquidity spectrum of credit, Chenavari aims to profit from idiosyncrasies and inefficiencies within credit markets, which are due to macro (such as banks' deleveraging, monetary policies, etc.) as well as technical factors. The Firm concentrates its investment activity on fundamental strategies that may offer attractive risk-reward profiles on a relative value basis with low market correlation and low beta to broad credit markets.

Chenavari’s investment strategies can be segmented across three groups: 

•	Liquid strategies, including investments in single name corporates, European financials, credit indices, asset-backed securities, across both cash and derivative markets;
•	Private Credit strategies, such as portfolio acquisitions of primarily performing loans; risk sharing/significant risk transfer, asset-based lending, and specialty finance (new loan origination) in consumer finance, receivables and leasing; and
•	CLO management, including investment in senior secured loans and revolving credit facilities through European collateralised loan obligation structures.
strategy_description:
The Fund seeks to deliver attractive risk adjusted returns and stable income by investing in granular, predominantly performing European loan portfolios through two complementary sub-strategies: Specialty Finance (Credit Origination and Portfolio Acquisitions) and Significant Risk Transfer (SRT) transactions. Underlying exposures may include large corporate, SME, trade finance, asset backed, and secured and unsecured consumer loans.

The Fund operates an institutional evergreen structure allowing continuous subscriptions and defined liquidity windows, enabling investors to adjust their exposure over time via a structured pass-through share class mechanism.

name: Otter Rock Advisors Fund
management_company_description:
Otter Rock is a global, fundamental equity long/short fund focused on TMT, fintech, consumer and industrials impacted by technological change. The portfolio will run mid-net through-cycle, while maintaining a concentrated, factor aware, but not factor constrained portfolio with significant exposure to small and mid-cap equities on the long and short side. The firm is committed to building a robust short book of single name alpha-generative ideas. 

Otter Rock is led by CIO Alix Karlan who brings over 10 years of investment experience and 18 years of entrepreneurial experience to the firm.  Otter Rock is the culmination of Karlan’s professional experiences. By leveraging his learnings from both Viking and Alua, Karlan will bring to bear the risk management, capital allocation and talent development approach he learned at Viking to a concentrated portfolio strategy he has developed with his own capital since departing Alua.  At first, the CIO will manage capital allocation and portfolio oversight entirely. Over time, we plan to cultivate internal sector leaders to act as discretionary portfolio managers much in the way Viking developed their sub portfolios, the structure of which Karlan helped revamp while there. We believe our sub-portfolios will allow sector experts to express their top ideas while also learning to manage a concentrated L/S, alpha-generating portfolio. The CIO's portfolio we believe will utilize insights from the sub-PMs to maintain focus on our best ideas. This approach we believe will benefit our investors by fostering firm-wide confidence in our top ideas, enhancing talent development, creating a performance focused culture while ensuring team continuity, and by developing the next generation of leaders so that Otter Rock endures to serve investors for the long term.

name: Voleon Institutional Strategies
management_company_description: Founded in 2007 by two machine learning scientists, The Voleon Group (Voleon) is a global investment management and technology firm. Voleon is a pioneer in the application of machine learning to a wide range of financial markets and prediction problems. Today, Voleon manages ~$20Bn in AUM from institutional investors globally. Voleon's team of 400+ employees includes ~270 technical staff, spanning researchers, software engineers, and development and production operations personnel. This technical team includes one of the largest specialized machine learning research and development teams in the finance industry, with ~90 PhDs. Voleon applies the science of machine learning to build quantitative investment strategies that seek to deliver stable, uncorrelated alpha across market environments. Voleon applies machine learning throughout the investment process, not just for signal generation. Machine learning breakthroughs in areas such as portfolio construction, risk management, and trade execution have been critical to the firm's success. Voleon has now applied the science of machine learning across asset classes, regions, and time horizons.
strategy_description: Voleon Institutional Strategies Fund LP (the "Fund") is a fund that deploys machine learning quantitative market-neutral strategies. The Fund seeks to preserve capital and maximize absolute returns with limited drawdowns, high Sharpe ratio, and low correlation to returns available elsewhere. The Fund is a feeder fund generally for U.S. investors that invests substantially all of its assets in Voleon Institutional Strategies Holdings, LLC (“Voleon Institutional Strategies Holdings”). The Fund accesses Voleon's global short, mid, and long-horizon equities capabilities.

management_company_description:
Linear B Partners is a specialist relative value credit manager investing in global developed corporate and structured credit markets.

The flagship fund employs a market-neutral and absolute return strategy targeting consistent risk adjusted returns over a market cycle with no correlation to global credit and equity risk indices.

strategy_description:
Linear B Master Fund LP ("the Fund") is an opportunistic relative value credit fund investing in global corporate and structured credit markets. The Fund aims to produce differentiated returns by taking advantage of both the splintered and complex nature of the developed credit markets and targeting risk capital inefficiencies left behind by the Global Financial Crisis’ regulatory changes.

The strategy employs a market-neutral, bottom up portfolio construction coupled with detailed risk management.

Typical portfolio composition can include loan warehouses, credit derivatives indices and bespoke portfolios, cash bond and derivative single name credit relative value transactions (e.g., curves, basis trades, etc.), trade receivable financing, and opportunistic investments in CLO liabilities.

management_company_description:
Svelland Capital, founded in 2016 by Tor Andre Svelland, is a commodities and freight-focused investment firm managing approximately USD 1bn. Tor brings over 30 years of commodity and shipping market experience from Trafigura, Goldman Sachs, Carnegie, and Klaveness. The firm’s flagship Svelland Global Trading Fund (launched 2017) employs a discretionary, trading-oriented long/short strategy across energy, metals, and freight markets, delivering returns with low correlation to equity and credit markets. The strategy expresses risk through a blend of commodity and freight derivatives and related equities. Svelland also manages the Svelland Commodities Futures Plus strategy, a discretionary L/S futures-only strategy with a 3-year track record, accessed via SMA and benefiting from low margin requirements. In addition, the firm co-owns and manages a physical gold ETC in partnership with Edmond de Rothschild. 

Svelland Capital (Cayman) Ltd is the manager (the “Manager”) of Svelland Global Trading Master Fund (the “Fund”) and has appointed Mirabella Financial Services LLP as the AIFM of the Fund. 

Svelland Capital (UK) Ltd is a wholly owned entity of Svelland Capital (Cayman) Ltd and is an Appointed Representative of Mirabella Advisers LLP, which is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority.
strategy_description:
The Svelland Global Trading Fund is a fundamental, absolute return trading strategy focused on the commodity complex. The strategy's investment objective is to deliver superior net returns to investors in all market conditions with low or negative correlation to listed equity and fixed income markets. The team will leverage their experience in commodities to benefit from structural tailwinds driving value in the sector. These include an inexorable transition to a renewable energy future and managing geopolitical shocks and risks in energy interdependence. The strategy seeks to add alpha through deep fundamental research, its extensive network of commodity and freight market intelligence and proven commodities risk-taking experience of the team.

The strategy brings knowledge of the entire commodities supply chain and expresses asymmetric risk positions across commodity futures, freight derivatives, and commodity-related equities. The broad mandate allows the team flexibility in terms of how it wishes to express its views - directionally, relative value or often with options where appropriate.

portfolio_additional_details:
Strategy can express risk through a blend of three core asset classes i) commodity futures, ii) commodity related equities and iii) freight futures (FFAs). The strategy is agnostic to the instrument selected, it depends on which instrument offers the best risk reward. The strategy does not compartmentalize a certain % of exposure in equities or in futures and options. The portfolio exposure to these asset classes is changeable.  The strategy does not trade all commodities, only those that the team have deep experience in trading from both a physical and paper standpoint. The strategy trades across the energy, metals and freight complex.

Portfolio typically composed of 4-5 themes, 40-50  line items, a mix of longs and shorts across the three core instrument types (equities, futures and FFAs).  

The strategy is trading orientated. We can turn the portfolio 20-25x a year (worth noting those turnover figures can seem large but when we trade a mix of futures and equities a good bulk of the turnover is in futures (in and out on Brent etc). Whilst trading is part of the strategy, certain equity names can be longer term holds and can be quite concentrated if the equity meets certain criteria: high dividend paying, takeover candidate. A typical large equity position will be 8-10% of NAV, but on occasions the positions can be larger. A typical large futures positions can be ~10-15% of NAV.

Gross and net figures provided above are typical ranges.

Derivative and Leverage Risk - The Fund may engage in leverage through financial derivative instruments for investment purposes. Use of leverage may magnify both gains and losses in a portfolio. Theoretically, this could result in an infinite loss.

Credit Risk - The Fund invests a portion of its assets in debt securities whose value would be significantly affected if the issuers or borrowers were unable to or were perceived to be unable to pay. This may adversely affect the Fund’s return.

Liquidity Risk - The Fund may be unable to sell certain investments readily at their fair market value. This may affect the value of the Fund and could affect performance.  

Counterparty Risk - The risk that a counterparty will be unable to honour its financial obligations for a trade, contract or other transactions, on the due date. The insolvency of any institution providing services such as the safekeeping of assets or acting as counterparty in respect to financial derivatives or other instruments may expose the Fund to financial loss.

Currency Risk - The Fund may hold investments in currencies other than the base currency and fluctuations in these exchange rates may affect the returns on investments.

Operational Risk - The risk of direct or indirect loss resulting from inadequate or failed processes, people and systems including those relating to the safekeeping of assets or from external events.

Targeted Return Risk - There is no guarantee that the Fund will achieve its targeted objective.

management_company_description:
RBC Global Asset Management (RBC GAM) offers a range of investment management solutions and services for institutional and individual investors globally. Within institutional markets, RBC GAM operates as RBC GAM in the United States, as RBC GAM and PH&N Institutional in Canada, and as RBC BlueBay Asset Management (RBC BlueBay) across EMEA APAC. With 17 specialist investment teams located in eight cities in Europe, Asia, and North America, RBC GAM manages across a spectrum of asset classes and strategies.

We believe that in addition to capabilities in equity, fixed income, liquidity management and alternative strategies, we also have expertise in responsible investing (RI) - including environmental, social and governance (ESG) integrated investing, and impact investing - enabling us to respond to a range of RI objectives and requirements.

Our affiliation with Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) is an important strength. RBC is one of the largest banks globally, with a purpose-driven, principles-led approach to delivering performance and creating value for clients and communities. RBC's financial stability, security, and scale enable RBC GAM to invest in proprietary product development and investment research, support advanced technology platforms and security, and attract and retain talented people, providing comfort to clients and driving business growth. Our multi-national workforce and access to global markets bolster local knowledge in key regions, enabling RBC GAM to do our part in delivering on RBC's overall goal to help clients thrive and communities prosper. 

RBC Global Asset Management Inc. and PH&N Institutional
PH&N Institutional was founded in 1964, and was a privately held entity until 2008 when it was acquired by RBC. In 2010, the entity was amalgamated with RBC Asset Management Inc. to form RBC Global Asset Management Inc. (RBC GAM Inc.), an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of RBC, and the manager of the RBC, Phillips, Hager & North (PH&N), and BlueBay Funds in Canada. Today, PH&N Institutional serves Canadian institutional investors as a business division of RBC GAM Inc.

RBC Global Asset Management (U.S.) Inc. (RBC GAM-US)
Founded in 1983, RBC GAM-US was known as Voyageur Asset Management Inc. when RBC acquired the firm in 2001, and ultimately changed its name to RBC Global Asset Management (U.S.) Inc. in 2010 to reflect the firm's role as the US institutional asset management business for RBC GAM in the United States. RBC GAM-US is an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of RBC.

RBC BlueBay Asset Management (RBC BlueBay)
RBC BlueBay refers to the combination of RBC's equity capabilities located in London and Asia; and BlueBay's specialty fixed income platform. The combined business offers institutional investors and intermediaries a full range of fixed income, equity, and alternative strategies. 

In the UK, RBC GAM was originally founded in October 1998, ultimately becoming RBC Global Asset Management (UK) Limited in 2013, at which time its investment-focused operations were expanded to include distribution. RBC GAM-UK is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Royal Bank of Canada Holdings Limited, itself a wholly-owned subsidiary of RBC.

The BlueBay business was founded in 2001 as an active fixed income specialist asset manager and was acquired by RBC GAM in 2010 in order to expand its franchise in EMEA, including regional offices located across Europe and Japan. Following the acquisition, BlueBay Asset Management PLC changed its corporate status to a private limited company; and in 2012, the investment management business of BlueBay was transferred to an English limited liability partnership.

In 2020, the two London-based businesses, RBC GAM-UK and BlueBay LLP, began evolving toward a single operating model to better harness the capabilities and growth of the respective businesses. Effective April 1, 2023, BlueBay LLP and RBC GAM-UK consolidated the businesses' UK legal entity structures, with BlueBay LLP transferring its business to RBC GAM-UK. Bringing together equity, fixed income and specialist alternative strategies under one operational umbrella allows RBC BlueBay to streamline service for clients in EMEA APAC.

RBC Global Asset Management (Asia) Limited (RBC GAM-Asia)
Founded in 1978, RBC GAM's Asian presence was renamed to RBC GAM-Asia in 2019, and is 100% owned by RBC Trade Asia Limited, which is, in turn, owned by RBC. RBC GAM-Asia comprises primarily a single investment team focused on Asian Equities, and provides investment management services and products to clients across Asia, and worldwide through its affiliates.
strategy_description:
A discretionary global macro strategy investing in a portfolio of interest rates, currencies, and sovereign credit in developed and emerging markets globally. The Strategy targets a net annual return of 10% over the market cycle with an expected annualised volatility of 8% with a 5-15% range. The Strategy may only invest up to 50% of its net assets in fixed income securities rated below investment grade and employs an active use of financial derivative instruments.

The Strategy translates top-down global macro themes into bottom-up individual asset selection by implementing a combination of fundamental directional, relative value and tactical positions, with a strong emphasis on liquidity. The global reach of the Strategy and its broad guidelines provide the flexibility to direct exposure opportunistically to different assets and instruments and allow for minimising downside risks during times of market stress.

management_company_description:
RBC Global Asset Management (RBC GAM) offers a range of investment management solutions and services for institutional and individual investors globally. Within institutional markets, RBC GAM operates as RBC GAM in the United States, as RBC GAM and PH&N Institutional in Canada, and as RBC BlueBay Asset Management (RBC BlueBay) across EMEA APAC. With 17 specialist investment teams located in eight cities in Europe, Asia, and North America, RBC GAM manages across a spectrum of asset classes and strategies.

We believe that in addition to capabilities in equity, fixed income, liquidity management and alternative strategies, we also have expertise in responsible investing (RI) - including environmental, social and governance (ESG) integrated investing, and impact investing - enabling us to respond to a range of RI objectives and requirements.

Our affiliation with Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) is an important strength. RBC is one of the largest banks globally, with a purpose-driven, principles-led approach to delivering performance and creating value for clients and communities. RBC's financial stability, security, and scale enable RBC GAM to invest in proprietary product development and investment research, support advanced technology platforms and security, and attract and retain talented people, providing comfort to clients and driving business growth. Our multi-national workforce and access to global markets bolster local knowledge in key regions, enabling RBC GAM to do our part in delivering on RBC's overall goal to help clients thrive and communities prosper. 

RBC Global Asset Management Inc. and PH&N Institutional
PH&N Institutional was founded in 1964, and was a privately held entity until 2008 when it was acquired by RBC. In 2010, the entity was amalgamated with RBC Asset Management Inc. to form RBC Global Asset Management Inc. (RBC GAM Inc.), an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of RBC, and the manager of the RBC, Phillips, Hager & North (PH&N), and BlueBay Funds in Canada. Today, PH&N Institutional serves Canadian institutional investors as a business division of RBC GAM Inc.

RBC Global Asset Management (U.S.) Inc. (RBC GAM-US)
Founded in 1983, RBC GAM-US was known as Voyageur Asset Management Inc. when RBC acquired the firm in 2001, and ultimately changed its name to RBC Global Asset Management (U.S.) Inc. in 2010 to reflect the firm's role as the US institutional asset management business for RBC GAM in the United States. RBC GAM-US is an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of RBC.

RBC BlueBay Asset Management (RBC BlueBay)
RBC BlueBay refers to the combination of RBC's equity capabilities located in London and Asia; and BlueBay's specialty fixed income platform. The combined business offers institutional investors and intermediaries a full range of fixed income, equity, and alternative strategies. 

In the UK, RBC GAM was originally founded in October 1998, ultimately becoming RBC Global Asset Management (UK) Limited in 2013, at which time its investment-focused operations were expanded to include distribution. RBC GAM-UK is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Royal Bank of Canada Holdings Limited, itself a wholly-owned subsidiary of RBC.

The BlueBay business was founded in 2001 as an active fixed income specialist asset manager and was acquired by RBC GAM in 2010 in order to expand its franchise in EMEA, including regional offices located across Europe and Japan. Following the acquisition, BlueBay Asset Management PLC changed its corporate status to a private limited company; and in 2012, the investment management business of BlueBay was transferred to an English limited liability partnership.

In 2020, the two London-based businesses, RBC GAM-UK and BlueBay LLP, began evolving toward a single operating model to better harness the capabilities and growth of the respective businesses. Effective April 1, 2023, BlueBay LLP and RBC GAM-UK consolidated the businesses' UK legal entity structures, with BlueBay LLP transferring its business to RBC GAM-UK. Bringing together equity, fixed income and specialist alternative strategies under one operational umbrella allows RBC BlueBay to streamline service for clients in EMEA APAC.

RBC Global Asset Management (Asia) Limited (RBC GAM-Asia)
Founded in 1978, RBC GAM's Asian presence was renamed to RBC GAM-Asia in 2019, and is 100% owned by RBC Trade Asia Limited, which is, in turn, owned by RBC. RBC GAM-Asia comprises primarily a single investment team focused on Asian Equities, and provides investment management services and products to clients across Asia, and worldwide through its affiliates.
strategy_description: The Strategy invests in developed market Securitized credit securities, with a particular focus on equity and mezzanine tranches, though has the flexibility to invest across the full capital structure. The Strategy will invest in asset-backed securities covering all collateral types, including senior secured leveraged loans, mortgages, credit cards and auto loans. The Strategy represents our most compelling ideas across the securitized credit market, adopting a catalyst-based approach to investment whereby the portfolio will be rotated on an active basis once catalysts are met and value is created. The Strategy aims to deliver 11-13% net of fees per annum over a full credit cycle. Active management is key to deliver this return, with a focus on deep structural and collateral analysis and relative value between instruments and markets.

name: Lone Mountain Pine
management_company_description:
Lone Pine is a research-driven, fundamental equity investor founded in 1997. Since inception, we have focused on developing a leading investment platform that distills global, cross-sector idiosyncratic and thematic research into concentrated portfolios of our best ideas. Our integrated investment team works collaboratively to invest in public equities and private growth companies to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns for our partners.

Public Equity:
Since inception, Lone Pine has focused on developing a leading research-driven, fundamental equity investment platform. Our investment team is organized to facilitate global equity market coverage, guided by transparency, collaboration, and pattern recognition. We use our research lens and a consensus-driven approach to construct portfolios that blend long and short ideas or are long-only. Our team aims to synthesize global fundamental research into concentrated positions in best ideas, investing behind companies that drive innovation and benefit from longer-term secular trends. We employ a recursive process, where key insights and discoveries can inspire, support, or challenge ideas across geographies, sectors, and markets. While their business models, geographies, sectors, and customers may vary, the companies we invest in commonly share similar attributes that contribute to long-term success - we look for capable, ethical, and trusted management teams running industry-leading companies that can deliver sustainable growth and durable or expanding margins. Over our history, we believe the matched duration of our investment time horizon to our capital base has been a meaningful driver of outperformance against the broader market.

Growth Equity:
Lone Pine began systematically investing in private growth equity in 2016. In private markets, we seek to leverage our rigorous research and deep market knowledge to identify and take concentrated positions in capital-efficient growth-stage (typically Series C) companies with the potential to achieve significant public market capitalizations. Generally, we strive to form an average of six (6) new partnerships per year over a cycle, with quality management teams at companies that deliver high-value products and services at attractive and sustainable unit economics to meaningful addressable markets. Our integrated investment team pursues opportunities in software, financial technology, healthcare, and consumer, where we believe our reputation, network, institutional knowledge, and team offer an advantage in sourcing, selecting, and accessing innovative private companies. We believe our longstanding track record in public markets and integrated team positions the firm to deliver accretive and differentiated value-add to management across corporate strategy, customer/partner/supplier introductions, executive talent, financial planning & analysis, and capital markets.
strategy_description: Lone Mountain Pine seeks to achieve compound annual long term returns that are superior to the MSCI World Index.  Lone Mountain Pine will generally consist of 15-20 high-conviction investments in companies with wide operating moats, high barriers to entry, durable end markets, exemplary management teams and long runways for growth. To benefit from the compounding of business value over the long term, the strategy will aim to hold these positions for five years or longer. The fund is generally fully invested and there is no intention to lever the portfolio.

Each individual fund in a given Lone Pine strategy (collectively, the "Funds") may have holdings that differ significantly from the securities that comprise this index and will vary over time. Each Fund is actively managed and has the ability to use leverage, engage in short selling and derivatives transactions, and invest in illiquid securities, as well as in securities that may have a greater degree of risk and volatility than those within this index. The Funds’ strategy will not seek to replicate the performance of this index or any other index. This index has been selected for comparative purposes only.  
Past performance is not indicative of future results.

name: Lone Cascade
management_company_description:
Lone Pine is a research-driven, fundamental equity investor founded in 1997. Since inception, we have focused on developing a leading investment platform that distills global, cross-sector idiosyncratic and thematic research into concentrated portfolios of our best ideas. Our integrated investment team works collaboratively to invest in public equities and private growth companies to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns for our partners.

Public Equity:
Since inception, Lone Pine has focused on developing a leading research-driven, fundamental equity investment platform. Our investment team is organized to facilitate global equity market coverage, guided by transparency, collaboration, and pattern recognition. We use our research lens and a consensus-driven approach to construct portfolios that blend long and short ideas or are long-only. Our team aims to synthesize global fundamental research into concentrated positions in best ideas, investing behind companies that drive innovation and benefit from longer-term secular trends. We employ a recursive process, where key insights and discoveries can inspire, support, or challenge ideas across geographies, sectors, and markets. While their business models, geographies, sectors, and customers may vary, the companies we invest in commonly share similar attributes that contribute to long-term success - we look for capable, ethical, and trusted management teams running industry-leading companies that can deliver sustainable growth and durable or expanding margins. Over our history, we believe the matched duration of our investment time horizon to our capital base has been a meaningful driver of outperformance against the broader market.

Growth Equity:
Lone Pine began systematically investing in private growth equity in 2016. In private markets, we seek to leverage our rigorous research and deep market knowledge to identify and take concentrated positions in capital-efficient growth-stage (typically Series C) companies with the potential to achieve significant public market capitalizations. Generally, we strive to form an average of six (6) new partnerships per year over a cycle, with quality management teams at companies that deliver high-value products and services at attractive and sustainable unit economics to meaningful addressable markets. Our integrated investment team pursues opportunities in software, financial technology, healthcare, and consumer, where we believe our reputation, network, institutional knowledge, and team offer an advantage in sourcing, selecting, and accessing innovative private companies. We believe our longstanding track record in public markets and integrated team positions the firm to deliver accretive and differentiated value-add to management across corporate strategy, customer/partner/supplier introductions, executive talent, financial planning & analysis, and capital markets.

strategy_description: The Pharo Gaia Fund, Ltd. is a global macro hedge fund that specialises in Emerging Markets. It aims to deliver positive risk-adjusted returns, independent of the market cycle and external conditions. The Fund is managed by the Firm’s most senior members of the investment team (Guillaume Fonkenell and Nicolas Beckmann). They trade the full Emerging Market universe (e.g., Latin America, Asia, Central and Eastern Europe, Middle East and Africa) as well as developed markets (e.g., North America, Japan, Western Europe and Australia). The Fund’s core asset classes are foreign exchange, credit (primarily sovereign, but also, quasi-sovereign and corporate), and local market rates. Guillaume Fonkenell and Nicolas Beckmann have access to a shared pool of human and technological resources: economists, execution traders, quantitative analysts, and quantitative strategy tools. From there, each individual's idea generation and trade expression are unique. They have full discretion over their capital allocation, subject to well-defined risk controls. Capital is allocated by the Risk Committee.

management_company_description: Pharo Management is a global macro hedge fund manager specialising in emerging markets. Founded in 2000 by Guillaume Fonkenell, the Firm has offices in London, New York and Hong Kong and manages capital across five funds. Pharo trades foreign exchange, sovereign credit and interest rate markets in over 70 countries with an investment approach that combines macroeconomic fundamental research as well as technical analyses. Pharo's investor base consists primarily of large financial institutions, such as pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, foundations, family offices and fund-of-hedge-funds.
strategy_description: The Pharo Trading Fund, Ltd. is a global macro hedge fund that specialises in Emerging Markets. It aims to deliver positive risk-adjusted returns, independent of the market cycle and external conditions. The Fund is managed by Guillaume Fonkenell who has over 30 years of experience trading currencies, bonds and derivatives in developed and emerging markets, through macroeconomic cycles including stressed market environments. Guillaume is a generalist who trades the full Emerging Market universe (e.g., Latin America, Asia, Central and Eastern Europe, Middle East and Africa) as well as developed markets (e.g., North America, Japan, Western Europe and Australia). The Fund’s core asset classes are foreign exchange, credit (primarily sovereign, but also, quasi-sovereign and corporate), and local market rates. Guillaume utilises Pharo’s human and technological resources which include economists, execution traders, quantitative analysts, and quantitative strategy tools. He has full discretion over his capital allocation, subject to well-defined risk controls.
share_class_additional_details:
The Class A Series 1 U.S. dollar-denominated shares are the longest running share class of the Fund and the returns shown for those shares demonstrate the performance of the Fund since its inception through multiple investment cycles and market conditions.  Past performance is not indicative of future results. The Class A shares are charged a management fee of 2% and a performance fee of 20%, calculated as described on the Disclosures tab under “Fund Performance – Classes A to F Fees,” and the performance shown is net of those fees.  The Fund’s Class B through F shares are denominated in different currencies and charged the same fees as the Class A shares. Returns on the other share classes are available on request and will vary from the Class A shares.  In 2016, the Investment Manager waived management fees for the calendar year for investors. The net returns for 2016 were calculated using a model monthly management fee equal to one-twelfth of two percent (2%) of the net asset value of the Class A Shares at the end of each month. The model management fee was calculated and applied in the same manner as, and accurately reflects, the actual management fee charged in all other performance periods and the management fee that is currently offered to investors.

NAV is calculated in accordance with IFRS accounting standards at month-end. Starting May 1, 2024, the Pharo Macro Fund, Ltd. (Macro Fund) invests a portion of its NAV in Pharo Africa Fund, Ltd. (Africa Fund), which increases Africa Fund’s NAV by the size of Macro Fund’s investment. Pharo does not double count the amount of this investment in the Firm calculation.
