management_company_description:
Founded in 2015, Century Frontier Asset Management is a private fund manager specialised in quantitative investment in China market. The firm is 
registered with Asset Management Association of China (AMAC) in 2018 and now manages over US$9 billion of total assets.

Frontier Asset Management (Hong Kong) Limited, established on 16 June 2023,  is an affiliate of Century Frontier Asset Management. The firm is licensed and regulated by the Securities and Futures Commission of Hong Kong (“SFC”) in March 2024 to conduct Type 9 (Asset Management) Regulated Activities.
strategy_description:
The fund applies a quantitative active long-only strategy to invest in China A-shares. By analyzing various types of data in a systematic approach to generate signals for share price movements, risk and return are balanced based on optimization models and methods. Meanwhile, execution strategies are designed to minimize trading cost, with the core objective of pursuing long-term stable performance.
Unlike index-enhanced products that track a specific index, active long-only strategy can effectively capture a variety of market style betas and seize alpha returns. History has consistently demonstrated the existence of rotation between large-cap and small-cap styles in the market. Active long-only strategy can, to a certain extent, alleviate investors’ selection anxiety when faced with choosing 
between large-cap and small-cap indices.
Active long-only strategy is not strictly tied to specific index characteristics, freeing them from the style limits of benchmark. It can flexibly adjust the portfolio’s style based on the relative alpha of individual stocks, aiming to boost long-term returns without increasing risk unnecessarily. 
We adopt an analytical and systematic approach in our investment process and focus on execution excellence under a disciplined risk framework. Our team members are graduated from the world’s top universities including Mathematics and Physics Olympicia Medalists. Our collaborative team culture and competitive incentive scheme are essential to talent retention and our core team has ZERO turnover since our inception.

management_company_description:
Clean Energy Transition LLP was launched on 1 December 2021 when Per Lekander’s Global Energy Team spun-out from Lansdowne Partners bringing their funds under the management of the new firm. The flagship hedge fund Energy Dynamics has a track record since 2015 and long only fund Clean since 2017. 

Clean Energy Transition aims to take advantage of the major shifts occurring in the global energy landscape, with the disruptions resulting in winners and losers. Current investment themes include the trend toward electrification, the transformative technological innovation including AI infrastructure, and the rapid expansion of renewables (despite political headwinds). It’s anticipated that around 5% of global GDP will be invested in the energy transition annually over the next 30 years.

The firm focuses on investing in established mid- large-cap companies primarily located in the USA and Western Europe, across energy and energy-related sectors. These include utilities, infrastructure, capital goods, transport, technology, automotive, renewables, commodities, and mining.

The investment team employs a thematic investment approach looking for changes in market trends across key industries, technology and regulation to assess how these affect sub-sectors and regions. On a micro level, the team evaluates the company-specific outlook with a focus on competitiveness, management and financial position.
strategy_description:
CLEAN is offered in two separate legal structures: an Irish ICAV and a US Delaware LP.

CLEAN is a global long-only equity fund that holds a concentrated portfolio of 15 to 25 positions, managed with an investment horizon of one to three years. The fund excludes companies involved in coal, oil, and gas extraction, and all investments undergo thorough environmental, social, and governance (ESG) screening. Its investable universe includes sectors such as utilities, infrastructure, capital goods, transportation, technology, automotive, and renewables.

esg_approach_description:
ESG Process
The energy sector is one of the largest contributors to global environmental pollution, including the largest source of carbon emissions and other airborne pollutants and a key contributor to poor land and water use. There are also significant risks and negative externalities associated with nuclear power, uranium and coal mining. The emerging new power system promises to be significantly more sustainable, from both an environmental and an economic perspective and we see ample new investment opportunities in this transformation process. The core of CLEAN’s mandate is to invest in companies that reflect this trend towards sustainability. 

The Firm utilises a proprietary three-step process: 

Step 1 - Exclusion: 
Carbon Underground 200
The Carbon Underground 200 list identifies the 100 largest public coal and 100 largest public Oil & Gas reserve owners based on the potential CO2 emissions of their reported reserves. All of these companies are excluded from the CLEAN investment universe.

Norges Bank Investment Management published Exclusion Lists
As managers for the Norwegian Government Pension Fund Global, Norges produce product and conduct based exclusion lists restricting investments in companies that do not meet certain criteria. CLEAN is committed to not investing in any companies involved in the Production of Coal or Coal-Based Energy product-based exclusion list, or companies listed on any of the conduct-based exclusion lists.

Paris Aligned Benchmark
CLEAN follows the exclusions for the EU Paris-aligned benchmarks as set out in Article 12(1) of the Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/1818 and will not invest in corporate issuers which, in the opinion of Clean Energy Transition LLP:
1.	are involved in any activities related to controversial weapons;
2.	are involved in the cultivation and production of tobacco;
3.	are companies in violation of the UNGC principles or the OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises;
4.	derive 1% or more of their revenues from exploration, mining, extraction, distribution or refining of hard coal and lignite;
5.	derive 10% or more of their revenues from the exploration, extraction, distribution or refining of oil fuels;
6.	derive 50% or more of their revenues from the exploration, extraction, manufacturing or distribution of gaseous fuels;
7.	derive 50% or more of their revenues from electricity generation with a GHG intensity of more than 100g CO2 e/kWh.

Clean Energy Exclusion List
In addition to the Carbon Underground 200 and the Norges Bank Exclusion Lists, the Firm has established a set of internal guidelines to exclude companies that derive more than 1% of net external sales from oil, gas, or coal extraction activities.
The Firm’s ESG Committee meets on a monthly basis to review existing companies in CLEAN’s portfolio, as well as the proposed addition of new companies to the portfolio and/or the exclusion of companies from CLEAN’s universe based on the “Step 1” process summarised above. The Committee is comprised of Eirik Hogner (Portfolio Manager), Per Lekander (Deputy Portfolio Manager and CEO), Benjamin Singh (COO & CCO; Chair of the Committee), Nick Rodgers (Quantitative Analyst & Trader), and Naomi Gill (Client Relations Associate). 

Step 2 - Proprietary rating: 
In the second step, we seek to assess four basic questions. (1) What ESG challenges does the relevant company have? (2) To what extent does the company acknowledge these? (3) Do we see a strategy to tackle these challenges? (4) Do we believe that the company has the financial and human resources to implement that strategy and overcome the relevant challenges?

Examples of such strategic plans range from clear actions to reduce environmental impact; programs aimed at improving the health and safety of employees and contractors, and initiatives geared towards increasing staff empowerment. We believe that these strategic plans should form part of a company’s “tone from the top” working culture, and therefore we seek clear evidence that the relevant company’s management team embraces ESG.

It is essential that the company exhibits a conscious ESG culture, not only internally, but also within the whole supply and distribution chains, including waste.

One could rely on external ratings to assess all the criteria above, or the ESG reports published by many companies these days, but as explained above, we prefer a more personalised approach. We like to discuss these issues directly with the company, and better yet, assess them ourselves through company site visits.

Step 3 - Invest and Monitor: 
The third step includes monitoring ESG news flow at the regulatory, industry, and company levels; company site visits to search for evidence of ESG measures; ongoing dialogue with management; and systematic voting on companies’ resolutions.

It is clear that the selected companies are not immune to disappointments, especially in the case of concealed malicious intentions in some divisions. However, if the culture is right, these cases should be few and far between.

Only constant dialogue with companies, their suppliers and customers, and even ex-employees, through management meetings, attendance at capital market days (which give us opportunities to meet managers at lower levels) and company site visits, can help us develop a true appreciation of the culture.

Our decision to incorporate ESG factors into our investment process is founded upon the core belief that:

1. ESG factors can have a material impact on the long-term success and economic value of any business, particularly those companies within our investment universe.
2. ESG factors will gain in influence over time, impacting the attraction of shares as investments as reporting requirements evolve, governments take action and younger generations influence market trends.
3. Engagement with companies is core to active fund management. We can help ensure the performance of public companies over the long term by offering management teams strategic advice that includes feedback on ESG-related topics.
4. All stakeholders should strive to contain and minimise the environmental challenges to our planet, whilst promoting responsible business practice, encouraging diversity, and protecting human rights.

The investment team is responsible for considering such ESG factors and their impact on shareholder value throughout the investment process.

strategy_description:
One River’s Volatility Relative Value Strategy combines the investment team’s expertise in volatility trading into an absolute return, all weather strategy. The strategy is highly differentiated to other relative strategies because it embeds the following features:

-	Positive Convexity Structuring:  In developing the expertise to deliver years of consistent alpha generation across bespoke convexity mandates, the team has built a unique suite of tools and honed an approach that places convexity optimization and risk mitigation as central tenets of our investment philosophy. 
-	Macro Awareness:  The team considers traditional volatility market inputs while also taking into account macro risks and opportunities. 
-	Data Driven Process:  One River applies a specialized quantitative volatility infrastructure to support our fundamental portfolio managers using inputs such as valuation, microstructure data, structured product data, and dealer hedging activity. 
-	“Anti-RV”:  One River’s strategy seeks to identify when to participate in traditional RV trades and when to take the other side of these trades by predicting when market distortions are likely to erupt and/or persist.

management_company_description: Founded in 2013 by Eric Peters, One River Asset Management is an investment manager that aims to deliver high-conviction absolute-return strategies that help our clients build superior portfolios. We see the world in a period of major economic and political transition, with the investment landscape shifting in ways that will make the coming five years look profoundly different from the past five. We believe our strategies are built to profit from this dynamic environment while providing diversification benefits to traditional investment portfolios. Each is developed and managed in-house by our team of investment professionals with expertise in volatility and systematic trading/investing. We believe our strategies are delivered at sensible fees and enhanced volatility via commingled funds, and/or in bespoke combinations for large institutions via fund-of-one structures.
strategy_description: Our Dynamic Convexity Strategy is designed as an offset to equity market exposure in a carry efficient way. The strategy never sells options to fund long volatility positions because relative value relationships can behave in unpredictable ways in a market shock. Instead, One River has designed strategies to modulate the long exposure and/or take advantage of volatility surface distortions which we believe will provide a superior reward/risk payoff.

name: Coast Capital Engaged Fund
management_company_description:
Coast Capital seeks to generate outsized risk-adjusted returns across market cycles by applying a differentiated investment philosophy and process. The Firm takes a concentrated, “Private Equity” approach to analyzing, and unlocking value, in publicly traded securities, primarily in European developed markets.

Coast Capital is a long-biased small and mid-cap value investor, which invests in a concentrated set of companies which we believe are leaders in growing and profitable industries generating high returns on capital, but trading at dislocated valuations due to structural or operational inefficacies. We then work to build positions of significant influence and partner with leading C-level executives to engage with companies for value creation.
strategy_description: Our investment process has been and remains simple and streamlined, yet vastly underemployed by investment managers across markets. We buy high quality businesses that are leaders in growing and profitable industries, which trade at material discounts to fair value, and then actively work towards long-term value creation in partnership with leading C-level executives. We focus on our highest quality ideas and run a concentrated portfolio of 8-12 investments. As a result, our returns have had little correlation to the markets in which we invest. We believe that this strategy, which we apply to an overlooked set of small and mid-cap companies in less efficient European public markets, will continue to help us generate long-term value for our investors.
region_exposure_description:
Western European public markets with greatest focus on the UK.

European public equity valuations stand near all-time-lows vs US markets, despite a very favorable economic backdrop that is for once positively decoupled from the US. Increasing fiscal stimulus, the rebirth of industry, falling interest rates, and the likelihood of a post-war economic recovery will, we believe, position Europe as a preferred destination of capital during this phase of heightened volatility in US equities. We also note that Europe benefits from a steady and predictable legal and regulatory framework, which are the founding pillars of stability that in turn begets capital flows. Accordingly, global equity funds have begun to shift allocations away from the US toward Europe at a record pace in the first quarter of 2025. We are emphatically not macro investors, but we believe these trends are set to continue.

Risks Associated with Investing in the Funds 

 

An investment in the Fund involves a high degree of investment risk, including the risk that the entire amount invested may be lost. The Fund will make investments using strategies and financial techniques with significant risk characteristics. No guarantee is made that the investment objectives of the Fund will be realized. The success of the Fund’s investment strategy may require, among other things: (i) that the Investment Manager properly identify companies whose securities prices can be improved through corporate and/or strategic action; (ii) that the Fund acquire sufficient securities of such portfolio companies at a sufficiently attractive price; (iii)  that the Fund avoid triggering anti-takeover and regulatory obstacles while aggregating its position; (iv) that management of portfolio companies and other security holders respond positively to the Investment Manager’s  proposals; and (v) that the market price of a portfolio company’s securities increases in response to any actions taken by portfolio companies. Past performance is no guarantee of future results and there can be no assurance that any of the foregoing will succeed. 

 

Successful execution of an investment strategy will depend on the cooperation of security holders and others with an interest in the portfolio company. Some security holders may have interests that diverge significantly from those of the Fund and some of those parties may be indifferent to the proposed changes. Moreover, securities that the Investment Manager believes are fundamentally undervalued or incorrectly valued may not ultimately be valued in the capital markets at prices and/or within the time frame the Investment Manager anticipates, even if the Fund’s strategy is successfully implemented. Even if the prices for a portfolio company’s securities have increased, there is no assurance that the Fund will be able to realize any increase in the price of such securities. 

 

The Fund may engage in short selling of securities, currencies, or indices, including all forms of derivatives. A short sale will result in a gain if the price of the instrument sold declines sufficiently between the time of the short sale and the time at which another is purchased to replace it. A short sale will result in a loss if the price of the instrument sold short increases or does not decline sufficiently to cover transaction costs. Short sales on equities may expose the Fund theoretically to unlimited losses, due to the lack of an upper limit on the price to which an investment can rise. Any gain would be decreased and any loss would be increased by the amount of any premium or interest that the Fund may be required to pay with respect to the borrowed instrument. 

 

The Fund may utilize leverage including through engaging in trading on margin by borrowing funds and pledging securities as collateral. While such use of borrowed funds increases returns if the Fund earns a greater return on the incremental investments purchased with borrowed funds than it pays for such funds, the use of leverage decreases returns if the Fund fails to earn as much on such incremental investments as it pays for such funds. The effect of leverage may therefore result in a greater decrease in the net asset value of the Fund than if the Fund were not so leveraged. Any use by the Fund of short-term margin borrowings will result in certain additional risks to the Fund. For example, the securities pledged to brokers to secure the Fund’s margin accounts could be subject to a “margin call,” pursuant to which the Fund would be required to either deposit additional funds with the broker or suffer mandatory liquidation of the pledged securities to compensate for the decline in value. A sudden, precipitous drop in value of the Fund’s assets accompanied by corresponding margin calls could force the  Fund to liquidate assets quickly, and not for what the Investment Manager perceives to be their fair value, in order to pay off its margin debt. In addition, the Fund may engage in certain derivative transactions that implicitly contain leverage and subject the Fund to the same risks discussed above. 

 

The investments of the Fund that are not denominated in the U.S. dollar are subject to the risk that the value of a particular currency will change in relation to one or more other currencies. Among the factors that may affect   currency values are trade balances, the level of short-term interest rates, differences in relative values of similar assets in different currencies, long-term opportunities for investment and capital appreciation, and political developments. Officials in foreign countries may, from time to time, take actions in respect of their currencies that could significantly affect the value of the Fund’s assets denominated in those currencies or the liquidity of such  investments. The Fund may, but is not required to, invest in foreign currencies, foreign currency futures contracts and options thereon, forward foreign currency exchange contracts, or any combination thereof for hedging purposes, but there can be no assurance that such strategies will be implemented, or if implemented, will be effective. 

 

Although the Investment Manager may choose to limit the amount of the Fund’s capital that may be committed to any single industry, the Fund is not otherwise limited in the amount of capital that may be committed to investments in companies in any particular industry, sector, or geography. As such, its assets may not be diversified and, if its assets are concentrated in a particular company, industry, sector, geography, or similar category,  the Fund would be subject to an increased risk of loss if there was a decline in the market value in any security in which the Fund had invested a large percentage of its assets or there are adverse consequences to such industry,  sector, geography, or other group of companies. Investment in a non-diversified fund will generally entail greater risks than investments in a diversified fund. 

 

The market price of securities owned by the Fund may go up or down, sometimes rapidly or unpredictably. A risk of investing in the Fund is that the equity securities in the Fund’s portfolio will decline in value due to factors affecting equity securities markets generally or particular industries represented in those markets. The values of equity securities may decline due to general market conditions that are not specifically related to a particular company, such as real or perceived adverse economic conditions, changes in the general outlook for corporate earnings, changes in interest or currency rates or adverse investor sentiment generally. In addition to other risks  not enumerated here, they may also decline due to factors that affect a particular industry or industries, such as labor shortages or increased production costs and competitive conditions within an industry. 

 

The Fund expects to invest in non-U.S. securities. Such investments may be subject to a greater risk than U.S. investments due to non-U.S. economic, political, and legal developments, including favorable or unfavorable  changes in currency exchange rates, exchange control regulations (including currency blockage), expropriation of assets or nationalization, imposition of taxes on dividends, interest payments, capital gains, or other income, the  need for approval by government or other authorities to make investments, and possible difficulty in obtaining and enforcing judgments against non-U.S. entities and other factors beyond the control of the Investment  Manager. Furthermore, issuers of non-U.S. securities are subject to different, often less comprehensive accounting, reporting or disclosure requirements than U.S. issuers. 

 

An investment in the Fund is a relatively illiquid investment because interests are not generally transferable and the redemption rights of investors are restricted, including for the Fund’s Lock-Up Period. In addition, transfer of  the interests may be affected by restrictions on resales imposed by federal and state securities laws and, in the case of the requirement that the Board of Directors or General Partner consent, dependent upon whether an  investment is the Domestic Fund or Offshore Fund. The Fund is not intended as a complete investment program and is designed only for persons who are able to bear economic risk of investment and are sophisticated persons  in connection with financial and business matters who do not need liquidity with respect to their investments. 

 

Although the Investment Manager is registered with the SEC, The Fund is not registered and does not intend to register as an investment company under the 1940 Act, and, accordingly, investors in the Fund are not accorded  the protections of the 1940 Act (which, among other matters, requires most registered investment companies to have a majority of disinterested directors, requires securities held in custody at all times to be segregated and  marked to clearly identify the owner of such securities, and regulates the relationship between the investment adviser and the investment company). The Master Fund is not within the definition of a “Mutual Fund.” Accordingly, the Master Fund is not registered or regulated under the terms of the Mutual Funds Law. The Master Fund does not offer its interests for direct investment. 

 

The Domestic Fund and the Master Fund expect to be treated as partnerships and not as associations taxable as corporations for U.S. federal income tax purposes. Partners should be aware that they will be required to take into account their allocable shares of Fund income and realized gains (including the Domestic Fund’s share of the Master Fund’s income and gains), if any, regardless of whether they receive cash distributions from the Domestic Fund. 

 

The Offshore Fund and the Master Fund intend to conduct their affairs so that they will not be treated as engaged in a trade or business within the United States. Certain categories of income (including dividends, certain  payments with respect to derivative instruments that are treated as “dividend equivalent payments,” and certain types of interest income) that are not effectively connected with a U.S. trade or business but that are derived by  the Master Fund from U.S. sources will nonetheless be subject to a U.S. tax at a rate of 30%, which tax is generally withheld from such income and will reduce the total return to the Master Fund’s investors, including  Shareholders of the Offshore Fund. Provided certain documentation requirements are satisfied, other categories of income not effectively connected with a U.S. trade or business, generally including capital gains (including  those derived from options transactions), interest on certain portfolio debt obligations, and original issue discount obligations having an original maturity of 183 days or less, will not be subject to this 30% withholding tax. 

 

Neither the Offshore Fund nor the Master Fund is subject to any income, withholding, or capital gains taxes in the Cayman Islands. The Offshore Fund and the Master Fund have each obtained an undertaking from the  Governor-in-Cabinet of the Cayman Islands pursuant to the Tax Concessions Law (Revised) of the Cayman Islands that for a period of twenty years in the case of the Offshore Fund and for a period of fifty years in the case of  the Master Fund, no law which is thereafter enacted in the Cayman Islands imposing any tax to be levied on profits or income or gains or appreciations will apply to the Offshore Fund or the Master Fund or their operations. 

 

Within 120 days after the end of each fiscal year or as soon thereafter as is reasonably possible, each Partner will be furnished certain tax information for preparation of its tax return. Within 120 days of the end of each fiscal year or as soon as reasonably practicable thereafter, the Fund will distribute audited financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP with respect to the previous fiscal year to all Partners and Shareholders. 

 

There can be no assurance that the U.S. or Cayman Islands tax laws will not be changed adversely with respect to the Offshore Fund, the Master Fund or their Shareholders, or that the Offshore Fund's or the Master Fund’s income tax status will not be successfully challenged by such authorities. 

 

Investment in the Fund is generally open to pension and other funds subject to the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (“ERISA”) or the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the “Code”), as well as governmental and other plans not subject to such laws. The Fund may require certain representations or assurances from investors subject to ERISA or the Code to determine compliance with provisions of ERISA and the  Code. If 25% or more of the total value of any class of equity interests in the Fund, determined in accordance with ERISA, is held by “benefit plan investors,” the Fund will be deemed to hold “plan assets” under ERISA.  However, the Fund serves merely as a conduit for the investment of amounts contributed by the Shareholders in the Master Fund. It is intended that neither the General Partner nor the Investment Manager be considered a  fiduciary under ERISA with respect to the assets of the Fund if the Master Fund does not hold plan assets, and all Shareholders and Partners will be required to agree with the Fund and the General Partner and Investment  Manager that the parties do not intend under such circumstances to establish any relationship that would cause the General Partner, the Investment Manager or other person to be a “fiduciary” subject to ERISA with respect to  the Fund. It is expected that the assets of the Master Fund will not constitute “plan assets” under ERISA. In this regard, the Fund currently intends that investment by “benefit plan investors” in the Fund will be limited to the  extent necessary for the Master Fund to satisfy the so-called “25% test” applicable for these purposes. 

 

Prospective investors should consult their own legal and tax advisors regarding the consequences of owning an Interest in the Fund in light of their particular circumstances, including under the laws of their citizenship,   residence or domicile and any other U.S. federal, state or local, non-U.S. or non-income tax laws.

name: SpesX
management_company_description: FIEE is an established, pioneering, dedicated European fund manager active both in private and public markets founded in 2015 to make growth-oriented sustainable investments in Energy Transition.
strategy_description:
SpesX is a global Energy Transition fund that seeks to generate absolute, low double-digit returns. 
The portfolio is actively managed, investing via long and short positions, based on the assessment of relative value opportunities between climate advantaged and disadvantaged companies. 
SpesX invests globally in the securities active in Energy Transition, mainly in equity, but with a flexible allocation of around 30% in credit on average. Energy Transition companies are those exposed to the transition to a cleaner energy world including, but not limited to, energy production, storage, efficiency, management, and optimisation and includes technologies, components and systems that can improve energy efficiency, reduce carbon emissions or facilitate the transition to cleaner energy. 
The Fund takes long positions in climate-advantaged companies that, on a relative basis, have a strong or improving position with respect to climate mitigation and/or climate adaptation; and short positions in climate disadvantaged companies with a relatively weak or weakening position with, as well as “green bubbles”.

management_company_description: The PSquared Group was founded in February 2013 by Patrick Bierbaum (CIO), formerly Partner and Portfolio Manager at Centaurus Capital Ltd and Dr Patrick Schmitz-Morkramer (CEO) formerly Head of Investment Banking of Nomura Bank in Asia (ex Japan). strategy_description: PSquared Event Opportunity Master Fund operates a global event driven strategy with an emphasis on Europe & Asia. The strategy focusses on fundamental research and bottom up analysis with a view to identifying events in the short to medium term (3-9 months). PSquared has an investment philosophy which is based on (i) deep value opportunities, (ii) avoiding crowded situations, (iii) short to medium term catalysts and (iv) active management and monitoring of macro risks. The strategy is market neutral with an ability to deviate within a limited range on a beta adjusted basis dependent on market conditions. The portfolio construction is based on a concentrated number of investment position blocks, which we believe show a high correlation between the long and short legs in order to protect from significant market movements. The strategy seeks to generate returns purely through events crystallizing rather than a reliance on market direction or beta. The strategy will invest across the entire spectrum from soft to hard catalyst events, as well as given the principals’ backgrounds the strategy will look to express events throughout the entire capital structure to enhance the risk reward. However, only liquid/listed credit positions will be considered (bonds, convertibles, CDS etc). Position sizing will be determined by risk / reward as well as loss limits of every position block. Furthermore, there is a strong emphasis on underlying liquidity and the number of trading days it would take to unwind every position.

name: Redwood Master Fund
management_company_description:
Redwood was formed in 2000 to focus on investing in distressed and stressed credit. The Firm manages four strategies including a flagship hedge fund, distressed drawdown dislocation fund, a safer long-only strategy and an opportunistic private credit fund.

Redwood was founded by Jonathan Kolatch to focus on distressed credit investing. Prior to founding Redwood, Mr. Kolatch spent 17 years at Goldman, Sachs, where he retired as a partner in 1999. During that time, Mr. Kolatch headed the High Yield and Distressed Trading group from 1992 until 1996. He then started and managed the Credit Arbitrage Group, which focused on proprietary investing in high yield, distressed and emerging market opportunities.

There are 31 professionals at our firm. Our investment team is comprised of two portfolio managers, thirteen analysts and two traders. We believe in a tightly knit, focused and collaborative investment culture where our team members have a significant stake in the funds and where everyone is compensated based on net returns to investors. We offer investors four distinct ways to invest in opportunities across the credit markets:

1) Redwood Master Fund - Hedge Fund focused on distressed and stressed credit opportunities
2) Redwood Opportunities Fund - Long-only fund focused on bank debt and loans in the top part of a company's capital structure
3)Redwood Drawdown Fund - Drawdown fund focused on distressed and stressed opportunities in periods of dislocation (4-year investment period, 3-year harvest, Fund IV will accept commitments in Q1 2025)
4)Redwood Enhanced Income Fund - Opportunistic private credit fund investing in capital solutions and misunderstood private companies in the middle-market
strategy_description:
Our seventeen-person investment team works in a highly collaborative fashion to identify credit opportunities across the capital structure. We are contrarian by nature and strive for strong returns in all environments by judiciously adding risk when dislocations arise and de-risking as stress subsides. Our portfolio is long-biased with 30-40 core positions and three main areas of focus: 

(1) Distressed Situations 
(2) Stressed situations that don't involve restructurings
(3) Undervalued credit / new issues

We think about and manage risk in three categories:

(1) As part of our investment process  
• Waiting for attractive entry points
• Moving up capital structure when market risks are high
• Infrequent use of leverage

(2) As part of portfolio construction
• Maximum position size of 5% at cost
• 15% industry concentration limits
• Maximum risk of loss of 1.5% of any single position

(3) Hedging
• Individual stocks
• ETF’s or sector baskets
• CDS
• Currency

strategy_description:
Landseer’s European Smaller Companies Equity Long/Short strategy focuses on developed pan-European small caps. Landseer AM acquired the Chilton SC European strategy managed by Jamie Carter, who will join Landseer on 1st October 2023 as a Partner, and will continue to run his previous investment approach. The strategy will move from the Waystone platform to the IAM platform in September/October 2023. Jamie will fully utilize the Landseer infrastructure, execution, and shared research hub. Paul Graham (CEO and CCO) and Roger Guy (Chairman) will provide full, all-encompassing support.

The fundamental bottom-up research process focuses on developed European stocks with market caps between $200mn-$5bn (c. 20% in $5bn+). They seek to identify unrecognized under and overvalued companies with a strong focus on the following three pillars: 1. company management; 2. cashflow; and 3. catalysts. They aim to complete comprehensive due diligence through over 500 company meetings per year across all sectors, and with in-house modeling. The single stock alpha short book consists of overvalued / mispriced situations, supplemented by sector/indexes if required for balance sheet management. 

The net exposure is variable depending on the current and future opportunity set, ranging from -20% up to 40%, but is typically longer-biased. Gross exposure is managed to a maximum of 200%. The average holding period for longs & shorts is 12-24 months. The approach will have 50-70 positions in the book (on both the long and short side). 

The strategy will benefit from Landseer’s proprietary risk management framework which they have developed over many years. They aim to minimize overall market risk through a more active and variable management of the net/gross exposures and a generally stricter approach to factor and sector exposures. They will seek to limit drawdowns, while positioning for upside when appropriate.

name: Envestra Capital Master Fund Limited
management_company_description: Envestra Capital was founded in February 2023 by Ali Benzakour (ex-Millennium). Envestra is currently preparing for November 2023 launch of an equity long/short fund focusing on the energy transition thematic.
strategy_description:
Envestra is a market neutral long-short strategy which seeks to take advantage of asset mispricing linked to the energy transition thematic. The investment mandate is global with a European focus. The strategy aims to generate consistent alpha through both its long and short holdings with returns that are uncorrelated to equity markets. In order to achieve this, the manager combines his focus on fundamental stock analysis with top-down and thematic views to identify what we believe to be mispriced stocks, while adding further value through active trading and use of derivatives.

It is our view that the energy transition to net zero emissions is one of the largest and most complex economic and industrial transformations. The strategy seeks to focus on the sectors that are disrupted most by this transition: utilities, energy, renewables, infrastructure, transport and industrial sectors. We believe that the key to the investment philosophy is a holistic approach integrating industry and regulatory dynamics with bottom up fundamental stock research. The portfolio is comprised of a selection of 50-60 high conviction positions where the top 10 would typically represent 30-40% of GMV and is constructed with an aim to maximize alpha by reducing exposure to non-idiosyncratic risk factors.

strategy_description:
North Rock Capital allocates capital to multiple PM Teams. North Rock is principally comprised of fundamental relative value equity strategies, with some quantitative equity strategies. The Fund is diversified by geography, sector/industry, and investment style at the aggregate Fund level. Underlying PM Teams tend to be sector/industry/regional specialists.

North Rock Capital allocates capital to a diversified set of relative value and long/short equity strategy-focused PM Teams. The North Rock portfolio strives to produce net returns based on strong alpha generation with low dependence on traditional market direction. North Rock seeks to generate risk-adjusted returns primarily through stock-specific (idiosyncratic) risk while limiting market beta and other market factors. The strategy is global in nature and exposure is managed to be diversified across sectors, geographies, and styles. The strategy invests in both fundamental and quantitative sub-strategies. North Rock deploys capital across multiple PM Teams that principally pursue sector-specific strategies. We continue to remain focused on fundamental stock selection as a key alpha driver, however, we also continuously evaluate strategies and approaches that can allow us to continue to evolve as the future opportunity set changes. In our view, the combination of diversification and continued refinement of our investment approach gives us the best opportunity to be successful in the future.
North Rock's investment philosophy centers around its sector-specialist model. North Rock believes that combining sector-specialist PM Teams focused on a defined universe of securities in a single hedge fund structure offers long-term sustainable sources of alpha. In short, North Rock's sector-specialist model allows the Fund to harness the experience of its PM Teams with the aim of achieving high-quality returns primarily driven by idiosyncratic risk and low dependence on market direction.

strategy_description: The TabCap Balanced Credit Fund (TBAL) aims to generate returns while maintaining a low correlation to global equity and credit markets. The strategy is systematic in nature and takes both long and short exposure to credit options and credit indices, aiming to exploit inefficiencies in the credit volatility market while remaining market neutral. TBAL uses a systematic approach to monetising inefficiencies in credit option markets offering uncorrelated returns vs. market beta and common factors. TBAL's core instruments are credit default swap indices and credit index options. management_company_description: Tabula Capital (trading as "TabCap") is an independent alternative investment firm focused on liquid credit strategies. strategy_description:
The Tabula Liquid Credit Income UCITS Fund (TLIQ) is a long-biased liquid credit strategy that uses CDS index products and seeks to generate a high income with downside protection, while remaining compliant with UCITS rules. TLIQ aims to outperform traditional high yield investments over the long term by taking advantage of the high risk-adjusted return of CDS indices relative to corporate bonds. TLIQ uses leveraged investment grade exposure rather than unlevered high yield exposure to generate returns and has low interest rate exposure. TLIQ’s core instruments are highly liquid credit indices, credit index options and government bond collateral. TLIQ has an embedded systematic tail-risk hedging strategy to mitigate downside risk during large market shocks. The proprietary systematic strategy generates return through three main components:
• An income portfolio, where income is generated through a rolling long risk position in the iTraxx Main and CDX IG indices;
• A hedge portfolio, where a systematic programme of credit payer options is used to protect the Fund from downside risk; and
• A risk-free rate from collateral assets within the fund. 
TabCap’s proprietary analytics actively monitor markets for ways to generate relative outperformance while retaining a similar risk profile. When such instances are identified, the strategy may employ an active fund management overlay which allows an active divergence from the core systematic strategy. Risk controls limit the amount that the portfolio managers can deviate from the core systematic strategy.

Maverick’s fundamental research process devotes significant resources to every investment decision.  A team of 32 research and trading professionals seeks the best long and short opportunities globally, guided by risk-reward dynamics rather than value or growth style factors, market capitalization or index weighting.  While bottom-up fundamental analysis drives security selection, quantitative research plays a critical role in portfolio construction and risk management.

The investment team is structured into four sector groups—Consumer, Healthcare, Cyclicals, and Technology—supported by two dedicated private investment teams (Silicon and Ventures), as well as specialized quantitative research and trading teams. strategy_description:
Maverick’s Hedged Equity Strategy generally targets 120% long exposure and 80% short exposure, resulting in approximately 40% net market exposure.  The portfolio is invested primarily in medium- and large-cap equities, diversified by both region and industry.  Performance is driven by individual security selection, rather than market timing, sector rotation, or index trading.

Maverick’s fundamental research process devotes significant resources to every investment decision.  A team of 32 research and trading professionals seeks the best long and short opportunities globally, guided by risk-reward dynamics rather than value or growth style factors, market capitalization or index weighting.  While bottom-up fundamental analysis drives security selection, quantitative research plays a critical role in portfolio construction and risk management.

The investment team is structured into four sector groups—Consumer, Healthcare, Cyclicals, and Technology—supported by two dedicated private investment teams (Silicon and Ventures), as well as specialized quantitative research and trading teams.  Team members are responsible for developing both long and short ideas, deepening analytical expertise and enhancing their understanding of competitive dynamics.  Collectively, the 32 investment and trading professionals average 14 years of industry or investment experience and nine years of tenure at Maverick.

management_company_description: BlueBalance Capital is a specialist asset management firm, renowned for its derivatives expertise. strategy_description:
BlueBalance Global Opportunities is a discretionary RV/Macro strategy that aims to profit from dislocations across term structures in equities, rates, and FX. The strategy has a track record of more than 10 years. The portfolio mainly consists of non-directional, relative value transactions, as well as macro- and volatility trades. The strategy invests across liquid asset classes primarily via derivatives and focuses on medium- to long-term structural dislocations that are considered significantly more interesting and less crowded than at the short end of the curve. To mitigate drawdowns inherent in relative value trades during a correlation shock, the strategy constantly holds a hedging book, which seeks to smooth returns over the long term by softening the left tails. name: Vision Opportunity Master Fund Limited Partnership
exact_name: Vision Opportunity Master Fund Limited Partnership
management_company_description:
Vision Capital Corporation (“Vision”),  registered as a Portfolio Manager, Investment Fund Manager and Exempt Market Dealer with the Ontario Securities Commission and reports to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) as an exempt reporting adviser, is the Manager of the Vision Opportunity Funds (the “Funds”), alternative investment funds that focus on investments in publicly-traded securities in the real estate sector. 

Vision targets inefficiencies that generate a lower cost base, less risk and superior liquidity compared to direct property investments. The Funds have the flexibility to invest globally; however, they operate primarily in North America to benefit from unique inefficiencies inherent in the pricing of select U.S. and Canadian publicly-traded real estate securities.

Vision employs a value-based approach in a long-short equity strategy and selectively utilizes active investing strategies to improve total returns. 

Vision brings to the Funds a collective wealth of knowledge and experience, spanning over 100 years, of its portfolio management team members: Jeffrey Olin, Frank Mayer, and Andrew Moffs, who possess a deep understanding of the real estate sector along with valuable insights and well-established industry relationships.
strategy_description:
Vision Opportunity Master Fund Limited Partnership (the "Fund") is the "master fund" in a master-feeder structure, in which Vision Opportunity Fund Limited Partnership, Vision Opportunity Fund Trust, Vision Opportunity U.S. Fund Limited Partnership, and Vision Opportunity TE & Non-U.S. Fund Limited Partnership, operating as "feeder funds", invest all of their subscription proceeds in the Fund to achieve their investment objectives. 

The Fund has a significant real estate focus and invests primarily in North America, including a focus on market inefficiencies unique to Canada and selectively in the United States. Where appropriate, Vision will seek to be an active investor by utilizing the combination of its real estate experience together with its capital market knowledge and relationships to benefit the Fund. The Fund may be selectively concentrated in Vision's best ideas as it seeks to identify specific opportunities to capitalize on the arbitrage between private and public real estate valuations. Portfolio investments in the Fund can be long or short, although Vision has historically had a majority of investments as long holdings reflecting the aforementioned market inefficiencies which will enable the Fund to have exposure to real estate investment more cheaply through the stock market than in the property market.

Vision uses an active management approach to achieve the Fund’s investment objectives of generating consistently favorable risk-adjusted total returns to investors. Vision employs numerous quantitative and qualitative factors to identify and profit from trends and mispriced securities that do not adequately reflect the underlying value and growth prospects of the issuer. 

Vision's investment strategy seeks out undervalued or overvalued corporations/REITs both absolutely and relative to their peers. The strategy involves the identification of corporations’/REITs’ Net Asset Value (NAV) of the underlying real estate as compared to the pricing of its equity (or debt) securities. Focusing on NAV: i) avoids excessive and myopic focus on near-term earnings and cash flow; and, ii) assesses impact from (undervalued or off-balance sheet) assets which do not have current earnings or liabilities which may not be sufficiently understood.

The strategy utilizes a combination of “top-down” and “bottom-up” approaches to pinpoint investment opportunities. A top-down strategy for assessing asset sectors or regions, and a bottom-up approach to select specific investments based on the merits of the specific entity and preference for internalized and aligned management. Vision also assesses balance sheet considerations including near-term liquidity factors. The strategy also involves investments in debt, convertible debt, and preferred shares, particularly when equity-like returns are available with a lower level of risk.

name: Versor Merger Arbitrage Strategy
management_company_description:
Versor Investments was founded in January 2014 by Founder and Managing Partner Deepak Gurnani and Founding Partners: Ludger Hentschel, Andrew Flynn, DeWayne Louis, and Nirav Shah. Versor is a pioneer in applying AI and alternative data to global equity markets. As a quantitative equities boutique, we focus on systematically delivering uncorrelated alpha across single stocks, equity index futures, and corporate events. Versor’s 50+ professionals drive the creation and implementation of alpha forecast models, risk models, portfolio construction and the trading process.

Asset Under Management data as of June 30, 2025.  AUM based on internal estimates. AUM as per SEC definition for the purposes of Item 5.F on the Form ADV Part 1a.
strategy_description:
The Merger Arbitrage strategy invests in announced merger deals across the US, Canada, UK, and Europe and capitalizes on the spread between a company’s current share price and its acquisition price. The strategy uses an active fundamental investment style, based on 20+ years of merger arbitrage investing experience, combined with superior systematic processes and technology. Every step of the investment process relies on solid fundamental and economic theory. Sophisticated machine learning techniques are used to process vast amounts of information saved in a proprietary merger database. 

Alternative data sources track real-time merger data and a proprietary database of 4000+ deals (since 2000) stores both fundamental data (on target and acquirer companies) and market data, including intra-day spreads, for the life of the deal. The comprehensive deal-by-deal evaluation process uses machine learning and the proprietary database to estimate probability of deal success versus failure, determine downside risk and perform competing bid analysis. The investment process also incorporates market assessment of valuation and risk & regulatory approvals. Electronic trading significantly enhances trading efficiencies and reduces costs.

We believe that the Versor Merger Arbitrage strategy has one of the highest ESG impacts of any investment strategy. Historically, the ESG scores for the merger targets in the portfolio have improved by 57% from a year prior to the merger to a year after the merger. For investors who seek to raise the ESG standards of publicly listed companies, Versor Merger Arbitrage is likely to be one of the most impactful investment strategies.

management_company_description: Sone Capital Management (“Sone”) was founded in 2024 by George Panos alongside several senior investment and operations professionals from Echo Street Capital Management (“Echo Street”). George founded Sone after 12 years at Echo Street, where he was most recently a Partner and Portfolio Manager. Sone manages a market-neutral equity long/short strategy and employs a structured and repeatable approach to fundamental investing. The Firm is based in New York City and embraces a culture of curiosity, diligence, and urgency.
strategy_description: Sone Capital seeks to generate attractive, uncorrelated returns with low volatility through the pursuit of a market-neutral equity long/short strategy. The strategy uses proprietary in-house fundamental Net Asset Value (NAV) data to systematically construct Relative Value (RV) trades within a curated universe of global developed market equities. The universe is comprised of quality companies with durable earnings streams driving stable, narrowly bounded NAVs. Sone’s investment team is responsible for continuously updating the underwriting of NAVs using a Bayesian process, ensuring the integration of new information in real time. The strategy pursues tight fundamental fit of longs and shorts, allowing for leveraged market-neutral exposure, while emphasizing idiosyncratic mispricing. Sone manages this RV strategy using the proprietary data and code base developed over two decades at Echo Street. Portfolio construction incorporates higher gross exposure and little to no net exposure.

name: Solken Convertible Arbitrage
management_company_description:
DCM Systematic SA is an independent, quantitative investment manager based in Geneva, Switzerland. The business was founded by two senior quants from BlueCrest and they were joined by a head of business development from Pictet. The team launched the flagship strategy, Diversified Alpha, in February 2016. The firm is built upon the premise of applying scientific methods to identify a wide range of opportunities within liquid financial markets. Research is at the core of the business and the team is continually striving to improve by exploring new quantitative methods, learning from the markets and enhancing processes. The aim is that with this approach the company can successfully navigate different market environments and the variety of challenges they present.

In 2022, two experienced portfolio managers joined to launch a new venture called Solken Convertible Arbitrage. This is a distinct product within DCM Systematic and combines quantitative techniques with discretionary analysis to explore opportunities in the convertible bond markets.
strategy_description:
DCM RAIF – Solken Convertible Arbitrage pursues an alternative, relative value strategy generically called convertible arbitrage. It consists in identifying convertible securities that trade at a discount to their fair value or whose valuation is expected to fluctuate, and set up hedges in an effort to neutralise traditional market premia and isolate returns generated by the move in relative value of the components. The Fund follows an innovative strategy by building a systematic extension of the
common discretionary approach.

strategy_description:
Orion Commodities Fund ("OCF") employs a discretionary, sector-specialist strategy that solely trades precious and base metals via derivatives and physicals.

The fund seeks to achieve uncorrelated, absolute returns with controlled volatility by primarily employing relative-value, calendar spread, and arbitrage trades while maintaining limited directional exposure to metals. Additionally, OCF receives optionality through its ability to take delivery of metals via warehouse receipts (warrants), allowing it to discern the veracity of fundamental trends not readily apparent in outright market price movements while retaining its liquid profile. Currently, the strategy trades the CME (US), LME (London), and SHFE (Shanghai) exchanges.

Since inception, the strategy has maintained low correlation and beta to traditional markets, including equities, fixed income, and even broad commodities – all while controlling downside risk. 

OCF is the hedge fund division of Orion Resource Partners ("ORP"), an $8bn AUM metals and mining investment firm that accesses the global supply chain through its separate private equity, royalty, venture capital, and trade finance divisions.

Through its relationship with its parent firm, OCF is able to access proprietary research and glean additional insight into the underlying fundamental drivers of metals prices, providing it with an edge in the metals trading space.

esg_approach_description:
As stewards of capital, we have a duty to ensure that we are operating and investing sustainably; making a fully effort to identify and mitigate all risks to our portfolios.  Given our focus on advanced economy sovereign bond markets, Ardea sees climate change as the ESG risk of most concern.  We are committed to use our knowledge and to effect change in government bond markets arising from the realisation of risks related to climate change. Our aim is to influence practical change by using our frequent and high-volume trading of government bonds to foster the growth and development of the green bond market, contributing materially towards improving market liquidity and price discovery for green government bonds.

To meet our commitments to ESG and sustainability, Ardea has prioritised the following activities:

1.         Research,

2.         Integration,

3.         Engagement, and

4.         Corporate Sustainability.

Importantly, the Ardea Global Alpha UCITS fund is classified as an Article 8 Fund. The Fund is thereby committed to a measurable sustainability objective - the development of the green bond market - which we believe will encourage sovereign issuers to increase green bond issuance and other market participants to invest. Our commitment to invest a minimum of 5% of fund assets in green bonds and (importantly) actively trade those bonds will increase both primary and secondary market depth, fostering an awareness of this market and bolstering the liquidity of green bonds. A lack of liquidity in this market is often quoted as the primary objection from investors who are reluctant to support this new and important segment of the bond market. Ultimately, we hope to broaden the volume and scope of green bond issuance and hence the environmental projects that are funded in this manner.

strategy_description:
The objective of the Fund is capital appreciation while closely controlling risk. In addition, it intends to deliver absolute returns that have a low correlation with equity and bond markets. 
The Fund aims to achieve its investment objective by investing primarily in a portfolio of equity securities of companies located worldwide and listed or traded on Regulated Markets and by pursuing the strategy detailed below. It is not proposed to concentrate investments in any one geographical region or sector. 
It aims to deliver an absolute return over rolling 12 month periods, in other words, at any one time the portfolio of Jupiter Merian Global Equity Absolute Return Fund will typically be constructed with reference to an investment horizon of no greater than 12 months. 
It will be structured as a market neutral portfolio. A universe of major market, large capitalisation global equity stocks will be assessed, and long positions taken in the stocks determined most likely to deliver a positive relative return, and short positions taken in the stocks determined most likely to deliver a negative relative return. The total value of the long positions will be approximately matched by the total value of the short positions. Under normal market conditions and depending on the shorting opportunities in the markets, the Investment Manager expects that the Fund’s short exposure will normally be less than 125% of Net Asset Value. Under normal market conditions, the Investment Manager expects that the Jupiter Merian Global Equity Absolute Return Fund’s long exposure will not normally exceed 125% of Net Asset Value. Accordingly, under normal market conditions the Jupiter Merian Global Equity Absolute Return Fund’s net exposure to investment markets is likely to be in the range of –5% to +5% of Net Asset Value.

name: Asterion Program
management_company_description: Tidan Capital is a Stockholm-based, independent investment management company established in 2020 by Brummer & Partners alumni with several decades of investment experience across the capital structure. Our flagship strategy, a market-neutral credit relative value approach, is built on a foundation of deep fundamental analysis and a disciplined investment process. With a presence in Europe and expanding globally, Tidan Capital operates under rigorous regulatory standards and an organisation relying on premier service providers ensuring a scalable and governance-focused investment platform for our clients.
strategy_description: The Asterion strategy is a short-term systematic multi strategy taking directional positions across Global Markets. The strategy utilizes an ensemble approach to extract alpha from short term predictions. It is designed to generate absolute returns by capitalizing on a variety of market behaviors across global futures markets. The strategy exploits inefficiencies and patterns driven by biases and behavior created by a variety of market participants, ranging from sophisticated institutions to activities driven by retail flows. The strategy is designed to overwhelmingly carry directional exposure. While the program aims to be market neutral over a cycle, it will rarely be market neutral on a particular day and may hold positions against the prevailing market trends. The strategy currently trades liquid Futures across a variety of sectors and geographies but may opt for other asset classes to reflect future opportunities and to exploit liquidity pockets (e.g. ETFs, FX Forwards, look-a-like swaps, etc.). The program is set up to be highly dynamic and can shift exposure from neutral to large positive or negative views in any particular market. Unlike traditional CTAs, that tend to heavily depend on long-term trend-based strategies, the Asterion strategy deploys a multitude of different strategies, currently clustered within three families: Mean Reversion, Behavioral, and Trend Following, with a short average holding period. In expectancy terms, over a longer period, the approach utilized by the Asterion strategy seeks to deliver a higher Sharpe ratio compared to a pure Trend Follower strategy as the different families offer uncorrelated returns streams, thereby creating a more robust investment opportunity.

name: First Turn Rx
management_company_description:
First Turn, managed by Lisa Wheatley (former head of M&A at Life technologies), is a HC sector-focused strategy which seeks to capitalize on
opportunities created by the accelerating pace of innovation and corresponding scientific breakthroughs in the life sciences industry. The
strategy is focused on investing in later development-stage and early commercial-stage companies across the life science ecosystem. The
portfolio manager typically invests with an 18-24 month investment time horizon.

At the start of 2Q25, First Turn launched a new, therapeutics-focused (biotech & pharma) strategy – First Turn Rx. The strategy can be
implemented as long-only, market neutral (using benchmark/basket hedging). The firm supports custom institutional SMAs including active extension/portable alpha (SMA) implementations via recognized managed account platforms. The FTRX strategy is anchored by a large institutional investor with a portable alpha implementation.  

Summary: 
FTRx is managed as a standalone Long-only strategy that places emphasis on the SMID Biotech and Pharmaceutical segments of the healthcare sector. The portfolio construction is a combination of later stage clinical development (Ph II/III) companies and emerging commercial stage companies.  The strategy will continue to follow our long-held investment tenants, investing in those companies that have successfully demonstrated a compelling safety, efficacy, and durability profile in clinical development. 

Since the inception of the First Turn strategy in 2017 (fka NicHealth), our key investment goal has been to seek out and invest in companies that are pursuing and commercializing practice-changing medicine; therapies that have the potential to significantly improve patient outcomes. This remains our guiding principle.

As a result, identifying the best growth businesses and understanding what their future may look like, and having a long-term view on how intrinsic value can be created can be an advantage in capturing opportunities. management_company_description:
Mercator is a sector-specialist asset manager focused on global electricity and energy markets. With an experienced portfolio construction team and an investment process built around a commitment to primary research, Mercator seeks to generate differentiated returns through deep fundamental insight.

The firm applies first-principles research, scientific analysis, and rigorous company-level diligence to identify opportunities arising from structural shifts across the evolving power landscape. Mercator was founded in 2018 and has offices in Princeton (NJ) and New York City.
strategy_description:
The energy transition represents a multi-decade capital cycle across global power systems. While energy has always enabled societal change, we are witnessing an ongoing transformation in the nature of energy sources and technologies, at a time where the industry is also seeking to accommodate a sharp inflection in power demand.

The Mercator Convergence Fund, a long/short global equities mandate, was established to capitalize on this multi decade structural investment opportunity. Positioned across the breadth of electricity capex and supply chain, the Fund deploys risk across ca. 40-60 positions. With an average trade duration of 24-36 months, the Fund targets structural shifts across the global energy system where value creation unfolds over extended investment horizons. By underwriting themes such as the growth in energy generation, grid modernization, and critical hardware solutions, Mercator seeks to capture persistent dispersion between structural winners and losers with a thesis focused on compounding returns.

A disciplined portfolio construction methodology which applies a risk-weighted capital allocation framework is a further defining characteristic of the strategy. The Fund’s exposure is actively managed to capture compelling upside asymmetry and to protect capital by tactically de risking and rotating exposures through windows of opportunity.

management_company_description: Wolverine Asset Management, LLC ('WAM" or the "Investment Manager") is an alternative asset management firm that seeks to generate returns by investing in the equity, credit, commodity, and volatility asset classes. Wolverine Flagship Fund (‘Fund’ or ‘WFF’) seeks to generate absolute returns on capital primarily through the use of arbitrage and relative value strategies. strategy_description:
i)  Capital Structure Arbitrage is a derivatives-based, relative value approach to investing across corporate capital structures. The Investment Manager seeks  to purchase mispriced securities relative to their fair value using a combination of theoretical valuation and trading judgement based on the Investment Manager’s experience in the marketplace. The Investment Manager  buys underpriced securities and sells short (sells without owning) overpriced securities. This strategy primarily trades corporate bonds, preferred securities, warrants, listed equities, equity options, credit default swaps, and futures to express its positions.
(ii) Event-Driven is a strategy that seeks to capture excess risk premium in securities whose value is expected to be impacted by an upcoming corporate transaction or other catalyst. These events may include mergers and acquisitions, tender offers, asset sales, spinoffs, debt refinancing actions, litigation, other capital markets transactions, and earnings announcements. The Investment Manager combines knowledge of event mechanics with trading judgement about how security prices will potentially react to identify securities with the best investment potential. Corporate bonds, warrants, and listed equities are the primary instruments traded to pursue this strategy.
(iii)NAV Arbitrage is a relative value approach to investing in trusts, funds, and other pooled investment vehicles. The Investment Manager establishes a net asset value of the investment vehicles by estimating the current fair market value of their underlying assets. The Investment Manager then incorporates the fair market value estimates into a trading signal to guide opportunistic buying, selling, and short selling of the investment vehicles. Offsetting positions in hedging instruments are used to minimize the residual exposure to the underlying investments vehicles. This strategy primarily trades closed-end funds, real estate investment trusts, exchange-traded funds, equities, mortgage-backed securities, and interest rate futures to attain its positions.
(iv) Volatility Arbitrage is a relative value approach to investing in derivative securities and their related underlying instruments. The Investment Manager utilizes both real-time and historical theoretical fair values to construct offsetting positions that embed incongruent assumptions about the future state of the market. Options, futures, volatility and variance swaps, other derivatives, and related underlying instruments are mainly traded to achieve its investment targets.

management_company_description:
Formed in 2008, International Standard Asset Management (iSAM) is an Alternative Investment Adviser with significant experience within the quantitative alternative investment space. The company manages two separate businesses, iSAM Funds and iSAM Securities. The two businesses are managed at a group level but operate independently and are separately regulated.

iSAM Funds is comprised of iSAM Vector and iSAM Helix.

iSAM Vector commenced trading in its current form in May 2010 with 75 markets and an AUM of US$135 million. Over the years, the program has evolved into a specialist in deriving profits from persistent price movements across a broad spectrum of opportunities.

iSAM Vector is a specialist quantitative strategy trading a diverse set of global financial and commodity markets in a highly disciplined and systematic framework. The program captures profits from persistent movements in prices on time frames ranging from intraday to several months, with a continual focus on diversification and dynamic risk balancing.

iSAM Helix is a quantitative strategy that trades liquid equities globally. The strategy uses a broad range of statistical methodologies applied over a wide set of timeframes. The program uses data on individual companies to take long or short positions and seeks to remain market neutral. The strategy currently trades internal capital and is being prepared for launch to external investors.

Formed in 2014 as part of the iSAM Group, iSAM Securities is a multi-regulated (FCA, SFC, CFTC) organisation with over 50 employees. iSAM Securities operates from UK, US, Cayman Islands and Asia and is a leading provider of liquidity, risk advisory technology and consultancy services to brokers all over the world.

iSAM has 150 employees worldwide with offices in Grand Cayman, London, Florida, Hong Kong and Michigan.
strategy_description:
iSAM Vector is a specialist quantitative strategy trading a diverse set of global financial and commodity markets in a highly disciplined and systematic framework. The program seeks profits from persistent price movements on time frames ranging from intraday to several months and employs a dynamic portfolio construction framework aiming to deliver diversifying absolute returns.

The strategy is applied to over 600 global markets in an integrated portfolio, with a strong emphasis on alternative markets, diversifying commodity exposures and allocations to short-term trading engines. iSAM allocates ~70% of the portfolio’s risk budget to alternative markets. iSAM aims to limit the capacity of the strategy to ensure the ongoing delivery of maximum diversification.

management_company_description: Alamut Investment Management was founded in 2024 by Faiz Bhanji and is based in London. Alamut manages a global and concentrated long/short equity strategy that seeks to combine unconventional research with a repeatable investment approach to deliver an alpha-driven return profile.
strategy_description:
Strategy Overview:

Alamut manages a global and concentrated long/short equity strategy that seeks to combine unconventional research with a repeatable investment approach to deliver an alpha-driven return profile.

Key Principles of Portfolio Construction:

• Highly concentrated portfolio, 8-12 longs and 5-10 shorts
• Concentration allows for deep understanding of businesses and their
industry dynamics
• Portfolio construction reflects our research-based convictions and
sizing adjusted to account for degree of downside protection
• Seek to ensure a margin of safety in every position in case we are wrong
• Goal of our concentrated approach is to ensure we do not make our LPs shoulder the burden of diversification that primarily manages our firm's risks

Types of Investments:

• Generalist approach leveraging TMT expertise
• Focus on high-quality compounding longs where we believe we have a differentiated view on earnings power, durability, strategic positioning and/or valuation
• Shorts will have what we deem to be under-appreciated accounting issues / unsustainable capital structure. Alpha, rather than volatility management, is the goal
• Seek to avoid consensual trades, 'black box' businesses, and overly complex situations

Objective & Management - Longs:

• Goal of long book construction is to build a differentiated portfolio of well-researched ideas with clear theses based around clear misunderstandings
• Quality of business is a necessary but not sufficient condition - no business will be owned simply because it is a good, or even great, business
• Looking for opportunities with at least 100% upside over a 3-5 year view
• Focus on $1-20bn market caps

Objective & Management - Shorts:

• Shorts are initiated to generate alpha rather than to manage volatility
• Looking for opportunities with at least 50% downside over a 1-2-year horizon
• Short book will be managed as a high conviction, concentrated book, similar to the long book, but with greater focus on catalysts and timing when determining sizing
• Emphasis on deep accounting analysis

Transformation of underlying story

• Declining fundamentals as emphasis is put on cost cutting
• Deteriorating quality of deals while deal size increases
• Earnings misses, a loss of faith in story, and concerns about debt level
