name: Linden Capital LP
management_company_description:
Linden was founded by four members of the JP Morgan US Arbitrage Desk, which is JPM’s proprietary trading group focused on convertible and credit arbitrage strategies. Linden is a global, multi strategy approach with three main components: 1.) fundamentally driven convertible strategy with a focus on credit, convertible arbitrage, event driven and special situation trades; and 2.) SPAC strategy that can be used as an alpha generator; and 3.) credit strategy focused on special situations and catalyst trades, covering the entire credit spectrum.

Linden has 48 employees, 25 of which are investment professionals, with complementary skill sets in trading, fundamental and legal research, quantitative analysis, and operations and systems.
strategy_description:
The Fund’s objective is to generate superior risk-adjusted returns through three principal investment strategies: (1) the convertible strategy, (2) the credit strategy, and (3) the SPAC strategy. In pursuit of this objective, the Investment Manager employs a flexible, multi-strategy investment approach which stresses inter-disciplinary cooperation and teamwork and aims to deliver market neutrality, capital preservation and steady, non-correlated, returns. 

Convertible Strategy: The Investment Manager closely tracks the universe of global convertible securities through proprietary models to identify investment opportunities. The Investment Manager utilizes three sub strategies to take advantage of current opportunities in the convertible marketplace. The first sub-strategy is classic convertible arbitrage, capturing mis-priced equity volatilities through convertible bonds or creating so called “synthetic put” hedged convertible positions. The second sub-strategy focuses on mis-priced credit opportunities in the convertible market. The Investment Manager seeks to obtain long/short credit exposure to convertible issuers due to the undervaluation/overvaluation of the convertible bonds relative to other parts of the issuer capital structure or comparable companies in the same industry or sector. The third sub strategy focuses on potential event driven or catalyst driven opportunities, e.g., company buybacks, tender offers, debt-for-equity swaps and restructurings. When considering the relative valuation of convertible securities, the Investment Manager uses a proprietary mathematical model to analyze such factors as: (i) the level of equity volatility, (ii) the credit worthiness of the issuer, (iii) interest rates, and (iv) dividends. The Investment Manager then performs an extensive, bottom-up fundamental review of the individual company, the sector and the industry as a whole. This fundamental analysis may also include a detailed capital structure analysis as well as a legal analysis of various convertible bonds, corporate bonds, and other fixed income issues. In addition, the Investment Manager actively participates in public tender offers and exchanges and may pursue bi-lateral transactions with issuers to maximize the value of its investments. 

Credit Strategy: The Investment Manager combines quantitative analytical tools with fundamental research to monitor specific issuers and spot potential mispricing among either securities within an issuer’s capital structure or within an industry or a sector. The Investment Manager puts emphasis on identifying event driven/catalyst trades resulting from, for example, mergers, acquisitions, reorganizations, covenant violations or balance sheet restructurings. The Investment Manager will perform both a fundamental and legal analysis on the potential impact of an event catalyst on a particular security’s price. In addition to traditional arbitrage opportunities, the Investment Manager may also make directional trades based on undervaluation / overvaluation of certain securities relative to other parts of the issuer capital structure, or comparable companies in the similar sectors or industries. As part of the research process, the Investment Manager may seek to maintain regular dialogue with company management via conference calls, participation in industry conferences, in-person meetings and on-site visits. Final investment decisions will ultimately be based on the particular risks and rewards of each situation.

Strategy Mix: We invest in SPAC units, at or after the IPO, and trade or hold the shares and warrants that make up the units.  Investors in SPAC IPO shares can get their initial investment back if they don’t like the SPAC’s acquisition target, but have the option to participate in the equity upside if the SPAC shares trade higher; in that way, investments in SPACs have a return profile that is similar to that of convertible securities.
We sometimes commit to purchasing private placement (PIPE) shares from a SPAC after it has identified an acquisition target but before it publicly announces the potential business combination with the target.  The purchase of these PIPE shares is canceled if the business combination is not completed.  After the business combination, we are restricted from trading these shares until after the shares clear SEC registration, which poses short term illiquidity risk, but these shares have upside potential because they are normally purchased at or near the IPO unit price of the SPAC. 
In addition, we may invest in vehicles acting as the sponsors of SPACs in exchange for interest in the SPAC that will have value only to the extent that a business combination is consummated by the SPAC and we continue to hold interests in the SPAC thereafter. strategy_description:
The fund is a high-conviction, concentrated and liquid portfolio of long and short ideas forecasted over a multi-year horizon. It has a European focus, but with a global mandate; thus, the majority of investments are expected to be in Europe with the bulk of the remainder in North America.
When selecting long positions, three principle attributes are sought: duration, quality and value.
*Duration: operational visibility in excess of 25 years
*Quality: superior business franchises which will consistently return more than their cost of capital
*Value: the best risk-adjusted IRRs on a four-year view
Given the duration and quality criteria, an investible universe of 130 companies has been identified, mainly from long-cycle industries. Of these, 15-20 will be selected for the long portfolio dependent on the risk adjusted IRRs on offer.
The fund looks to short companies whose operations are being impacted negatively by secular trends which management are attempting to conceal with dishonest accounting.
*Negative secular trends: trends which ultimately lead to a good business becoming a poor one – this process can take years
*Dishonest accounting: profits can relatively easily be manipulated; cashflow is much harder. A focus on cashflows
High Ground does not seek to short on valuation alone. In fact, it prefers to short expensive companies that have halved to those that have doubled. Ultimately, the real economic earnings of short positions are well below reported earnings and over time the market will recognize this causing the stock prices to reset. The aim is to have 20-25 alpha generating short positions.
The relative performance of the fund is expected to be strongest in a moderately rising market seeing a decline in investors’ risk appetites.
It will perform worst in a rapidly rising market where investor confidence is improving markedly.
The fund is differentiated when compared to peers in what it focuses on versus what it’s not interested in:
Focus: franchise risk, intrinsic value, cash generation, GAAP results, time with customers, historical data, long-term secular changes in society and technology, enterprise value based valuation metrics, accounting, the real costs of acquisitions and stock options
Less interested in: investor sentiment, volatility, catalysts, EPS, non-GAAP results, management meetings, broker forecasts, what’s happening this quarter, equity based valuation metrics, missing a hot name, upgrades.
On the long side the fund focuses on companies meeting exacting duration and quality criteria. So far, 135 names globally have been identified that meet these two required thresholds. Generally, these names are found in the infrastructure, aerospace and defence, healthcare services, property and exchanges sectors. However, there are some exceptions; possible long candidates exist in the software and restaurant sectors, amongst others.
Potential shorts exist across all sectors. Given a focus on shorting names being impacted by secular challenges, there is bias towards sectors seeing disruption such as media, CPG, tobacco, autos, retailing and logistics.

strategy_description:
Arbury Fund is a fundamental, concentrated, conviction portfolio typically comprising 15-20 long positions and 0-20 short positions. 

Our targeted long investments are multi-year compounding European growth companies that benefit from secular tailwinds, enabling them to compound their earnings and cashflows over many years.  We find many underappreciated long opportunities in the healthcare and technology sectors; industries in which we have successfully invested over the past 25 years.  We believe our companies have a long runway of growth ahead of them and we expect our long portfolio to significantly outperform the European index over time.

We require attractive valuation entry points and to have a forecast edge for each of our holdings.  We make proprietary forecasts for each holding over at least three years.  The excess returns we target should be driven by the combination of our valuation entry point and the magnitude of the difference between our forecasts and consensus.   We set target prices for each of our holdings, typically projecting 30%+ upside on a 24-month horizon.  We hold stocks for significantly longer than 24 months where our holdings operationally outperform, allowing us to increase our forecasts and target price.
On the short side we look to harness absolute downside opportunities, varying our short gross exposure (0%-30%) according to the prevailing short opportunity set.  Our multi-year track record demonstrates strong short side returns in similar strategies. When compelling short opportunities arise, we increase the gross exposure of our long book to maintain full market exposure, operating a flexible extension strategy.

The goal of the fund is to significantly outperform the STOXX Europe 600 (USD) Index over the medium to long term. Performance fees are only charged if we achieve outperformance against this index. We want our economic incentive to be aligned with our investors so the management fee we charge will decrease as the AUM grows, based on predetermined thresholds.

Arbury Fund will remain focused on Europe, leveraging our strong investment expertise in the region.  We see a compelling, region-specific opportunity set which we seek to harness with our strategy.

Our investment universe includes companies which are headquartered or domiciled in Continental Europe and the UK. We are geographically agnostic within Europe, seeking the best opportunities across the continent.  Many of our companies will have significant international (and USD) revenue exposure because they operate globally rather than being confined to their domestic markets.

name: Paloma Fund
management_company_description:
Paloma has been a trusted foundational capital partner to hedge fund business builders for over 40 years. Founded by industry pioneer Donald Sussman, we have partnered with over 130 managers through customized structures that combine seeding benefits with multi-strategy platform capabilities. The firm allocates across three core strategies -quantitative, equity long-short, and liquid credit - with opportunistic exposure to diversifying capital-efficient approaches, within a rigorous risk management framework. We seek to position our managers to scale durable investment strategies, while delivering our investors with a distinct investment portfolio.

For additional information regarding Firm Inception and Paloma Management, please refer to the Paloma Fund Disclaimer included in this profile for important disclosures and definitions.
strategy_description:
The Paloma Fund is a multi-strategy hedge fund that seeks to achieve attractive long-term risk-adjusted returns through dynamic capital allocation among a changing set of investment strategies and portfolio managers. As conditions and opportunities dictate, the Paloma Fund will invest in a wide range of possible strategies: relative value, quantitative, fundamental, directional, and others. The "Paloma Fund" includes Paloma International L.P. as the Master Fund, and three feeder funds: Paloma Partners L.L.C., Paloma International Limited and Paloma Offshore Limited. Paloma Management has ultimate discretion and control over the Master Fund and its investments. Paloma Management pursues its investment program primarily by allocating capital to investment teams that advise and invest on behalf of the Paloma Fund and by making strategic direct investments into external standalone funds. 

For additional information on the Fund Inception Date and Domicile: Please refer to the Paloma Fund Disclaimer included in this profile for important disclosures and definitions.

management_company_description:
Boussard & Gavaudan ("BG") was founded in 2002 by Emmanuel Boussard (CIO), former head of equity derivatives proprietary trading at Goldman
Sachs and Emmanuel Gavaudan (Executive Chairman and CRO), former partner at Goldman Sachs. BG is 100% owned by its employees, and has a strong team of 55 people, consisting 25 investment professionals who are supported by 30 people in risk management, legal, compliance and operations. BG has offices in London, Paris & New York.

BG manages a multi-strategy hedge fund : BG Master Fund ICAV / BG Umbrella Fund Plc ("BG Fund"), which applies an event driven and multi-strategy/multi-assets investment approach to generate consistent returns over different market cycles. The management style combines bottom-up fundamental analysis with a thorough expertise of financial instruments. BG Fund dynamically allocates capital in a diversified range of positions across equities, credit, convertibles, based on individual market opportunities while aiming to structure each position to be market neutral and with the overall portfolio long volatility/convexity.

The French entity Boussard & Gavaudan Gestion ("BGG") manages a luxembourg-domiciled UCITS fund: Boussard & Gavaudan Convertible ("BGCB"), which invests in European, North American and Asian convertible bonds. The fund intends to capitalise on not just Credit or Equity, but also Volatility, Special situations and Primary issuances.
strategy_description:
BG Fund is a multi-strategy event-driven and arbitrage fund.
The investment team applies an approach which combines robust fundamental analysis with deep technical expertise across financial instruments.
The strategy aims to be long volatility, positive convexity at all times and with most investments structured with minimal beta.
The fund operates across asset classes (equity, credit and volatility) and the investments are rigorously screened to focus on events, catalysts and arbitrage opportunities.
The capital is allocated by the Investment Committee to the best available ideas, driven by the corporate cycle, market conditions and mispricing opportunities.
Combining deep analysis with strong risk management and trading expertise, BG Fund’s hedged, convex risk profile differentiates itself by delivering idiosyncratic and uncorrelated returns.
The Fund was launched in March 2003 under the name Sark Fund and now has more than 23 years of continuous track record. The Sark Fund changed its legal structure and name in November 2010 to become BG Master Fund.

management_company_description: Amia Capital LLP is the Investment Manager of Amia Capital Macro Fund (the “Fund”). The London-based specialist team is led by Antoine Estier and offers a valuable blend of sell-side and buy-side expertise with an average of 20 years of business and trading experience. The majority of the team worked together for several years in building and managing their previous hedge fund business. The firm offers institutional infrastructure with clear segregation of responsibilities between CIO, CEO, COO and CRO. The team monitors controls, processes, procedures and systems in efforts to ensure compliance with best market practices and delivery of high governance standards.
strategy_description:
Amia Capital Macro Fund is a discretionary global macro fund focusing on multi-asset class opportunities in developed and emerging markets. The team has a specialist “no tourist” approach to markets, with a history of capturing returns across various asset classes and market cycles. Portfolio diversification is sought through a wide range of markets and products, complemented by disciplined investment and risk management processes. There is collaborative and transparent non-silo approach and open communication within the team, in efforts to ensure market signals are recognised promptly. The investment model has the flexibility to channel expertise and mobilise resources quickly for a given situation. Investors have a direct access to the CIO and the investment team.

The investment objective of the Fund is to seek to achieve long-term capital appreciation. The Fund aims to achieve this objective by employing an absolute return focus utilising strategies focused primarily on developed and emerging markets. The specialist strategies include - EM Sovereign Credit, EM Corporate Credit, EM Rates, DM Credit, DM Rates, Dynamic Hedging – and focus on four main investment styles - directional, relative value, liquidity and recovery. Capital is used dynamically across investment strategies driven by the risk/reward analysis of the opportunities. The Investment Manager employs a dual top down and bottom up approach to identify investment opportunities. The Investment & Risk Committee meets daily to review and discuss the portfolio, risk correlation, exposures, concentration and performance. Multi-dimensional, granular risk analysis and oversight is integral to the whole investment process. Cross-oversight within the investment team provides an additional layer of risk management.

exact_name: Astignes Systematic Relative Value Macro Fund
management_company_description: Astignes Capital Asia Pte. Ltd. ("Astignes Capital" or the "Firm") is a Singapore based alternative investment management firm focused on capturing global macro and relative value opportunities, primarily through liquid asset markets and derivatives.
strategy_description:
The Fund aims to offer a diverse source of alternative alpha streams with low correlation to beta markets via liquid and transparent futures markets.

ASRM's primary objectives are three-fold:

1. Deliver superior risk-adjusted returns independent of business cycles and market environments
2. Deliver a unique alpha within the systematic universe uncorrelated to known factors and styles of investments
3. Primary of capital preservation and risk management

The strategy consists of multiple proprietary alphas, each of which is managed by one of two different algorithms:

• Debra is a time series algorithm that draws on prices and volatility to construct relative value opportunities in contracts of the same underlying across different maturities.
• Frank is a cross sectional algorithm that constructs relative value trades while considering both economic data and historical price movements to invest in established macro alphas

From the combined pool of alphas, trades with the highest risk-adjusted return are selected after taking into account the current market environment and are sized appropriately given capital allocation, portfolio construction and risk management constraints. After which intraday execution is optimized as price information is captured and fed back, making our algorithms liquidity-aware and transaction cost informed.

The process - from data sourcing, return calculations, portfolio construction, risk management, algorithmic execution and trade reconciliation - is automated and fed through a feedback loop on realized trade and risk-adjusted performance data.

The Fund seeks to provide returns that are uncorrelated to the underlying asset class and to broad market indices.

esg_approach_description:
Astignes Capital cares about and takes ESG very seriously. While there may be no natural setting for ESG to play a direct role in the Firm’s investment process, the Firm addresses some of society’s greatest challenges through its business, operations, and philanthropy. In order to ensure that our ESG commitments are deeply integrated into the business over the long term, the board passed an ESG Statement in January 2021 to increase the Firm’s ESG efforts in three main dimensions:

1. Wallet Allocation - Our corporate eco-system – how our wallet is allocated to third-party service providers
2. Charities - The Firm continuously identifies and supports charities that speak directly to the scope of ESG
3. Money Market Facilities - ESG-compliant money market facilities are actively included in our treasury management

We built upon our initial efforts by incorporating the following additional ESG-related elements within our business in the second half of 2021:

1. Formal ESG Committee  - comprised of both employee volunteers and senior management sponsor(s)
2. Board Item - ESG as a standing topic of discussion for all future Board of Directors meetings. 
3.  Adherence to Principles - The Firm became a signatory to the Principles of Responsible Investing (PRI)
4. Active Research - to identify the most effective way to offset future business-related travel through the acquisition of carbon offsets.

name: CFM Cumulus Program
management_company_description:
Capital Fund Management (CFM) is an investment management firm whose strategies are based on a quantitative and systematic approach to financial markets. Our culture blends a unique mixture of the scientific backgrounds of our researchers and IT engineers, supported by an experienced corporate team.
Research and technology are the key enablers of the investment process at CFM, which involves creating strategies derived from the analysis of industrial quantities (hundreds of terabytes per annum) of financial data allowing trading decisions to be executed in a highly systematic and disciplined way. We look for statistically significant patterns from which investment strategies are created, then rigorously tested, before being implemented by algorithms. 
CFM maintains an industrial strength straight-through-processing infrastructure across six data centers on three continents. Trading is conducted with leading global counterparties.
CFM’s entities are registered with the CFTC, the SEC, the AMF in France and the UK FCA.
CFM is also a member of AIMA (Alternative Investment Management Association), SBAI (Standards Board for Alternative Investments) and AFG (Association Française de la Gestion Financière).
Additional information about CFM is available on the SEC’s website at www.adviserinfo.sec.gov.
There are significant risks associated with the trading strategy. Please review carefully any risk factors and related disclosures that may be available in the Fund’s confidential offering memorandum.
strategy_description: CFM Cumulus is a multi-strategy absolute return program, which offers a complementary mix of market neutral, directional and defensive strategies. The program includes directional trading and relative value components and may take long and short exposures through a variety of financial instruments including securities, foreign exchange, futures, forwards and other derivatives on bonds, shares, rates, currencies, commodities, credit and indices, as well as derivatives on all the foregoing. The investment objective is to achieve long term capital appreciation through returns that seek to be low correlated with traditional and alternative benchmarks (* Correlations generally inferior to 0.3 over multiple year periods with indices such as Barclays Capital Global Aggregate Bond Index US$ Hedged, Morningstar Developed Markets Index NR USD, HFRI Fund Weighted Composite Index.

Capital Fund Management (CFM) is an investment management firm whose strategies are based on a quantitative and systematic approach to financial markets. Our culture blends a unique mixture of the scientific backgrounds of our researchers and IT engineers, supported by an experienced corporate team.
Research and technology are the key enablers of the investment process at CFM, which involves creating strategies derived from the analysis of industrial quantities (hundreds of terabytes per annum) of financial data allowing trading decisions to be executed in a highly systematic and disciplined way. We look for statistically significant patterns from which investment strategies are created, then rigorously tested, before being implemented by algorithms. 
CFM maintains an industrial strength straight-through-processing infrastructure across six data centers on three continents. Trading is conducted with leading global counterparties.
CFM’s entities are registered with the CFTC, the SEC, the AMF in France and the UK FCA.
CFM is also a member of AIMA (Alternative Investment Management Association), SBAI (Standards Board for Alternative Investments) and AFG (Association Française de la Gestion Financière).

strategy_description:

The program’s trading universe covers equity indices, credit, bonds, short-term interest rates, commodity certificates and currencies. 
CFM ISTEC uses technology developed within the firm to build robust signals and deliver constant risk using our proprietary portfolio construction tools. The program is a multi-asset long-term trend following, which includes multiple layers to offer protection in equity downturns: multiple trend following timescales, short timescale protection and Equity Beta Cap.

name: Varenne Valeur
management_company_description:
Varenne Capital Partners (‘Varenne’) is a research and process driven investment manager based in Paris, France, where it was founded by its current management team in 2003.

The firm first operated as an advisor to VEGA Finance – private banking unit of the CDC/CE Group – before establishing itself as a fully independent investment manager in 2007. 

With 8 nationalities in a team of 50 people, including 21 investment professionals, the management team fosters a culture of openness and diversity translating into very low turnover and an average tenure of 9 years in the investment team. 

All senior investment associates are shareholders or stock option holders in the firm and co-invest a significant portion of their wealth alongside long-standing clients in Europe, Asia, and the Americas.
strategy_description:
VARENNE VALEUR aims at delivering superior long-term returns with the minimum necessary risk-taking. To do so, Varenne combines complementary investment frameworks in a single strategy: Long Equity, Short Equity, Merger Arbitrage and Tail Risk Hedging. The central idea is to separate risks from opportunities and deal with them independently and attempt to deliver an optimized risk-return profile. The firm adopts a ‘no broker research’ policy and seeks to make extensive use of technology to rely exclusively on internal origination and proprietary research.

The Long Equity framework starts with a core of 30 to 35 high-quality businesses in global developed markets. Additional diversified positions allow access to themes, sectors, or situations that can be absent from the core concentrated selection in order to optimize strategies’ behavior. Proprietary fundamental and behavioral databases provide original investment ideas to different teams (‘Origination’) which contribute their highest convictions to the portfolios.

The Short Equity framework has a core portfolio with the goal of producing uncorrelated returns, particularly in adverse economic or credit conditions. Core exposure is expressed through companies facing at least one among: unsustainable profitability, business deterioration, or financial issues. Diversified short layers provide exposure to themes, situations or industries that may be absent from single name selections in order to optimize overall portfolio behavior. We combine proprietary fundamental and behavioral factors to identify the above idiosyncratic ideas and manage the timing of the trades as well as their risk.

Merger Arbitrage focuses on friendly and announced deals only. Each deal is analysed internally to establish a probability of success allowing highly selective ‘deal-picking’, with the ability to take advantage of increased volatility and to act as a liquidity provider to the market. However, the team is under no obligation to be ‘in play’ all the time and the exposure can range from 0%-100% exposure. The aim of the strategy is to fund, entirely or partially, the 1.5% annual budget for the Tail Risk Hedging.

Tail Risk hedging is designed to attempt to mitigate the effects of residual risk, which is defined as the impact from an event leading the S&P 500 index down 20% or more from its 52-week peak. Implementation is done through internal research looking for asymmetric instruments with a maximum annual budget of 1.5% of AUM. The framework is implemented through two families of hedges: Market Risk & Root Causes of Market Risk. Market risk hedges are typically shorter-mid dated, using non-vanilla equity optional strategies. Root causes can be longer dated and can trade on five possible asset classes: equities, credit, rates, fx, and commodities.

The four frameworks are combined using a rule-based portfolio construction methodology. The investment process therefore aims to bring together what we believe to be the depth of analysis and judgement of independent and experienced teams together with the rigor and systematicity of a rule-based portfolio construction model.

The Fund’s Equity Long and Short Equity frameworks have a gross exposure limited to 110% maximum (MtM), and typically range between 60-90%. Short Equity exposure varies from 0% to a maximum of 20%. The Merger Arbitrage framework has a gross exposure varying from 0% to 100% with an average of 25-35%. The Tail Risk Hedging framework has an annual budget of 1.5% per year with a typical notional exposure of 30-100%.

strategy_description:
The One River Dynamic Convexity Equity Overlay Strategy utilizes the One River Dynamic Convexity Strategy with a 120% S&P 500 Overlay, using the same capital for both equity appreciation and long convexity protection. One River has run the Dynamic Convexity (Systematic Long Equity 
Volatility) strategy since 2015 for large institutional clients in various separately managed accounts and a commingled fund that launched in December 2019. The Dynamic Convexity strategy aims to produce strong performance during equity market crises, monetize that benefit before the crises subside, and mitigate the expected bleed during non-crisis periods. The strategy has three sub-components (1) "Quant VIX" - a long-only VIX and VSTOXX futures momentum strategy (2) "VIX Convexity"-a strategy that seeks to own VIX options in a carry-efficient way, and (3) "Short-Dated Equity Straddles"-a value strategy that seeks to own equity index options with positive expectancy.

name: Varenne Global
management_company_description:
Varenne Capital Partners (‘Varenne’) is a research and process driven investment manager based in Paris, France, where it was founded by its current management team in 2003.

The firm first operated as an advisor to VEGA Finance – private banking unit of the CDC/CE Group – before establishing itself as a fully independent investment manager in 2007. 

With 8 nationalities in a team of 50 people, including 21 investment professionals, the management team fosters a culture of openness and diversity translating into very low turnover and an average tenure of 9 years in the investment team. 

All senior investment associates are shareholders or stock option holders in the firm and co-invest a significant portion of their wealth alongside long-standing clients in Europe, Asia, and the Americas.
strategy_description:
VARENNE GLOBAL aims at delivering superior long-term returns with the minimum necessary risk-taking. To do so, Varenne combines complementary investment frameworks in a single strategy: Long Equity, Short Equity, Merger Arbitrage and Tail Risk Hedging. The central idea is to separate risks from opportunities and deal with them independently and attempt to deliver an optimized risk-return profile. The firm adopts a ‘no broker research’ policy and seeks to make extensive use of technology to rely exclusively on internal origination and proprietary research.

The Long Equity framework starts with a core of 30 to 35 high-quality businesses in global developed markets. Additional diversified positions allow access to themes, sectors, or situations that can be absent from the core concentrated selection in order to optimize strategies’ behavior. Proprietary fundamental and behavioral databases provide original investment ideas to different teams (‘Origination’) which contribute their highest convictions to the portfolios.

The Short Equity framework has a core portfolio with the goal of producing uncorrelated returns, particularly in adverse economic or credit conditions. Core exposure is expressed through companies facing at least one among: unsustainable profitability, business deterioration, or financial issues. Diversified short layers provide exposure to themes, situations or industries that may be absent from single name selections in order to optimize overall portfolio behavior. We combine proprietary fundamental and behavioral factors to identify the above idiosyncratic ideas and manage the timing of the trades as well as their risk.

Merger Arbitrage focuses on friendly and announced deals only. Each deal is analysed internally to establish a probability of success allowing highly selective ‘deal-picking’, with the ability to take advantage of increased volatility and to act as a liquidity provider to the market. However, the team is under no obligation to be ‘in play’ all the time and the exposure can range from 0%-100% exposure. The aim of the strategy is to fund, entirely or partially, the 1.5% annual budget for the Tail Risk Hedging.

Tail Risk hedging is designed to attempt to mitigate the effects of residual risk, which is defined as the impact from an event leading the S&P 500 index down 20% or more from its 52-week peak. Implementation is done through internal research looking for asymmetric instruments with a maximum annual budget of 1.5% of AUM. The framework is implemented through two families of hedges: Market Risk & Root Causes of Market Risk. Market risk hedges are typically shorter-mid dated, using non-vanilla equity optional strategies. Root causes can be longer dated and can trade on five possible asset classes: equities, credit, rates, fx, and commodities.

The four frameworks are combined using a rule-based portfolio construction methodology. The investment process therefore aims to bring together what we believe to be the depth of analysis and judgement of independent and experienced teams together with the rigor and systematicity of a rule-based portfolio construction model.

The Fund’s Equity Long and Short Equity frameworks typically range between 95-115% (MtM). Short Equity exposure varies from 0% to a maximum of 30%. The Merger Arbitrage framework has a gross exposure varying from 0% to 100% with an average of 20-30%. The Tail Risk Hedging framework has an annual budget of 1.5% per year with a typical notional exposure of 30-100%.

strategy_description: Destination Value Total Return is a multi-asset, multi-strategy portfolio built with the expected target of generating 8% annualized gross return (in USD) with <75% of equity markets volatility across the cycle. The strategy has a benchmark-free, high conviction (around 120-150 positions) approach to security selection anchored in fundamental valuations. By allocating to 5 proprietary strategies rather than asset classes, the portfolio focuses on identifying idiosyncratic opportunities across a global opportunity set of traditional and alternative liquid asset classes. The 5 strategies are: Income, Compounders (the cornerstone strategies), Macro, Special Situations and Alternative Risk Premia (the de-correlating strategies). An important aim of the portfolio is to achieve true diversification by recognizing time and correlation as key diversifiers. Net exposure is dynamic and bond to the volatility budget. Hedging overlays via derivatives can be implemented to reduce risk, particularly in tail risk scenarios, to enhance alpha and to optimize convexity.

management_company_description: Boothbay manages two multi-PM hedge funds and selects and allocates capital to strategies and managers and is responsible for risk management at both the manager and funds level. Boothbay uses a combination of proprietary technology and qualitative judgment to target traditional and non-traditional sources of alpha by allocating capital across strategies with what we believe are idiosyncratic sources of return. Allocations are made through a managed account structure on the Fund’s own balance sheet, aimed at creating a number of alpha streams within a single product, whose whole is greater than the sum of its parts.
strategy_description:
BBARS seeks to generate absolute returns with low volatility and low correlations to traditional asset classes through all market conditions, while maintaining target portfolio level net exposure within (+/- 10%). Capital is deployed based on perceived portfolio manager edge, background, strategy, volatility and correlations to the market and to other strategies. Live aggregated data allows for Boothbay to dynamically allocate capital and manage risk, at both the manager and overall fund level. 

BBARS allocates via an ‘open architecture’ structure and has a focus on niche strategies. Allocations can also be made via what we believe to be a down side protected ‘first-loss’ capital allocation tool. 

BBARS believes in combining, what we believe are, non-correlated positive expectancy strategies into a cohesive portfolio, which we believe is further enhanced by operational and structural alphas. The fund attempts to optimize manager selection, allocation size, and concentrations through the use of its proprietary portfolio tool. The selection process involves customized terms and risk parameters for every strategy, and live, daily position-level transparency enables market neutral stance.

name: Verso Partners (Fund)
management_company_description:
Verso Partners is a short-focused equity fund managed by Josh Sweren, CFA, former Managing Director in the long-short equity group at Farallon Capital Management, and Michael Siliciano, former Partner at CPMG Inc. (Cardinal), a dedicated short equity fund.  Josh and Michael began their investing careers together as Analysts at Cardinal and have extensive experience collaborating on investments over the past 18 years.  The two have a combined 35 years of experience shorting stocks.  

Verso's goal is to generate exceptional alpha from a portfolio of equity shorts in a responsible and replicable manner across different market environments.  In addition to offering pure short exposure (in which case Verso serves as a true market hedge), Verso also offer its single name short book paired against an index long so that the fund runs market neutral or with a beta 1 (in which case Verso serves as an uncorrelated and differentiated source of alpha).  Verso runs a commingled ‘variable beta’ fund that gives LPs the flexibility to adjust the beta of their Verso exposure (from -100% net to +100% net).

name: Metacapital Mortgage Opportunities Fund
management_company_description:
Metacapital Management, L.P. (“Metacapital”) is an experienced absolute return manager specializing in MBS and structured credit. Founded in 2001 by Dr. Deepak Narula, a former Lehman Brothers Senior Trader and Head of Mortgage Strategy. Metacapital has a long track record of generating attractive risk-adjusted returns with low correlation to broad market indices. 

In addition to its flagship strategy, Metacapital has, on numerous occasions, identified special situations that provide exceptional attractive risk-reward opportunities. The most recent of these is the Carbon strategy that invests in California Carbon Allowances.
strategy_description:
The Metacapital Mortgage Opportunities Fund invests primarily in Mortgage Backed Securities (MBS) and derivatives associated with them that are issued by the US Housing Agencies (Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and Ginnie Mae).  This a multi-trillion dollar market whose liquidity is second only to US Treasuries.  Since these securities are guaranteed by the US Agencies, they are not exposed to the credit risk of the underlying borrower.  Instead, borrower's prepayment behavior is the main driver of returns. 

Investment thesis are expressed using a variety of strategies including long/short relative value within MBS, MBS versus Treasuries and long exposure to Interest Only (IO) and Principal Only (PO) securities.  

The Fund targets absolute returns and is managed duration neutral. By leveraging its expertise and understanding of prepayment trends, the Fund has been able to generate attractive returns with low correlations to broader market since inception in 2008.

name: DSC Meridian Dislocation Opportunities Fund
management_company_description: DSC Meridian Capital LP is an opportunistic, event-driven credit investment firm founded by Sheru Chowdhry, former Head of Credit Research and Co-PM of the Paulson Credit Fund (2004-2017). The strategy seeks to generate absolute returns through the credit cycle. DSC Meridian prioritizes principal protection, liquidity and shorting here at the top of the credit cycle, and then plans to shift portfolio focus to capital appreciation and equity-like upside at the bottom of the cycle. DSC Meridian invests both long and short, across small, mid and large-sized capital structures, and across the full spectrum of credit opportunities from performing, stressed and distressed credit (bankruptcy reorganizations, litigations, liquidations) to post re-organization/event-driven equities and capital structure arbitrage. The firm integrates material sustainability factors throughout the investment process and pursues an active corporate engagement strategy to help shape positive sustainability-related outcomes.
strategy_description: DSC Meridian’s Dislocation Opportunities Fund (DOF) soft launched in June 2025 with $245mm of anchor commitments. There will be a final close October 1, 2025. The vehicle is a series based, closed-end, drawdown Fund targeting distressed dislocations across bankruptcies, reorganizations and debt restructurings within small to mid-sized high yield and loan issuers. DOF’s objective is to target SOFR +1000bps return opportunities across 10-15 positions, per series.  Each series will have a 12-month investment period, followed by an 18-month harvest period. At the end of the investment period, LPs auto-roll into the next 12-mo series, allowing DOF to serve as a longer-term distressed allocation (LPs may elect to opt-out of the auto-roll feature).

strategy_description:
DSC Meridian Credit Opportunities Fund is an opportunistic credit fund focused on generating absolute returns across the credit cycle. The Fund will manage risk and portfolio positioning based on the credit cycle. We will invest up and down the capital structure and across the entire credit spectrum with a focus on North American and Western European opportunities. There are six keys areas of focus: 1) Performing Credit, 2) Stressed Credit, 3) Distressed Credit (work-outs, liquidations, litigations), 4) Post Re-org/Event-Driven Equities, 5) Capital Structure Arbitrage, and 6) High Conviction Shorts. 

Our Investment Approach Seeks to be:
Bottom Up: DSC Meridian utilizes bottom-up fundamental research to drive its investment decisions.  Specifically, DSC Meridian analyzes competitive dynamics and key drivers of revenue and margins, performing deep dive valuation with an emphasis on cash flow and asset coverage and understand capital structure, covenants and creditor incentives among other forms of analysis.

Opportunistic: DSC Meridian may invest opportunistically to capitalize on market inefficiencies from one-off dislocations to systemic market-moving events, embrace and exploit complex and misunderstood situations and invest in asymmetric events with multiple ways to win, cheap options and convex payoffs. 
Flexible: DSC Meridian may invest across the capital structure of an issuer, from senior secured bank debt to equity, depending on where DSC Meridian perceives the best risk-adjusted return.  Event Driven: DSC Meridian may invest in companies undergoing a corporate event, such as a bankruptcy, restructuring, covenant default, liquidity event, merger or LBO, etc.

name: Fortlake Sigma Opportunities Fund
management_company_description:
Fortlake Asset Management was established in late 2020 and founded by Dr Christian Baylis, who managed $10 billion at UBS and worked at the Reserve Bank of Australia before that. 

Fortlake is a global absolute return fixed income specialist. Fortlake uses a variety of silos to add value and reduce correlations to traditional asset classes, utilising its capability within the fixed income market. Fortlake is also regarded as a specialist in the default arbitrage market – a negative correlation market that actively harvests defaults across High yield and Investment grade markets in the US and Europe. 
 
Fortlake sets strategic priorities across its portfolios and reflects these via active tilts across the relevant silos in order to manage correlations and risk.  Fortlake then undertakes a detailed review of implementation strategies to make sure that risk is managed in a way that is commensurate with the Fund risk and return objectives. Each silo has its own factors and quantitative research process. The process seeks an optimal balance between risk and return using the silos as levers. Therefore the investment team’s main function is to constantly review the ex-ante risk environment, maintain balance with the silos/levers and update implementation, so as to maintain an optimal ex-ante portfolio.
strategy_description:
Return objective: Targets a minimum return of 7%-10% above the current US Effective Federal Funds Rate

The fund seeks the most compelling risk-adjusted return opportunities within global fixed income markets. The primary focus is to seek out market distortions, dislocations and distressed opportunities within the higher returning parts of the capital structure. Strict risk controls aim to provide strong capital protection.

management_company_description: Long Pond Capital, LP ("Long Pond" or the "Firm") is an investment management firm that specializes in real estate by employing a fundamental, bottom-up research process. The Firm was founded in 2010 by John Khoury, Managing Partner, who has been investing in real estate for over two decades. Mr. Khoury oversees all investment-related efforts and is supported by a team of experienced analysts. The Firm seeks to leverage its position as a real estate sector specialist to identify and exploit asymmetry, which it defines as a disconnect between price and intrinsic value. Long Pond is in its 16th year in business and believes its expertise, reputation, network, robust research process and specialized investment team provide it with a highly differentiated research funnel and viewpoint. This competitive advantage has resulted in a long-term track record that has substantially outperformed all major real estate indices. In addition to the Firm's flagship long/short product, Long Pond serves as sub-advisor to an actively managed long-only product.
strategy_description:
Long Pond manages a dedicated long/short equity strategy that focuses on fundamental investing in real estate and real estate-related companies. The investment team implements a rigorous, bottom-up research process across a broad investable universe to identify and exploit asymmetry, which it defines as a material disconnect between stock price and intrinsic value, in companies that it believes are misunderstood by the public markets. The investment team operates a well-defined and uniform coverage model whereby each analyst focuses on specific sub-sectors of the investable universe. The analysts have a deep knowledge of key industry trends, asset level valuations, company fundamentals as well as long-standing relationships with management teams. The firm endeavors to take a medium to long term view on investments and maintains a willingness to trade short-term volatility for medium to long-term returns. Opportunities are identified through a robust, multi-step research process and are typically evaluated based on the following investment criteria:

1. Is this security cheap (expensive)? 
2. Why is it cheap (expensive)? 
3. Why will it cease to be cheap (expensive)? 
4. What is the downside protection while the thesis plays out?

name: HonTe LH Macro Fund
management_company_description: HonTe Advisors, LLC is a Bay Area, discretionary global macro investment firm that focuses on long-horizon, thematic, multi-asset class investing across developed and emerging markets. Our objective is to construct a superior portfolio, which creates a revenue stream uncorrelated to traditional assets. We employ formal logic in conjunction with a rule-based trade selection process to capitalize on relative mis-pricing of global assets.
strategy_description:
Firm History: Founded in 2015 by Alex Gurevich CIO and Christopher Lutton CEO, CCO
Area of Expertise: Global Macro (discretionary)
Products: Macro products including FI, FX, Commodities, and Equities

Management & Organization Structure
Internal - Team of 7 includes, Alex Gurevich (CIO), Qin Zhu (COO & CRO), Joann Shie-Chen (Operations), Chris Kelley (Trading), Kushan Balasooriya (Controller), Jessica Carvin (Investor Relations), Melanie Jordan (Office Manager). All senior members traded through the last two market cycles and worked together for over 15years. Alex earned his PhD in mathematics from the U. of Chicago and ran the macro book at JP Morgan from 2002-2007 with a verified track for US dollar p/l >$500m. 
External – We have two very experienced professionals to serve on our advisory committee to the master fund & as directors of the offshore feeder - Josh Barlow, Valhalla (prior head of ODD at PAAMCO) & Yolanda Banks, HighWater (former head of Inv & Securities at CIMA)

Investment Strategy
Current Outlook: As the late-cycle transition consistent with 2000 and 2007 has been completed and we have capitalized on directional rates bets, a more nuanced approach to trading the yield curve will be critical. Alex leverages his fixed income derivatives expertise and experience trading over the previous three easing cycles to source opportunities while running a balanced portfolio. 
Strategy: Our investment strategy is "long-horizon" w/ particularly long holding periods (>1yr) relative to our macro peers which allows us to trade dislocations that others can't. Our success stems from trade selection & scoring, optimization, and quant risk mgmt.

Investment Process and Philosophy
Alex wrote a book in 2014 that explores in detail his trade selection & portfolio construction process. Since the book was published in '14, our investment workflow continues to evolve with greater focus on risk management and portfolio optimization techniques to address the needs of institutional investors. While the strategy is fully "discretionary" there is material assistance from quant tools & we intend to continue building out these capabilities. 

Our philosophy on fees is in line with our long-term vision in everything we do. By employing an "OR" fee model, we achieve best alignment with investors, focusing on long-term performance rather than management fees.

Operational Capabilities
While we have an extensive performance record to highlight, we are also proud of the build-out of our operational infrastructure over the past four years which has included an up-tiering of our external partners along the way. In this highly competitive fundraising environment, we have benefited greatly from strong internal funding and a l-term vision. 

We currently have the internal and external teams in place to grow our macro fund through institutional investor capital. Our target raise is $500m AUM in our Founder's share class with a total fund capacity in all our share classes up to $3billion AUM.

name: Tyrus Capital Global Alpha Fund
management_company_description: Tyrus Capital is a leading special situations investment manager founded in 2009. Tyrus Capital invests across the capital structure, in both public and private markets. The Firm seems to achieve uncorrelated returns through asymmetric risk/reward investments, structured with limited downside risk and upside optionality.. Tyrus Capital manages assets for institutional investors globally with offices in Monaco, Barcelona, Madrid and Abu Dhabi.
strategy_description:
Launched in August 2021, Global Alpha is an open-ended fund which focuses on exploiting the inefficiencies that occur in the secondary private equity market and today encompasses a fully funded, mature, diversified and cash generative portfolio w.

Based on our 12-year track record and over $1bn deployed, this fund has been structured to allow seamless re-cycling of proceeds and thereby targeting quick compounding of returns. In addition to the underlying fund performance, new investors could benefit from the initial valuation uplift at entry as a result of discounts achieved on new opportunities. Investors can subscribe on a monthly basis and have a semi-annual redemption option via a liquidating class of interests.

The Global Alpha Fund offers many features including:
- Asymmetric risk-return profile through a diversified portfolio with downside protection
- Extracting alpha by acquiring mature and cash generative assets at attractive discounts (historical average of 20%)
- Compounding of returns through high investment velocity (approx. 20% of portfolio monetized and reinvested annually)
- Access to short duration investment opportunities frequently facing less competition, targeting attractive cash returns
- Flexibility for investors to size their exposure through a monthly subscription option and a semi-annual redemption feature through a liquidating class

Scope of address:
o	JPM accepted making a deletion with respect to the funds – for Tyrus it was preferable to make clear it is the Management Company that is party to the services – under the understanding that when the agreement is accepted by the entities, it is accepted by the funds by implication. Liability:
o	“You agree that in the absence of fraud, negligence or willful default” which Tyrus added in their initial markup of the document – Tyrus believes that specifically “fraud” is not something that can be “carved out” and potentially “willful default” too. Tyrus appreciates JP Morgan is not receiving a fee as part of these services, but they would like to make absolute certain that JPM have not carved out their responsibility with respect to legal matters, and anyway are asking for a high threshold.
o	JPM accepted adding "gross" negligence: Tyrus has advised: "In terms of threshold of liability, I note that you have included fraud and wilful misconduct as exclusions to the limitation, but have deleted negligence. While (as discussed) we can understand why you would not want to be held to that standard in these particular circumstances, I should be very grateful if you would reconsider this point and, as a compromise, agree to “gross negligence”, which is a pretty high bar anyway. This is quite important to us, bearing in mind the fact that our headquarters (whilst in Europe) are not within the EU and that many of our Funds are Cayman Islands based, therefore we have to operate within quite tight restrictions. We are certain that JP Morgan operates and will operate with the highest standard in any event, so this should be just a formality."

management_company_description:
Cheyne Capital was founded in 2000 by Jonathan Lourie (CEO) and Stuart Fiertz (President) after working together at Morgan Stanley. 

Cheyne is one of Europe's leading alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs) with c. 170 partners and employees.

Cheyne invests across the capital structure from the senior debt to the equity of corporates and real estate. With an investment philosophy grounded in rigorous fundamental analysis, the firm’s main areas of expertise are: Real Estate Debt, Corporate Credit and Risk Transfer, European Strategic Value Credit, and Liquid Alternatives.
strategy_description:
The Cheyne SVC Hybrid Credit Fund seeks to capitalise on an observable funding gap that exists within the European non-sponsored lending market, providing bespoke financing solutions to support the development capital needs of predominantly family-owned and founder-led mid-market enterprises which are structurally underserved by banks and traditional (sponsor-led) direct lending funds.

The fund focuses on the provision of flexible capital to support business expansion, where shareholders express a strong preference for a debt-based solution as an alternative to dilutive equity capital. The strategy emphasises downside risk mitigation and loss avoidance, with a focus on first lien secured lending with upside participation.
region_exposure_description: The portfolio maintains a strong European focus (UK & Ireland, Spain, France, Germany/DACH, Nordics, Benelux and Italy), capitalising on the continent’s divergent economic trajectories and the complexity of its cultural, linguistic, and legal frameworks. management_company_description:
VOLORIDGE INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT, LLC is a private fund manager founded in 2009 by David Vogel, an award winning predictive modeling scientist. Our mission is to deliver superior risk-adjusted returns for qualified investors using proprietary modeling technology and risk management.

Our approach to investment management is based on three pillars: 
     • We are a quantitative shop, focused on applying mathematics and technology to exploit alpha opportunities
     • We scale capacity conservatively, with a goal towards maximixing investor returns.
     • We approach investment management with the goal of building a long-term track record 

We continue to assemble a talented team of individuals that are seeking to be a part of an entrepreneurial minded investment management firm. Our team is committed to building long term performance and we nurture this commitment with every opportunity.

strategy_description: The Voloridge Trading Aggressive Fund, LP (“VTAF” or the “Fund”) seeks to deliver absolute returns in various market environments by investing in VTAF Master, L.P. ("VTAFM"). VTAFM invests in US listed equities and global futures with minimal correlation to the S&P 500 Index. Proprietary predictive modeling technology drives the quantitative approach for each strategy. The strategies utilize sophisticated risk models to optimize liquidity, correlation, volatility, and beta exposure. The portfolio is actively managed with a relatively short-term holding period. Generally, between equities and futures, the program will hold in excess of 2000 securities. Monthly correlation to the S&P 500 Index has been close to zero and is expected to remain close to zero. The Fund is expected to experience a volatility range of approximately 15% to 30% on a gross basis going forward. The program is available through onshore and offshore feeder funds, but is currently at its capital raising target.

management_company_description: Founded in 2013 by Eric Peters, One River Asset Management is an investment manager that aims to deliver high-conviction absolute-return strategies that help our clients build superior portfolios. We see the world in a period of major economic and political transition, with the investment landscape shifting in ways that will make the coming five years look profoundly different from the past five. Each is developed and managed in-house by our team of investment professionals with expertise in volatility and systematic trading/investing. The strategy combines these strategies into one integrated vehicle and deploys additional leverage to each sleeve, with the intention of providing robust risk mitigation in both market crises (Dynamic Convexity) as well as during prolonged risk asset declines or macro asset regime shifts (Trend).

strategy_description:
Itaú Multi Strategy fund is a Macro Discretionary, Multi-Strategy, Multi-PM fund with a focus on Emerging Markets. The Fund's objective is to achieve double digit returns with no structural correlation to equities and bonds, exploring opportunities in Emerging Markets through uncorrelated portfolio managers and strategies with different investment processes and geographic focus.

There is a monthly committee meeting to determine rebalancing and allocations to each pod, during which both qualitative and quantitative variables are used. First, the Quantitative Portfolio Optimization (OQPA) model identifies the optimal allocation by evaluating performance, risk utilization, correlation, and drawdown metrics for each strategy. Second, a qualitative evaluation process complements the OQPA by incorporating discussions on trading concepts, risk management, position sizing, and style drift, derived from daily interactions among Itaú Multi-Strategy Platform stakeholders to improve our allocation efficiency. There is no macro-overlay and each team operates with full discretion, encouraging independent decision-making and avoiding groupthink. This rigorous and consolidated process ensures that capital allocation is systematic and incorporates qualitative inputs, designed to minimize potential bias from past performance and enhance our comprehensive understanding of current circumstances.

As a Macro Discretionary Platform focused on Emerging Markets, we have a robust economic research department. Our team supports investment decisions with forecasts, live economic indicator coverage, model development, and access to central bankers and world-class consultants, especially in Latin America and G-10.
Risk management is a core element, with our platform built on a daily NAV regime. We manage intraday liquidity, exposure, and PnL control, setting VaR and stress limits for each pod and the entire fund. Additionally, we apply drawdown limits for each pod.

Operations and Trading are fundamental components of our platform, facilitating over 10,000 trades executed daily across more than 50 countries. We maintain front-to-back integration with prominent market participants and have established relationships with five leading prime brokers. Trading is also responsible for ensuring best execution, fair allocation, and implementing trade surveillance programs.

name: The Kintbury Equity Fund
management_company_description:
Kintbury is research driven fundamental LS equity firm focused exclusively on European equities with a market cap over $3bn. Chris Dale, CIO, has a track record of running capital for over 20 years and focused on European equities for over 30 years. We are a generalist fund but and have a proprietary accounting lens. We hold our longs on average for 2-3 years and shorts 12-18 months.  The strategy aims to combine fundamental long-term company analysis with a low net to the market and a pragmatic risk management approach.  The investment philosophy of the firm is that the consensus is too focused on the short term and real value is generated in long term analysis.  By minimizing the market exposure and with the stock picking process driven by micro rather than macro factors the returns should be driven by idiosyncratic single stock risk.
The portfolio will typically have up to 25-35 long and 40-50 short positions. The net exposure is up to +/-20% on a cash and beta adjusted basis but over time the returns are expected to be driven predominantly by alpha generation on the long and short side of the portfolio, rather than by beta exposure.  We see ourselves as an all-weather fund and have demonstrated this by our alpha split on longs and shorts since inception.
The team is 8 on the investment side and 14 in total.
strategy_description: The Kintbury Equity Fund was launched on May 1, 2015. The fund invests in developed European equities with a market cap greater than $3bn. The aim of the strategy is to build a book that maximizes idiosyncratic stock risk and simultaneously aims to minimize all other risks to an acceptable level. Chris Dale is the founder and portfolio manager, he has 20 years of European equity experience 18 of those as a portfolio manager, including 9 years at Millennium in London, where along with his partner, he was responsible for one of the largest equity books at the firm. name: Shenkman Opportunistic Credit Master Fund LP
exact_name: Shenkman Opportunistic Credit Master Fund LP
management_company_description:
Shenkman is a stable asset manager, with no significant changes in organizational structure since our inception in 1985 other than expanding our employee ownership. We believe that asset manager independence is critical to remain focused on our fiduciary responsibility to our clients. It is our strong corporate belief that too many asset management firms pursue mergers, acquisitions and public offerings, which can distract the principals from their investment activities and fiduciary responsibilities to their clients. As such, we remain independent and will continue to offer senior team members the opportunity to become shareholders of the firm.

The firm is recognized as a pioneer in the leveraged finance market. Over its history, Shenkman has consistently and methodically evolved with the ever-changing market landscape, industry technology and growing client needs. This evolution has included the creation of alternative total return-oriented product offerings, the addition of experienced team members with a diverse set of backgrounds and skill sets, the creation of a global presence and the continual enhancement of our operational systems and analytical tools.

The history of Shenkman can be divided into six phases:

Phase I: 1985-1994 – Established Infrastructure - In Phase I, Shenkman established and developed its unique credit methodology, recruited a core senior team, and laid the foundation for the systems capabilities necessary for portfolio oversight. 

We developed two key proprietary tools: the C.Scope® credit scoring system and Quadrant Analysis — which were both created as part of our rigorous credit research process. Shenkman has been managing high yield bond portfolios since its founding in 1985.

Phase II: 1995-1999 – Solidifying Track Record - In Phase II, Shenkman broadened its marketing efforts. A nine-year performance record established Shenkman as a premier high yield money manager and enabled it to market its investment management services to consultants and plan sponsors. During this time, 15 new team members were added, including a general counsel, a controller and four analysts. In 1998, our leveraged loan strategy was launched.

Phase III:  2000-2004 – Rapid Growth - In Phase III, Shenkman commenced a concerted effort to advise public pension funds, foundations, endowments, and insurance companies. Shenkman continued to reinvest in its business by opening a second office in Stamford, Connecticut and adding additional resources throughout the firm. 

Phase IV:  2005-2012 – New Product Initiatives and International Expansion - In Phase IV, Shenkman extended its high yield product offerings. Leveraging off the breadth of its credit research platform, Shenkman began to offer convertibles in 2005 and short duration high yield and multi-asset credit (“MAC”) in 2010. All these strategies were established as separate products to meet client demands for solutions across the leveraged finance sector. Shenkman also embarked on a strategy to broaden its international client base. 

To that end, we opened a London office to service our existing and future clients in Europe and hired a third-party marketer in Australia to seize new opportunities. Additionally, Shenkman partnered with a major Japanese financial institution to offer Shenkman’s short duration high yield strategy in a fund offered exclusively to Japanese institutional investors. 

Phase V: 2013-2019 – Strengthening of Leveraged Loan/CLO Strategies, Launch of Alternative Strategies - In Phase V, Shenkman began a focused effort to deepen our leveraged loan and CLO platforms. As a result, we hired David Lerner in 2013 from Credit Suisse’s Credit Investments Group to lead these efforts. We also hired Matt Shepard in 2014 from Lord, Abbett & Co. as a Portfolio Manager for our structured credit capabilities. Subsequent to David and Matt’s hires, in 2014, we launched a structured credit strategy, investing in third-party managers’ CLO debt and equity. 

Furthermore, with the addition of Justin Slatky in 2011 and Ned Oakley in 2016, Shenkman expanded its opportunistic and tactical credit capabilities, culminating in the launch of an opportunistic credit fund focused on event driven situations across the corporate credit spectrum in 2018 and a closed-end tactical credit fund focused on similar, but less liquid, investments in 2019. Both of these funds are co-managed by Justin and Ned.

Phase VI: 2020 to Present – Investment in Infrastructure – In Phase VI, the firm accelerated efforts to bolster its infrastructure in support of its evolution from traditional, long-only investing to a fully integrated traditional and alternative credit manager. This transition has entailed substantial enhancements of analytical tools (particularly those focusing on quantitative metrics), improvements to data management systems, upgraded cybersecurity, more robust integration of our ESG analytics, an increased commitment to diversity and inclusion, and key team member additions and appointments (e.g., a newly-appointed CIO, a new CFO with extensive hedge fund expertise, a new Chief Risk Officer with alternative credit experience, and a newly-appointed Global Head of Business Development & Investor Relations who has been with the firm for several years).

In addition, after 27 years in the same location, we moved our New York City headquarters to a new, state-of-the-art building located at 151 West 42nd Street. Our new office building, which was recognized as the nation’s first “green skyscraper” after its completion in 1999, offers upgraded facilities and amenities and accommodates any plans for future growth. In addition, we opened a satellite office in Boca Raton, FL.
strategy_description:
Our analytical process includes using our proprietary tools to analyze historical and projected operating performance and trends, including liquidity, cash flow, and a working capital analysis. We believe this process is essential to properly manage the inherently higher credit risk associated with below investment-grade assets.

Our investment philosophy for our alternative strategies (including our Opportunistic Credit strategy) is based on fundamental, bottom-up research and understanding of capital structure and market dynamics. We seek to take advantage of the deep, bottom-up fundamental credit analysis used in our traditional credit strategies to evaluate investment opportunities that could have a higher risk/return profile or more complex capital structure opportunities than our traditional credit strategies. While deep credit analysis is at the core of our investment philosophy, assessing relative value amongst potential investments in the market can also be an important component to trades we implement using longs and shorts.

Specific to the Opportunistic Credit strategy, Shenkman allows its seasoned investment staff to fully express their credit opinions unencumbered by the Firm’s traditional, income-oriented style. Investments include, but are not limited to, those credits subjected to the Shenkman research process that do not fit our traditional, income-oriented style, but offer attractive total returns. These investments are in the themes of market transition, capital arbitrage long/shorts, stressed credit, catalyst-driven long or short, restructuring/deep value, and liquidations. We believe these six investment themes can provide opportunities for compelling risk-adjusted returns. The Portfolio Managers adjust exposure to these broad categories throughout the market cycle.

Investment Strategy: 
The Shenkman Opportunistic Credit Master Fund LP (the “Fund”) focuses on event-driven opportunities, typically in underfollowed, liquid credits that suit one of six investment themes: Market Transition, Capital Arbitrage Long/Shorts, Stressed Credit, Catalyst-Driven Long or Short, Restructuring/Deep Value, and Liquidations. We believe these themes can provide investment opportunities for compelling risk-adjusted returns throughout a full market cycle by calibrating exposures based on current and near-term market conditions. 

The Fund generally targets companies in the $500mm to $3.0bn total debt range, which represents over half of the combined high yield bond, leveraged loan, and convertible bond markets and seeks to exploit pricing inefficiencies across these markets. These inefficiencies can arise from a number of factors, including overall market technicals, government intervention, credit valuations, rating changes, and misinterpreted industry dynamics. 

The Fund’s objective is to generate low double-digit returns through active rotation of portfolio exposures across the different thematics as the market cycle evolves. Underpinning these thematic portfolio allocation shifts is our bottom-up credit research process, which has been tested over multiple market cycles. This process enables us to repeatedly identify trades in the targeted themes and to evaluate their upside/downside potential.

name: Marek Mosaic Fund
management_company_description:
Marek Capital is an alternative investment manager that looks beyond surface-level econometrics, delving deep into the inner workings of the financial system and consumer behavior to uncover overlooked opportunities. 

Marek specializes in thematic and relative value multi-strategy investing across mortgages, rates, structured credit, corporate credit, and related equities within a rigorous risk framework. 

Marek Capital is co-founded by Matthew Cherwin, former Chief Investment Officer and Treasurer of JP Morgan, and Derek Goodman, former Managing Partner of Autonomy Capital.
strategy_description:
Marek Capital employs a specialized approach to thematic and relative value investing across mortgages, rates, structured credit, corporate credit and related equities utilizing a rigorous risk framework. 

Marek’s Investment Strategy: 

At the core of Marek's investment process are two key elements: (1) a distinctive understanding of the forces of the financial system - Money, Capital, Credit, Liquidity and Regulation ("MCCLR") - that drive economies, markets, and prices, and (2) a knowledge base and investment process that amplifies our ability to capitalize on opportunities arising from market mispricings and investor misunderstandings of critical intersections and gaps in information, pricing, and value across markets and securities.

Investment Process

* CIO, Matt Cherwin, leads our investment team investing across assets, capital structures, and securities

* Top-Down: Marek's macroeconomic analysis - driven by our MCCLRTM framework - seeks to go beyond headline econometrics delving deep into the inner 
   workings of the global financial and banking systems and consumer behavior to identify high conviction investment themes

* Bottoms-up: Precise fundamental research, quantitative analysis, and security selection derives the best expression of the thematic views and relative value 
   opportunities

* Position and portfolio are constructed seeking to limit downside and add convexity wherever possible

* Robust risk management process operates within a well-defined framework seeking to improve returns while reducing risk


A few of Marek's investment strategy differentiators are:

Expertise: Matt's tenure as JP Morgan's CIO & Treasurer endowed him with a differentiated understanding of the global banking and financial system, particularly the dynamics of Money, Credit, Capital, Liquidity, and Regulation ("MCCLR"). Significant regime shifts are currently reshaping financial markets, driven by transformations in our "Big 5" - Money, Capital, Credit, Liquidity, and Regulation (MCCLR). The MCCLR framework forms the foundation of our top-down lens and informs our perspectives on monetary policy, real estate, consumer behavior, banking, and regulatory developments. With over 20 years of experience in dissecting and trading securities and capital structures, Matt seeks to equip Marek with a distinct edge in deciphering macroeconomic trends and capitalizing on regularly misunderstood fundamentals and their impact on market and securities mispricings.

Differentiated Approach: Marek's strength lies in our ability to connect the dots across mortgage, rates, and structured and corporate credit markets. Our strategy integrates Matt's "top-down" expertise in global financial systems with precision bottom-up security analysis by our PM teams, with the goal of producing better investment decisions and superior trade structuring, enhancing returns and reducing risk. Our collaborative culture keeps everyone in sync and connects the dots, driving real-time capital allocation and risk management, aiming to give us a distinct advantage in seizing opportunities and managing risk.
