strategy_description:
The PSquared Credit Opportunity Fund is an unconstrained long/short credit strategy that targets uncorrelated double-digit net returns. 
•	The strategy aims to deliver this by profiting from valuation dislocations that are caused by structural inefficiencies in global credit markets, and deploys an opportunistic approach that can invest across a broad-spectrum of credit and related instruments. 
•	Starting in 2023, several tweaks were made to the strategy, including replacing the previous Portfolio Manager with Lino Schaus (ex-Centerbridge).

The strategy is distinguished from L/S Credit HF peers due to: 

(1) its focus on event-driven situations (e.g. mergers & acquisitions, debt refinancings, accounting red flags for shorts) which leads to excess returns that are primarily driven by idiosyncratic, rather than market factors; and 
(2) the depth of the Firm’s experienced investment team of industry, accounting and product specialists with diverse geographic backgrounds that assists in navigating the fragmented European market, the core focus region of the strategy.

management_company_description:

Strategies range from credit funds covering major US and European markets with AUM of $6.7bn, through a CLO platform with $17.7bn under management and Real Asset Strategies managing $1.7bn of capital. strategy_description:
The Deep Value Credit Fund III (the “Fund”) is a contingent capital, drawdown vehicle which seeks to maximize absolute returns within credit markets following the next market dislocation. The Fund is focused on investments in non-IG public credit across the US and Europe and Structured, Index, Derivative and Single Name products. It is also the segment of credit which we believe is prone to more frequent and deep market corrections due to liquidity interruptions, something which has become a feature of these markets since a secular change of these markets post-GFC. It is these corrections that can lead to highly attractive return opportunities in periods following dislocations. 

Capital is drawn upon a determination by the Fund’s Portfolio Manager that investments can generate a 15%+ net multi-year return threshold being met, under stress case scenarios. As a result, the investment strategy is designed with the objective of achieving strong double digit annualized net returns to investors over a multi-year period. Positions will be sold or realized during the harvesting period as liquidity conditions improve and asset prices normalize.

Napier Park's track record managing this strategy is demonstrated through predecessor funds. Deep Value I drew capital upon the onset of Covid-19 generating 57.1% Net IRR and 1.59x MOIC. Deep Value II began drawing capital at the end of 2022 and generated a 28.0% ITD Net IRR and 1.26x MOIC.

Please note Deep Value Credit Fund III has not yet launched and is currently fundraising. 

Refer to the Fund Disclaimer for details on the Return Trigger and prior performance.

Combining bottom up, fundamental credit analysis with structural analysis and active value creation on CLO level, while active hedging program aims to reduce correlation and mitigate volatility. 

The strategy targets equity-like returns of ~14%-16% p.a. net IRR, and has performed well relative to private debt and global equities on a since inception basis. 

Strategy highlights include 1) Flexibility to Capitalize on Entire CLO Universe: Sourcing CLO Equity from European and US primary and secondary markets, with flexibility to add opportunistic CLO mezzanine exposure 2) Reduced Volatility: Focus on mitigating risk via active hedges and shorts 3) Low Correlation: Exhibited a low correlation to traditional fixed income and equities products

Past performance is no guarantee of future results.  Actual results may vary. Please refer to the Fund Disclaimer for important information on the Return Objective and historical performance.

management_company_description:
Divisadero Street Partners, LP is a Miami-based hedge fund launched in October 2021. The firm employs a long/short equity strategy with a small-and-mid-cap focus and low net exposure, aiming to compound and protect capital in all market conditions. The catalyst-driven research process, rooted in fundamental  analysis, identifies both long and short opportunities with a focus on asymmetric risk/reward.

Led by William Zolezzi, CFA, with 10+ year buyside experience, the fund takes an active short-selling approach, viewing its short book as a profit center rather than a hedge.  

A substantial portion of the PM’s net worth is invested in the fund, reinforcing alignment with investors.

Strategies range from credit funds covering major US and European markets with AUM of $6.7bn, through a CLO platform with $17.7bn under management and Real Asset Strategies managing $1.7bn of capital. strategy_description:
Napier Park Value Credit Fund (the “Fund”) pursues an opportunistic strategy which invests across a broad range of credit markets and collateral types, in both private and public instruments. The Fund seeks to extract the complexity and illiquidity premium which has been created by the secular change in these credit markets following the Global Financial Crisis. The assets targeted by the Fund are higher returning, performing credit, typically with multiple structural features and exit options to provide downside protection. Napier Park’s differentiated proposition is a sophisticated ability to source, analyze, value and risk-manage complex and structured non-investment grade instruments, combined with fundamental credit underwriting, a commitment to diversification and an active management style. The Fund seeks to generate a 12-14% Net IRR and 1.5-2.0x Net MOIC over an expected 5-year term.

Napier Park held a first close of the Value Credit Fund on August 1, 2024.  The fund will remain open to new investors over a 1-year expected fundraising period. 

Please refer to the Fund Disclaimer for details on the Return Target.

strategy_description:
Please note Napier Park is currently fundraising for Deep Value Credit Fund III. Deep Value Credit Fund II is matured and all investor capital has been returned as of year end 2024.

The Deep Value Credit Fund II (the “Fund”) is Napier Park's second series contingent capital, drawdown vehicle which seeks to maximize absolute returns within credit markets following the next market dislocation. The Fund is focused on investments in non-IG public credit across the US and Europe and Structured, Index, Derivative and Single Name products. It is also the segment of credit which we believe is prone to more frequent and deep market corrections due to liquidity interruptions, something which has become a feature of these markets since a secular change of these markets post-GFC. It is these corrections that can lead to highly attractive return opportunities in periods following dislocations. 

Capital is drawn upon a determination by the Fund’s Portfolio Manager that investments can generate a 15%+ net multi-year return threshold being met, under stress case scenarios. As a result, the investment strategy is designed with the objective of achieving strong double digit annualized net returns to investors over a multi-year period. Positions will be sold or realized during the harvesting period as liquidity conditions improve and asset prices normalize.

Napier Park's track record managing this strategy is demonstrated through predecessor funds. Deep Value I drew capital upon the onset of Covid-19 generating 57.1% Net IRR and 1.59x MOIC. Deep Value II generated a 28.2% Net IRR and 1.26x MOIC (Jan 2023 - Dec 2024).

Please refer to the Fund Disclaimer for information on the Return Trigger and historical performance.

strategy_description:

The Firm relies on quantitative techniques to analyse historical data and statistics, with the goal of predicting returns to develop trading strategies. The Firm seeks to differentiate itself from its peers by deploying techniques that it considers to be innovative (such as "price-insensitive flow analysis" and "macro-informed quantitative equity systems") as part of its trading strategy development. The Firm's proprietary trading strategies will be implemented subject to strict portfolio guidelines aimed at managing risk. The Firm endeavours to manage risk via diversification over many strategies intended to capture alpha and through the use of quantitative models. The Firm strives to construct a portfolio that is balanced and comprised of numerous trading strategies that we believe will yield uncorrelated returns to the market and other commons sources of risk.

Our goal is to generate profitable returns in most market conditions. We also feel that our strategy will produce lower returns when price-insensitive market participants are less active and/or a lower relative share of market activity.

name: Vector Velocity Fund
management_company_description:
Vector Capital spun out of Ziff Brothers Investments, a family investment firm, in 1997. Vector Capital's mission is to create start-up momentum for existing technology companies. The firm typically invests in bootstrapped companies, spin-outs from larger corporations, consolidators of industries, or public companies undergoing significant change. Vector's main sector focus is on communications infrastructure, enterprise software and technology-enabled services.

The firm is based in San Francisco and manages approximately $4.1 billion as of June 30, 2022. Vector Capital has 47 employees, of which 29 are investment professionals. We have a Blue Chip investor base that includes a significant number of the nation’s top endowments & foundations, pension plans and family offices.

Given that technology is a fast-growing and ever-more-important part of the economy, we have developed a number of strategies (credit hedge fund and private equity) that will allow investors to smartly access this sector and capitalize upon the differentiated skill of a dedicated specialist with extensive experience. The tech sector, like healthcare and to some extent energy, is a sector where managers with distinct experience and skill have demonstrated the ability to persistently extract alpha. Many of our investment team members have deep functional technology experience and expertise and possess a true passion for this industry; hence, we understand the intricacies of the technology marketplace as practitioners, not merely investors, providing us a distinct advantage relative to many investors. We also benefit from having both credit and equity teams, as we are able to find interesting opportunities across various capital structures, thereby allowing us the ability to enhance return while carefully managing risk. Whether investing in credit or equity, our investment team applies a deep value-focused approach when considering any investment.

Vector’s investment team is comprised of seasoned technology investors with deep domain expertise. The team’s diversity of skills allows them to quickly analyze complex situations, develop detailed action plans and implement them.
strategy_description:
Vector Capital and its affiliates have been pursuing credit investment strategies since 2008.  In so doing, Vector Capital seeks to leverage the skill set, technology industry background and intellectual capital of Vector Capital’s established private equity and credit platform, and to benefit from Vector Capital’s extensive resources, including proprietary sourcing relationships, infrastructure and operations support, as well as a thorough investment due diligence process.

Vector Capital’s Special Situations Private Credit Fund (the “Fund”) will focus on investing in directly originated senior secured loans to lower middle market companies in the Technology and Tech-enabled ecosystem serving a diverse set of end markets. These are loans made to companies that are undergoing a significant change or experiencing transitional situations, as well as companies seeking capital for operating, acquisition, expansion, recapitalization or refinancing. The investment objective of the Fund is to seek attractive risk-adjusted total returns by structuring flexible and customized financing solutions tailored to the unique characteristics of technology companies. 

The Fund will generally hold 15-25 investments at any given time, ranging from ~$25M - $60M in size. The portfolio will be comprised of predominantly senior secured loans and to a lesser extent unitranche or mezzanine financings, primarily with floating rate structures.

We identify new investments by seeking out unique opportunities that arise from events such as lack of access to traditional capital sources, desire to take non-dilutive capital, desire to transition from growth to profit, spin-offs or divestitures. In many of these special situations, traditional collateral may not be readily available or valuable. Therefore, the Fund may focus on assets that are not typically considered as collateral, such as intellectual property, brand value, contractual cash flows, or other unique assets. This strategy requires specialized expertise to assess and price these non-traditional forms of collateral. In doing so, we provide tailored financing structures to meet the specific needs of the companies we lend to. This may include structuring debt instruments with flexible repayment terms, customized ARR to EBITDA covenants, unique call protection and variable interest rates. Lastly, many of these companies are also looking for operational support from our extensive network of affiliates and executives who can help navigate the unique challenges these businesses face. These customized solutions allow the Fund to mitigate risk and enhance potential returns resulting in a portfolio of loans that typically have attractive economics, lender friendly credit protections, and attractive loan-to-values (“LTV”).

Our investment decisions are based on a deep understanding of the sectors in which we invest, and our sourcing infrastructure is augmented by the assets and expert relationships of the broader enterprise. Given the complexity and inherent risks associated with special situations investments, the Fund conducts extensive due diligence before making an investment. This includes a thorough analysis of the company's financials, industry dynamics, management team, legal and regulatory considerations, and an assessment of potential risks and rewards. 

Vector’s credit team takes an active approach to managing our clients’ investments. This involves close collaboration with company management to support the transition from growth to profitability, operational improvements, financial restructuring, or strategic initiatives. As a part of our approach, our investment will frequently augment the board or executive team with Vector relationships that are uniquely qualified to add operational expertise.

esg_approach_description:
Vinci Partners believes that responsible corporate behavior from Environmental, Social and Corporate Governance (ESG) perspectives has a direct positive impact on the performance of its investments, reducing risk and generating long-term value, as well as being part of its fiduciary duty. Vinci Equities’ ESG integration process in asset valuation is based on four main elements:
1. Transversality: The evaluation of ESG issues occurs in parallel with the Fund’s regular investment
process, led by research analysts and managers, based on proprietary methodology.
2. Proportionality: In-depth analysis of ESG concerns occurs only for topics that the manager
considers relevant in terms of impact on the value of the assets it holds. In addition, the
integration of ESG considerations in its investments must respect the particularities of the
different Equities funds that Vinci manages.
3. Relevance: Asset evaluation from an ESG perspective will focus on those assets that are relevant
to Vinci’s portfolio and investment universe. No asset is excluded from the investment universe
based solely on ESG issues, except in cases of explicit requests from clients with exclusive
mandates, and which are foreseen within the Fund’s general documentation.

management_company_description:
Vector Capital spun out of Ziff Brothers Investments, a family investment firm, in 1997. Vector Capital's mission is to create start-up momentum for existing technology companies. The firm typically invests in bootstrapped companies, spin-outs from larger corporations, consolidators of industries, or public companies undergoing significant change. Vector's main sector focus is on communications infrastructure, enterprise software and technology-enabled services.

The firm is based in San Francisco and manages approximately $4.1 billion as of June 30, 2022. Vector Capital has 47 employees, of which 29 are investment professionals. We have a Blue Chip investor base that includes a significant number of the nation’s top endowments & foundations, pension plans and family offices.

Given that technology is a fast-growing and ever-more-important part of the economy, we have developed a number of strategies (credit hedge fund and private equity) that will allow investors to smartly access this sector and capitalize upon the differentiated skill of a dedicated specialist with extensive experience. The tech sector, like healthcare and to some extent energy, is a sector where managers with distinct experience and skill have demonstrated the ability to persistently extract alpha. Many of our investment team members have deep functional technology experience and expertise and possess a true passion for this industry; hence, we understand the intricacies of the technology marketplace as practitioners, not merely investors, providing us a distinct advantage relative to many investors. We also benefit from having both credit and equity teams, as we are able to find interesting opportunities across various capital structures, thereby allowing us the ability to enhance return while carefully managing risk. Whether investing in credit or equity, our investment team applies a deep value-focused approach when considering any investment.

Vector’s investment team is comprised of seasoned technology investors with deep domain expertise. The team’s diversity of skills allows them to quickly analyze complex situations, develop detailed action plans and implement them.
strategy_description:
Vector Capital and its affiliates have been pursuing credit investment strategies since 2008. In so doing Vector Capital seeks to leverage the skill set, technology industry background and intellectual capital of Vector Capital’s established private equity organization, and to benefit from Vector Capital’s extensive resources, including proprietary sourcingrelationships, infrastructure and operations support, as well as a thorough investment due diligence process.

VCCO provides investors access to a diverse technology credit portfolio. The strategy focuses on low volatility credit investments, generating returns through current income and capital appreciation, often crystallized through event driven situations. We identify investment opportunities by conducting thorough, fundamental and bottom-up due diligence of the securities of companies we believe are experiencing a dislocation in value due to complex, misunderstood events and situations which can be researched and analyzed. Our investment decisions are based on a deep understanding of the sectors in which we invest, and our sourcing infrastructure is augmented by the assets and relationships of the broader enterprise. As part of Vector Capital, the credit strategy has significant access to industry expertise and operations support to assist in portfolio management.

The investment objective of VCCO is to seek attractive risk-adjusted total returns by pursuing a variety of investment strategies that primarily focus on the U.S. credit markets, but with the flexibility to include equity investments, derivatives, cryptocurrency and other investments. VCCO’s investment program is currently expected to focus on middle market companies in the technology, media, telecom and business services sectors, but it may also invest across a diverse set of industries and sectors. It may also invest across diverse regions. VCCO will be flexible in its ability to invest across the capital structure and to select and dispose of investments in response to market opportunities, determinations of relative value, and other factors.

VCCO seeks to achieve its investment objective primarily through investments in bank loans, debt and debt-related securities. VCCO may also acquire equity interests, including preferred and common. VCCO may also seek exposure to such investments synthetically through derivatives, such as swaps, options and other instruments. Since the launch of VCCO in 2011, we have invested about $2.5 billion over 270 credit transactions.

name: Pertento Fund Limited
management_company_description: Pertento Partners LLP is a new London-based investment manager led by Eduardo Marques, formerly of Valiant Capital.  Pertento launched its long-short equity hedge fund in November 2021.  Pertento engages in investigative research to select the most attractive global growth companies run by ethical managers.  Conversely, the team seeks to uncover companies that are either engaging in fraud or in terminal decline.
strategy_description:
Pertento seeks to invest in what it believes to be businesses with a strong competitive profile which are undervalued relative to their respective future growth profiles.  Conversely, the team aims to uncover shorting opportunities in relation to businesses that it believes are either engaging in fraudulent activity or are in terminal decline.

In determining the value of a business, Pertento seeks to forecast the cash flow generation of that business in both the short and long term. Rather than emphasizing near term valuation multiples as an investment criteria, the team will instead focus on businesses that it expects to generate attractive cashflows in the next 3-5 years.

With regards to long investments, Pertento seeks to identify businesses it believes to have solid long-term growth prospects, run by management who it considers to be leaders in ethical business and with high unit economics. Such businesses typically, but not always, hold a competitive position in relation to their IP, brand or network effect. Their returns on invested capital are projected by Pertento to be high at scale, although many of these companies are still investing heavily in growth.

For short positions, Pertento seeks to focus predominantly on businesses which it believes either face long-term structural decline or are suspected to be engaging in some form of corporate malfeasance. A business which is deemed to be in decline is expected to face shrinking profitability and is perceived to have few strategic alternatives to turnaround its course. Malfeasance is a broad subjective category that may encompass various acts of poor corporate governance, ranging from outright fraud to aggressive accounting standards.

Pertento runs a relatively concentrated portfolio of around 20 longs and a highly diversified book of 60+ shorts. The team invests on a global basis, although it is expected that, typically, the portfolio would have around half of its exposure in the United States.

The investment approach is bottom up, fundamentally driven, and research-intensive. Pertento believes that the quality and depth of such fundamental analysis is important in seeking to identify intrinsic value and to generate attractive investment returns over time.

name: Sparta Capital Master Fund
strategy_description:
Sparta is a Europe focused, multi-strategy event driven hedge fund manager with active engagement as a core principle. It invests opportunistically across the full spectrum of event strategies and the capital structure from equity to credit. Sparta aims to protect capital and generate absolute uncorrelated returns through market cycles, by focusing on investments that offer the right kind of idiosyncratic risk and can be well hedged at an appropriate cost.

Each investment is selected on its individual merits; on an idiosyncratic and fully-hedged basis, across the range of possible scenarios. Sparta seeks to apply a disciplined and patient investment approach and looks for embedded optionality within the price-to- value gap, seeking an active engagement pathway to improve the outcome of the investment.  We aim to hedge systematic risk individually and at a portfolio level so that returns are not a function of market direction.

Sparta’s core target market cap range lies between $1bn - $10bn. The investment portfolio is typically comprised of 20-30 core positions, individually hedged. Portfolio construction is “bottom-up”, driven by the opportunity set and sized with conviction, up to a max 10% NAV for an individual investment. Sparta has no predetermined view on how capital is allocated across the sub strategies. Our aim is for a systematic portfolio hedging overlay to deliver capital preservation in market drawdown events, while minimizing any drag on performance.

name: Quantum QB Master Fund Ltd
management_company_description:
Quantum QB Ltd (QQ) is an alternatives business headquartered in the UK. Prior to launching in early 2023 the team worked together dating back to 2017 when the strategy was first deployed live. The IP and track record are fully owned by the 3 Founders in separate company in Switzerland called TSRCT Technologies (SA). Applying what is believed to be a unique and stable systematic approach to liquid markets.
 
As a business it is using computing technology and AI and Machine Learning techniques.
 
Currently QQ is running SMA monies for US Headquartered (SEC registered) financial services groups. A Cayman Commingled Fund launch will follow in 2024 once target launch assets have been secured.
 
The investment process is fully systematic allocating to opportunities identified from a range of liquid asset classes/instruments (Futures, Forwards, Single name Equities) in its investment universe and has no asset class, geographical, sectorial restrictions beyond those controls that seek to mitigate concentration risks. The analysis of data to buy and sell assets is carried out applying research using proprietary systematic models using a range of techniques and technologies that seek to identify investment opportunities in a large set of market environments by seeing the whole market as an interconnected network.
 
This multi-dimensional framework uses trend and reversal categorisation which we believe can be used to explain every short, medium, or long-term movement, driver, and factor in the market. We consider these to be the primary building blocks that would see any other market descriptor as secondary, tertiary, or even further removed. It is important to understand that this framework and philosophy is designed for dynamic movement. In this way the strategy does not even hold any statistical correlation to the traditional measures of trend or reversal. We observe that the traditional measures of these factors tend to be static measures leading to often quoted hypothesis that "trend (or reversal) goes through periods of not working", rather than our hypothesis which is that by using different tools which are capable of adapting their cadence and better measuring trend (or reversal) the market consistently remains in these two states.
 
All QQ research is fractal in nature allowing their application to be applied over multiple time horizons. The strategy captures performance over all time horizons, but when blended overall exhibits a sense of being shorter term in nature. In this way the strategy aims to provide diversification from traditional asset classes over reasonable medium to long term time horizons. Within the financial network we consider the dispersion (hierarchy) of signals/opportunities which are the building blocks cubes or "Qb's" that the process is identifying and creates our statistical edge.
strategy_description:
The investment objective of the Fund is to seek to generate attractive risk-adjusted absolute returns over the long-term. 

It may invest in listed and over-the-counter securities in single name securities and/or across global fixed income, credit, currency, commodity, and equity markets. The Investment Manager will seek for positions to be held across a wide range of futures, forwards, swaps, other derivatives, and cash instruments. The instruments can be changed from time to time, but generally remain in a stable investment universe of 600+ securities. 
The investment philosophy that ultimately informs the investment process is to use a range of research and technology techniques within a scientific framework that uphold the disciplines of Efficiency, Efficacy and Effectiveness. Applied systematically in the most simple and robust way possible to expanding data sets. The strategy is explicitly built on the assumption that data is becoming noisier, where change is the constant, and that volatility and dispersion are endogenous in financial markets. 

The Quantum QB (QQ) Strategy (the "Strategy") is a process that identifies a diversified combination of systematic programs/strategies structured as cubes “Qb's” aiming to generate long term absolute returns in as wide a range of market conditions as possible. The portfolio construction is rooted in maximizing the principles of diversification and risk / return efficiency. 

The investment process allocates to opportunities identified from a range of liquid asset classes/instruments in its investment universe and has no asset class, geographical, sectorial restrictions beyond those controls that seek to mitigate concentration risks. The analysis of data to buy and sell assets is carried out applying research using proprietary systematic models using a range of techniques and technologies that seek to identify investment opportunities in the widest set of market environments by seeing the whole market as an interconnected network. 

The process does not identify with traditional hedge fund strategies, although we do use familiar categories to sort / define opportunities, which are Trend & Reversal.  We have found these categories to be the most robust form of generalising the market that captures all other observed states, factors and conditions in the market. However, this is where the similarities end, as statistically meaningful results historically (as of Dec-2023) have had little in common with Systematic Global Macro or CTA buckets. Our own observations are that the returns will have more in common with a multi-strategy portfolio i.e., they may exhibit short term correlations with any number of strategies, but over longer time periods will remain orthogonal. Which we observe is down to the multi-dimensional nature of the strategy.

management_company_description: O'Connor is a leader in alternative strategies including hedge funds and private credit. From inception in 1977 to today, O'Connor's emphasis on innovation, thought leadership and investment excellence has resulted in investment solutions that focus on relative value and strong absolute returns. With approximately $9bn under management, O’Connor offers a range of strategies including:  Global Multi-Strategy Alpha (launched in 2000), Global Merger Arbitrage (2015), O’Connor Capital Solutions Private Credit (2017), China Long/Short (2021), Event Driven (2021) and Working Capital Finance (2022).
strategy_description:
The Co-Heads of O'Connor Capital Solutions have been working together for the past 15 years. They joined O'Connor in 2015 and closed their first Private Credit Opportunity (PCO) fund in 2017 with $1.1billion. In 2021, they closed their second Private Credit Opportunity fund with $1.75billion. The team has an 8+ year track record and 100+ transactions completed. Fund 3 held a first close September 2023 with $400mm and will be in the market for the next year, targeting $1.75billion.

The Fund will primarily target corporate lending and asset finance (both hard and financial assets) and predominantly focus on non-sponsor backed transactions.

A key differentiator is the team's access hard to penetrate and highly fragmented sourcing networks by utilizing relationships with UBS Wealth Management, UBS Investment Bank and its own external networks. PCO seeks to solve for borrower urgency, complexity and illiquidity and earn a scarcity premium by providing high-value borrowing solutions in markets where there may be limited competition.

PCO focuses on principal protection with collateral and covenants and generally makes loans of USD 20-200m+ that meet a wide range of borrowing needs from UHNWI to asset finance and corporate needs. PCO strives to have a diversified portfolio with low correlation by lending across sectors, asset-classes and geographies with flexibility of structure and format.

A core focus of PCO is to create a highly diversified portfolio at the loan and collateral level with target average position size of 3-4%. And strives for low correlation due to diversified collateral and multiple repayment sources.

The fund seeks to protect capital by focusing on fundamentals and lender protections with a strong bias towards senior secured priority. The team seeks robust financial covenants that provide protection in the event the borrower diverges from the base case.

The portfolio targets current cash income of approximately 10% net per annum paid quarterly and generally has floating rate pricing to provide inflation protection.

Portfolio Managers and the investment team actively monitor risk and investment performance using many approaches that include but are not exclusive to: direct and regular discussions with borrowers; implementing customized borrower covenants and regular reporting requirements; monitoring financial results, news, event, etc.; and ongoing credit reviews for analysis and evaluation of investments.

The Firm limits the categories of clients that it provides investment advice and services. To be more specific, Phoenix is a hedge fund manager; i.e., a manager of private investment funds and institutional separately-managed accounts that limit their investor base to qualifying high net worth individuals and institutional investors. strategy_description: JLP Credit Opportunity Fund is an event driven fund focusing on “stressed” US corporate bonds trading at a deep discounts to their principal values. These bonds may generate very high current income and offer a very attractive risk return profile. The Fund seeks to buy bonds at deep discounts to their par value in companies with adequate liquidity to continue paying all of their obligations. The Fund focuses on asset rich, positive cash flow companies with a near term catalyst for a business turnaround. The Fund hedges some of the long bias by shorting equities of the same or similar companies. The fund also has directional shorts in high yield bonds trading close to par or above which they believe have significant business risk and are candidates for downgrade.  The manager aims to limit downside volatility through some tail risk hedging, diversification, and detailed fundamental bottom up credit research. The Fund trades only cash bonds and thus has no single name CDS or counterparty risk, and uses little to no leverage.

strategy_description: Anson Investments Master Fund (AIMF) is a long/short uncorrelated multi-strategy fund. AIMF focuses on minimizing downside volatility and minimizing correlation with broad equity markets. Individuals affiliated with AIMF’s general partner and investment manager own approximately 25% of the NAV of the fund. Downside volatility is managed by making sparing use of leverage, and correlation is managed by keeping net exposure low. The fund primarily invests in North American issuers, but has the capacity to identify and capitalize on opportunities globally. AIMF does not have a sector focus, though some of the strategies it employs will have a sector tilt from time to time. management_company_description:
Marathon Asset Management LP (“Marathon” or the “Firm”) was formed in 1998 by Bruce Richards (Chairman and Chief Executive Officer) and Louis Hanover (Chief Investment Officer), to seek attractive absolute returns through investments in the global credit markets, with the long-term goal of building a world-class asset management platform. Marathon’s core competency is opportunistic investing in the global corporate, emerging market and structured credit markets based on fundamental, bottom-up research across distinct investment funds, managed vehicles, and separate accounts. Our team has significant experience and expertise investing in credit dislocations through multiple cycles. Marathon’s team is fully integrated to capitalize on credit opportunities globally. Marathon possesses a unique, broad-based skill set and proprietary platform to research, analyze and act upon complex capital structures and situations. 

In 2003, Marathon became an SEC-registered investment adviser in the U.S. Our U.K. office, MCap Global Finance (UK) LLP, is authorized and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority. 

In 2008, Marathon became a Delaware limited partnership, of which Bruce Richards and Louis Hanover are Co-Managing Partners. Marathon is owned by the Partners of Marathon, which consist of Bruce Richards (Chairman and Chief Executive Officer), Louis Hanover (Chief Investment Officer), Jamie Raboy (Chief Operating and Risk Officer), Andrew Springer (Head of Structured Credit), Gabriel “Gaby” Szpigiel (Head of Emerging Markets), Jeff Jacob (Opportunistic Credit Portfolio Manager), Jason Friedman (Global Head of Business Development), Christine Chartouni (Chief Legal Officer), Ed Cong (Structured Credit), and Blackstone Alternative Asset Management (as described below). Bruce Richards and Louis Hanover are the managing members of the General Partner and majority owners of Marathon. Precise ownership figures are considered proprietary and maintained with outside counsel.

In 2009, Marathon was one of nine managers selected by the U.S. Treasury to manage assets for the Public Private Investment Program (“PPIP”).  

In June 2016, Marathon was pleased to announce that Blackstone Strategic Capital Holdings Fund, a vehicle managed by Blackstone Alternative Asset Management, acquired a passive, minority interest in Marathon. Marathon maintains autonomy over its business management, operations, and investment processes and will leverage the partnership with Blackstone to capitalize on opportunities and expand our business.
strategy_description:
The Fund seeks to track and outperform the EMBIGD over a long-term basis, using key sources of Alpha to opportunistically generate risk-adjusted excess returns in prevailing markets, while minimizing tracking error and targeting a Beta of 1 relative to our benchmark. The Index is comprised of sovereign and quasi-sovereign U.S. dollar denominated Emerging Markets instruments. Our strategy is mandated to be fully invested and has the ability to invest in sovereign debt, quasi-sovereign debt, corporate debt, municipal or provincial/state debt, loans, investment and non-investment grade securities. The investment strategy is founded on rigorous value-based fundamental analysis and a keen understanding of underlying securities, allowing the team to select high conviction long positions, coupled with Index-based exposures that intend to result in a value-added portfolio vis-à-vis the Index. The portfolio is comprised of both on-Index and off-Index securities to varying degrees during the lifetime of the Fund based on our bottom-up approach to instrument selection. Off-Index elements are largely comprised of instruments such as Emerging Markets corporate bonds, municipal or provinces/states and other sovereign and quasi-sovereign securities that do not meet Index inclusion criteria due to income, ownership, size, or other Index specifications.

Through the portfolio construction process, both off-Index and on-Index securities come together to create a portfolio whereby key portfolio variables are neutralized (i.e., duration, sectoral exposures, country deviations relative to the Index), allowing for the merits of our credit selection to flow through to portfolio returns, unfettered by differences in portfolio variables vis-à-vis the Index that could otherwise impact total returns.

Our Emerging Markets team’s portfolio construction methodology follows a very regimented, methodical approach. While our portfolio has the ability to hold up to 50% of market value in off-Index securities which are geared toward generating Alpha across the portfolio, the team also aims to generate Alpha through inclusion/exclusion/over/under-weighting of on-Index securities within the portfolio. As our portfolio construction approach is largely reliant on a sampling methodology whereby the Fund holds only a small sampling of the Index itself, Alpha can be generated through more heavily weighting what are believed to be more attractively valued assets, while underweighting, or excluding altogether, assets where our team sees little value. 

Sources of Alpha in the portfolio can be classified as follows: (i) Credit Selection; (ii) Relative Value; (iii) Primary Markets; and (iv) Index Arbitrage/Technicals. 

Credit Selection refers to the inclusion or exclusion of both on- and off-Index securities, based on fundamental bottom-up analysis, in order to improve the relative quality, liquidity, and return prospects of the portfolio. 
Relative Value refers to the capture of risk-adjusted upside via positioning along and between curves of the various issuers within our universe, prioritizing value from a liquidity, spread, and dollar price point of view.
Primary Markets refers to the leveraging of Marathon’s deep franchise and extensive capital market relationships in order to source securities and rebalance the portfolio in a cost-effective manner, and to benefit from new issue concessionary pricing when available.

name: Vellichor Fund
strategy_description:
Vellichor Management (“Vellichor” or “The Fund”) is a fundamentally driven long/short fund that seeks to capitalize on industry dislocations and small and mid-cap companies going through multiyear growth and ROIC inflections. While we expect to primarily invest in equities, we will utilize almost two decades of experience across the capital structure to identify the best ideas across equities and credit.

We seek to capitalize on change. 
Companies and industries are constantly shifting and evolving. What is high quality today can often be competed away tomorrow and vice versa. 
By focusing on emerging themes and recognizing shifts in industry competitive dynamics we can identify reasonably priced companies that are transitioning to higher growth or becoming high quality. This allows us to target double-digit long-term returns while also protecting investor capital.

We take an opportunistic approach to investing. We will focus on the underfollowed, unloved or complex parts of the market where we will face less competition in identifying high quality companies at a reasonable price (HARP). Specifically, we will focus on 3 core opportunity sets:

•	Low growth companies about to go through a growth inflection
•	Industries going through disruption or dislocation
•	Companies with leverage where a sophisticated understanding of both equity and credit markets is required

Research Process:
Multi-disciplined approach to idea generation. We use a deep fundamental and collaborative research process that underscores the role of regular, vigorous, and open dialogue amongst the team and uses both qualitative and quantitative tools for idea generation. We also use a blind and risk focused parallel underwrite process for any position that may be taken over 3% of AUM to enhance objectivity and mitigate risk.

Portfolio Composition:
Primarily equity with selective credit investments. Geographic exposure will be 90% developed markets and mostly in the U.S. Portfolio will be moderately concentrated with 20-25 core long positions and 5-10 core short positions. 90%+ of the portfolio will be in liquid Level 1 assets. The average holding period will be 1-2 years.

Risk Management:
Single name risks are mitigated with micro hedging tools from our cross-asset background and portfolio risk is mitigated on a macro basis with sophisticated factor tools. Position sizing is optimized using tools from Alpha Theory. Fund will be low leverage with average gross exposure of 125-175%. Net exposure will typically average 50-80% but will be variable and adjusted based on returns available in the market.

management_company_description:
Varenne Capital Partners (‘Varenne’) is a research and process driven investment manager based in Paris, France, where it was founded by its current management team in 2003.

The firm first operated as an advisor to VEGA Finance – private banking unit of the CDC/CE Group – before establishing itself as a fully independent investment manager in 2007. 

With 8 nationalities in a team of 50 people, including 21 investment professionals, the management team fosters a culture of openness and diversity translating into very low turnover and an average tenure of 9 years in the investment team. 

All senior investment associates are shareholders or stock option holders in the firm and co-invest a significant portion of their wealth alongside long-standing clients in Europe, Asia, and the Americas.
strategy_description:
VARENNE LONG SHORT aims at delivering superior long-term returns with the minimum necessary risk-taking. To do so, Varenne combines complementary investment frameworks in a single strategy: Long Equity and Short Equity. The firm adopts a ‘brokers are not welcome’ policy and makes extensive use of technology to rely exclusively on internal origination and proprietary research. Investment frameworks are the result of years of R&D and comprise original methodologies, formalized processes, dedicated teams of analysts and bespoke information systems.

The Long Equity framework starts with a core of 30 to 35 high-quality businesses in global developed markets. Additional diversified positions allow access to themes, sectors, or situations that can be absent from the core concentrated selection in order to optimize strategies’ behavior. Proprietary fundamental and behavioral databases provide original investment ideas to different teams (‘Origination’) which contribute their highest convictions to the portfolios.

The Short Equity framework has a core portfolio with the goal of producing uncorrelated returns, particularly in adverse economic or credit conditions. Core exposure is expressed through companies facing at least one among: unsustainable profitability, business deterioration, or financial issues. Diversified short layers provide exposure to themes, situations or industries that may be absent from single name selections in order to optimize overall portfolio behavior. We combine proprietary fundamental and behavioral factors to identify the above idiosyncratic ideas and manage the timing of the trades as well as their risk.

The frameworks are combined using a rule-based portfolio construction methodology. The investment process therefore aims to bring together what we believe to be the depth of analysis and judgement of independent and experienced teams together with the rigor and systematicity of a rule-based portfolio construction model.

The Fund’s Equity Long and Short Equity frameworks have a gross exposure limited to 150% maximum (MtM), and typically range between 90-130%. The Net Target Exposure ranges between 30-50% with a Long Exposure between 70-90%.

strategy_description: The Lynx Program is our original strategy that was launched in May 2000. The objective of the Lynx Program is to generate a high risk-adjusted return while maintaining attractive portfolio characteristics. The characteristics have been chosen with the aim of making the strategy suitable as a building block in an institutional investor's portfolio. Examples of these characteristics include a low correlation to equities and bonds, a positive correlation to volatility and positive skewness of returns. Other characteristics relate to the ability to react to trend reversals and profit from prolonged bear market conditions (often referred to as "crisis alpha"). The Lynx Program's main approach is systematic advanced trend following. The program is employing a multi-model approach applying a range of statistical techniques to identify and capture trends over a span of time frames. In addition to trend following concepts, the strategy includes an allocation to diversifying models that aim to exploit other market phenomena than price momentum. These diversifying models consists of systematic global macro concepts based on fundamental data as well as models utilizing various machine learning techniques. In total the program consists of approximately 40 different models. The Investment Committee is responsible for strategy including setting the risk allocation to each model in the program.

Asset & Wealth Management (AWM) includes our previously unified Asset Management businesses, as well as Private Wealth Management, our Workplace and Personal Wealth offerings, and Goldman Sachs Marcus. strategy_description:
Overview
Global Opportunities (GO) is Goldman Sachs Asset Management’s flagship, direct global multi-strategy hedge fund. It invests across global fixed income, equity, commodity, currency and volatility markets, through discretionary and quantitative (roughly 60 / 40% split), relative value and macro (roughly 55% / 45% split) alpha strategies.  The fund combines 38 existing alpha engines from across Goldman Sachs Asset Management’s public investing business to deliver our highest conviction strategies. The strategy leverages existing people, data, technology, infrastructure, and the full resources of the business and firm, to deliver returns consistent with the multi-strategy hedge fund universe, but in more investor focused terms. The fund does not have pass-through fees, and offers monthly liquidity with no lock up on capital.  The solution is designed  to deliver a high Sharpe, low beta to risk assets (~0.0-0.1), cash +7 to 10% net  returns, and 5% to  8% annualized volatility.

The fund is managed by co-CIOs Dennis Walsh and Simon Dangor.  Dennis is also co-CIO of our Quantitative Investment Solutions business and Simon is deputy CIO of Fixed income and head of Global Fixed Income Macro Strategies.

strategy_description:
Crabel Gemini is a systematic portfolio of predominantly short holding period strategies designed to target behavioral and structural market inefficiencies across a broadly diversified set of global futures and foreign exchange instruments. The portfolio is structured to provide low correlation to traditional and alternative asset classes. Made up of over 50 differentiated and stand-alone strategy frameworks, the program offers a unique source of returns. Crabel’s focus on execution excellence provides a further advantage in efficiently accessing unique exposures in approximately 200 markets. Strategies are generally driven by price or derivatives of price such as volatility, correlation and term structure. Most strategies are designed to work symmetrically, either long or short. The program has an approximate eight-day average hold timeframe (with a range of two days to several months) and targets a 10% annualized standard deviation. The program utilizes a multi-tiered approach to risk control that includes dynamic sizing of new trades relative to market volatility, the use of price as well as time-based stops and a real-time VaR-based position sizing mechanism that seeks to constrain overall portfolio risk.

name: Samlyn Portable Alpha Fund
management_company_description: Samlyn Capital, LLC (the “Firm”), is a global asset management company that manages a Delaware limited partnership and two Cayman Islands exempted companies in a mini-master fund structure that employ a long/short equity strategy (collectively, the “Flagship Fund”), a traditional master-feeder fund structure that employs a long only equity strategy (the “Long Alpha Fund”), a traditional master-feeder fund structure that employs a market-neutral investment strategy (the “Net Neutral Fund”) and a portable alpha investment strategy that invests its assets in shares of a Net Neutral Fund and shares of an exchange-traded fund (the “Portable Alpha Fund” and collectively, the “Funds”).
strategy_description:
The Portable Alpha Fund's investment objective is to generate superior risk-adjusted returns over time. In seeking to achieve this objective, the Portable Alpha Fund invests approximately: (i) 50% of the Fund’s net assets in common shares of Samlyn Net Neutral Master Fund, Ltd. (the “Net Neutral Fund”); and (ii) 50% of the Fund’s net assets in shares of the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (ticker: VOO), as well as options thereon (such ratio, the “Target Ratio”). Samlyn rebalances the Fund’s portfolio as of the end of any month in which the Fund’s portfolio has deviated from the Target Ratio by more than 5% as a result of the relative performance of the Fund’s investment in the Net Neutral Fund vis-à-vis the Fund’s investment in shares of the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF and its other direct investments.
Upon the request of a prospective investor, the Fund may in the future establish a new sub-class of shares that invests in a different ETF (in lieu of investing in the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF) and maintains a different Target Ratio.

The Net Neutral Fund's investment objective is to generate superior risk-adjusted returns over time by employing a market-neutral investment strategy that makes long and short investments primarily in global equity securities. In particular, the Net Neutral Fund’s portfolio generally mirrors both the long and short positions held by the long/short strategy. However, as the Net Neutral Fund’s portfolio is managed to be market-neutral, the positions held by the Net Neutral Fund are weighted differently than the same positions held in the respective portfolios of the long/short strategy to: (i) neutralize the Net Neutral Fund’s net exposure; and (ii) achieve higher gross exposure for the Net Neutral Fund through the use of increased leverage. The Net Neutral Fund’s gross exposure typically ranges from 300% to 400%. The Net Neutral Fund maintains short basket hedges that are typically adjusted by the Investment Manager on a daily basis in order to neutralize net exposure resulting from daily trading activity and market movements. Short basket hedges may also be used in order to mitigate certain sector and factor exposures, as well as to address macro risks, in each case, as the Investment Manager determines to be appropriate in its discretion. The short basket hedge will also be used to offset net exposure resulting from pair-trades and merger-arbitrage transactions. The Net Neutral Fund’s short basket hedges will consist of broad-based stock indices, sector indices and factor baskets and will generally not exceed 15% of the Net Neutral Fund’s equity. The Net Neutral Fund’s long and short ratios will generally be maintained as long as the Net Neutral Fund’s total gross exposure is typically between 300% to 400% of equity and the short basket hedge exposure is typically between 5% to 15% of equity.

A Portable Alpha Fund investor’s ability to redeem its shares attributable to a particular subscription in the Portable Alpha Fund will be subject to all of the applicable redemption terms set forth in the Samlyn Net Neutral CEM. A summary of the Net Neutral Fund Terms can be found in the Net Neutral Fund CEM (available upon request).

strategy_description:
The Covariance Fund (the “Fund”) utilizes a quantitative investment framework that is designed to incorporate the lessons of behavioral finance in the execution of a systematic long-short strategy. The Fund aims to deliver attractive and consistent returns while minimizing the risk of loss. Our absolute-return strategy seeks to: generate positive returns in every market environment, minimize downside risk, and add diversification in multi-asset portfolios by maintaining the following attributes:
 
Equity-like returns: Our strategy seeks to be capital efficient, moving enough that it delivers meaningful diversification benefits but not so much that it introduces unwanted volatility.
 
Low correlation to stock and bond markets: The Fund is designed to be a source of alpha that’s uncorrelated with major beta drivers in an effort to help our investors achieve better overall performance.
 
Minimal drawdowns: The Fund seeks to maintain a large number of uncorrelated and positively convex positions with upside potential that we believe exceeds their perceived risk of loss. This feature aims to keep the depth and duration of drawdowns to a minimum.

Investment Strategy Description: 

The Fund is an absolute-return strategy that seeks to deliver superior risk-adjusted returns in up or down markets. Cynosure’s systematic approach in managing the Fund combines three uncorrelated models that aim to make performance more consistent, explainable, targeted, and predictable.  

We believe that layering uncorrelated models provides the potential to boost risk-adjusted returns relative to a single-model-driven strategy. Cynosure may adjust the models over time consistent with its model management procedures. Cynosure retains discretion to determine the timing and manner of executing on trading recommendations from the quantitative models and whether to override such recommendations.

*There is no assurance that any of the three models, either individually or in the aggregate, will be successful or will result in positive returns. The expected attribution of performance to each model’s strategy is based on Cynosure’s assessment as of the date of this summary but may change over time. During any particular period of time, any of the three models could contribute more or less to the Fund’s overall return.

strategy_description:
The Covariance Fund (the “Fund”) utilizes a quantitative investment framework that is designed to incorporate the lessons of behavioral finance in the execution of a systematic long-short strategy. The Fund aims to deliver attractive and consistent returns while minimizing the risk of loss. Our absolute-return strategy seeks to: generate positive returns in every market environment, minimize downside risk, and add diversification in multi-asset portfolios by maintaining the following attributes:
 
Equity-like returns: Our strategy seeks to be capital efficient, moving enough that it delivers meaningful diversification benefits but not so much that it introduces unwanted volatility.
 
Low correlation to stock and bond markets: The Fund is designed to be a source of alpha that’s uncorrelated with major beta drivers in an effort to help our investors achieve better overall performance.
 
Minimal drawdowns: The Fund seeks to maintain a large number of uncorrelated and positively convex positions with upside potential that we believe exceeds their perceived risk of loss. This feature aims to keep the depth and duration of drawdowns to a minimum.

strategy_description:
The Emerging Markets Long/Short Strategy seeks mid‑teens annualised net returns via a blended top‑down and bottom‑up approach across the EM equity universe. The philosophy recognises that EM equities in aggregate can remain range‑bound for extended periods. However macroeconomic conditions can vary significantly across EM countries and sectors, meaning that country, sector and thematic dispersion is persistent. The strategy seeks to dynamically exploit these differences to generate consistent alpha, concentrating capital in the highest‑conviction themes on the long side and selectively using shorts and derivatives as an additional layer of alpha generation and downside protection.

·      Concentrated, conviction‑led: typically 20-80% net, gross 150-200% 

·      Blended research: macro country/sector thematics guide focus; stock selection driven by disciplined valuation–verification–catalyst (VVC).

·      Capital preservation: dynamic hedging (via shorting single names and ETFs, complemented by options strategies) reduces drawdowns during volatility spikes.

·      Deep integration with TT’s Global EM Equity team while retaining long/short implementation flexibility.

The team works closely with TT’s Global EM Equity team, with investment professionals based in Hong Kong, India, and the United Kingdom, leveraging their local expertise and corporate access. The strategy combines the highest conviction ideas from the Global EM Investment team, together with the ability to generate returns on the short side and hedge to protect capital. The ability to hedge allows the team to take higher conviction concentrated positions while mitigating market, sector, and company-specific risks.

The combined track record for the DYNE Fund has been calculated as follows: 

1. From January 2015 to March 2021: The period represents the "pre-portfolio" period prior to the addition of the Convergent and Divergent strategies to the Dynamic Equity strategy into the DYNE Fund track record. The pre-portfolio track record is constructed using the gross performance of the Dynamic Equity strategy of the portfolio manager ("PM") and the historical performance of the Divergent and Convergent strategies overseen by the same PM at a different investment manager, apply the model fees as described in point "2" below. The pre-portfolio net performance is using the following assumptions and adjustments for management and allocation fees as per below to arrive to the net performance represented in the combined track record table:

a.	The monthly dollar value profit and loss (“PNL”) for PM of Divergent and Convergent strategies from January 2015 to March 2021.

b.	Next, any performance related to the Dynamic Equity strategy is subtracted from the total from “a” above leaving a residual of monthly PNL, which is then divided by total of “a” and the Dynamic Equity strategy performance to create a monthly performance percentage.

c.	The monthly performance percentage is then multiplied by the percentage of PNL attributed to the DYNE Fund to create an adjusted Fund return (“AFR”) number.

d.	To create a gross monthly combined return, Dynamic Equity was multiplied by 20% while AFR was multiplied by 80%, reflecting the baseline allocation between the Dynamic Equity and Convergent and Divergent strategies. These figures were combined to reflect the 100% current construction of the Fund’s portfolio.

e.	Finally, the figure in “d” above was modelled through a fee simulation of 0.75% management incentive and 15% allocation incentive crystallized quarterly to arrive at the final monthly and yearly performance numbers. management_company_description:
Senator Investment Group LP (“Senator” or the “Firm”) is a private investment firm co-founded in 2008 by Douglas Silverman to pursue investments opportunistically across the capital structure with an emphasis on identifying companies undergoing change. The Firm manages the Senator Global Opportunity Funds ("SGOF", or, the "Funds"), its flagship event-driven hedge fund launched in July 2008. SGOF employs a fundamental investment approach identifying catalyst-driven equities and dislocated or otherwise attractive credit instruments, while being cognizant and thoughtful of macro factors. The Funds invest globally, with the majority of exposures in the U.S. and an average historical net long exposure between 30%-60%. Senator has managed several other funds, strategies, and accounts during its 18 year history. The Firm is also currently accepting outside capital for the Senator Strategic Resources Fund ("SSRF"), a long-biased, thematic equity fund initially funded with internal capital in 2023.  SSRF seeks to capitalize on companies, commodities, and currencies that are at the confluence of global megatrends including Fiscal Dominance, Deglobalization, and Societal Transformation.  

Senator is based in New York City and has 27 employees, of whom 13 are investment professionals. The Firm's analysts are ambidextrous with respect to both credit and equity investing. Senator believes this flexibility and breadth of expertise has enabled the Firm to pursue attractive risk returns throughout market cycles.
strategy_description: The Senator Global Opportunity Fund was formed in July 2008 to pursue opportunistic investments, long and short, in distressed and dislocated credit and catalyst-driven equities. The Fund will invest opportunistically across the capital structure wherever it identifies the best risk-reward, driven by a fundamentals first investment process and informed by its macro and risk framework; therefore the Fund may have a distinct bias toward equity or credit at different points in the cycle. Senator employs an “event-driven” framework in its investment process. However, unlike many event-driven funds where the “event” often leads the analysis and/or idea generation, Senator’s investment strategy is foremost rooted in identifying companies with strong fundamentals (although potentially in distress) at attractive valuations, and that may benefit from a corporate event or catalyst over a 6 – 18 month period.  Senator employs a bottom-up approach to analyzing all components of a company's capital structure and invests in a broad range of securities including bank debt, corporate bonds, equities, preferred stock, convertible securities, trade claims, credit default swaps, and options. Senator emphasizes capital preservation and seeks to mitigate risk through various hedging strategies at the position and portfolio levels. Senator also monitors a number of macro and risk factors to ensure the portfolio’s intended bets are expressed and unintended bets managed. These factors include, but are not limited to, concentration, sector, market cap, region, liquidity, crowdedness, momentum, and ESG scores. Net exposure levels have averaged ~40% since inception.

The success of Bayberry’s hedging strategy is subject to Bayberry’s ability to correctly assess the degree of correlation between the performance of the instruments used in the hedging strategy and the performance of the investments in the portfolios being hedged. Since the characteristics of many securities change as markets change or time passes, the success of the instances when Bayberry hedges portfolio positions in the Fund is also subject to Bayberry’s ability to continually recalculate, readjust, and execute hedges in an efficient and timely manner. 
Short Selling.  Bayberry may engage in short selling on behalf of the Fund.  Short selling involves selling securities that are not owned by the Fund.  A short position is established when the Fund borrows securities from securities brokers or other institutions and sells them in an open market transaction with an obligation to return the borrowed securities at a later date.  However, a short sale creates the risk of unlimited loss because in order to close out a short position, the Fund would need to return the borrowed securities by purchasing such securities at prevailing market prices.  There can be no assurance that the security necessary to close out a short position will be available for purchase.  Purchasing securities to close out the short position can itself cause the price of the securities to rise further if the demand to buy such securities outpaces the available supply, thereby exacerbating the loss.

management_company_description:
Founded in 1971 and based in Los Angeles, TCW manages a broad range of innovative, actively managed investment products that strive to enhance and protect clients’ wealth. TCW’s clients include many of the largest corporate and public pension plans, financial institutions, insurance companies, endowments and foundations in the United States, as well as a substantial number of international entities including central banks, sovereign wealth funds and private banks.

In 2001, TCW was acquired by Société Générale (SG), one of the largest global banking franchises with a presence in 85 countries. SG worked with TCW to grow and expand its global footprint for a dozen years. The partnership was very productive, including in early 2010, TCW’s acquisition of Metropolitan West Asset Management, LLC (MetWest), a top-ranked fixed income asset manager. As a result, key employees of MetWest assumed primary responsibility for the oversight of TCW’s fixed income mandates. Since that time, MetWest has operated as a subsidiary of The TCW Group, Inc. 

In February 2013, TCW’s management effected a management led buy-out of SG in partnership with The Carlyle Group. Following the buyout, The Carlyle Group held an approximately 60% stake in the firm, with TCW management and employees owning the balance of approximately 40%, on a fully diluted basis. TCW management negotiated strong governance provisions to ensure that TCW’s managerial autonomy would be preserved. Equity for the transaction came from TCW management and two Carlyle investment funds – Carlyle Global Financial Services Partners, a $1.1 billion financial services fund, and Carlyle Partners V, a $13.7 billion U.S. buyout fund. The Carlyle transaction facilitated a management initiative to increase employee ownership.  Prior to 2010, TCW employees did not have significant equity interests in the firm. Since the 2010 acquisition of MetWest by TCW, employee ownership has continued to increase.

On December 27, 2017, Nippon Life completed its acquisition of a 24.75% minority stake in TCW from Carlyle. As a result of this transaction, ownership in TCW by TCW management and employees increased to 44.07%, and Carlyle maintains a 31.18% interest in the firm through a purchase by its long duration private equity fund, Carlyle Global Partners.

There is a high level of employee ownership of the company, including most of TCW’s key decision-making investment and other professionals. TCW believes strongly that employee equity ownership aligns the interests of the decision-making employees with the interests of the firm and the firm’s clients, and creates a cohesive “ownership culture.”

Nippon and Carlyle have agreed to continue the existing strong governance protections for TCW management, which help to ensure that TCW’s current management and investment teams are primarily responsible for personnel and compensation decisions, and solely responsible for the management of investment portfolios.
strategy_description:
The investment team employs a fundamental research-driven and value-oriented approach as it seeks to to identify opportunities in the small cap equity markets. The team strives to distinguish market mispricings that may result from a transitional event, a complex corporate restructure, and lack of research coverage or institutional investor focus.

The team actively seeks out companies that are in transition and therefore, more likely to be under or overvalued by the market. Once an opportunity is recognized, the team performs a deep dive to determine the fundamental value of the company. While analyzing the single security, our selection process incorporates the overall portfolio impact by managing risk through extensive bottom-up research, active hedging, reassessing portfolio construction, and exposure monitoring.

We believe changes in regulation and the shift to passive indexing in the equity market should result in more opportunities since there should be less capital and fewer institutional investors following off-the-run names. We assert that these shifts are likely to result in larger differences between intrinsic and market value when a company is in transition.

Portfolio Manager, Jeremy Zhu established the strategy in 2003 and has managed the fund since inception. Each member of the team has over 15 years of investment experience and have been investing together the past decade. While they have different areas of expertise, they share the same investment philosophy.

strategy_description:
The investment objective of the  Master Fund is to seek to deliver risk-adjusted absolute returns, with low to moderate long-term correlation with global equity markets.  In order to achieve the investment objective, the Investment Manager will employ a discretionary approach to macro investing with the strategy focussing on macro-economic developments and opportunities arising as policy shifts and developments take place. 
The Investment Manager's investment methodology will be implemented based upon a top-down macro view, by investing in all asset classes on a global basis.
This is achieved by:
1.	Studying and understanding the prevailing macro-economic framework; 
2.	Understanding current policy maker’s objectives; and
3.	Assessing whether the current policy stance is consistent with those objectives or subject to change.  
Thematic investment opportunities are identified based on rigorous research into the above. This utilises the experience and network of the Investment Manager. Individual investment opportunities are assessed through focussing on changes or the rate of change in interest rates, foreign exchange, inflation, economic cycles and political circumstances.  
 The investment strategy is designed to be flexible enough to capture opportunities in a shifting macro environment, aiming to capitalise on policy-related moves in asset prices as the economic cycle plays out.

management_company_description: Arrow Capital was founded in 2017 by Martin Rosser and offers a single global equity market neutral strategy. The firm is wholly-owned by senior staff and has 6 full-time employees based in Sydney Australia. The strategy is offered to sophisticated and wholesale investors in Australia and New Zealand via an unregistered managed investment scheme and to international investors via the Arrow Mercury (Cayman) Fund. Arrow also offers Separately Managed Accounts, which are managed pari passu with the flagship strategy.
strategy_description:
The Arrow Market Neutral Fund is an Australian domiciled wholesale unit trust. The fund is offered to sophisticated and wholesale investors in Australia and New Zealand. International investors can access the strategy via the Arrow Mercury (Cayman) Fund, which is managed as a 2X levered version of the core strategy. The Manager also offers the strategy to institutional investors via separately managed accounts.

The Fund employs a global equity market neutral strategy constructing long and short portfolios of roughly the same value and characteristics. The Manager selects securities from a universe comprising 4 key geographies - Australia Hong Kong Japan and the United States restricting itself to large liquid securities only. Using a thematic approach the Manager seeks to identify structural and cyclical themes which it believes will have a material impact on the price of certain securities. Having identified and validated a theme the Manager builds baskets of 5-20 securities which it believes have a meaningful exposure to the theme. Through bottom-up fundamental analysis the Manager curates each basket to identify high quality companies which it believes are positively exposed to the theme and poor quality companies that are negatively exposed to the theme. Thematic baskets are managed dynamically to ensure the theme as a whole along with each constituent security is performing in line with the Manager's expectations.

The Manager has a strict risk management framework which requires that the net equity exposure of the portfolio (cash & beta adjusted) is kept at or close to zero at all times. Each geographic block is also kept neutral at all times to ensure FX or other regional factors are neutralized. The Manager constructs broadly diversified long and short portfolios with the Fund typically holding 150-180 individual positions (skewed higher to shorts). Liquidity is also a key consideration with constant monitoring to ensure that a high liquidity hurdle is retained for all investments. This allows the Manager to control drawdowns by cutting losing positions quickly.

strategy_description:
The Aspect Absolute Return Programme is an enhanced, systematic alternative risk premia programme. Multiple risk premium factors are captured systematically, exploiting both relative and absolute effects across multi-asset derivatives, with no single factor dominating the return profile. This wide range of well-understood risk premia factors can be broadly categorised into three themes: momentum, value, and carry. The themes include both enhanced implementations of traditional factors and more esoteric or idiosyncratic approaches to capture the risk premia. In all cases, the factors are characterised by an underlying hypothesis about economic or behavioural factors which drive persistent effects in markets. A dynamic risk parity approach is used to combine the different underlying strategies. The aim is to maximise diversification by spreading risk evenly across the different alternative risk premia.

The investment objective is to capture multiple alternative risk premia to provide diversifying and consistent returns. The Programme aims to achieve a positive absolute return independent of overall movements in traditional stock and bond markets, with a risk profile that is less volatile than stock markets. The Programme targets an annualised volatility of approximately 5-8%. The Programme aims to perform as consistently as possible over time, regardless of the prevailing macro-economic environment.

This new strategy builds directly on the established operational platform and investment framework of the flagship commingled Master Fund, leveraging the same experienced portfolio management team and disciplined, fundamentally driven investment process.
