The Strategy is agnostic to geography, sector and instrument and seeks to achieve attractive risk-adjusted returns with low volatility. The Strategy is intended to be market neutral and uncorrelated to any other asset class. The Strategy primarily invests in equities but can also express risk arbitrage investments via listed credit instruments, although these investments are limited in order to maintain the Strategy's desired liquidity profile. Investments are driven by bottom-up fundamental research and a top-down data driven analysis, seeking to benefit from market dislocations and inefficiencies. The Strategy typically holds 20-30 long positions (or long spreads) and 0-5 short positions (or short spreads). The Strategy aims to manage to a maximum estimated loss of 3% of AUM per position, a maximum position size of 15% of LMV, and maximum gross leverage of 320%. The Firm aims to manage the portfolio with limited leverage in tight or normal markets in order to be in a position of strength during periods of market dislocation. We believe this gives us the ability to increase our exposure and invest in opportunities that we believe to be mispriced. Risk LMV target of 80-120% in tight or normal markets and up to 200% in times of dislocation. The Strategy aims to have minimal market beta and utilises a convex portfolio hedge to help achieve this goal. The Fund aims to be highly liquid so that 90% of the portfolio could be liquidated within two weeks under normal market conditions.

strategy_description: Decagon Asset Management ("DAM")  employs a hard-catalyst event-driven strategy, investing globally and across the capital structure, focused on announced corporate events. The Strategy is agnostic to geography, sector and instrument and seeks to achieve attractive risk-adjusted returns with low volatility. The Strategy is intended to be market neutral and uncorrelated to any other asset class. The Strategy primarily invests in equities but can also express risk arbitrage investments via listed credit instruments, although these investments are limited in order to maintain the Strategy's desired liquidity profile. Investments are driven by bottom-up fundamental research and a top-down data driven analysis, seeking to benefit from market dislocations and inefficiencies. The Strategy typically holds 20-30 long positions (or long spreads) and 0-5 short positions (or short spreads). The Strategy aims to manage to a maximum estimated loss of 3% of AUM per position, a maximum position size of 15% of LMV, and maximum gross leverage of 320%. The Firm aims to manage the portfolio with limited leverage in tight or normal markets in order to be in a position of strength during periods of market dislocation. We believe this gives us the ability to increase our exposure and invest in opportunities that we believe to be mispriced. Risk LMV target of 80-120% in tight or normal markets and up to 200% in times of dislocation. The Strategy aims to have minimal market beta and utilises a convex portfolio hedge to help achieve this goal. The Fund aims to be highly liquid so that 90% of the portfolio could be liquidated within two weeks under normal market conditions.

OHF invests in the Shipping and Energy sectors, through long/short equity, bonds, commodities and freight. The investment process comprises a short-term trading strategy and a medium-term fundamental strategy. 

The short-term strategy utilities a proprietary vessel tracking and prediction software, “TRACS”, which provides real-time tracking of all ships on the water.  The fundamental analysis draws on a 150 year shipping market database, extensive in-house demand/supply analyses and stock specific asset valuations. The strategy also seeks to capture structural opportunities arising from the energy transition and applies operational and technical analysis to identify the winners and losers from increasingly stringent environmental standards.

management_company_description: LGT Capital Partners was formed as LGT Capital Management Ltd. in September 1998 as the investment management division of the LGT Group Foundation, providing investment management and advisory services with a specialization in multi-alternative investment strategies. The firm has over USD 100 billion in assets under management and more than 700 institutional clients in 44 countries. An international team of over 750 professionals is responsible for managing a wide range of investment programs.
strategy_description:
LGT Risk Premia SF is a largely market-neutral and dynamic long/short quantitative macro strategy with a live track record since April 2016. The fund has been designed to harness systematic premia beyond market beta, thus providing a truly uncorrelated alpha stream of returns. More specifically, the fund targets consistent long-term capital appreciation with an expected volatility of below 10% and an equity market beta of <0.3 measured over a rolling 3-5 year period. 

The investment process combines a machine-learning based, top-down portfolio construction framework with a diversified set of 30 systematic trading strategies aimed at generating performance from alternative risk premiums and lead-lag effects extracted bottom-up within and across over 200 liquid markets globally in all major asset classes, i.e., equity indices, single stocks, government bonds, money markets, interest rate swaps, currencies, commodities, and volatility.

portfolio_additional_details: Across the portfolio, a great emphasis is put on liquidity and robustness – to increase resilience by minimizing the dependency on any single asset class, trading style or signal.  |  Asset classes diversification – we actively trade in all major asset classes, focusing on the most liquid markets globally. We regularly add new instruments to access additional alpha sources.  |  Trading style diversification –  we trade financial markets primarily relative to one another to take advantage of intra-market and inter-market differences in expected returns and the forward pricing of assets as well as directionally long and short to capitalize on trends and reversals.  |  Signal input diversification – we rely on a broad set of inputs, such as relative movements in spot and futures prices, option markets or economic and company fundamentals. These inputs then feed into coherent 'if-then' rules, which we continuously review and enhance with new data sets to improve signal accuracy and robustness. In addition, many of our strategies have built-in investment functions that dynamically adapt their risk taking to prevailing conditions with trading speeds ranging from intraday and overnight to several days, weeks or months depending on the underlying thesis and targeted investment outcome.
esg_approach_description:

However, for the LGT Risk Premia strategy, sustainability is not an integral part of the fund’s investment objective, because for liquidity reasons, it mostly trades futures and does not make active selection choices in terms of securities traded. An active selection choice on sustainability criteria is most commonly associated with sustainable equities and corporate debt securities investing, but not with systematic macro and managed futures strategies like LGT Risk Premia.

strategy_description:
LGT Dynamic Protection is a quantitative crisis alpha strategy aiming to deliver the return profile of an equity put option without paying costly premiums for tail risk protection. More specifically, the strategy seeks to deliver strong capital gains during phases of elevated equity market stress while limiting the costs of carry in normal periods, thus providing a highly asymmetric return profile which makes the strategy a particularly valuable diversifier in a balanced portfolio context  - especially in comparison to solely relying on bonds for cushioning equity risks or trying to time markets with option-based crisis risk offset approaches. 

The strategy is well-diversified across different markets and asset classes, fully systematic and entirely futures-based in its implementation. It combines a top-down risk budgeting framework linked to equity market volatility with an equally weighted basket of eight fundamentally anchored and dynamically sized hedging strategies that exploit their risk budgets bottom-up. Each sub-strategy has its own diversified set of proprietary signals and trades independent from the others with trading speeds ranging from mid- to short term up to intraday and overnight. At portfolio level, this results in a high degree of versatility and robustness and allows the LGT Dynamic Protection strategy to cope with a wide range of possible future crisis scenarios.

strategy_description: At Quantique – Machine, Math & Mind, the investment decision, selection, and allocation process combines the discipline of data-driven quantitative models with the rigorous oversight of seasoned financial professionals. Our objective is to deliver beta-neutral, alpha-generating strategies that maximize the Sharpe ratio. The process begins with the acquisition and preparation of large volumes of market data through Extract, Transform, and Load procedures, ensuring that information is thoroughly cleaned and structured for use in our models. Once prepared, this data serves as the foundation for robust signal extraction. Using advanced statistical and machine-learning techniques, our proprietary models generate signals that identify investment opportunities by capturing inefficiencies across liquid emerging and developed markets. These signals are then assessed under explicit risk parameters and portfolio constraints, with the resulting insights feeding directly into portfolio optimization, where models are designed to achieve the highest possible risk-adjusted returns. Although Quantique operates under one unified investment framework, multiple strategies are applied within each stage to enhance diversification and resilience. This multi-strategy design, combined with systematic analysis and disciplined human supervision, enables Quantique to consistently generate alpha and deliver superior Sharpe ratios across market cycles. At the same time, all strategies are constructed to remain beta-neutral and robust against directional risks. To ensure reliability and consistency, every model undergoes rigorous training, in-sample validation, and out-of-sample testing before any allocation decisions are implemented.

The Firm looks for opportunities to capitalize upon the inefficiencies created by large pools of passive capital, the mechanistic use of "factors", and other capital flows insensitive to price discovery in the various global asset markets by investing in concentrated "information intensive" positions in merger arbitrage, capital structure arbitrage, legal/regulatory risks, volatility expressions, and highly liquid capture of duration and credit spread. strategy_description:
Birnam Oak has broad and flexible investment authority and intends to continually adjust the composition of the portfolio, which includes North American and non-North American long and short investments in equities, derivatives, debt instruments, and other securities or financial instruments, including those of investment companies. Birnam Oak constructs its alpha seeking portfolio through "bottom up" research and relies on numerous sources of publicly available information for its investment decisions. When deemed appropriate, Birnam Oak seeks tax efficiency when managing the equity risk premium component of the alpha + equity risk premium sleeve for onshore investors only.  Mr. DeLong has been managing the combined "alpha + equity risk premium" portfolio since May 2021 and Birnam Oak will assume management of that portfolio when the Firm launches in January 2024.

management_company_description:
Founded in 2006, Columbus Hill is a minority owned investment manager that seeks to achieve superior risk adjusted returns over a multi-year period through all phases of the market cycle. Kevin D. Eng, CIO & CEO, has ≈ 30years investment experience including positions with Duquesne and Appaloosa.

Columbus Hill focuses on exploiting dislocated equities, stressed and distressed corporate debt, and special situations. 
 - The team utilizes a deep fundamental approach, looks for catalysts to unlock value, and invests opportunistically across the capital structures of companies whose securities they deem to be meaningfully dislocated relative to intrinsic value.
 - Patient approach, pursuing long-term fundamental value and capitalize on distressed/stressed investments when dislocations occur.
 - The team believes that they excel at identifying the fulcrum part of the capital structure and seeks to maximize the returns for their investment thesis.
 - Concentrate the portfolio in best ideas and actively assess the ability to exit or liquidate as part of the investment risk evaluation.

management_company_description: Iguana Investments was founded in 2019 and is a wholly employee-owned investment manager based in Cambridge (UK).  We’re an active manager focusing almost exclusively on developed market equities, with an investment team consisting of four people with over 50 years’ experience, headed up by co-founder and CIO Chris Reid. strategy_description:
Investment Objective: To deliver long-term capital appreciation, measured over a market cycle. The investment target is to deliver 8 to 12% per annum returns with less volatility than than wider market indices. The Iguana Investments Long/Short equity fund is a value-focused low net fund invested predominantly in developed market (listed) equities with typical exposures of 40% US, 30% UK and 30% Western Europe and Scandinavia . The gross exposure is typically in the range of 150 to 170%, with a relatively low, variable net between 0 to 20%. The strategy relies on traditional fundamental company analysis supplemented by quant stock level factor analysis in order to aid with trade timing and execution (approximately an 80:20 split of fundamental: quant).               

UCITS: Iguana Investments have an Irish ICAV umbrella which acts as a host for the UCITS fund. The UCITS fund was launched on 1 April 2021, is a daily dealing vehicle with the initial target market for distribution being the UK and mainland Europe.

Founded in 2019, Astaris Capital Management is an opportunistic, event driven credit and equities fund manager which seeks to benefit from identifying debt and equity valuation dislocations among select European names where there is a catalyst to monetise that dislocation.

strategy_description:
The Astaris Special Situations Master Fund operates an opportunistic, event driven strategy, investing in credit and equities. The Fund aims to exploit catalyst-driven opportunities driven by dislocations between equity and credit and wider market dislocations.

Investors in equity and credit often have very different approaches, risk appetite and return objectives and this, coupled with a siloed approach to asset classes by both the sell-side and buy-side, creates investment opportunities where we can identify the relative value between asset classes.

The Investment Team carries out extensive fundamental research on every idea and deploys capital to long and short opportunities within three distinct sub-strategies: Capital Structure Arbitrage; Alpha Long Strategies; and Distressed Event Shorts.

The result is a concentrated portfolio comprising highly idiosyncratic positions with low correlations to markets and to each other. Disciplined, methodical and rigorous risk management allows the strategy to generate returns throughout the economic cycle, yet preserve capital.

management_company_description:
DCM Systematic SA is an independent, quantitative investment manager based in Geneva, Switzerland. The business was founded by two senior quants from BlueCrest and they were joined by a head of business development from Pictet. The team launched the flagship strategy, Diversified Alpha, in February 2016. The firm is built upon the premise of applying scientific methods to identify a wide range of opportunities within liquid financial markets. Research is at the core of the business and the team is continually striving to improve by exploring new quantitative methods, learning from the markets and enhancing processes. The aim is that with this approach the company can successfully navigate different market environments and the variety of challenges they present.

In 2022, two experienced portfolio managers joined to launch a new venture called Solken Convertible Arbitrage. This is a distinct product within DCM Systematic and combines quantitative techniques with discretionary analysis to explore opportunities in the convertible bond markets.
strategy_description:
Diversified Alpha uses a multi-strategy, non-trend systematic approach to trade liquid futures markets. It aims to deliver uncorrelated, absolute returns through all market environments, applying scientific methods to identify a range of alpha, diversified by asset classes and time-frames. 

Diversified Alpha runs over 30 uncorrelated strategies with a commodity focus. These strategies operate independently of one another and are each designed to capture a specific opportunity. Each has its risk system with controls and constraints that are relevant to the markets being traded and often include forward-looking scenarios. In general, they complement one another and have time horizons ranging from short- (5-10 days) to medium-term (2-8 weeks).

Risk management and portfolio construction combine longer-term strategic targets for the portfolio volatility, asset class allocations, and strategy weights with a daily optimization process designed to enable strategies to deliver their target volatility within their risk constraints. This process aims to ensure a high level of diversification by trading approach, time frame, and markets.

Research is viewed as a continuous process focused on enhancing and improving Diversified Alpha, either through discovering new sources of alpha, creating differentiated trading strategies, or updating existing processes.

management_company_description: Sagefield Capital, a Dallas-based hedge fund manager founded in 2019 by former Citadel Portfolio Manager Mark Schlueter and former Highland Capital Portfolio Manager Jonathan Lamensdorf, manages commingled funds and separately managed account assets. The equity-focused, market neutral multi-strategy fund includes equity relative value and event driven. The equity relative value strategy, which focuses on low-net and sector-specific investments covering Natural Resources, Utilities, Industrials, and Energy Transition, also has a standalone fund. Merger arbitrage strategies within the multi-strategy fund provide added diversification through additional uncorrelated return streams. strategy_description:
The Firm believes that by combining uncorrelated, market-neutral strategies into a multi-strategy fund, the Fund should be able to achieve its return objective with lower levels of volatility than could be achieved in a single strategy fund. The Investment Manager believes the overall risk of the Fund may be materially reduced due to the well-understood portfolio diversification effects received from combining such strategies together. The Firm also believes constructing a portfolio of market-neutral strategies may create a multi-strategy fund with performance that is both uncorrelated to traditional assets and absolute return driven. 

The Fund is an equity-focused, market-neutral fund employing six strategies at inception that the Investment Manager believes have little to no correlation with one another: (i) Natural Resources, (ii) Utilities, (iii) Industrials, (iv) Energy Transition, (v) Merger Arbitrage, and (vi) Special Situations. The Firm allocates capital across the Fund’s strategies by analyzing the risk and return characteristics of each individual strategy, the resulting risk/reward of the combined portfolio, as well as how the current or future market environment might affect each strategy and the Fund. The correlations of each strategy to one another and to the overall Fund are a major component of this analysis. The Firm may add additional strategies to the Fund’s portfolio over time.

management_company_description:
Oxbow Capital Management ("Oxbow") is a Hong Kong-based asset manager, which was founded in December 2014 by Wesley Wong. As the CIO, Wesley is responsible for leading the firm's investment process. Oxbow manages a Pan-Asia long/short equity strategy and a long-only India equity strategy that invest based on fundamental analysis.

strategy_description:
Oxbow invests long and short across Asian equity markets, as well as in non-Asian companies with significant Asia-related business drivers. The strategy has a core focus on India, Japan, Greater China, and South Korea, and employs a fundamental, concentrated and liquid approach. Key tenets of the firm's investment strategy are a collaborative and flexible research process that uses bottom-up fundamental analysis focused on assessing intrinsic value driven by earnings power and the path to value, and utilizing top-down thematic and sector analysis to develop differentiated long-term views on companies. 

Oxbow takes concentrated positions and uses clear trade construction to monetize high conviction opportunities. In addition, Oxbow strives to be patient and disciplined in position implementation and portfolio construction in order to take advantage when risk-reward dynamics move in its favor. 

Oxbow's risk management philosophy is based on the belief that the first line of defense is high conviction risk-reward assessment based on fundamentals. The Fund typically holds 15-25 core long positions and 20-35 core short positions. The Fund has typical gross exposures of 150-200% of NAV and the target range of net exposure is 0-50% of NAV, although such net exposure can exceed this range based on Oxbow's view of the opportunity set and market conditions.

Our platform is rooted across three key asset frameworks: [1] Equities (Fundamental, Event-Driven, Activism), [2] Credit (Corporate & Sovereign Credit, Structured Credit), and [3] Private Investing (Private Credit, Insurance Solutions, and Venture Capital).

strategy_description:
Since our inception in 1995, Third Point has been an active investor in corporate credit for much of the firm’s history. The Firm’s approach to corporate credit is catalyst-driven total return expectations based on a probabilistic assessment of upside/downside rather than yield to maturity.  Third Point employs its opportunistic investment style across the entire risk spectrum, looking for attractive idiosyncratic situations in Investment Grade, High Yield, Leveraged Loans and liquid Distressed. The Firm meaningfully increased credit exposure during the Telecom distressed cycle (2001-2003), the post-GFC distressed cycle (2008-2010), the Energy sector dislocation (2015-2016) and again at the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic. In the wake of the GFC, Ian Wallace joined the Firm to manage the corporate credit portfolio and Stephen Schatzman joined in 2014 as the Firm began to build out our credit investment team.

In September 2024, Third Point LLC launched a dedicated credit fund, Third Point Corporate Credit Opportunities (the “Fund”), to capitalize on the Firm’s track record of investing in dislocated corporate credit securities. We believe the current market backdrop is one of the most attractive for corporate credit since the GFC, with elevated interest rates, volatility, and sector dispersion creating attractive total return opportunities in liquid credit. 

The Fund seeks to generate attractive, risk-adjusted returns across long and short investments in performing (stressed) & non-performing (distressed) credit via a liquid, open-ended structure, targeting 60-90% average net exposure. Investors have an option to elect target distributions of 3 to 5% annualized.

strategy_description:
The World Carbon Fund (the “Fund”) employs investment strategies across multiple regulated carbon markets. The Fund has the dual objectives to generate absolute returns with a low correlation to traditional asset classes and to have a direct impact on climate change.

The Fund deploys capital across two complementary strategies within a clearly defined risk framework: Core Strategy and Alpha Strategies. The Core Strategy seeks to generate returns from directional tactical allocations across multiple carbon markets to capture the long-term risk premium in each carbon market combined with tactical alpha. The Alpha Strategies seek to generate returns by implementing a range of short-term alpha trading strategies, which are categorised as arbitrage, short-term directional, relative value and carry. Alpha Strategies are developed with the aim to extract positive returns irrelevant of market direction by identifying inefficiencies and idiosyncratic trading opportunities. 

The World Carbon Fund has Article 9 classification under the EU Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (“SFDR”) and EU Taxonomy. It seeks, through its investment activities, to contribute directly to the reduction in global CO2 emissions. In addition, the investment advisor contributes a fixed percentage of performance fees to purchasing and cancelling carbon allowances. 

The Fund achieved its 3-year track record on 24 February 2023 and has generated a total return of 88.6% (23.6% annualised return)* from inception to 31 January 2023. Assets under management now exceed $150m.

esg_approach_description:
PAAMCO Prisma is committed to incorporating environmental, social, and governance (“ESG”) factors into our decision-making processes.

We have adopted ESG principles to help guide our business; they represent the values of our organization and are factors we consider when evaluating potential corporate partners and conducting business.
• Trust and Transparency: Nurture a culture where honesty, integrity and fairness are the foundation of everything we do. Have clear accountability through oversight, proper governance, and strong alignment of interest.
• Foster Diversity & Inclusion: Promote a cohesive and diverse workplace, where a breadth of experiences and backgrounds are valued as instrumental to creating optimal outcomes for all stakeholders.
• Advocate for Planet Earth: Challenge ourselves to be more cognizant of our environmental responsibility and strive to improve our environmental footprint through employee and partner education.
• Community Commitment: Engage in local communities through active participation, service, and philanthropic efforts to enrich the lives of underserved members of such communities, employees, and their families.
• Employee Wellbeing: Provide competitive pay, healthcare, training and educational opportunities, as well as other family and wellness programs.

Due Diligence – As part of our due diligence process, we engage with third-party portfolio managers (“Portfolio Managers”) to understand how they incorporate ESG factors into their investment and business management processes.
At its foundation, our assessment, which leverages themes identified by the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board, considers if a Portfolio Manager has adopted a voluntary ESG framework or established an ESG policy. Our research also includes working to understand if a Portfolio Manager identifies and considers ESG risks as part of its investment due diligence and what data sources help to inform this process. Risk professionals also leverage a third-party ESG rating resource to provide ESG snapshot scores for a Portfolio Manager’s relevant exposures; this provides another data point in understanding ESG implications for prospective Portfolio Managers.
From a business management perspective, our research helps us understand the diversity and inclusion practices of a Portfolio Manager, what types of environmental initiatives they have established for their business, and if their governance framework incorporates industry best practices.
The results of this work are included in both the investment memo and operational due diligence risk report presented to the Firm’s Investment Committee (“IC”), which is ultimately responsible for determining whether a Portfolio Manager is eligible for investment.
ESG is just one of many factors considered in an allocation decision. Our expectation is that Portfolio Managers will be at different stages of ESG integration, and as such PAAMCO Prisma will have additional ESG-specific discussions and engagement with these Portfolio Managers. PAAMCO Prisma reserves the right to reject, or withdraw from, as applicable, a Portfolio Manager whose investment program, on balance, is determined to be incompatible with the Firm’s ESG principles.
Monitoring – For Portfolio Managers approved by the IC, ESG questions will be included in an annual ESG-focused due diligence questionnaire and covered within our ongoing monitoring reviews of Portfolio Managers. Depending on a Portfolio Manager’s investment strategy, ESG may also be a more regular topic for portfolio update meetings.

Oversight & Accountability
The ESG Taskforce (the “Taskforce”), comprised of PAAMCO Prisma’s CEO and leaders from legal, compliance, portfolio management, operations, and investor services, is responsible for the ESG policy, which is ultimately reviewed and approved by the firm’s Executive Committee (“EC”).
The Taskforce, which provides periodic reporting to the EC, also:
• Coordinates ESG training and resources for employees;
• Oversees the implementation of ESG activities that support the Firm’s ESG principles;
• Regularly reviews such activities for potential enhancements;
• Works closely with the Operations and Investment teams to establish ESG reporting requested by investors; and
• Encourages collaboration with third-party organizations to improve engagement on ESG principles.

Voya Investment Management (Voya IM) is the asset management business of Voya Financial (NYSE: VOYA), a leading health, wealth and investment company where 6,000 employees help over 14 million clients be well-planned, 
well-invested and well-protected. Reliability is why our clients hire us and why they trust us to navigate the path ahead.

Voya IM is one of the 50 largest institutional asset managers globally,[1] overseeing USD 342 billion[2] in assets across public and private fixed income, equities, multi-asset solutions and alternative strategies. Drawing on a 50-year legacy of active investing and the expertise of over 300 investment professionals, Voya IM offers both traditional products and solutions and actively managed strategies that cannot be easily replicated by an index. We partner with a substantial and diversified client base—from insurance companies, pension funds, endowments and foundations, sovereign wealth funds and consultants, to financial intermediaries and individual investors. 

[1] Pension & Investments, Largest Money Managers 2022 Survey, based on assets as of 12/31/21.
[2] Data is as of 03/31/2025. Voya IM assets of 342B include proprietary insurance general account assets of $34,296 million on a market value basis. Voya IM assets, as reported in Voya Financial SEC filings, include general account assets valued on a statutory book value basis and total approximately $343B
strategy_description:
The Voya Mortgage Investment Fund invests in the U.S. residential mortgage market and investments related to U.S. residential mortgages. Voya has developed a balanced approach that blends quantitative prepayment modelling with fundamental research on the housing market, mortgage origination and mortgage servicing. Outperformance is driven by the ability to identify prepayment trends before consensus. The Fund is not a distressed or credit mortgage fund and invests primarily in GNMA and Agency MBS and related instruments with a strong concentration in mortgage derivatives, such as inverse floaters, interest-only (IO), inverse IOs (IIOs), and principal-only (POs), as well as mortgage-related investments such as credit risk transfers (CRTs) and mortgage servicing rights (MSRs). Fundamental drivers include (i) prepayment analysis and research, (ii) exploiting structural market inefficiencies, and (iii) targeting relative return opportunities in the broad mortgage market.  The Fund is also managed towards a zero duration on both a portfolio basis and a key rate duration basis. As a result, the Fund has exhibited strong performance over time with little to no correlation with other asset classes or other hedge funds.

We have been managing structured mortgages since the early 1990s and as of June 30, 2023, manage approximately US $4.8 billion in mortgage derivative portfolios, making Voya IM one of the largest participants in this arena. The Voya Mortgage Investment Fund was launched in January 2011 and is managed by a highly experienced mortgage team comprised of PhDs and seasoned mortgage investors. The genesis of the Fund came from a proprietary fund—managed in the same investment style, excluding the use of leverage or shorting—which Voya IM started managing in 1995. As such, we have a long track record in successfully managing mortgage derivatives.

name: Deltroit Directional Opportunities Fund
management_company_description:
Deltroit is a London based alternative investment firm managing assets for institutional investors, private banks and individuals. 

Lord Hintze founded Deltroit Asset Management to continue the management of his long-standing Directional Opportunities Fund, established in 2005. At Deltroit Asset Management, Lord Hintze and his team manage research-driven credit strategies through a bottom-up fundamental approach, supplemented and balanced by top-down geopolitical and macro analysis. This process also provides for thematic investments across adjacent global markets, to build a multi-asset investment portfolio to further supplement returns. 

Deltroit Asset Management (UK) LLP (“Deltroit”) is a limited liability partnership incorporated in England and Wales under partnership number OC448813, and with its registered office at 1st Floor, 50 Pall Mall, London, United Kingdom, SW1Y 5JH. Deltroit is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FRN: 1020296).
strategy_description:
The Deltroit Directional Opportunities Fund (DOF) is a high conviction, credit centric fund managed directly by Lord Hintze since 2005 and supported by his long-standing investment and operations teams. 

The Fund seeks to harvest the excess risk premia we believe is available from credit index tranches as the market persistently overpays for credit default insurance. To augment returns, this Core Credit strategy includes global Single Name credit investments and Opportunistic credit positions that present through time in both physical and synthetic markets. 

The Fund's investment process combines geopolitical, macroeconomic and thematic analysis with bottom-up fundamental corporate research. The Fund team's wider expertise then extends the core investment process to identify long/short opportunities across adjacent global assets in equity and macro, building a multi-asset investment portfolio to further supplement returns.

management_company_description: Eicos is an alternative asset management firm founded by Pierre de Chillaz (CIO), Erwan de Lepinay (Head of Research & Trading) and Askan Denstaedt (CEO) focusing on a European opportunistic credit strategy. strategy_description:
Eicos Master Fund is Eicos’s flagship absolute return strategy focusing on European opportunistic credit investments . The fund is unlevered, long-biased and invests in idiosyncratic and event-driven opportunities. Eicos utilises bottom-up and fundamental underwriting coupled with thorough relative value analysis as part of its investment process to (i) identify the best risk adjusted investment opportunities considering margin of safety and (ii) constantly re-underwrite the portfolio in light of applicable market dynamics. 

The strategy utilises a Transition Framework incorporating micro, macro and structural factors which aim to anticipate changes in risk profile amid the prevalent market fragmentation in Europe. 

Eicos utilises a dynamic risk management model with regular stress testing of the portfolio to identify applicable risk factors in order to optimise the portfolio coupled with an active hedging overlay.

name: Perryridge Capital
management_company_description:
Perryridge Capital is is a global, bottom-up fundamental long-short fund focused on investments predominantly within the healthcare, industrials, business services and adjacent technology sectors that launched July 15, 2024.  

Perryridge’s Founder and Chief Investment Officer is Arthur Wit.  Arthur was most recently a Partner and Managing Director at Lone Pine Capital for over 10 years, and the senior investment professional responsible for healthcare and industrial investments. While at Lone Pine, Arthur pursued a substantively similar strategy and investment approach from 2013 to 2023 to that which will be deployed at Perryridge. Lone Pine Capital backed the launch of Perryridge Capital via an investment in the Perryridge Capital management company.

Perryridge seeks to be relatively concentrated with a focus on long-term value creation – compounding capital at a rate that exceeds the broader equity market with less volatility over the long term – and event-driven short selling. The investment strategy is based on a repeatable process of first-principles analysis and deep, immersive research. It seeks to preserve capital and limit volatility through disciplined underwriting, active portfolio management, and by deploying capital across diverse and uncorrelated sectors. Investments center around companies with monopolistic structure in complex and/or niche markets where there is durable growth and long-term pricing power. The Fund’s opportunity set includes companies in developed markets across the market cap spectrum with a significant portion of exposure in market capitalizations between $1B and $10B as well as in less discovered and/or under-covered companies predominantly in the U.S and Europe. 

Perryridge will deploy a concentrated portfolio of 10-20 long positions and 15-30 short positions.  Expected exposure is ~100% long by 50-60% short, although net exposure may vary from 20-70% according to the opportunity set available.  Average position sizing will be 6% for longs, with the highest conviction positions at 10-12%.  Average short position size will be 1.5% with the highest conviction shorts at 2-3%.
strategy_description:
Perryridge Partners is a concentrated, sector-focused long/short equity fund that launched July 15, 2024.  The firm's investment objective is to deliver superior risk-adjusted returns by applying deep expertise across the firm's core sectors, including healthcare, industrials, business services and adjacent technology companies. 
The investment strategy for the fund is based on what we believe to be a repeatable process of first-principles analysis and deep, immersive research. Perryridge will make concentrated investments in areas of elevated market inefficiency, with a focus on long-term value creation. The strategy seeks to preserve capital and limit volatility via disciplined underwriting, active portfolio management, and by deploying capital across diverse and uncorrelated sectors.
The fund’s opportunity set includes companies in developed markets across the market cap spectrum and emphasizes event-driven short selling. Perryridge will focus on areas of elevated technical and business model complexity, firms that span sector boundaries, and areas of rapid change. Perryridge will target these companies in the healthcare, industrials, business services, and adjacent technology sectors. The portfolio will include meaningful exposure to all target sectors given the large target universe and advantages of constructing a portfolio of varied and unrelated securities.
region_exposure_description: Perryridge will concentrate on the richest ecosystems of healthcare and industrial innovation: The United States and Europe. We may also consider investments in other developed markets, primarily Japan, Korea, Australia, and New Zealand.

Through our multistrategy investment platform, we deliver customized solutions across global public equities and US alternative assets, serving as a trusted partner to family offices, ultra-high-net-worth individuals, and select institutional clients who value long-term thinking and aligned interests. 

Our Houston-based platform leverages global networks cultivated over three decades to source and execute investments across distinct strategies. We combine deep fundamental research capabilities with the agility inherent to a principal-backed structure, enabling us to act decisively when opportunities emerge. Each investment vehicle operates under clearly defined mandates designed to capture specific market opportunities while managing risk through thoughtful portfolio construction. We empower family offices and ultra-high-net-worth investors with solutions that preserve generational wealth through expertise, seamless cross-border capabilities, and privileged access to exclusive opportunities.
strategy_description:
Tempest Peak Global Opportunities is an equity hedge fund pursuing absolute returns through disciplined value investing across global public markets. Founded in 2020 by seasoned investment professionals Vivek Rao (CIO) and David Chao (CEO), the fund targets undervalued securities worldwide using fundamental analysis and a patient capital approach.

Core Investment Philosophy: The fund identifies companies trading at significant discounts to intrinsic value with measurable catalysts for price appreciation. Unlike US-focused value strategies, the fund's global mandate provides access to a substantially larger opportunity set spanning developed and emerging markets across Asia-Pacific, Europe, Latin America, and North America.

Strategy Implementation: Portfolio construction emphasizes high-conviction positions (typically 15-25 holdings) with position sizes ranging 4-8% of net assets. The fund maintains 85-100% net long exposure with selective use of leverage not exceeding 130% gross. Investment decisions integrate quantitative screening with qualitative management assessment and systematic risk evaluation.

Competitive Differentiation: The investment team's established global networks provide institutional-level due diligence capabilities typically unavailable to similarly-sized managers. This infrastructure advantage, combined with sector expertise spanning technology, industrials, chemicals, and telecommunications, enables identification of overlooked opportunities in less-efficient international markets.

Talent-Driven Business
Artisan Partners’ business is designed to optimize the time and focus of investment talent. The experienced business leadership team supports the firm’s investment management capabilities by managing a centralized infrastructure, which allows investment professionals to focus primarily on making investment decisions and generating returns for clients.

Thoughtful Growth
Firm evolution requires thoughtful growth. A lack of growth or growth for growth's sake can make a business unattractive to investment talent. The firm’s entrepreneurial mindset keeps us actively looking for ways to maximize long-term career opportunities for existing investment professionals and make the firm attractive to prospective investment talent. It also ensures that Artisan stays committed to providing investment solutions that are aligned with long-term global trends and that are relevant to clients.

strategy_description:
The Artisan Partners Credit Team launched the Artisan Credit Opportunities Fund with a straight-forward goal: generating attractive risk-adjusted returns through an opportunistic approach that pursues long and short investments along the capital structure of leveraged corporate issuers. Using a high-conviction, bottom-up fundamental research process, our team looks to take advantage of the illiquidity premium and inherently asymmetric risk profile of credit investments across multiple sectors, regions and styles. Having honed our skills through years of investing in the asset class, we believe the disciplined execution of our process enables the building of a portfolio that can deliver value regardless of the market environment.

The team utilizes quantitative screens and qualitative factors to identify overlooked and under-appreciated investment opportunities. The team’s research process has four primary pillars: business quality, financial strength and flexibility, downside analysis and value identification.
region_exposure_description: There are no specific limits on the instrument type or geographic location of the portfolio’s holdings in the Credit Opportunities strategy. While the strategy is not geographically constrained, the team’s expertise and experience leads them to focus primarily on US-based issuers. Attractive investments are, however, occasionally found outside of the US, most commonly in Canada and Europe.

name: First Light Focus Fund
management_company_description:
First Light Asset Management is an investment firm focused on identifying health care companies it believes provide high investment potential for clients. Its 14 team members, including six senior investment professionals, invest primarily in micro- to mid-cap stocks across a diversified set of health care subsectors — biotech, medical devices and equipment, diagnostic tools, health care information technology, health care services, and specialty pharmaceuticals. 
First Light believes the following are key to their approach to health care investing:
• History of finding innovative and disruptive companies that change the way health care is practiced
• A consistent process that drives us to companies that are delivering better care at a lower price
• Limited-capacity investment vehicles, allowing for high concentration in the firm’s best ideas, even though they are often micro- to small-cap stocks
• Capitalizing on greater pricing inefficiency among smaller companies
• Diversification to take advantage of low correlation between subsectors
• Probability-weighted analysis to form firm’s view of a stock’s intrinsic value, which determines long or short position and sizing
strategy_description: The First Light Focus Fund (the “Fund”) is a concentrated, long-biased small- to micro-cap limited partnership seeking to invest in innovative and disruptive companies within the large and growing health care sector. The Fund aims to achieve a high level of capital appreciation and opportunistically looks to short for alpha creation, while minimizing undue risk to the portfolio. First Light Asset Management, LLC (“First Light”) primarily pursues this investment objective through longer-term investments in publicly traded equity securities it believes will create value over a 2 to 5+ year time horizon. The firm diversifies the portfolio among what it believes are “best-of-breed” health care companies operating in various health care subsectors, including medical devices and equipment, diagnostic tools, health care information technology, biotech, health care services, and specialty pharmaceuticals. First Light believes the inefficient pricing of securities within the small- to micro-cap range, combined with the growth in health care spending, is creating opportunities the investment team can capitalize on through its proprietary investment process. In First Light’s view, small companies are, in certain instances, better positioned to react to the changing health care landscape as they can often more quickly respond to changing market dynamics and provide innovative solutions to address market needs — such as reducing the cost of care and improving patient outcomes.

management_company_description: Starboard Value LP (“Starboard”) is an investment adviser with a focused fundamental approach to investing, primarily in the public and private securities of publicly traded U.S. companies.  Starboard seeks to invest in deeply undervalued companies and actively engage with management teams and boards of directors to identify and execute on opportunities to unlock value for the benefit of all shareholders.
strategy_description:
Starboard's Established Investment Strategy: Value, Plan, Path:

• 'Value' is a determination based on hard asset values and/or highly discounted cash flows (not relative value multiples).
• 'Plan' is the identification of companies with (i) a good core business generating substantial earnings and cash flow and (ii) a failing growth initiative losing money and negatively impacting consolidated results. In order to refocus on the good core business, these failing growth initiatives should be exited, potentially resulting in significant improvements in consolidated earnings and cash flow.
• 'Path' relates to Starboard's ability to mount an election contest, if necessary, with the goal of making changes to the board of directors to seek to ensure that the 'Plan' to create value is implemented.

Starboard's Investment Opportunities:

• Focus on situations where there is an opportunity to drive operational change
• Seek to have a consistent and formulaic approach to measuring position and portfolio risk
• Typical portfolio of 20 - 35 investments divided between "lead" and "seed" positions
• Aims to practice a disciplined methodology around position sizing and portfolio hedging

name: Lykos Global Master Fund LP
management_company_description: Lykos Global Management is a newly launched Event-Driven investment firm focused on Equity Capital Markets. Lykos was founded by Nick Laster, the youngest ever Partner at Soros Fund Management (“SFM”). Nick worked at SFM for nearly a decade as Global Head of Equity Capital Markets and Late-Stage Privates. Lykos believe they have developed an “All-Weather”, idiosyncratic strategy that can generate uncorrelated, positive returns in any market environment. They feel their approach preserves the appeal of traditional Event-Driven mandates (i.e., short duration trades, clearly defined catalysts), while also enabling greater capital efficiency and a less cyclical return profile than conventional strategies.  Lykos went live with two sizable anchors in March, 2024 and have generated performance despite muted activity in capital markets. With a historic backlog of companies needing to tap public markets, they believe the set-up for 2025 and beyond is highly compelling.
strategy_description: The Fund seeks to compound capital at attractive risk adjusted returns through the market cycle by investing in high quality, competitively advantaged businesses undergoing event driven dislocations.  The three distinct but complementary sub-strategies are Late Stage Privates (LTSP), Core Equity Capital Markets (ECM) and Tactical Opportunities (TacOpps). The LTSP piece focuses on high quality pre-IPO privates (companies going public within twelve months) that comprise up to twenty five percent of the portfolio. The ECM piece seeks to establish positions in exceptional businesses through IPOs and other equity issuance while the TacOpps seeks to capitalize on idiosyncratic, liquidity-driven events in newly public companies.

name: Bengal 2 Fund
management_company_description: Bengal Asset Management, LLC, a U.S. SEC registered investment advisor, was formed in April 2013 to focus on investment opportunities in Japan. In June 2013 BAM launched its Japan focused equity Long/Short strategy. Driven by a core team of diverse individuals who have been with the firm since inception, the team leverages their extensive collective experience both in Asia and globally to bring a powerful network of relationships, research depth, and broad market expertise across all facets of the business.  In June 2019, Bengal Research Japan, KK(“BRJ”) was established and licensed in Japan for investment advisory.
strategy_description:
The Bengal 2 Fund is a Japan focused long-short equity fund. Our investment philosophy combines a core fundamental approach that allows us to express our medium-long term outlook, with a shorter term tactical component that utilizes a broad range of quantitative tools. The balance between the various styles will vary depending on the type of market environment we are facing. Our varied approach to investment makes our strategy more dynamic in nature and allows us to deploy capital in a manner that aims to optimize our focus towards the best opportunities in a highly risk managed fashion. 

The Fund makes public equity investments predominately in Japan through a hedged approach by taking long as well as short positions. Investments are identified through a combination of our fundamental, tactical and quantitative research. The portfolios are built from the bottom-up. They generally do not have significant idea or theme biases but will take advantage of any short-term or long-term trend identified through bottom-up or top-down analysis. At any given time expect the Fund to have 7-15 themes in the portfolio. Investments are made across the market cap structure (from small to mega cap) with the balance of the portfolio primarily dependent on liquidity and the prevailing market environment. Short positions are used to both mitigate against general market risk and to enhance performance.

strategy_description:
The fund is dedicated to artificial intelligence and related investments, guided by three core principles:

1/Intelligence technology breakthroughs as the primary investment thesis
2/Intelligence itself representing the largest-scale application
3/Focus on tracking globally leading innovation teams and R&D capabilities

The fund combines fundamental research and a balanced approach to risk.  emphasizing technical expertise, business model innovation, and sustainable long-term returns through multi-strategy portfolio management.

Portfolio Allocation：
Infrastructure Layer (25%): high-performance computing design and manufacturing houses, data centers, cloud infrastructure, and networking equipments
Platform Layer (30-35%): LLM developers, AI training platforms, cloud service providers, enterprise AI solutions, and open-source framework creators
Application Layer (30-40%): Internet platforms, enterprise digitalization solutions, and AI-native applications

Stock selection is based on competitiveness (technology moat, product roadmap and etc), market position (market share, customer retention and etc) and financial metrics (revenue growth, profitability, cash flow) and valuation comparisons.

The fund employs long-short strategies with dynamic position adjustment, derivatives-based hedging, and diversification limits (no single position exceeding 20%). The investment process combines industry research, company assessment and risk-optimized portfolio construction.

Annualized ITD Net Return is a hypothetical rate of return that converts the cumulative ITD return of the fund to an annual rate computed on a time-weighted basis. ITD net returns represent the cumulative returns since inception, compounded monthly.

Firm AUM represents the unaudited estimated net assets under management of LibreMax and Trimaran and includes subscriptions/redemptions as of the date of this document. Trimaran Advisors’ AUM is calculated based upon the principal balance of collateral obligations and cash within the CLOs under management, as well as the principal balance of collateral obligations held in warehouse facilities. For entities within their respective investment periods, LibreMax’s AUM includes committed but uncalled capital.  For entities outside their respective investment periods, LibreMax’s AUM includes the NAV of the Fund and uncalled capital commitments required to pay down any subscription facility utilization or fund future trade commitments.

Annualized ITD Standard Deviation is a measure of the portfolio’s variation of return from its average return since inception. 

Sharpe Ratio is a measure of excess return per unit of risk of the portfolio since the Fund’s inception. It is the annualized value of the excess return over the annualized return of 1 month US Treasury Bills, which is used to represent a risk free rate of return, divided by the portfolio’s Annualized Standard Deviation. 

Max Drawdown represents the largest consecutive percentage decline from peak to trough since the Fund’s inception. Months to Recover represents the number of months from the Fund’s trough to a new high (the recovery).

Correlations measure the relationship between the Onshore Feeder Fund’s performance to the S&P 500 and the Barclays HY Bond Indices since the Onshore Feeder Fund’s inception (10/1/10). The S&P 500 Total Return Index is an unmanaged index of common stock prices of 500 widely held U.S. stocks that include the reinvestment of dividends. The Barclays U.S. High Yield Index provides a measure of performance for USD-denominated, high yield, fixed-rate corporate bond market. Securities classified as high yield if the middle rating of Moody’s, Fitch and S&P is Ba1/BB+/BB+ or below. Gross Exposure is calculated as total market value of all long credit positions held by the Fund, plus the notional value of credit derivatives where the Fund is selling protection (the “Gross Long Credit Market Value”), divided by the Fund’s estimated net asset value, prior to any adjustments for end of month redemptions or subsequent month subscriptions, (the “Fund NAV”). Cash, cash equivalents and derivatives used for hedging purposes are excluded. 

Net Exposure is calculated as (A) Gross Long Credit Market Value less (B) the sum of the market value of all credit securities held short by the Fund, the market value adjusted notional of any credit derivatives where the Fund is buying protection, and the delta adjusted market value of any options (the “Gross Short Credit Market Value”); divided by the Fund NAV. Cash, cash equivalents and interest rate derivatives are excluded.

IInterest Rate Duration, or effective duration, is a calculation of the interest rate sensitivity of a security to a change in interest rates. Interest Rate Duration is calculated using cash flows based on internal cash flow projections based upon changes in interest rates derived from LibreMax’s proprietary model using base case assumptions, which are available upon request.

Spread Duration, or modified duration, is a metric of price sensitivity calculated as a percentage change in price for a unit change in spread. Bond cash flows are generated from LibreMax's proprietary model using base case assumptions, which are available upon request. Price sensitivity is measured after the discounting spread (over the spot curve) is shocked up and down by 50 basis points.

management_company_description:
Cheyne Capital was founded in 2000 by Jonathan Lourie (CEO) and Stuart Fiertz (President) after working together at Morgan Stanley. 

Cheyne is one of Europe's leading alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs) with c. 170 partners and employees.

Cheyne invests across the capital structure from the senior debt to the equity of corporates and real estate. With an investment philosophy grounded in rigorous fundamental analysis, the firm’s main areas of expertise are: Real Estate Debt, Corporate Credit and Risk Transfer, European Strategic Value Credit, and Liquid Alternatives.
strategy_description:
The flagship Cheyne European Strategic Value Credit (SVC) Fund series invests in predominantly senior secured debt obligations, with a focus on providing constructive capital solutions to mid-market corporates. The strategy focuses primarily on the secondary purchase of senior secured loans from original lenders at significant discounts to par, providing holistic restructuring solutions and/or rescue capital to facilitate a normalisation and recovery following a period of financial stress. 
 
To maximise flexibility and capitalise on less crowded, underserved segments of the credit market, the funds are capacity constrained, with a strategic emphasis on mid-market opportunities and smaller transaction sizes. The team places emphasis on downside protection and loss avoidance, with entry valuations that correspond more closely with recovery value floors under worst case outcomes.
region_exposure_description: The portfolio maintains a strong European focus, capitalising on the continent’s divergent economic trajectories and the complexity of its cultural, linguistic, and legal frameworks. These dynamics create pricing inefficiencies and a broader spectrum of opportunities for private credit managers to exploit.

portfolio_additional_details:
The portfolio is broken down into four main components; Stressed Situations, Restructuring, Rescue Financing and Opportunistic.

Stressed Situations: the fund targets secondary purchases of debt at meaningful discounts to fair value, underpinned by comprehensive fundamental analysis. Investment theses are generally predicated on discounted entry prices with a clear path to par and may incorporate covenant relief or other waivers to facilitate operational turnaround.

Restructuring: this approach focuses on acquiring debt at significant discounts to par and intrinsic value, where the thesis is driven by a formal balance sheet restructuring. Transactions typically involve partial debt-to-equity conversions alongside the reinstatement of new debt facilities or revised borrowing terms.

Rescue Financing: the fund originates and provides new money solutions to businesses facing financial or liquidity challenges. These may include stressed refinancing arrangements or liquidity bridge financings, structured as senior or super-senior secured instruments.

Opportunistic: this strategy seeks to exploit periods of elevated market volatility and price dislocation in tradeable debt securities following sector or market shocks.

These exclusions enable us to filter out companies at an early stage that are highly unlikely to make it through our due diligence process.

exact_name: Zentific Asia Opportunities Offshore Feeder Fund Limited
management_company_description: Zentific Investment Management Limited is a Hong Kong-based equity quant boutique. Our quantitative insights aim to emphasize faster Trading Strategies with an intraday to several week time horizon alongside gauges of Local Sentiment. The research process seeks to focus on local and niche data sources with a robust technology infrastructure for natural language processing (NLP) and AI techniques to gather large/unstructured/text data sets.
strategy_description:
The Zentific team consists entirely of investment professionals who have been Asian quantitative specialists for the vast majority/entirety of their careers and who bring together what we believe to be deep local knowledge combined with cutting edge data science abilities. The team members are all based locally and work in an integrated PM-research-trading team which we believe allows the group to be more focused and connected to Asia-Pacific's diverse and nuanced markets and drives innovative research ideas.

The Zentific Asia Opportunities Offshore Master Fund is a systematic market neutral equity long/short hedge fund launched in July of 2015 with two feeder funds: Zentific Asia Opportunities Offshore Feeder Fund ("Fund") and Zentific Asia Opportunities Offshore Feeder Fund II ("Fund II") sit under the Master Fund. Fund II has a higher risk profile than Fund. The Fund targets meaningful exposure across Asia and has markedly more exposure in EM markets than DM markets. Zentific's research process is focused on local and niche data sources and judicious use is made of NLP and AI techniques (for large/unstructured/text data sets) in all parts of the investment process where it makes sense.

Zentific's investment process uses four main alpha drivers - the Macro Model and three sets of stock selection insights: Fundamentals, Trading Strategies and Local Sentiment. The Macro Model gauges current market conditions versus history and targets more weight to stock selection signals that are expected to work in the coming macro environment. This model is based on a deep set of slow and fast moving country-specific macro-level data sets. Additionally, if the model views the period to offer fewer opportunities, the level of gross exposure will be adjusted.

The strategy's stock selection drivers are grouped into three categories: Trading Strategies - react to flows and events, trading on shorter term mis-pricings, some of which can be implemented intraday or real-time; Local Sentiment - access local data sources (news, portals, blogs) to gain insights on the sentiment of local market participants, often using multi-lingual NLP/deep learning techniques; Fundamentals - focus on the fundamentals of companies and their values in the medium term and uses for example alternative data, industry and country specific insights and accounting insights.

Zentific uses a customised risk model (adjusted to measure many country-specific risk factors) and an in-house transaction cost model, along with the alpha forecasts from the stock selection models, to build the portfolio. Risk management is built into all levels of the investment process, from selective neutralisation of risk factors in the alpha weighting process to both linear and non-linear controls on exposure to common style factors like momentum, value and low risk in the optimisation.

strategy_description:
The Suvretta Master Fund, Ltd. (“Suvretta Master Fund” or “Suvretta”) is a long/short equity strategy that began investing on September 1, 2012, and is managed by Aaron Cowen. Suvretta Master Fund’s investment objective is to generate positive absolute returns throughout market cycles by investing primarily in highly liquid, large-capitalization equity securities, both long and short. Suvretta adheres to an “industry before company” investment framework that we believe enables us to construct an “all-weather” portfolio across sectors and market factors.

Suvretta’s core investment strategy is to own good companies in industries that we perceive to have secular growth and on the short side, seek companies in industries that we believe are in secular decline. Utilizing what we believe to be our differentiated “industry before company” investment framework, the team conducts due diligence on both industry and business fundamentals, focusing on competitive strengths and weaknesses, revenue growth, profitability, liquidity, and free cash flow. The investment team develops models for each company in which it may invest to determine earnings potential and underlying intrinsic value. Suvretta typically aims to hold core investments for one to three years, however, positions and position sizes are managed relative to disciplined price-target estimates, subject to changing fundamental theses and economic conditions. The portfolio contains approximately 20 to 40 long positions and 15 to 30 short positions, and the top 10 long positions typically comprise around 60% of the portfolio. On average, gross exposure ranges between 150% and 225% and net exposure ranges between 30% and 60%. The portfolio is primarily focused on companies in North America and Western Europe.

The Suvretta Master Fund portfolio is managed by Aaron Cowen, in collaboration with Director of Research, Corey Metz, and their team of sector-focused analysts. Mr. Cowen has over 28 years of experience as a Portfolio Manager and analyst at Suvretta, Soros, SAC (now Point 72), Karsch and Baupost. Mr. Metz spent 15 years as a Portfolio Manager and Analyst at Point 72 and Caxton Associates, prior to joining Suvretta in 2022.

name: Unifi Alpha Master Fund Ltd
management_company_description:
Unifi Asset Management is a market-neutral relative value asset management firm based in NYC. We primarily invest in USD and EUR-denominated credit derivatives, while taking cross-asset views in corporate credit, cash equities and options. Our discretionary investment process is underpinned by extensive in-house quantitative infrastructure. We leverage in-house technology to preprocess large sets of market data and model the risks and returns of every asset in our investment universe. This enables us to identify mispriced trade pairs across markets, which we opportunistically combine into market-neutral strategy portfolios. The Unifi portfolio is actively managed to have no directional market exposure, limited left-tail drawdown risk and mitigated secondary exposures to convexity, jump to default and other risk factors. 
Unifi was founded by Omer Gundogdu, previously Senior Partner and Portfolio Manager at One William Street. Omer is joined by 4 seasoned Partners with strong relationships and a history of working together. Unifi plans to launch in Q1 of 2025 with launch AUM of over $500mm.
 Unifi's mission is clear: to serve our investors by aiming to provide strong returns and uphold the highest standards of integrity and accountability. Equally important is our commitment to our employees - we recognize our team members are our greatest asset, which is why we are focused on fostering a supportive and collaborative environment. Unifi is dedicated to delivering exceptional value to investors and our employees.
strategy_description:
Unifi seeks to generate significant alpha via an actively managed market-neutral portfolio of pair trades in credit derivatives, corporate credit and equities. Using a robust suite of asset pricing models, we identify pricing discrepancies between markets we believe are interconnected (e.g. CDS vs. bond, CDX tranche vs. CDX index, CDS vs. equity) and construct relative value pair trades that stand to benefit from these discrepancies. We combine these pair trades into strategy portfolios that seek to have no directional market risk, limited left-tail drawdown risk and positive exposure to the return drivers that we believe will generate long term outperformance.
 
Our investment process begins with data pre-processing and normalization. We evaluate all the data that is used in our models for timeliness, quality and consistency. We then perform a number of market data normalizations that allow us to interpret and use the data consistently across asset classes. Unifi uses this data to power instrument-level asset pricing models that allow us to estimate the risk and return of every asset we review in our investment universe. We choose and calibrate our asset models to reflect real world market dynamics, economically meaningful parameters and robust quantitative fundamentals. 
 
Our asset models allow Unifi traders to flexibly and rapidly evaluate paired investment opportunities across markets in real time. We use market dashboards we have developed using our proprietary software to visualize inter- and intra-market pricing discrepancies, allowing traders to quickly identify and act on investment opportunities we believe provide high risk-adjusted returns. Unifi's portfolio objective is to construct a market-neutral portfolio through trade pairs with offsetting risk exposures, maximizing the potential for excess returns while minimizing portfolio risk. 
 
We have an acute focus on execution quality, which we feel is uniquely important in markets such as credit derivatives where liquidity can be scarce. To that end, our choice of investment strategies is highly responsive to market conditions, transaction costs and liquidity. At any given time, we expect to be looking for opportunistic entry points into 5-10 larger positions, even as we remain flexible and responsive across markets. 
 
The Unifi portfolio is actively managed in an effort to have no directional market exposure, limited left-tail drawdown risk and acceptable secondary exposures to convexity, jump to default and other risk factors.

strategy_description:
Mane Global’s core universe and opportunity set are classified by sub-sector and covered by lead analysts that are sector specialists who bring extensive knowledge and historical context.  The continuous focus on each vertical allows each sector head to identify changes/inflections in businesses and/or dislocations in stock prices, as they arise.  Internally-developed models allow the team to quickly forecast and dissect risk when new information is released.  All team members aim to follow a consistent process to ensure all required aspects are covered before making an investment decision.

A proprietary Data Product has been developed over the past several years that allows the team to aggregate and evaluate many alternative data sets across the globe.  The Data Product automatically ingests data feeds on a daily basis, allowing for continuous updates and constant real-time information.  It eliminates time-consuming and laborious work involved with transforming data into useable forms and enables the team to tailor the presentation of data sets for efficient consumption.

The combination of sector expertise alongside efficient use of alternative data results in a process that enhances both idea generation and the timing of investment implementation.  The team strives to be effective on both the long and the short sides of the portfolio; a discipline has been developed to look for key characteristics on the short side in particular.  Finally, the culture at the firm around investing is to remain objective; when selling a long position, the team considers whether that investment may now be a short idea (similarly, when covering a short position, the team scrutinizes whether that investment may now be a long idea).

portfolio_additional_details:
The investment process yields a thoughtfully constructed portfolio consisting of differentiated ideas selected from the core universe.  The team takes an alpha-centric approach to investing and portfolio construction.  The portfolio’s low-net exposure is designed to reduce beta risk and market correlation.  The net exposure generally ranges from 0-30%, while gross exposure generally ranges from 125-250%.  The team invests globally, with approximately 65-90% of the investments in North America and 10-35% outside of North America (in Asia, Europe, and other).  The team is acutely focused on the liquidity profile of the portfolio; a large majority of positions held will not exceed one day’s trading volume and the portfolio is not expected to own positions greater than two days’ trading volume. 

As it relates to portfolio construction, the team typically manages the portfolio with approximately 80-140 securities.  Position sizes for long investments (excluding investments for hedging purposes) are typically between 1-8% of net asset value (“NAV”).  Maximum long position sizing is generally 15%.  The sizing of short positions carries a different approach versus long investments.  Position sizes for short investments (excluding investments for hedging purposes) are typically between 1-3% of NAV and are rarely expected to exceed 4% of NAV.  The typical holding period for positions in the portfolio is 6-24 months, though at times short positions may be held for a shorter duration.  

There is an emphasis on risk management throughout the investment process.  Positions are sized with a skew-based risk/reward framework, promoting discipline around entering and exiting investments.  The team spends time monitoring all ideas within the portfolio for thesis creep, earnings estimate differentiation, and the robustness of the catalyst path. 

The team continuously monitors risks to avoid unintended exposure and mitigate drawdowns in the portfolio.  In particular, the team analyzes risks by looking at several metrics, including but not limited to delta, beta, (Barra) factor, sector, and country exposures as well as any themes that it believes may be relevant at the time (interest rate, COVID-19 recovery, etc.).  The liquidity profile of each investment and of the overall portfolio is also of the utmost importance and is evaluated daily.  Finally, in addition to internal quantitative tools and capabilities, Mane Global also leverages the resources of its fund administrator, Morgan Stanley Fund Services (“MSFS”), as well as its order/execution management system, Enfusion Ltd. LLC (“Enfusion”), to assist with risk analytics and reporting.

Further, the team leverages valuable macro knowledge learned from the time spent at Moore Capital, providing an extra layer of context to its risk management approach.  This macro knowledge involves the regular monitoring of economic signals, news flow, and themes that may impact the portfolio.

This is complemented by a macro lens gained from the longstanding relationship with Louis Bacon and Moore Capital and a strict emphasis on risk management.
