name: Silverback Convertible Fund
management_company_description:
Silverback Asset Management LLC (“Silverback”) was founded in 2002 in Chapel Hill, NC. the firm focuses on finding investments with asymmetric risk-reward profiles and utilizing its core expertise in credit, equity, volatility, and convertible markets. 

Silverback's investment team has deep knowledge of many different types of companies—from distressed to IPOs—and has experience working alongside management/creditors to align disparate priorities. The resulting deep understanding allows for new, creative ways to leverage expertise in volatility and convertible arbitrage and embed greater amounts of convexity when the market allows. 
 
Although convertible securities remain a primary focus, Silverback has also found increasing success and opportunities throughout the capital structure. Silverback continues to view the convertible market as one of the best markets for capitalizing on significant market dislocations that may occur, and it is likely that Silverback may meaningfully allocate the Fund’s capital to convertible investments if and when dislocations occur. In general, Silverback uses convertibles in various ways, which depends on the market cycle and security life cycle.
strategy_description:
The Silverback Convertible Fund is an open-ended co-mingled product that focuses on convertible arbitrage, exploiting perceived mis-pricings in volatility and credit spreads.
The Fund is the successor to the Silverback Opportunity Fund, which was a limited-life fund designed to take advantage of widespread mis-pricing brought about by the pandemic.
Silverback has been managing convertible strategies in hedge funds since 2002.

We believe the recovery has left credit and equity investors exposed to significant risk and credit is asymmetric in the wrong direction. Equity recovery has pushed valuations to all time highs—though we know they can go even higher! We believe convertibles currently offer better risk/reward than non-convertible debt and believe that convexity is great to own in a correction,

Current market environment calls for a barbell approach with regards to the following:
          •Busted Convertibles: a key driver and an asset with which Silverback has expertise in building portfolios
         •Mispriced Credit: leveraging the team’s experience and knowledge base to find overlooked opportunities
         •Hedged In-The-Money Convertible Bonds: a defensive way to take a position in overvalued equities in a convex manner

management_company_description:
Kapitalo is a global macro multi-manager asset management firm, located in São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro.

Founded in 2009, Kapitalo has been successful in delivering consistent and high-quality results while maintaining a strong commitment to its principles: Excellency, Integrity, Discipline and Transparency. 

As a multi-manager organization, Kapitalo does not have a Chief Investment Officer (CIO). Instead, the firm built a robust governance structure and relies on an independent Risk Management team led by the COO, which is one of the founding partners.

Our 11 independent asset management teams have proven track records when it comes to allocating risk across various asset classes and geographies. 

Led by experienced PMs and analysts, the teams have their own unique investment processes and NAVs. With well-defined mandates and diversified strategies, each team competes for capital allocation in our flagship funds, Zeta and Kappa, as well as for stakes in our partnership.
strategy_description: K10 is one of the 11 independent asset management teams within Kapitalo’s multi-manager structure, and it is also a global macro and commodities hedge fund. Kapitalo encourages each pod to have its own standalone vehicle, which is the case for K10. The strategy is managed by a single, cohesive investment team led by a CIO, who oversees the entire portfolio and investment process. The strategy is discretionary, opportunistic, liquid, diversified, and highly active, operating across all major markets—particularly equities, commodities, interest rates, and currencies worldwide. K10 combines macroeconomic analysis with deep commodities expertise to capture macro trends and relative value opportunities globally. The fund maintains a target volatility between 6% and 8% per year, balancing return generation with disciplined risk management. With over 20 years of experience in macro and commodities trading, the investment team leverages proprietary research, long-standing expertise, and a centralized portfolio construction approach to deliver consistent results with a strong focus on liquidity and risk control.

name: Pictet Total Return - Atlas Titan
management_company_description:
Pictet Asset Management is an independent asset manager, investing for our clients across a range of equity, fixed income, and alternative and multi-asset products. 
With over 1,000 permanent employees, we operate from 19 centers worldwide. We provide specialist investment management solutions to leading institutions globally. Our clients include some of the world’s largest pension funds, mutual funds, sovereign wealth funds and financial institutions.
Our business is investment led and centered around a long term perspective with a dedication to client service.
strategy_description:
PTR-Atlas Titan is the 2x levered version of the PTR-Atlas fund. PTR Atlas follows a global long/short equity strategy combining intensive bottom-up fundamental research with top-down analysis to manage market exposure and guide positioning across regions and sectors. The fund aims to outperform global equity markets with approximately half the volatility over the cycle and has an emphasis on mitigating downside risk during market drawdowns. 
Managed by a focused team of four, headed by Matthieu Fleck who has over 20 years’ investment experience, the fund can also draw on Pictet Asset Management’s global investment platform of economists, strategists and investment specialists. 
Our disciplined top-down assessment focuses on the business cycle, liquidity conditions, credit conditions, valuation and sentiment, looking for the changes in these to assess macro improvement or deterioration by region. The in-depth bottom-up analysis aims to identify mispriced securities and understand upside and downside risks to the team's view. 
The final portfolio is typically composed of 40-60 long positions and 20-30 shorts and represents the team’s highest conviction ideas. Overall portfolio exposure is managed dynamically in line with the team’s macro views. Gross exposure averages at 200%, while net exposure is typically around 50% and is diversified across regions and industries. The fund uses liquid instruments including single stocks, CFDs, futures, options, ETFs.

The aim of the strategy will be to focus on delivering consistent uncorrelated returns with limited volatility throughout a cycle.

strategy_description:
The strategy’s investment objective is to achieve long-term capital appreciation while providing a degree of downside protection. To achieve this, we employ a long/short equity approach aiming to benefit from structural winners and losers in our investment universe. The fund invests primarily in the Greater China region (China, Hong Kong and Taiwan) whereby China accounts for the majority of exposure.

For long positions, we seek stocks with rising earnings forecast and low valuations. We call these stocks “Rising Stars.” In our view, typically such companies are subject to multiple expansion following positive earnings revisions. We hold a total of 50-80 long positions. Shorts comprise of companies with what we believe to be declining earnings momentum and hefty valuations. From our experiences, earnings disappointment is often followed by price declines. We call these “Fallen Angels.” We typically hold up to 40 short positions. Equally important is what we don’t do and that is companies where we believe the franchise is fully priced in or cheap companies with falling earnings, where negative news results in further price depreciation.

Gross exposure is between 60% and 200% while net exposure is typically between 20% and 80%.

The selection process involves customized terms and risk parameters for every strategy, and live, daily position-level transparency enables market neutral stance.

management_company_description:
Finch Bay Capital ("FBC") is an activist investment firm that seeks to generate strong multi-year returns by taking c.10 long-term positions in mid-cap public companies. FBC looks to identify investments with asymmetric outcomes, with a key driver of the asymmetry being the fact that each investment’s opportunity for improvement is misunderstood by the market. FBC will look to engage with management teams on strategic as well as operational topics, sometimes over a number of years, in order to unlock such value. The proactive ownership approach will be aided by FBC's network of advisors, which includes several former executives and directors of public companies with whom FBC investment professionals have built relationships.

FBC is a fundamentally-hedged activist which seeks to protect its investors’ capital in all market conditions. FBC’s position-level hedging strategy, which combines fundamental and quantitative analyses, looks to hedge out exposures which are unrelated to what FBC sees as the idiosyncratic attractiveness of a specific investment. Consequently, it is anticipated, but not guaranteed, that FBC’s returns will, therefore, be uncorrelated to other assets. 

Each investment is typically comprised of 1 long position hedged with an accompanying basket of short positions. As per the above the short positions are looking to hedge non-idiosyncratic risks to the long position (macro, sector, FX, etc.); they are not meant to express a directional view on those securities. The overall composition of the portfolio is expected to be ~0% net (~100% gross long & ~100% short) with minimal use of leverage.

FBC’s evaluation of its investments will include an assessment of what it views as the total probability adjusted upside of the long (passive mis-valuation + activism upside levers * probability of achieving those upside levers) against the quality of the hedge. FBC’s underwriting process seeks to identify activism upside levers that can drive meaningful value-creation in its portfolio companies and thereby aims to generate meaningful and uncorrelated returns for FBC’s investors, while preserving capital in downturns.

The FBC investment team is comprised of investors from Elliott, ValueAct, Cevian, Carlyle, and Hannover that have, in aggregate, invested $10B+ of capital in activist strategies.  Chief Investment Officer Leo Markel was involved in many of Elliott's activist investments in Europe during his nearly decade-long tenure. FBC's investment philosophy is inspired by its team’s heritage: Elliott's hedging philosophy and track record of uncorrelated returns and ValueAct's approach of long-term proactive engagement with public companies. 

Finch Bay Capital has an experienced team of nine people.

strategy_description:
The EJF Financial Debt Strategies Fund (“FDS”) is a private credit fund focused on Credit Risk Transfer “CRT" and direct lending to financial institutions. EJF’s seasoned portfolio team intends to leverage its large network of financial institutions to originate transactions that are not broadly syndicated to deliver what we believe will be attractive risk-adjusted yields.

CRT is favorable at a time where U.S. regional banks are facing unique capital constraints and lingering market fears. EJF believes the current regulatory landscape and market dynamics will create a rapid increase in the espousal of CRT by small U.S. banks as the industry adapts to keep pace with its larger counterparts.

equity financing to promising companies and we unlock liquidity for their historical 
shareholders. 
Amundsen IM was founded in 2021 by two partners, Gautier Rousseau and Per Einar 
Ellefsen. The two partners are former employees of Norges Bank Investment 
Management (NBIM), the Norwegian sovereign wealth fund, where they worked 
together for 7 years. 
Gautier Rousseau and Per Einar Ellefsen established Amundsen IM with the objective 
of becoming a leading investor in equity capital markets transactions, providing their 
investors with high excess returns arising from equity investments related to these 
transactions.
strategy_description:
Amundsen IM seeks to deliver returns through investment in companies going through equity capital markets (ECM) events. We believe investing in listed companies at the time of their ECM events allows Amundsen IM to perform differentiated due diligence from other investors, at a crucial time of the companies' lifecycle.

The investment team sources, selects and executes ECM events, through differentiated due diligence and a high level of engagement with the companies, owners, advisors and investment banks. We believe Amundsen IM differentiates from other investors through a dedicated product focus, long time horizon and best-in-class execution process.

management_company_description:

We openly acknowledge that Lingotto is not the right home for everybody. It’s a home for those willing and able to embrace the extraordinary.

At Lingotto, we have assembled a unique team of outstanding investment professionals who can express themselves in order to generate outperformance for our clients. At Lingotto they are free to pursue their passion for investing without the bureaucracy of most large organisations, or the loneliness of standalone funds.

The team aim to become trusted partners to the highest-quality companies that are solving the toughest problems across both public and private markets. The Strategy is built around the knowledge that market returns are driven by just a few outlier companies with extraordinary growth characteristics. These include being backed by secular trends which support explosive growth, having leadership and cultures with an unwavering focus on innovation, as well as a visionary understanding of their industry and the capacity to execute.

name: Cisu Capital Master Fund
management_company_description:
Cisu Capital Partners is a specialist alternative asset manager focused on the financial services sector in Europe and North America. The firm has a deeply fundamental investment philosophy and a rigorous risk management framework. The strategy is equity-focused with the flexibility to invest opportunistically in credit, targeting opportunities with deeply asymmetric return profiles to deliver alpha on a consistent basis. 

The firm was founded by Mark Wills, who until 2022 was a portfolio manager at Elliott Investment Management. Cisu launched its market-neutral strategy in August 2024 via an SMA, with the commingled fund going live in March 2025.
strategy_description: The Cisu Master Fund aims to generate a mid-teens target return with low volatility and negligible correlation to the broader markets by managing a market neutral portfolio. The portfolio will be comprised of 9 - 12 of the most deeply mispriced financial services securities in Europe and North America, each hedged bottom-up with a diversified basket of hand-picked single name shorts aimed at neutralising all unwanted risks (incl. equity market, credit spreads, interest rates and FX). Cisu will employ a deeply fundamental investment strategy to aim to identify issuer-specific idiosyncratic sources of alpha with clear catalysts to drive outperformance over designated periods of time.

name: PrimeStone Capital Masters LP Cayman
management_company_description:
PrimeStone is a fundamental long-term investor in European equities with a focus-bias towards the mid-cap space. The business was Founded in 2014 by three former Carlyle Global Partners who have worked together for 25+ years; starting the PrimeStone Compounders Fund in 2019 with internal capital and opening externally in Q4 2025.
PrimeStone is built on the core pillars of (i) Private Equity-style due diligence applied to public markets, combined with (ii) active engagement with target companies. The PrimeStone Compounders Fund aims to build on these strengths. It leverages the teams history of engagement as a tool rather than as a mandate, allowing the team to prioritize identifying and holding exceptional compounders within a strict valuation framework.
Business quality is the starting point of thr process. Whilst "quality" is a broad term, the Fund adheres to a strict framework and look for businesses exhibiting strong pricing power and barriers to entry, durable competitive advantages, attractive returns on capital and scale advantage / operating leverage. An assessment of management’s quality and the governance structure is also an integral part of our analysis. 
PrimeStone currently manages circa 850m USD of capital of which c. 20% is internal. The senior team has remained stable since inception led by CIO Franck Falezan.
strategy_description:
Primestone Capital seeks to be a long-term investor in European Mid-cap Public equities, deploying a constructive engagement approach with management teams, boards and other market participants.
The Fund composition typically consists of 12 core positions representing 60-70% of the portfolio’s exposure, with the remainder consisting of “farm” positions. It deploys little to low leverage and hedges FX exposure back to the fund currency.

The firm was established in 2020. Our CIO, Sean Ho, previously worked at Tybourne Capital Management (a Lone Pine Capital spin-out), where he focused on Consumer and TMT and helped setup the alternative data team. name: The Value Active Fund, Ltd.
management_company_description:
Varenne Capital Partners (‘Varenne’) is a research and process driven investment manager based in Paris, France, where it was founded by its current management team in 2003.

The firm first operated as an advisor to VEGA Finance – private banking unit of the CDC/CE Group – before establishing itself as a fully independent investment manager in 2007. 

With 8 nationalities in a team of 50 people, including 21 investment professionals, the management team fosters a culture of openness and diversity translating into very low turnover and an average tenure of 9 years in the investment team. 

All senior investment associates are shareholders or stock option holders in the firm and co-invest a significant portion of their wealth alongside long-standing clients in Europe, Asia, and the Americas.
strategy_description:
THE VALUE ACTIVE FUND aims at delivering long-term returns with the minimum necessary risk-taking. To do so, Varenne combines complementary investment frameworks in a single strategy: Long Equity, Short Equity, Merger Arbitrage and Tail Risk Hedging. The central idea is to separate risks from opportunities and deal with them independently and attempt to deliver an optimized risk-return profile. The firm adopts a ‘no broker research’ policy and seeks to make extensive use of technology to rely exclusively on internal origination and proprietary research.

The Long Equity framework starts with a core of 20 to 25 high-quality businesses in global developed markets. Additional diversified positions allow access to themes, sectors, or situations that can be absent from the core concentrated selection in order to optimize strategies’ behavior. Proprietary fundamental and behavioral databases provide original investment ideas to different teams (‘Origination’) which contribute their highest convictions to the portfolios.

The Short Equity framework has a core portfolio with the goal of producing uncorrelated returns, particularly in adverse economic or credit conditions. Core exposure is expressed through companies facing at least one among: unsustainable profitability, business deterioration, or financial issues. Diversified short layers provide exposure to themes, situations or industries that may be absent from single name selections in order to optimize overall portfolio behavior. We combine proprietary fundamental and behavioral factors to identify the above idiosyncratic ideas and manage the timing of the trades as well as their risk.

Merger Arbitrage focuses on friendly and announced deals only. Each deal is analysed internally to establish a probability of success allowing highly selective ‘deal-picking’, with the ability to take advantage of increased volatility and to act as a liquidity provider to the market. However, the team is under no obligation to be ‘in play’ all the time and the exposure can range from 0%-100% exposure. The aim of the strategy is to fund, entirely or partially, the 1.5% annual budget for the Tail Risk Hedging.

Tail Risk hedging is designed to attempt to mitigate the effects of residual risk, which is defined as the impact from an event leading the S&P 500 index down 20% or more from its 52-week peak. Implementation is done through internal research looking for asymmetric instruments with a maximum annual budget of 1.5% of AUM. The framework is implemented through two families of hedges: Market Risk & Root Causes of Market Risk. Market risk hedges are typically shorter-mid dated, using non-vanilla equity optional strategies. Root causes can be longer dated and can trade on five possible asset classes: equities, credit, rates, fx, and commodities.

The four frameworks are combined using a rule-based portfolio construction methodology. The investment process therefore aims to bring together what we believe to be the depth of analysis and judgement of independent and experienced teams together with the rigor and systematicity of a rule-based portfolio construction model.

The Fund’s Equity Long and Short Equity frameworks have a net exposure targeting around 100% (MtM), and typically range between 95-110%. Short Equity exposure varies from 0% to 30%. The Merger Arbitrage framework has a gross exposure varying from 0% to 100% with an average of 25-35%. The Tail Risk Hedging framework has an annual budget of 1.5% per year with a typical notional exposure of 30-100%.

management_company_description: Founded in 2013 by Eric Peters, One River Asset Management is an investment manager that aims to deliver high-conviction absolute-return strategies that help our clients build superior portfolios. We see the world in a period of major economic and political transition, with the investment landscape shifting in ways that will make the coming five years look profoundly different from the past five. We believe our strategies are built to profit from this dynamic environment while providing diversification benefits to traditional investment portfolios. Each is developed and managed in-house by our team of investment professionals with expertise in volatility and systematic trading/investing. We believe our strategies are delivered at sensible fees and enhanced volatility via commingled funds, and/or in bespoke combinations for large institutions via fund-of-one structures.
strategy_description: One River has built an elegant and robust alpha strategy with an investment-principle-first approach (benefiting from extensive discretionary trading experience) rather than an academic-first or data-first approach. The investment model uses 5 types of signals across a wide range of term horizons. The strategy focuses on medium/long term trends to reduce whipsaw. Using models in a consistent manner across different markets and asset classes, with a limited number of parameters and standardized parameter values, and a heavy emphasis on risk mitigation. The exit methodology we use provides superior risk mitigation and crisis alpha. Although we share the view that it is important to focus on long term trends (to avoid whipsaw risk), we believe that it is important to be nimble and to be able to fully exit positions quickly if needed, especially in Alternative Markets. At our target capacity, we can get into or out of positions in one trading day without having a significant market impact. Controlled strategy capacity also enables us to allocate risk in a more beneficial manner. We can allocate more balanced risk to all markets (instead of skewed towards the most liquid ones), which improves diversification. Although over time our risk allocation across asset classes is balanced, if at any particular moment there is no clear trend in a particular market/asset class, our strategy will not force itself to hold positions there. The ability to have zero exposure in a non-trending market reduces whipsaw.

management_company_description: O'Connor is a leader in alternative strategies including hedge funds and private credit. From inception in 1977 to today, O'Connor's emphasis on innovation, thought leadership and investment excellence has resulted in investment solutions that focus on relative value and strong absolute returns. With approximately $9bn under management, O’Connor offers a range of strategies including:  Global Multi-Strategy Alpha (launched in 2000), Global Merger Arbitrage (2015), O’Connor Capital Solutions Private Credit (2017), China Long/Short (2021), Event Driven (2021) and Working Capital Finance (2022).
strategy_description:
The UBS (Irl) Investor Selection - O'Connor China Long/Short Alpha Strategies UCITS is a low net, relative value Equity Long/Short strategy investing primarily in corporates predominantly listed in Greater China. The fund seeks to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns with target return of 12-15% net at 8-10% volatility annualised over a market cycle, with low correlation and beta to both equity and credit markets. Portfolio construction is based primarily on fundamental bottom-up research combined with macro overlay based on a strong emphasis on the team's understanding of Chinese government policy, leveraging extensive long-standing relationships with both corporate management teams as well as the research community in our coverage universe to generate ideas.

The portfolio manager implements investment ideas using a relative value strategy to identify long and short opportunities either within one sector or across different sectors. Portfolios are managed proactively and dynamically with daily team meetings to review new macro, sector and corporate developments. We constantly review our Investment thesis versus the changing market environment and will move our capital to where we see the best risk reward. Risk management is of fundamental importance to our approach, and we use multiple in-house and third-party quantitative models to measure and monitor risk.

management_company_description: O'Connor is a leader in alternative strategies including hedge funds and private credit. From inception in 1977 to today, O'Connor's emphasis on innovation, thought leadership and investment excellence has resulted in investment solutions that focus on relative value and strong absolute returns. strategy_description: The Nineteen77 Global Multi-Strategy Alpha Fund is a non-directional, fundamental relative value multi-strategy hedge fund focusing on generating alpha and absolute returns across strategies and sub strategies as guided by macro and markets outlook, structural alpha opportunities and a highly experienced investment team. The Fund invests in three core strategies: Global Long/Short Equities, Global Event Driven, and Credit. The Fund's objective is to realize consistently high risk-adjusted absolute returns by dynamically allocating to more than 15 distinct sub strategies that generally exhibit minimal or negative correlation to each other and to the overall equity and fixed income markets.  We employ risk management on three levels: fund, strategy and sub strategy level and historically have a very low beta to markets. We generally expect our realized return volatility to be in the 6-8% range, with opportunistic periods of additional risk to take advantage of structural, cyclical or technical forces in the markets. With open architecture we have a transparent and collaborative culture which enables us to be quick and dynamic in response to a fast evolving macro landscape.

name: Irth Strategic Master Fund, LP
management_company_description: Irth Capital Management is a public/private thematic investor founded by Matthew Bradshaw and Mohamed bin Abdulla Al Thani to make investments in globally strategic industries.
strategy_description:
Irth implements a systematic, event driven, fundamental, constructivist investment strategy. Irth focuses its research primarily on areas where it has deep domain expertise and long-term relationships such as: Food and Agriculture, Consumer Goods, Restaurants, Leisure, Hospitality, Supply Chain Logistics, Government, Data, and Technology.

Irth's investment decisions reflect Irth's core principles: concentration, deep fundamental research, and control. Accordingly, Irth seeks to run a concentrated long portfolio of investments that can compound at exceptional rates and use its control-oriented playbook as a key advantage. 

Irth believes that the best investments typically emerge from temporary dislocations where Irth's domain expertise and relationships with industry-leading operating partners can unlock value.

name: Sandglass Select Fund II
management_company_description: Founded in 2013, Sandglass Capital is a privately-owned global emerging markets manager with offices in New York City, London and Dubai. Specializing in sovereign and corporate debt, the firm’s investment edge is achieved through prudent asset selection and nimble portfolio construction coupled with proactive engagement with issuers and marketplace participants. Each Sandglass investment portfolio combines fundamental bottom-up research, macro-analysis, dynamic hedging, and robust risk tools to deliver repeatable award-winning performance to global institutional investors.
strategy_description:
Sandglass Select Fund II is a drawdown fund that will invest in a concentrated portfolio of credit and equity opportunities, primarily in distressed, dislocation, and deep value situations in Emerging Markets ex-China. The Fund’s goal is to generate robust IRRs over a 3-4 year horizon. The target portfolio will focus on 6-8 investment themes with compelling and convex return potential. The Fund will employ an active engagement approach that may include participation in creditor committees, restructuring teams, or Boards of Directors to enhance returns and mitigate risks. 

Sandglass Select Fund II is a successor fund to Sandglass Select Fund I which launched in October 2019, has completed its investment period and is currently in the monitoring period with a run rate LP level gross IRR of ~+19% (as of end of Q2) and MOIC at 1.6x. Over the fund’s short 5-year life, we expect to exceed our 20% gross IRR and 2x MOIC targets. 

The Fund's anchor investor is a top-ten university endowment.

management_company_description:
Soleus Capital Management is a healthcare investment firm primarily focused on the innovative areas of life sciences, including biotech, medtech, diagnostics, and genomics. We launched our funds in September 2018.  Guy Levy, Managing Partner and CIO, has over 23 years of industry experience with the various healthcare sub-sectors. The Firm employs a fundamentals-based stock selection process based on qualitative and quantitative research. Soleus Capital's proprietary research is the basis upon which all investment decisions are made. 

The Firm seeks to capitalize on the synergies in its fundamental due diligence by managing a long/short healthcare equities fund, a series of private equity funds focused on late-stage private investments, and a private credit fund that seeks to partner exclusively with commercial-stage life sciences companies via senior secured loans, existing and synthetic royalty streams, and bespoke convertible and preferred securities. The Firm has a strategic relationship with an affiliate of Stone Point Capital pursuant to which the affiliate has made a significant investment in the Soleus Funds.
strategy_description:
Soleus Capital, L.P. ("Soleus Capital"; the "Fund") is a long/short hedge fund focused on the innovative areas of the life sciences sector, including therapeutics, devices, diagnostics, and genomics. The Fund's exposure across life sciences differs from some peers who focus solely on biotech. Soleus Capital seeks to generate significant capital appreciation on a risk-adjusted basis through idiosyncratic, catalyst-driven investing with a focus on small/mid-cap equities that we believe are undervalued and underfollowed. 

Risk management occurs on both a portfolio and individual security basis where risks are identified and mitigated through the continuous monitoring of various risk metrics including delta-adjusted gross and net exposures, position limits, sub-sector/factor exposures, correlation, and portfolio liquidity. All long positions are based on an in-depth risk/reward analysis, beginning with an assessment of downside value. Downside is typically supported by cash on the balance sheet, a base business, or a portfolio of assets, while upside is generally supported by what we believe are a number of unrecognized and/or underappreciated potential catalysts. Long position sizing generally starts with downside assessment to seek to limit loss to typically no more than 1.0% to 1.5% to the Fund.

Although the opportunity set and market conditions will ultimately determine the portfolio construction, Soleus Capital typically targets the following: 20-30 core long positions; 30-50 opportunistic long positions; 10-20 short positions including custom short baskets focused on removing the factor risks embedded in the long portfolio; 85-135% long exposure; 70-95% short exposure; 150-230% gross exposure; and 30-50% net exposure.

management_company_description: DeepCurrents Investment Group ("DCIG") is a 5-year old Spinout from a larger multi-strategy firm (Verition). DCIG launched their commingled vehicle in Feb 2018, and soft closed to new investors when hitting ~$500mm in September 2019. The Firm is now reopening to new investors.
strategy_description:
High Level: 
DeepCurrents is a multi-asset relative value investor, with a focus on idiosyncratic volatility. We invest using multiple relative value styles, but do so as a single strategy, and in an un-siloed manner. These styles include elements of credit arbitrage, convertible arbitrage, volatility arbitrage, capital structure arbitrage, and event arbitrage. We evaluate and analyze opportunities in all of these areas through one lens, or framework, which we call the ‘volatility continuum’. The volatility continuum enables us to compare convex instruments of different asset class types to one another in an apples-to-apples manner. Our investment process marries a proprietary quantitative filtering process with deep fundamental research.

Key Tenets & Portfolio Composition:
Our focus is on finding cheap (or mispriced) convexity, and, as such, our positions will [essentially] always have at least one convex instrument (e.g. convert, corporate bond, CDS, options, etc.) which will be paired with other instruments from the same issuer (hedges). At any given time, we have approximately 150 positions, each of which will generally have between 2 and 5 instruments from the same underlying issuer, and together, these instruments comprise the trade package. 

Process:
High level, our investment process involves identifying opportunities that we deem attractive from a convexity and risk : reward perspective, and then seeking to optimize the ratios between the instruments that make up the position so that we are, ideally, hedging away the directional / delta dimension, and focusing on the convexity itself. Our positions, and their ratios, are dynamically adjusted in an effort to continuously optimize our exposure and Greeks to capture only the exposure we are looking for. 

To identify opportunities, we rely on each of our three pillars working together: Quant, Fundamental, and Macro. The Quant Engine is constantly scouring the tradeable universe to show us convex opportunities at the instrument level, using proprietary metrics we've developed. The fundamental team is also looking for potentially attractive opportunities, largely focusing first on catalyst identification in issuers with capital structures that fit our parameters. When ideas are identified / flagged by one pillar, they are passed through to the other pillars to be evaluated from their perspective. Ideas determined to be potentially actionable in the near term will move on to further fundamental analysis and are also evaluated by the Quant Engine from a timing (entry point) perspective. For ideas that will ultimately go into the portfolio, the Quant Engine plays a key role in position construction as well, and is a crucial part of determining the ratios between instruments within the position. 

Holding Period:
Holding periods can vary and are ultimately driven by our view on the associated catalysts (or lack thereof). On average, we turn over the book approximately three times per year. We may have positions with holding periods of one month (in the case of specific, near-term catalysts), or positions that are in the book for 18 months or more (in the case of positions without a specific catalyst, but where the risk : reward profile remains attractive). Regardless of the holding period, each position is dynamically hedged and rebalanced in an effort to maintain what we believe is optimal exposure for our purposes.

name: Cevian Capital II
management_company_description:
Cevian is a European-focused activist investor currently managing c. $15 billion, with a track record dating back to 1996. The current fund, Cevian Capital II, was established in 2006. Cevian's c. 30 person investment team are split across Stockholm, Zurich and London. 

Cevian takes large minority stakes (typically 5-20%) in a limited number (avg. 10-15) of European listed companies, that it believes are undervalued and have the potential for significant value creation. 

Cevian uses deep fundamental research to identify hidden value and capture alpha by aiming to take a significantly different view on mid-term value and earnings potential than “normal” analysts and investors. Cevian targets:

Fundamentally attractive businesses at times of extreme valuation discounts
Companies with strong competitive positions within attractive industries, with predictable medium-term outlook and strong cash flow generation

Cevian then aims to create additional alpha by fundamentally improving its companies through hands-on activism:

As a large owner, Cevian can drive value-creation programs in an assertive but constructive manner (with Cevian Partners joining the boards of companies in the majority of cases)
These value-creation opportunities are essentially “for free” in public markets as most other investors are passive/index orientated and assume there will be no change at companies

Cevian’s work today benefits from strong support from other shareholders, relationships and credibility that has been built over 26+ years of experience driving change at 60+ European companies (with board seats in 50+ companies).

Cevian targets companies that have each of three main characteristics:
Attractive on an “as-is” basis – deeply undervalued and fundamentally attractive companies. Typically, blue-chip names with businesses that exhibit positive long-term dynamics but are not performing at their full potential.
Broad value-creation potential – multiple initiatives designed to drive fundamental improvements across operations, strategy/structure, financial, governance and sustainability
Positive influence dynamics – Conviction that, by drawing on existing experience, networks and relationships, we will be able to implement the majority of our value-creation initiatives in a hands-on, constructive manner
strategy_description:
Cevian Capital II is a dedicated activist fund, managing c. $14 billion from c. 300 clients, primarily pension, endowment, foundation and other institutional investors. 
Approximately 90% of the funds capital is comprised of 3 and 5-year capital, supporting Cevian’s long-term investment horizon and value-enhancement work. 

Within Europe, the main area of focus are the Nordic countries, the UK,  Switzerland, France and Germany. The portfolio is concentrated, with c. 10-15 investments at any one time, enabling extensive fundamental research and hands-on engagement.

The fund does not typically short, hedge or use leverage.

Cevian’s conviction is that ESG performance has a direct impact on the long-term performance and valuation of a company - “values” and “corporate value” are fully symbiotic. ESG considerations impact, among other things, companies’ business opportunities, revenues, costs, risks, employee engagement, societal attitudes and corporate valuations.  Improving ESG performance at portfolio companies is fundamental to sustainable and long-term value creation for shareholders (including the Cevian Funds) and other stakeholders alike.

ESG considerations are fully integrated into Cevian’s investment process and active ownership work, both as part of the pre-investment fundamental analysis, as well as being a focus of Cevian’s value-creation work. ESG assessments are specific to each company, based on the material ESG aspects that are relevant for that company. ESG assessment are documented and included in Cevian’s research documents and Investment Committee Memorandums (ICMs).   

As part of its fundamental research process, Cevian’s investment team analyzes companies’ ESG performance, opportunities and risks, just as it does for its other core value-creation areas. This typically includes benchmarking vs sector leaders to help identify improvement potential which Cevian can seek to realize through its active ownership work. 

ESG is a core value-creation focus area for Cevian, sitting alongside our work to improve companies’ operations, corporate strategy, organizational structure, and financial management.

portfolio_additional_details:
With respect to the broad investment universe, BDCM focuses on industries that are asset intensive with defendable business models regardless of the market cycle. BDCM believes that targeting companies with significant tangible assets at a discount to underlying collateral value limits downside risk. As such, sectors of focus include metals, chemicals, automotive, manufacturing, communications, real estate and farming and agriculture. At the macro level, BDCM will assess macroeconomic trends, regulatory issues, cyclicality, barriers to entry and the competitive landscape to formulate both a sector and security-level investment thesis.

Within the BDCS portfolio there are three primary sub-strategies:
1)	Performing Credit: typically accounts for approximately 35% of the portfolio and consists primarily of secured corporate debt.  
2)	Distressed Credit and Special Situations: typically accounts for approximately 35% of the portfolio.  Bank loans are the primary exposure where the firm believes it will get back par value.  Some exposure is in the form of equity, both private, post-reorganization and public equity.  Importantly in this allocation, paramount priority is placed on seeing cash flows from a company’s business versus the amount of cash it has invested, or ‘cash-on-cash’ returns. 
3)	Structured Credit: typically accounts for approximately 20% of the portfolio and consists primarily of senior tranches of asset backed securities and some limited exposure to junior tranches.

The cash balance will vary depending on the in-house view of the broader credit cycle, and historically has averaged 10% of the portfolio.  BDCM views this allocation as both a risk management lever and ‘offensive’ tool during market dislocations, where portfolio managers can add to the portfolio opportunistically.
esg_approach_description: BDCM’s approach to ESG is pragmatic and seeks to address ESG opportunities and risks through the development of strategies consistent with the economic reality and investment thesis of each individual investment. BDCM has implemented a cross-portfolio ESG initiative with the objective of integrating ESG principles into investment management processes and ownership practices. The Firm seeks to encourage responsible management of ESG issues across the portfolio and serves as a facilitator for identifying potential areas for improvement and sharing of best practices across portfolio companies. In addition, BDCM has made the consideration of ESG issues an integral part of its credit analysis of prospective investments.  BDCM believes ESG principles are important social considerations and risk management measures but also have a value-enhancing impact on future financial performance and sustainability.

management_company_description:
Cadian Capital Management is an investment manager, founded by Eric Bannasch in October 2007. The Firm launched with its flagship fund, Cadian Fund, a long/short equity strategy concentrated in companies <$25 billion in market capitalization. This fund is focused on the technology, media, and telecommunications sectors, with additional exposure to consumer, healthcare, industrials, and related sectors.

In August 2022, the Firm launched Cadian Opportunities Fund, a best ideas strategy that is concentrated on select long positions derived from the flagship fund. 

The Firm has a sophisticated investor base, most of whom have been with us for more than 10 years. The Founder and senior professionals have significant investments in the funds, approximately 12% of AUM.  The Firm has a single New York City office with 21 employees.
strategy_description:
Our fundamental, bottom-up investment process focuses on understanding product cycles and dislocations that can create long-term value. The Team has been investing in and around Silicon Valley's ecosystem for years and utilizes its network of technology, healthcare, and consumer product buyers, supply chain networks, and industry experts to help identify product cycles, trends, and disruptors to help find mispriced companies.

For longs, we look for competitively advantaged companies with strong product cycles and good management teams that have been overlooked by other investors; often the stock price is dislocated. We want to own companies with a superior product or service, in a growing market, that is gaining share, has a defensible position, and a long runway for growth at a discounted valuation. The investment horizon on longs is typically greater than two years. We seek investments that are “off-the-beaten-path” and require substantial research and due diligence to drive conviction.

For shorts, we look for companies facing structural deterioration of growth or competitive positioning. We want to short competitively disadvantaged companies or high growth stocks with fundamentals inflecting downward. Often this includes weak management teams, bad balance sheets, and share donors priced at a premium relative to these fundamentals.  We tend to target companies transitioning from “great to good” or “good to bad” and try to avoid “already bad” businesses where other investors are aware of challenges.  Short positions are expected to contribute to absolute performance, not to hedge exposure.

name: Numerai One
strategy_description: Numerai analyzes over 8,000 equity securities to create its investment universe of roughly 5,000 securities.  Utilizing stock specific financial data that covers roughly two decades, Numerai employs data cleaning and regularization techniques to curate its data sets for financial modeling.  Numerai then encrypts that data using a technique that generalizes the data from the financial domain to a purely mathematical domain for inclusion in weekly data science tournaments. In the weekly data science tournaments, hosted by Numerai Inc., roughly 5000 unique machine learning based models are sourced from all over the world to compete in the data science tournaments created by Numerai.  Because the data is generalized in its encryption, there is no need for financial domain expertise to participate.  The tournament consists of two data sets: training data for the development of AI algorithms; and a tournament data set against which users submit predictions.  In the submission set from the users, predictions are provided for encrypted identifiers only; no intellectual property is transferred. The tournament submissions contain predictions for both live and historical (out of sample) data.  For the tournament, submissions are evaluated solely based on their performance on the live predictions.  Monetary prizes are distributed to top performers.  By having data on a given model’s out of sample performance, its live prediction attributes, as well as meta-data about the data scientists, Numerai is able to employ a proprietary meta-model to filter and weight the predictions sets to ensemble a single alpha forecast for each security in its investable universe.  The result of the above process is a forecast return for each security in the trading Numerai universe.  At this point, Numerai employs a proprietary portfolio optimization engine to create a portfolio that seeks to maximize forecast return while minimizing forecast risk and cost.  This process also ensures the target portfolio conforms to Numerai’s internal risk parameters.  Portfolio optimization is where considerations such as factor exposure, specific risk exposures and market impact costs are considered.

QSM Asset Management is a London-based investment boutique, set up by a team of long-term colleagues, who previously worked together at Majedie Asset Management. The team are highly experienced on both the Operations and Investment side of managing institutional mandates.

QSM is domiciled in the UK and its function is Investment Management of the QSM Global Equity Long Short Fund (GELSF).
strategy_description:
The Fund’s investment objective is to generate positive returns on a five-year rolling basis by investing primarily in liquid equity and equity-related securities.

The Fund’s investment selection and portfolio construction approach combines micro and macro analysis. The Investment Manager applies a value framework, meaning that they are looking for long positions in companies that they believe are under-valued and have depressed profitability versus their history and/or peers, and short positions in companies they think are over-valued and have unsustainably high profitability versus their history and/or peers.

The Fund’s investment philosophy is one of asymmetric payoffs. Looking for long positions, where potential share price upsides are significantly larger than potential downsides, and short positions where the potential share price downsides are significantly larger than potential upsides. This involves taking positions where the market is not pricing in a change in a company’s prospects (for the better, for longs, for the worse, for shorts), but where our research has identified a catalyst – taking an Alternative Perspective.

strategy_description:
Oribel Capital is a fundamental equity long/short fund that invests in technology and tech-enabled businesses. The firm currently has ~$1.5 billion in AUM. This is Oribel’s 9th year as an independent firm, although the three co-founders Greg Brenner, Adam Brenner, and Mikal Patel have been working together for over a decade. Their philosophy believes that minimizing drawdowns is the best way to compound absolute returns. Oribel strives to be an all-weather, alpha-seeking fund that can both participate in market upside and preserve capital during challenging times. Oribel believes its track record proves that it has consistently generated alpha, outperformed during difficult market environments, and produced returns that are generally uncorrelated with equity indexes and other TMT funds.
The Oribel ALPHA share class takes minimal net exposure to the market's direction.
The Oribel AlphaPLUS share class combines Oribel ALPHA’s core strategy with additional market exposure. Please note, this is not a separate vehicle, it is a separate share class in the same fund.

name: Spring Subordinated Debt Fund
management_company_description:
Spring Investments SA is a wealth and asset management company based in Geneva, Switzerland. The Company commenced its wealth management operations in 2018 by Mr. Guy Avneon. The Company is authorized and regulated by FINMA .

 The Company offers discretionary portfolio management services and acts as the investment manager for Spring Subordinated Debt Fund, a Cayman Islands-domiciled fund launched in February 2020. 

The Company is highly experienced in fixed income investment strategies and also offers special mandate investment solutions for corporates, high net worth individuals, and family office clients.
strategy_description:
The vast majority of fund investments are in European bank AT1s.  The fund has a 5-year track record and was augmented in April 2024 by the arrival of Jackie Ineke, now co-managing the Fund. Jackie headed up European financials credit research at Morgan Stanley for 23 years and was voted #1 analyst in her sector in II for over 10 years.  She brings her expertise in the $230bn sector of European bank AT1s.  
•	Research differentiates the Fund.  Core holdings typically make up two-thirds of the Fund, focused on names which show strong relative value but are essentially boring, such as Caixa, Commerzbank, NWG, Sabadell, Alpha.  We run three sub-strategies which make up the other third. First, a focus on M&A, which we believe is key for alpha generation in the next few years.  This is linked to overcapitalisation, certainty on ultimate share count, and bank stock valuations.  A value anchor is a must and then we’re happy to take any upside from an acquisition – CCF, NIBC, Van Lanschot are examples.  Second, a focus on bonds impacted by regulatory change, such as Julius Baer’s need to refinance/restructure outstanding AT1s, in the investor’s favour. Finally, special situations, including Metro and MunHyp.  Fundamental and regulatory research knowledge is a pre-requisite for bond selection – as is easy access to management and to syndicate desks, considering Jackie's connections in the industry.
•	Agility and size differentiate the Fund.  Many of the bonds in our M&A and Special Situations sub-strategies are less than $300m in issue size – making them inaccessible to larger Funds.  
•	Accessibility differentiates the Fund.  We have quarterly webinars, we talk regularly to our investors, we discuss the Fund, we can give advice on new issues or secondary bonds, we understand regulatory changes and their implications – and can explain them.  Many of our investors buy AT1s elsewhere in their firms and strongly benefit from these conversations.
•	Our Fund is Cayman with weekly liquidity – in our view the best structure for such a strategy, whilst acknowledging this limits our marketing reach.  AT1s can be volatile and as witnessed at Morgan Stanley, daily liquidity brings forced sellers at exactly the wrong time.  We can take leverage only up to 30% of the Fund – we are no hedge fund - and can quickly deploy this with high conviction during a volatility event.
region_exposure_description: We can take exposures outside of European banks and have for example invested in Canadian non-called AT1 floaters when relative value opportunities arise.

name: Ruffer Total Return International
management_company_description:
Founded in 1994, Ruffer is an independent, owner-managed, London based investment firm with $23bn of assets under management. Led by our founder and Chairman, Jonathan Ruffer, and co-CIOs, Henry Maxey and Neil McLeish, we have a team of over 300 employees and provide an investment service to pension funds, endowments and foundations, family offices and other institutions globally. 

We have a single global, macro-driven, absolute return investment strategy. Our aim is to deliver positive returns in all market environments, with a particular focus on downside protection in times of market stress. The entirety of the firm's AUM is managed this way. For over 30 years, our approach has been successful in delivering returns with a low correlation to equities and other asset classes. 

This is the result of an investment philosophy grounded in capital preservation, and a disciplined and genuinely different process. We conduct our own independent research, actively manage the underlying securities and operate freely, without the constraint of market benchmarks.
strategy_description:
The fund follows Ruffer's single global, macro-driven, absolute return investment strategy, aiming to achieve positive returns in all market environments. This capital preservation aim is unchanged since the firm was founded in 1994.

The investment strategy and asset allocation are set by Henry Maxey (Co-Chief Investment Officer), Neil McLeish (Co-Chief Investment Officer) and Jonathan Ruffer (Chairman), with input from senior fund managers and the independent in-house research team.

The investment process is predominantly driven by fundamental economic, market and company research. We believe top-down, asset allocation decisions are the key drivers of our returns. These are supported by bottom-up security selection and direct ownership, to reflect the ideas that best express our macroeconomic views.

The investment approach starts with managing the risk of losing money, identifying assets that will protect against potential market risks, before then being opportunistic to capture upside. 

We do not rely on historic correlations between asset classes, instead considering a range of possible future scenarios, and positioning the portfolio accordingly.  There will always be a balance of offsetting investments in protection and growth, to remove the need for market timing, though the balance will change depending on the conviction of our views. The qualitative, forward-looking assessment of markets is supported by quantitative inputs and stress testing to understand the vulnerabilities in the portfolio.

The mandate is completely unconstrained, with no control ranges and no strategic asset allocation. We seek to build a multi-asset portfolio of individually risky but offsetting assets with asymmetric payoff profiles to provide a linear outcome. Historically, the portfolio has consisted of equities, fixed income, commodities, currencies, alternative assets, and their associated derivatives; the composition and weightings will vary considerably over time.

name: Sagil Latin Americas Opportunities Fund
management_company_description:
Sagil was established by an experienced investment team to take advantage of opportunities in Latin America. The team has focused on Latin American companies and markets since 2004, initially as part of the proprietary trading desk of Rand Merchant Bank and subsequently with the launch of the Sagil Latin American Opportunities Fund in 2009. Sagil continues to make use of the team’s regional knowledge and local relationships to execute the same proven and highly successful strategy. Sagil launched the Fund with the knowledge that Latin American markets tend to be more volatile, but that greater volatility and dispersion of individual stock performances enhances the value of stock selection and the potential for attractive returns. This plays to the investment team’s strengths of experience in the region and disciplined investment process.

Sagil Capital LLP is a UK incorporated partnership (FCA Regulated) founded in late 2008. The firm is controlled by the founding partners.
strategy_description:
The fund deploys a thorough and disciplined investment process with a strong focus on risk management to identify opportunities, utilising four complementary strategies focused on listed Latin American opportunities. We believe that local market knowledge coupled with a global perspective allows for the identification of opportunities without ignoring macro-economic drivers that may impact a company’s performance.
Strategies include Arbitrage, Relative Value and Directional trades. Arbitrage strategies are considered to be lower risk and contain a clear convergence event. Types of trades include risk arbitrage and debt versus equity. Relative value involves positioning for outperformance between related securities and includes pair, share class and group structure trades. This strategy is considered to be low to medium risk and typically involves being market neutral. The Directional strategy invests in opportunities, both long and short, without a specific hedge. These are considered to be medium risk with overall directional exposure of the portfolio being limited

management_company_description: Carmignac is a family owned and independent asset management firm established in 1989, which manages long-only and hedge fund strategies.
strategy_description:
Carmignac Portfolio Long Short European Equities is a fundamental long/short equity strategy, focused on the European market. The Fund's net exposure to equity markets ranges between -20% and 50%. 

Fundamental stock picking is the bedrock of the process. The portfolio managers focus on high conviction ideas with a clear investment thesis, a non-consensual view, a defined event path/catalyst and an asymmetric risk/return profile. 

The portfolio is constructed into four buckets:
-Core Longs – The core long portfolio is invested in high conviction positions with a long investment time horizon (9 to 36 months) 
-Trading longs – Positions we fundamentally like and offering a nearer term catalyst. The risk / return profile is usually slightly less attractive than core longs or alpha shorts, but comparable on an annualized basis.
-Relative value / Special situations – Positions which could benefit from specific short-term catalysts. These can be numerous, from relative value ideas, event driven, occasionally risk arbitrage: corporate events, M&A, management change,etc
-Alpha shorts – Shorts in companies that we think are structurally challenged and/or grossly overvalued, focus on fundamental, non-consensual ideas with a quantifiable delta and catalysts. 

This leads to a portfolio of 50 to 70 stocks (long + short).

Cheyne Capital was founded in 2000 by Jonathan Lourie (CEO) and Stuart Fiertz (President) after working together at Morgan Stanley. 

Cheyne is one of Europe's leading alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs) with c. 170 partners and employees.

Cheyne invests across the capital structure from the senior debt to the equity of corporates and real estate. strategy_description:
The Cheyne Thematic Long Short Equity Fund is a European mid-cap focused, dynamically managed low-net strategy that combines robust fundamental and thematic analysis with active trading. 

The fund is managed by Richard Woolf, who has more than 25 years’ investment experience across several asset classes and numerous market cycles.  

The Fund’s core focus is on under-researched, liquid European mid-caps with additional flexibility to invest globally. The investment team employs a repeatable research process that seeks to identify and capitalise on uncorrelated macro and structural investment themes that are misunderstood by the market in the short run, leading to pricing anomalies and trading opportunities within underlying stocks. Combining this with stock-specific fundamental analysis translates into a portfolio of 10-15 uncorrelated thematic investment theses, each implemented via specific differentiated equity ideas. 

Paramount emphasis is placed on risk management and capital protection, which is supported by the PM’s strong trading acumen and full alignment of interest. This translates to a modest approach to leverage (125% average gross exposure) typically running a low net exposure (+/-20% range) where returns are not dependent on the general economic environment and demonstrate a very low correlation to broader equity indices.

Prior to the launch of the standalone fund in November 2019 there was a dedicated portfolio, managing the same strategy, within Cheyne equity funds from February 2013.

name: Cheyne EMEA Fund
management_company_description:
Cheyne Capital was founded in 2000 by Jonathan Lourie (CEO) and Stuart Fiertz (President) after working together at Morgan Stanley. 

Cheyne is one of Europe's leading alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs) with c. 170 partners and employees.

Cheyne invests across the capital structure from the senior debt to the equity of corporates and real estate. With an investment philosophy grounded in rigorous fundamental analysis, the firm’s main areas of expertise are: Real Estate Debt, Corporate Credit and Risk Transfer, European Strategic Value Credit, and Liquid Alternatives.
strategy_description:
Dynamically managed, long biased strategy, focusing on investing in liquid equities within the EMEA region; principally Eastern Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Turkey. 

The fund seeks to provide a diverse source of returns to its investors from typically uncrowded names on an attractive risk adjusted basis. Investment philosophy is centred on a core belief that risks and returns in Emerging Markets are largely driven by country and sector themes, as well as the prevailing macroeconomic conditions. The annual dispersion of returns in MSCI EM EMEA since 2009 has been c.3x that of Developed Markets, with very little correlation within the region. Therefore, against this backdrop, being able to successfully identify the winning geographies and themes within the region can provide a meaningful basis to enhance returns.

The fund employs a repeatable investment strategy based upon top down asset allocation to sector, country and thematic opportunities, which seeks to optimise the risk profile of the fund, with a fundamental bottom up overlay to pick the best companies to capitalise on ideas and enhance alpha from idiosyncratic stock selection.

Risk management and capital preservation are central to the strategy,  both through maintaining a highly liquid portfolio (aiming to ensure that as close as possible to 100% of the portfolio can be exited within one trading day where possible) and actively managing the gross and net exposure of the fund. Typically the fund has a portfolio of 30-40 positions, whilst also making active use of futures and options to limit short term market gyrations that are common in Emerging Markets.

Carl Tohme, the portfolio manager, has over 20 years' experience investing in Emerging Markets and the fund has a 15 year audited track record, with a consistent record of strong outperformance vs Emerging Market indices on an absolute and risk-adjusted basis.

management_company_description:
Welton Investment Partners is an alternative asset manager with expertise in systematic strategies. The firm seeks to deliver absolute returns with a low correlation to the broader markets. Welton serves institutional and private investors from offices in California, New York, with a research center in Paris, France.

INVESTMENT PHILOSOPHY. We believe the greatest attributes of alternative investments are the potential to provide uncompromising returns, real diversification, and performance when equity and credit assets falter.

TEAM. We foster a culture of collaboration among highly driven individuals with expertise in conducting rigorous and innovative research across several branches of mathematics.

EXPERIENCE. Drawing upon a library of investment strategies developed over the course of three decades, we seek to harness enduring global returns from four major asset classes: foreign exchange, commodities, fixed income, and equities.

PROCESS DISCIPLINE. We believe that focusing on a portfolio of recurrent market events, harnessing well-researched team insights, and applying rigorously tested mathematical models, leads to superior absolute return opportunities fit for all market environments.
strategy_description:

It trades a diversified group of highly liquid global markets including fixed income, equity indices, commodities and currencies.

PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES.
1. Annualized returns greater than 2% over broad CTA indices over an investment cycle
2. Low correlation to broad equity and credit markets
3. Equity bear market performance

PROCESS. We adhere to a disciplined investment process across a broad set of assets and strategies in pursuit of repeatable returns. Our investment team fuses decades of market trading experience with quantitative insights to pursue recurrent macroeconomic and capital market return sources.

The long only option portfolio is designed and dynamically managed to maximize reliability, reactivity, convexity, and asymmetry and minimize cost and carry. management_company_description: Founded in 1992, Mariner Investment Group is an alternative investment management firm that invests across diversified portfolios of fixed income and credit strategies, in both public and private markets. Mariner has an exceptional track record of identifying and attracting some of the industry’s leading senior talent and providing them with the infrastructure and investment oversight necessary to build successful investment businesses.  All of Mariner’s investment strategies are supported by a robust institutional framework that sustains deep counterparty relationships and includes a strong, centralized risk management culture and compliance function. strategy_description: The Mariner Glen Oaks Fund (“the Fund” or “MGO”) employs an event-driven long/short credit strategy with an opportunistic, fundamental value-oriented approach to investing in the securities of companies experiencing financial stress or distress.  The Fund focuses on middle market, credit investments globally in a range of developed markets.  MGO invests actively in distressed situations including exchanges, liquidations, and restructurings, where we seek to create equity positions at meaningful discounts to private and public market valuations.  The Fund also invests in performing credit investments with potential event catalysts.  Particularly at points in the cycle when distressed opportunities are less prevalent, MGO will invest heavily in underfollowed, “stressed” leveraged loans trading below par with potential liability-management event drivers for early principal repayment or improved terms. The goal of this effort is to attain superior equity-like returns through realized event catalysts, while still benefiting from the relative higher safety provided by a senior, secured position in the capital structure.  The Fund’s active short credit portfolio, in tandem with the event-driven nature of its strategy, has historically mitigated correlation to the broad credit markets while preserving capital during market declines. We believe the Fund’s size maximizes opportunities to establish positions in a range of less-followed situations in the securities of middle market U.S. and European corporate borrowers.

strategy_description:
BMARK launched on November 1, 2023 to execute an Agency MBS REIT-like investment strategy, which is intended to capitalize on the high yield and opportunistic trading environment in Agency MBS. Bright Meadow is targeting a 2Q 2026 launch of a private, non-traded Agency mortgage REIT that will invest directly into the existing BMARK Master Fund (“Prospective BMARK mREIT”), aiming to deliver a hedged and levered Agency MBS investment strategy with the added tax efficiency of a REIT structure. We believe the combination of a non-traded REIT format and BMARK’s alpha-driven approach represents a new paradigm for Agency mREIT investing—enhancing the income-generating attributes of traditional mREITs but taking out the equity volatility. In our opinion, Agency MBS not only offers the potential for high yields, but—compared to other high-dividend or income-generating strategies—an Agency mREIT approach provides exposure to distinct risk and return drivers that can enhance portfolio diversification and reduce correlation with broader markets.


* This overview also reflects the Bright Meadow Team's opinion and beliefs about the Bright Meadow Agency Markets Fund (“BMARK” or the “Fund”), the prospective Agency MBS REIT (“mREIT) entity that will invest all of its assets into the existing BMARK Master Fund (the “Prospective BMARK mREIT”), mREITs in general, and the current perceived investment opportunity, as well as the Team's perceived advantages as compared to other investment managers.

strategy_description:
Bright Meadow Agency MBS Fund (”BAMS") is a diversified Agency MBS hedge fund that seeks to deliver attractive absolute returns through its unique multi-strategy approach to the asset class. We utilize three main sub-strategies to extract alpha from the Agency MBS market: Structured MBS Investing, CMO Creation Arbitrage and Relative Value Trading. We believe this combination of distinct return drivers helps us generate returns across a wide range of market environments. Agency MBS is a multi-trillion dollar market with securities issued by Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, or Ginnie Mae; principal and interest payments are either implicitly or explicitly guaranteed by the U.S. Government, allowing for efficient risk-weighted capital treatment. We employ a disciplined relative value approach to identifying undervalued bonds, sectors, and relationships in an effort to build a cash flow generative portfolio with low duration, low correlation to the broader markets, and an asymmetric risk-return profile. Income-oriented returns are enhanced through active trading and potential capital appreciation as a result of diligent asset selection, robust modeling, active sector rotation and creativity of trade expression.

*The Fund Description reflects the Bright Meadow Team's opinions and beliefs about asset class characterizations, the opportunity set and the team's perceived advantages. management_company_description: Eagle Health Investments LP ("Eagle Health") is a Greenwich, CT-based investment management firm organized on October 10, 2019, as a Delaware limited partnership. The Firm was founded by Gary Stern, who serves as Chief Investment Officer and is responsible for all investment-related decisions. Mr. Stern is a former CIO of Ziff Capital Partners with over 20 years of experience in the healthcare space.
strategy_description: Eagle Health Investments LP ("Eagle Health") invests in publicly traded securities in seeking to capitalize on innovation and disruption in the healthcare sector. Eagle Health focuses on chronic disease, inadequate care, and misaligned incentives that are driving the need for a dramatic change in the healthcare industry, as well as strong innovation addressing a defined market need. Eagle Health believes that the convergence of key innovative forces has the potential to dramatically change the healthcare system in the coming years, creating an unprecedented investment landscape. The acceleration of progress in different disciplines - specifically biology and data science - is beginning to redefine what is achievable to the benefit of patients and the healthcare system. The resulting investment climate will present both winners and losers. Eagle Health's strategy is focused on capitalizing on these trends throughout the healthcare sector. Eagle Health pursues a bottom-up diligence process to understand how innovation or disruptive change will impact portfolio candidates' financial results over 3-, 5- and 7-year periods. Eagle Health's diligence process seeks to overlay rigorous thematic research with the aforementioned bottom-up research process to identify the most attractive investment opportunities. Position sizing is determined by the overall P&L opportunity, the IRR profile of the investment (across several periods), forecast realization and numerous other considerations of the investment, such as company stage of lifecycle, risk of permanent capital loss, liquidity, signpost diligence, event path and other risk factors. Eagle Health's idea generation process is designed to produce an ongoing pipeline of investment ideas that Eagle Health actively monitors. Eagle Health is highly selective as to what goes into the portfolio at any given time, based on an evaluation of the thematic opportunity and the risk/reward of an individual security over the near- and long-term.
region_exposure_description: The Fund predominantly focuses its investments on publicly listed equities in North America, Europe, and Japan. portfolio_additional_details:
Portfolio candidates typically exhibit three essential characteristics. First, they experience significant change, whether positive or negative, driven by innovation or disruption. Second, this change is anticipated to have a substantial impact on financial results over the next 3-7 years. Lastly, the management teams of these candidates boast a proven track record of success and maintain a laser-focused approach towards long-term opportunities.

If our firm identifies a company with promising potential either presently or for future prospects, our attention then shifts to determining where that issuer stands in terms of its life cycle. This categorization is primarily based on three distinct stages. Firstly, the "Pre-Proof of Concept" stage refers to companies that are introducing new products or services. These offerings might still be untested, but they hold the promise to significantly influence their respective sectors over the ensuing five years. Secondly, there's the "Proof of Concept" stage. Companies in this category have cemented their presence in the market and have either recently started turning a profit or are projected to become profitable in the forthcoming three years, all within a realm offering substantial growth potential. Lastly, companies in the "Replication" stage distinguish themselves with a robust competitive stance, consistent profitability, and ample opportunities to delve deeper into lucrative market segments.
