MAN GROUP TODAY – KEY FACTS
•	Trading since 1783 with more than 30 years of experience in alternative investments
•	USD 213.9 billion assets under management
•	Headquarters in London with offices in every major region
•	Global footprint – a powerful distribution network that serves a highly-diversified and global client base
•	Constituent of the FTSE 250 Index (UK:EMG)


Man Group’s business model comprises a compelling array of investment products and investment management expertise. Whilst the underlying specialists operate independently of one another, they all benefit from Man Group’s robust risk and operational infrastructure, financial strength and centralised support functions.
strategy_description:
Man Strategies 1783 ('1783') is a diversified multi-strategy fund, run with established portfolio construction and risk management techniques. 1783 directly trades all asset classes and aims to perform in a variety of market conditions, and offers unique access to c.75 established discretionary and systematic strategies from across Man Group, in an efficient structure.

Our investment universe is a platform of alternative and absolute return strategies which all benefit from Man Group’s robust infrastructure, financial backing and centralised support functions. This allows our specialist teams of investment professionals to concentrate solely on investment management and research to find value adding investment opportunities. These range from identifying market trends and other inefficiencies which can be traded systematically to discretionary
expertise in fundamental security selection across equities, credits, convertible bonds, and other asset classes.
share_class_additional_details:
Please note all performance statistics and charts are based on the lead reporting share class. Simulated past performance is not indicative of future results. Returns may increase or decrease as a result of currency fluctuations. 

From September 2024 onwards, performance shown is for Man Strategies 1783 Class B2 USD and is net of a 1.0% management fee and a performance fee of 15%, plus additional talent pass through costs included within the underlying portfolio funds. Between 31 January 2020 and September 2024, net performance is represented by modelled performance derived by applying the fee structure of Class B2 USD to actual gross performance achieved by another Man Strategies 1783 share class which is no longer available to new investors. Different share classes may have different fee levels, please see the Fund’s prospectus for more information. 

Talent pass -through costs - Talent acquisition costs: we have modelled the historical talent acquisition costs and 1783's pro rata share of those costs. We have taken a prudent view and added, per annum or pro -rata as appropriate, additional talent acquisition costs and extra uncovered guarantees to reflect future hiring drive, primarily in Discretionary. Talent Acquisition costs are applied at the master level , thus reducing the return which is subject to the 15% performance fee.

management_company_description: AllianceBernstein (AB) is a leading global investment management firm that offers high-quality research and diversified investment services to institutional investors, individuals and private wealth clients in markets worldwide. We are one of the largest investment management firms in the world, with $647 billion in assets under management as of June 30, 2022. Our global client base includes some of the world’s leading institutions as well as private wealth clients and retail investors. We maintain research, portfolio management, wealth-management and client service offices around the world, reflecting our global capabilities and the needs of our clients. Partnering closely with clients, our research and portfolio management teams collaborate across asset classes, regions, sectors, and investment strategies to spark new thinking and deliver attractive risk-adjusted returns to keep our clients “Ahead of Tomorrow.”
strategy_description: AB Event Driven seeks to generate returns by systematically investing in companies affected by known corporate transactions.  The portfolio combines two underlying strategies: 1) a hard catalyst strategy which invests in companies tied to M&A transactions where the outcomes and timelines are clearly defined and 2) a systematic catalyst strategy which targets a broader set of corporate, sentiment, flow, and price-based events where timeline and market impact are less predictable.  Positions can be long or short and the strategy is diversified by region and event type with an emphasis on risk management, minimizing equity market beta, and portfolio volatility.  AB Event Driven is managed within a UCITS framework and thus allows for daily liquidity and consistent exposure to event driven return sources.

management_company_description: Whitebox Advisors LLC (“Whitebox”) is a multi-strategy alternative asset manager that seeks to generate optimal risk-adjusted returns for a diversified base of public institutions, private entities and qualified individuals. strategy_description: The investment objective of Whitebox Relative Value Partners, LP (the "Partnership") is to generate an attractive risk adjusted return. Whitebox seeks to identify "relative value arbitrage" opportunities, primarily but not exclusively involving convertible securities. In relative value trading, Whitebox seeks to identify and opportunistically profit from temporary price differentials between related, highly correlated financial instruments. Whitebox may sell short the instrument it believes is overpriced and buy the instrument it believes is underpriced. As pricing inefficiencies persist or become resolved, Whitebox positions are modified accordingly - holding positions that continue to be undervalued and closing positions that become priced more efficiently. Whitebox's investment portfolio generally consists of long positions in debt or preferred equity securities, which are offset with short positions in junior securities, usually the underlying equity security related to the long position. In most cases, the long position is a security which is readily convertible into the underlying short position.

name: Regents Gate Capital Master Fund
management_company_description: Regents Gate Capital LLP (“RGC”) was incorporated in May 2023 in the UK, RGC was founded with the objective of delivering consistent, uncorrelated returns, driven by a proven investment process pioneered by the Co-Founders. The Strategy is a continuation of the investment philosophy that Joshua White, CIO, has practiced throughout his career, with the integration of enhanced sophistication of Large Data, and AI Machine Learning techniques. Each of the three Co-Founders have long-standing experience and expertise in each of their respective fields and have partnered together successfully earlier in their careers.
strategy_description:
The fund pursues a fundamental equity market-neutral strategy that is focused on extracting idiosyncratic alpha and generating uncorrelated returns. The strategy combines deep fundamental analysis with a differentiated approach to data processing and AI machine learning. 

The strategy utilizes fundamental domain expertise to determine what predictive KPIs drive idiosyncratic stock performance. RGC focuses on KPIs where we can have a consistent, differentiated edge by combining numerous data sources with a significant explanatory power. With RGC’s purpose built technology infrastructure, the process excels when examining large, mature and complex company business models. Currently, this includes a substantial part of the global industrials universe.

The strategy offers returns that are uncorrelated by design with a beta of less than 1% and idiosyncratic risk of greater than 80%. As a result the strategy has a historical Sharpe Ratio of greater than 2 and an expected target volatility of 6-8% leading to double digit returns net of fees historically.
Currently 90% of the portfolio is in Industrials across US, Europe and Asia from a liquid universe of stocks with a market cap of greater than $1bn with maximum position sizes of less than 2%. The gross exposure range will typically be 200-300% with the fund holding 80-100 listed single name long and short positions across cash equities and equity swaps.

strategy_description:

Portfolio structured to be a ‘pure alpha’ strategy that does not require commodities to trend up or down to be profitable, but rather where returns are driven by expertise in trade structuring, execution and timing. Implemented via liquid futures and options. 

Seasoned commodities portfolio manager with experience trading through multiple cycles over 30-year period, as a market maker, sell-side trader and buy-side portfolio manager.

name: Axebrook Credit Alpha Fund
management_company_description:
Axebrook Capital LLP ("Axebrook") is a London-based partnership established by founder and CIO Jack Land.  Axebrook is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority to act as an Alternative Investment Fund Manager.  

Prior to Axebrook, Jack was at York Capital Management ("York"), where since July 2020 he was lead portfolio manager for the Axebrook Credit Alpha Fund ("ACA" or the "Fund", formerly known as the York Global Credit Income Fund).  With effect from 1 February 2022, Axebrook replaced York as investment manager of the Fund.  The master and feeder fund vehicles remain unchanged and existing investors fully consented to the spinoff. Day 1 capital was in excess of $100 million, with substantial support via a seeding arrangement with York affiliated investors. 

The Axebrook team was built up during 2021 and brings with it significant industry experience.
strategy_description:
ACA is a liquid credit fund investing primarily in corporate credit in the US and Europe (bonds, loans and CDS), both long and short. This absolute return strategy is based on fundamental, bottoms-up research, with an event-driven tilt.  Axebrook believes that corporate credit markets are inherently inefficient due to various systemic factors (e.g. sharp decline in broker dealer holdings post 2008, limited “electronification” in credit markets, the rise of CLOs and ETFs, non-economic buy and sell decisions driven by ratings agency actions, etc), and aims to generate high risk-adjusted returns at all points in the credit cycle by exploiting mispriced risk in these markets. 

The Firm will apply an active trading strategy and vary its net exposure to manage risk throughout the cycle.  Portfolio construction will typically consist of 40-50 long positions and 10-20 short positions, with a targeted gross exposure of 100-200% and a net exposure of 40-60%.  The strategy’s short book is comprised of single name alpha shorts as well as overlay hedges (both risk and rates) that seek to minimize volatility and drawdown risk.

The Fund is structured as a Cayman master feeder with an onshore and offshore feeder. Liquidity terms are quarterly with 90 days notice.  There are no investor level or fund level gates.  The Fund will have two share classes, a Founders Class and a Standard Class, which differ as to lock up term and management fees and performance fees charged.

name: MY Asian Opportunities Fund
management_company_description: MY.Alpha is a Hong Kong-based investment manager specializing in pan-Asian investment opportunities. Utilizing a fundamental catalyst-driven approach, MY.Alpha seeks to capitalize on themes of change that are occurring across the region. MY.Alpha is regulated and licensed by the SFC under CE number APJ354 for the Regulated Activities of Asset Management and Advising on Securities. The Firm currently has 14 Investment Professionals, two of whom are Co-Portfolio Managers, headed by Masa Yamaguchi as CEO & CIO. The Investment Team is supported by 13 Non-Investment Professionals locally.
strategy_description:
MY Asian Opportunities Fund invests primarily in the securities of Asian companies using a catalyst-driven, fundamental value approach. The Fund targets event-driven situations with asymmetric return profiles, including M&A, corporate restructurings, distressed opportunities, and arbitrage opportunities created by market dislocation.

We target investments with the potential for transformative change and where we believe there is an asymmetric return profile: 
1.	Special Situations: Opportunities as a result of increasing corporate activity through spin-offs, asset sales, divestitures, and stock buybacks
2.	Arbitrage: Opportunities as companies seek growth or to increase value via mergers and acquisitions
3.	Credit: Opportunities in bankruptcies, restructurings, refinancing, M&A, convertible bonds and credit default swaps

Additionally, the Special Investments Class was established with the purpose of allowing investors to participate in certain private assets, while not impacting the liquidity of the Fund. Investors can Opt-In on a monthly basis and Opt-Out annually on July 1 with 60-day notice. Private assets examples include pre-IPO positions, distressed debt and private investments in public equity, among others. At the time of investment, the aggregate amount of the Special Investments Class will not exceed 15% of eligible interests in the Fund.

name: LMR CCSA Fund
management_company_description:
LMR Partners was set up in November 2009 by the founding partners, Ben Levine, Stefan Renold and Andrew Manuel.
The flagship Fund, the LMR Master Fund Limited, was launched on 1st February 2010 and runs a global, liquid, multi-asset investment strategy, employing both systematic and discretionary sub-strategies across asset classes.

Our investment philosophy is to exploit relative value opportunities across a range of asset classes, regions and time horizons.
We aim to build a diversified investment portfolio with a low correlation between separate strategies and strive to achieve absolute returns with a low correlation to markets.

Firm assets under management are approximately $10.7bn (as at 30th August 2023).
There are currently 260 employees Firm-wide, across London, Hong Kong, New York, Zurich, Dubai And Glasgow, with 110 investment professionals and 150 non-investment professionals (as at 30th August 2023).
strategy_description:
The CCSA strategy has been managed within the flagship Multi-Strategy Fund (the LMR Multi-Strategy Fund) since November 2018. The CCSA strategy
continues to be traded within the LMR Multi-Strategy Fund, pari passu to the LMR CCSA Fund. The LMR CCSA Fund employs a global convertible and capital structure arbitrage strategy that seeks to target returns on a predefined time horizon through fair value convergence and asymmetric implementation of catalyst driven trades. The Fund aims to achieve consistent risk-adjusted returns for its investors, in a market agnostic fashion.

strategy_description:
The LMR Alpha Rates Trading Fund was launched on 1st June 2014 and is run by Co-Fixed Income CIOs, Domenico Iuliano and Danny Mitchell. Domenico and Danny joined LMR in May 2012 and May 2013 respectively, initially trading the Fixed Income Relative Value strategy within the LMR flagship Fund, LMR Fund Limited. The CIOs previously worked together at Morgan Stanley from 2004 – 2007 before reuniting at LMR Partners in 2013.

The strategy is Fixed Income Relative Value with a core focus on investing in liquid rates markets in G10 economies. Prior to the launch of the Alpha Rates Trading Fund on 1st June 2014, Domenico Iuliano and Danny Mitchell managed the strategy within the LMR Fund from May 2012, returning >30% net performance with a Sharpe ratio of ~4 during the period.

The CIOs have invested in the LMR Alpha Rates Trading Fund since inception along with the original founding partners of LMR.

name: LMR Multi-Strategy Fund
management_company_description:
LMR Partners was set up in November 2009 by the founding partners, Ben Levine, Stefan Renold and Andrew Manuel.
The flagship Fund, the LMR Master Fund Limited, was launched on 1st February 2010 and runs a global, liquid, multi-asset investment strategy, employing both systematic and discretionary sub-strategies across asset classes.

Our investment philosophy is to exploit relative value opportunities across a range of asset classes, regions and time horizons.
We aim to build a diversified investment portfolio with a low correlation between separate strategies and strive to achieve absolute returns with a low correlation to markets.

Firm assets under management are approximately $10.7bn (as at 30th August 2023).
There are currently 260 employees Firm-wide, across London, Hong Kong, New York, Zurich, Dubai And Glasgow, with 110 investment professionals and 150 non-investment professionals (as at 30th August 2023).
strategy_description:
We deploy capital across a diverse selection of mostly market neutral investment strategies spanning a variety of asset classes, regions and horizons. 
We aim to balance capital across sub-strategies focused on exploiting inefficiencies within fixed income, equity, credit, volatility, equity arbitrate & event, and commodities driven markets. Each of these product lines / asset classes are overseen by a dedicated Product Head.
Each sub-strategy within the Fund is run by an expert portfolio manager or trading team, with each group working independently, effecting investments for their own segregated investment portfolio. 
Trading teams managing separate sub-strategies may be led by one or more portfolio managers. Teams with multiple portfolio managers may work collaboratively on investments for such portfolio. Such collaborative teams and their portfolios are however functionally segregated from other portfolio managers / trading teams.
All portfolio managers / trading teams are overseen by a formal Risk Committee comprised of Product Heads, the Chief Operating Officer, and Chief Risk Officer.
As a result of the segregation of portfolio managers / trading teams and as an inherent facet of our multi-strategy approach, such teams may take opposing positions in the same investments / securities, notwithstanding that such trading positions have been affected for the same fund.

strategy_description:
Wellington Global Technology Long/Short Fund is a technology hedge fund managed by Bruce Glazer. The fund combines experienced technology investors in a proven investment process that is grounded in bottom-up fundamental research. The fund was launched in January 2000.

The portfolio manager looks for investments across the spectrum of global technology companies, with a focus on those subsectors and companies that are likely to generate attractive absolute returns while also leveraging the research produced by other Wellington Management technology analysts.

The investment process is based on bottom-up, fundamental analysis of technology companies worldwide. The portfolio is continually rebalanced so that investments are made in those sectors and companies that are most appealing at any time. As a result, exposure to individual sub-sectors within technology will depend on supply-demand characteristics, secular trends, existing product evaluations, and new product developments. Focus is on direct contact with company management, suppliers, and competitors to identify favorable investment opportunities not yet recognized by the market. The key objective of the partnership is to achieve superior total returns on an absolute basis. In order to achieve this goal, the manager invests in companies with growth potential and good stock appreciation potential, while taking short positions in poorly positioned companies with unsustainable valuations.

strategy_description:
The Fund is an absolute return focused, lower beta, long/short approach investing in global equities. It is diversified across sectors and regions, with an emphasis on TMT/Consumer (50-60% exposure) in the US (50-75% exposure). The strategy is managed by Mike Toman, who began running the Fund in October of 2022 after managing discretionary capital at Citadel from 2016-2021. Mike draws on the idea generation from a dedicated team and Wellington’s 18-person Growth Equity Platform, as well as Wellington’s expansive fundamental equity research across sectors and regions, macro resources, risk analytics, and derivatives trading.

The Fund's edge resides in the art of marrying short, medium, and long-term perspectives, seeking to time and size investments appropriately, recognizing when short-term data provides differentiation and when it may obscure long-term opportunity—such as underappreciated product launches or structural shifts. The Fund seeks to generate alpha through security selection in both the long and short book, protect the downside, and generate a Sharpe Ratio >1.

strategy_description:
- Long/short fundamental European equity strategy focused on identifying long and short return opportunities across European companies.
- Low net exposure, flexible and bottom up driven, typically between 20%-60% net and often lower on a beta-adjusted basis. Realized beta and correlation since inception below 0.1. 
- Identifies long opportunities in stocks of companies that demonstrate structural growth, a competitive advantage, and reasonable valuations against the market.
- Identifies short opportunities in stocks of companies that show signs of weakening structural growth, worsening competitive advantage and often signs of aggressive accounting.
- Strives to generate alpha from both longs and shorts, we expect all shorts to be single name alpha shorts.
- Typically invests in 50-90 longs and 60-100 shorts, 200-300% gross exposure.
region_exposure_description:

strategy_description:
Bay Pond:
Bay Pond is an opportunistic long/short equity approach with a focus on financials and fintech and a track record dating back to 1994. Bay Pond is managed by Nick Adams, who leads (along with Matt Lipton) a six-person dedicated portfolio management team with over 100 years of combined professional experience, and is supported by an 11-member global finance research team and the broader resources of Wellington Management Company. Investing successfully across the financial services sector requires both specialization and a deep network of relationships cultivated over years of interactions. At Wellington, we believe our edge in is in the proprietary data we collect, our specialist focus, and our decades of relationships in the sector.

Investment Approach: 
Bay Pond seeks capital appreciation by investing in both long and short positions primarily in the financial services and related sectors. The portfolio invests primarily in banks, insurance companies, asset managers, broker dealers, mortgage banks, commercial and consumer finance firms, REITs, and financial technology companies. Bay Pond is typically directional but dynamically hedged to protect capital in down markets.

Our investment framework focuses on deep, bottom-up, fundamental research, through which we look up and down the capital structure and across sub-sectors and geographies. The impact of disruptive technologies, interest rate levels, yield curve shape, credit markets, regulation, and the health of the economy is embedded in our investment lens. The approach does not require a directional view on financial stocks, just an appreciation that high volatility and meaningful dispersion within the sector will offer attractive investment opportunities across this diverse and nuanced sector. We utilize a wide range of hedging techniques to potentially enhance returns, mitigate risk, and protect capital.

strategy_description:
Global Research Equity Extended is a long/short equity fund that seeks to outperform the MSCI World (Net) Index consistently over market cycles through stock selection by a team of experienced industry-focused sub-portfolio managers. Each sub-portfolio manager is responsible for a sleeve of the fund, investing within their industries of expertise. The fund will aim to maintain a net exposure of 100%. In contrast to traditional long-only equity funds, gross leverage provides each sub-portfolio manager with additional flexibility to overweight and underweight stocks versus the benchmark. With capital allocated across a diverse set of industries and managed by sub-portfolio managers with differentiated investment styles, the fund aims to maintain high active share with a moderate and balanced risk profile versus the benchmark. Allocation of capital across the sleeves and the overall risk profile of the fund are managed by the Fundamental Factor Platform team.
The fund consists of multiple industry-based sleeves managed by a team of sub-portfolio managers, and each sleeve will hold long and short positions in individual equity securities while seeking to maintain a net exposure of approximately 100%. The fund is expected to have sector exposures which are typically similar to the MSCI World (Net) Index, a gross exposure between approximately 200-250%, a net exposure of approximately 100%, and a beta close to 1.0. In addition, exposures to risk factors for the fund will be managed by Edward Baldini and John Smallcomb, who are members of the Fundamental Factor Platform team, through capital allocation, gross leverage allocation, and risk-based hedges.

strategy_description:
US Research Equity Extended is a long/short equity fund that seeks to outperform the S&P 500 Index consistently over market cycles through stock selection by a team of experienced industry-focused sub-portfolio managers. Each sub-portfolio manager is responsible for a sleeve of the fund, investing within their industries of expertise. The fund will aim to maintain a net exposure of 100%. In contrast to traditional long-only equity funds, gross leverage provides each sub-portfolio manager with additional flexibility to overweight and underweight stocks versus the benchmark. With capital allocated across a diverse set of industries and managed by sub-portfolio managers with differentiated investment styles, the fund aims to maintain high active share with a moderate and balanced risk profile versus the benchmark. Allocation of capital across the sleeves and the overall risk profile of the fund are managed by the Fundamental Factor Platform team.

The fund consists of multiple industry-based sleeves managed by a team of sub-portfolio managers, and each sleeve will hold long and short positions in individual equity securities while seeking to maintain a net exposure of approximately 100%. The fund is expected to have sector exposures which are typically similar to the S&P 500 Index, a gross exposure between approximately 120-250%, a net exposure of approximately 100%, and a beta that is comparable to the S&P 500 Index. In addition, exposures to risk factors for the fund will be managed by Edward Baldini and John Smallcomb who are members of the Fundamental Factor Platform team, through capital allocation, gross leverage allocation, and risk-based hedges.

strategy_description:
Fund Summary:
The Fund's objective is to generate consistent alpha, independent from market beta and risk assets through time, by combining specialization, diversification, and risk management. The process combines the discipline of fundamental macro research with independent risk-taking. The investment opportunity set consists primarily of fixed income (both rates and credit), currency and equity markets.
Investment Approach:
The investment process has three key components: idea generation, capital allocation, and risk management.
Investment ideas are generated based on an objective and risk-managed macro research process designed to identify structural imbalances, turning points in the business cycle and implications for the macro policy environment. Macro research is a specialized process purely focused on idea generation and is independent of market risk-taking. This separation enables the minimization of behavioral biases in interpreting macro data and allows for timely shifts in the macroeconomic outlook. The focus of the global bond strategists is to identify the macro scenarios that are most likely to occur. The identification of key guideposts is critical in assessing how the probabilities of different scenarios are evolving.
Capital is allocated to each portfolio manager based on an objective evaluation of his individual investment skill. This assessment utilizes a quantitative ranking system which focuses on measures such as demonstrated Sharpe ratio, average annual return to maximum drawdown, liquidity, and correlation to market beta and correlation among portfolio managers. Macro investment ideas are expressed through directional, non-directional and extension strategies across our opportunity set.
Risk management is fully integrated into the investment process. The daily risk management process is designed to ensure that the portfolio's aggregate risk profile is consistent with its return objective and risk tolerance. There is an emphasis on minimizing drawdown by limiting concentration and correlation risk, which is achieved by clearly identifying and measuring factor sensitivities across the portfolio. The risk monitoring process evaluates pre- and post-trade positioning across multiple dimensions, including aggregate interest rate, credit, and currency sensitivities, ex-ante value at risk (VaR), sensitivity to macro factors, as well as through a spectrum of historical scenarios and stress tests.

name: Covalis Capital Master Fund
management_company_description:
Covalis Capital is multi-sector specialist that focuses primarily on equities of Utilities, Infrastructure, Real Estate, Autos Value Chain, Industrials, Materials, Energy, Telecommunication and Renewables sectors globally.

Founded in 2012, Covalis manages $2.8bn in capital across both private and public equities, spanning low net hedge fund products, directional strategies and co-investments.

While the business started in 2012, the core Covalis team has been successfully managing capital with a consistent investment philosophy since 2004. Prior to founding the business, Zach Mecelis, CIO, and Peter Murphy, Head of Research, ran a hedge fund strategy at Nobel Group and prior to that, were running a strategy at GLG Partners.

At the core, the investment philosophy is based on ensuring deep sector specialism and a rigorous proprietary research approach. The investment team is comprised of over 50 Investment Professionals organized by sector focus. That said, the team operates on an integrated basis with strong collaboration, ensuring we extract valuable research synergies that are becoming more relevant as the energy transition is increasing the interconnections amongst our core sectors.

Our hedge fund products are focused on equity long short investment. Stylistically, the approach is relative value, where we seek to implement ideas hedged at the trade level within sectors, and we are agnostic between long and short alpha. At the over all fund level this leads to a tight factor exposure and uncorrelated profile.
strategy_description: The Covalis Capital Master Fund Limited (the “Fund”) follows an equity focused long short strategy. The team’s fundamental research approach is centered on developing a clear variant perception in our investments, and identifying catalysts that will unlock value. In terms of asset class exposure, over 80% of risk is expressed through equities, with the residual being in fixed income and commodities. In addition, the Fund has the ability to invest up to 15% in privates. The implementation of the equity book is relative value, with sub-sector hedging at the idea level, that results in a low market exposure of ± 15% and constrained factor risk.

The Covalis Capital Partners Master Fund Limited (the “Fund”) employs a long-short, low-net strategy, focused primarily on equities of Utilities, Infrastructure, Real Estate, Autos Value Chain, Industrials, Materials, Energy, Telecommunication and Renewables sectors mainly in developed OECD countries. The core investable universe consists of c. 800 companies globally in which the team is active at any given time. We are agnostic between long and short ideas, but have a strong preference for avoiding using index products to hedge. The Fund also utilizes European sovereign fixed income instruments opportunistically to hedge country risk.

strategy_description:
The Master Fund’s investment philosophy is founded on a belief in the value of specialization and decentralization. The Investment Manager believes that geographical and product specialization provides a persistent competitive advantage. Domain expertise allows a deeper understanding of idiosyncratic, geographical and product level market drivers. Based on this, the Investment Manager seeks to repeatedly extract risk premia from individual markets. Aggregating the modules’ return streams, which have historically exhibited low correlation amongst themselves, the Master Fund aims to achieve persistent steady returns with a high Sharpe Ratio. The investment philosophy permeates through the organizational structure of the Master Fund, the investment style and the nature of return streams.
The Investment Manager’s centralized research function supports individual modules with bottom-up analysis and works together with the CIO team to identify, predict and monetize top-down thematic trends. In doing so, the research team deploys a range of primarily quantitative tools, ranging from short-term tactical allocation models to long-term fundamental economic analysis.
The Master Fund will focus a significant majority of trades and investments in the Asia-Pacific region. Having already surpassed the US and Euro area as the largest economic region globally, the Investment Manager expects Asia-Pacific to grow at a significantly higher rate than major developed economies. Within the region, countries exhibit significantly different levels of economic and financial market development. Accordingly, the return streams available from different countries differ in magnitude and nature. The Investment Manager believes that market growth will provide ongoing opportunities to extract alpha.
Although the Master Fund’s portfolio will consist primarily of the strategies mentioned above, the Master Fund may also take positions in a wide range of asset classes, financial instruments and strategies, which may not clearly fall within those mentioned above, but which the Investment Manager believes are consistent with the Master Fund’s investment objective.

name: Amundi Chenavari Credit Fund
management_company_description:
Chenavari is an established, credit-focused asset manager with a core expertise in European markets. With expertise across the liquidity spectrum of credit, Chenavari aims to profit from idiosyncrasies and inefficiencies within credit markets, which are due to macro (such as banks' deleveraging, monetary policies, etc.) as well as technical factors. The Firm concentrates its investment activity on fundamental strategies that may offer attractive risk-reward profiles on a relative value basis with low market correlation and low beta to broad credit markets.

Chenavari’s investment strategies can be segmented across three groups: 

•	Liquid strategies, including investments in single name corporates, European financials, credit indices, asset-backed securities, across both cash and derivative markets;
•	Private Credit strategies, such as portfolio acquisitions of primarily performing loans; risk sharing/significant risk transfer, asset-based lending, and specialty finance (new loan origination) in consumer finance, receivables and leasing; and
•	CLO management, including investment in senior secured loans and revolving credit facilities through European collateralised loan obligation structures.
strategy_description: The Strategy is a European focused fundamental long/short credit strategy with a dynamic allocation to Chenavari’s two sub-strategies: Long/Short Corporate Credit (40-50% allocation) and Long/Short European Financials (40-50% allocation). The Strategy targets investments in the European credit market, from opportunities which arise from inefficiencies and dislocations driven by a combination of Central Bank actions, continuing bank deleveraging, corporate fundamentals and geopolitical uncertainty. Within the L/S European Corporate sub-strategy, the Fund intends to capture alpha through fundamental and technical analysis. The strategy aims at identifying any mispricing or misunderstood credit situations across Europe. This strategy is therefore long/short; shorts can be implemented via repos, total return swaps and credit default swaps (“CDS”). The strategy invests in corporate bonds with a minimum rating of B-, with no private placements or illiquid issues. Within the L/S European Financials sub-strategy, the Fund invests primarily in bonds such as Senior Non-Preferred, legacy Tier 1, Tier 2, Contingent Convertible AT1 bonds (“CoCos”), as well as CDS. Investments are also diversified across duration, geography and issuer typology (universal bank, investment bank, insurance company etc.). To enable an active trading approach, the strategy focuses on more liquid instruments and aims at limiting investments in AT1 bonds to a net exposure of a maximum of 15% of the Fund. The Investment Process uses a fundamental, research-driven approach, with a focus on alpha opportunities and low correlation to the main asset classes. Trade implementation is made across the instruments perceived to offer the best value (both cash and derivatives).

management_company_description: Fulcrum Asset Management focuses on providing macro-oriented investment products, with the objective of delivering positive returns irrespective of market conditions. The investment approach utilizes both discretionary and systematic inputs to construct a diversified portfolio of macro themes implemented across various time horizons. strategy_description:
The Fulcrum Horizon Fund aims to capture alpha from a diversified portfolio of equities across sectors and regions, focused on second and third order effects of long-term sector trends and tactical around short-term events. It is a highly differentiated, fundamental portfolio, with 75% of alpha generated from the short side, minimal stock-specific risk. The portfolio manager has been running this strategy for 13+ years at various firms including Moore Capital and Hadron Capital. 

The fund seeks to provide consistent long-term returns within a targeted volatility and zero beta to broad equity market, achieving historically significant convexity during market downturns. The portfolio aims to remain as highly diversified and liquid as possible across 20-30 views, each implemented via custom baskets of securities, long/short hedged against indices and custom baskets.

management_company_description:
Contingency Capital invests in legal assets: we finance illiquid assets where the primary driver for unlocking the asset’s value is related to a legal, tax, or regulatory process. This includes loans to law firms, buying and financing claims, financing portfolios of litigation claims, and investing in other special situations assets that are uncorrelated to the public equity and debt markets. Unlike other litigation funders, we look at a broader scope of investments and take a credit-oriented approach. We try to structure our investments to have seniority, floating interest rates, and downside and duration protection.

Our first fund, Contingency Capital Fund I launched in June 2021 and had its final close in December 2022. It is approximately 60% deployed and we expect to be fully invested during the second half of 2024. The investments in Fund I have generated a cash-on cash return of 13% over their life and are generally uncorrelated to the broader credit and equity markets. We are targeting a first close for Fund II in the second quarter of 2024.

The fund manager, Contingency Capital LLC, was founded by Brandon Baer, who has over 20 years of experience investing in legal assets at D. E. Shaw and Fortress before founding Contingency Capital in late 2020. In addition to Fund I, Contingency Capital manages a fund of one targeting both high and lower yield opportunities of shorter duration. As of September 30, 2023, Contingency Capital has approximately $690 million of AUM. name: System 2 Master Fund
management_company_description:
The fund invests in convertible and capital structure relative value opportunities, primarily in Europe.

System 2 uses a core group of nine relative value transaction types to exploit mis-pricings of securities in the same capital structure. They identify the optimal mix of transaction types at any one point in time to construct a portfolio that is “long the wings”, net flat to credit, net flat to equity, with positive carry System 2’s core relative value transaction types are: (i) long senior / short junior, (ii) long junior / short senior, (iii) credit vs options, (iv) synthetic calls, (v) synthetic puts, (vi) long volatility, (vii) long / short pari credit, (viii) event linked credit, and (ix) short credit System 2 uses quantitative methods to filter the universe of possible trades in each transaction type, then undertakes a fundamental and legal review of those trades that present the greatest asymmetry. Provided the fundamental and legal review supports a conversion thesis / does not reveal anything that would interfere with conversion or make the mispricing endure for longer than anticipated, the trade proceeds to the portfolio. 

The market hedges - including credit market, equity market, interest rates, FX and volatility - isolate exposure to the mis-priced pairs of securities in the same capital structure, insulating the portfolio from key market risks. 

When we find a compelling anomaly, we seek similar anomalies that might indicate a larger investment theme justifying further research and investment.

At System 2, we believe that human bias can put even sound investments at risk. To guard against the impact of emotions, human biases and changing circumstances, we use processes, including our risk management processes and checklists.

Investment Process: The investment process employed by the System 2 investment team utilizes four phases with respect to the flow of an investment idea from inception to trade execution as follows: (1) sourcing; (2) evaluation; (3) decision process; and (4) portfolio management. Risk is considered at every stage of this process, from capital allocation to security selection, hedge sizing, and performance review. Risk oversight permeates portfolio construction and results in the production of meaningful risk metrics that are consistent with how the portfolio manager views risk.

strategy_description: Tudor Riverbend Crossing Partners Portfolio Ltd. (the "Portfolio"), an event driven fund, seeks to provide consistent, non-correlated returns with a focus on dynamic risk management and low beta that has allowed the fund to deliver alpha in periods of market stress. Dr. Emil Dabora is the principal portfolio manager for the Portfolio. Dr. Dabora has a 25+ year career, including as a portfolio manager at Harvard Management Company and Caxton. Dr. Dabora’s philosophy is to act as a liquidity provider to capture opportunities during changes in ownership base. The strategy encompasses hard and soft catalysts including mergers, spin-offs, restructurings, and structural and management changes, principally in equities. The investment approach identifies mispricing utilizing proprietary processes for in-depth bottom-up fundamental research on corporate events, layered with quantitative modeling and statistical analysis. A rigorous process is used to determine how to best isolate and structure investments to mitigate unwanted risk factors. Dr. Dabora also trades a substantially similar portfolio within Tudor's multi-portfolio manager, global macro focused flagship strategy.

strategy_description:

PCA is an all-weather, cycle‑resilient strategy that combines the identification of mispriced volatility with selective credit opportunities to build a consistently convex, uncorrelated, low‑beta portfolio designed to generate alpha across market conditions.  The Fund is differentiated by the portfolio manager’s experience across multiple convert cycles coupled with the firm’s strong credit underwriting. Additionally, the fund’s dynamic portfolio rotation of strategies exploits opportunities across all convertibles markets and conditions. 



The Fund’s investment approach is driven by both quantitative analysis and fundamental credit analysis. Emphasis is placed on the portfolio’s construction as we look to optimize convexity through a balance of trade types. PCA constructs convex risk profiles while hedging out the related equity and interest rate risk, with active rebalancing / gamma trading. Palmerston leverages its fundamental credit analysis skill set and highly experienced team of analysts to manage credit risk in European and Asian Investment Grade and High Yield issuers. The portfolio is diversified, dynamically employing a range of strategies with the core volatility trading augmented with put trades that provide downside protection to equity selloffs, ratchet/special situation trades that provide attractive returns during corporate activity and more credit intensive trades in busted converts and HY issuers. 



PCA identifies the most convex opportunities in the asset class combined with a strong risk management framework encompassing portfolio liquidity, downside risk assessment and trade management to generate attractive risk adjusted returns over a long-term investment horizon with an emphasis on capital preservation.

management_company_description: Palmerston Capital Management LLP is a London based alternative asset manager which started trading in January 2014 and manages comingled and SMA hedge fund products.
strategy_description:
The Palmerston Credit Master Fund is a Cayman master/feeder absolute return fund implementing a European long/short credit strategy across the debt capital structure. The fund targets 10-12% returns with 5% volatility through the cycle, by focusing on convexity through a mix of deep dive fundamental research and instrument selection. The Fund's investment approach is driven primarily by strong fundamental credit analysis, and augmented by research into macro and regulatory drivers, as well as specific security documentation to assess the optimum medium in which risk is taken. The fund targets investment opportunities in both European financials and corporates with capital allocated dynamically between the two. The strong fundamental approach places emphasis on underlying credit trends, but risk positions also focus on potential event risk and changes in capital structure.

The portfolio consists primarily of cash securities, both long and short, with CDS contracts representing a small level of total investments. The fund has relatively concentrated positions with around 60/70 strategies typically employed, with individual name concentration and jump-to-default risk restricted by rigorous risk approach. Given the strong fundamental approach, trade time horizons are reasonably long, typically 4-6 months, with some positions being retained for longer. As such the portfolio turnover is typically around 1.5 times per year. Credit analysis is the dominant trade driver, but investments are also driven by event risk, relative value and specific instrument documentation. The fund has a rigorous investment process, with each strategy sized by conviction, convexity, anticipated volatility, market timing and limit framework. All positions are supported by a detailed write-up incorporating the reasoning for the trade, targets and loss management parameters, which all trades are then monitored against. 

Fund leverage is relatively low, and limited to a maximum of 300% on a gross basis, while net leverage is modest and cannot be more than 125%. Portfolio construction is designed to limit volatility with a focus on lower beta assets as long positions and higher beta assets as shorts, utilising the convexity of the underlying instruments. Additionally investments focus on market liquidity to ensure they can be traded in periods of market disruption. Risk is managed according to proportional shifts in the underlying credit spread, rather than credit ratings, which ensures leverage is reduced in periods of high volatility. The manager can take directional bets within the portfolio risk and leverage limits but the key investment driver is individual credit performance.

management_company_description:
Paradigm BioCapital manages an equity long/short hedge fund focused on the innovative biotechnology subsector of healthcare.

We believe that the most attractive investments deliver transformative benefits to patients and redefine the treatment paradigm for physicians. Paradigm’s investment strategy focuses on identifying such opportunities at the earliest proof of concept where the balance of reward and risk is at its apex. Identifying such opportunities requires not only rigorous scientific and medical analysis, but also a deep and nuanced understanding of the current treatment landscape and gaps in the standards of care. 

We bring decades of experience in biotech investing and medicine together with a proven, clearly defined strategy to deliver superior returns for our investors
strategy_description:
Paradigm BioCapital's investment strategy is fundamental equity long/short dedicated to biotechnology. The strategy consists of both Core and Event: 

Core Strategy:
* Aim to identify companies developing transformative products with sizable market potential and high unmet medical needs.
* Valuation sensitive entry/exit; seek to identify at the earliest point of scientific and clinical de-risking but prior to a broader recognition of value.
* Universe: ~350 relevant publicly traded companies.
* Investment horizon: Typically, 2+ years to allow positions to play through.

Event Strategy:
* Target investments based on significant events or catalysts that generate large stock price movements uncorrelated to the broader market.
* Selective positioning ahead of or immediately after key clinical readouts and regulatory events by mapping the market vs. internal expectations.
* Catalysts: ~250 per year.
* Investment horizon: 6-12 months with timed entry and exit after an event.

management_company_description:
Silver Point Capital, L.P. (“Silver Point”, the “Firm”, "we") was founded in 2002 by Edward Mulé and Robert O’Shea, both previously partners at Goldman Sachs (“Goldman”), where together they built and co-headed numerous global credit businesses for the firm. 

Upon departing from Goldman, Mr. Mulé and Mr. O’Shea partnered to establish Silver Point in 2002 to replicate the credit businesses that they had built and managed while at Goldman. The Founders’ vision for Silver Point was to build a world-class private investment firm that would specialize in investing in credit and special situations opportunities.  They believed that they could leverage their experience and expertise to build a global credit investing business that would seek to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns across credit cycles for its investors.

Today, the Firm manages approximately $45 billion in investable assets across synergistic credit strategies, comprising (1) opportunistic credit and special situations funds, which include an evergreen global special situations investing strategy focused on publicly traded credit markets (the “Flagship Hedge Funds”) managing $13 billion in investable assets, (2) a dislocation drawdown strategy (the “Dislocation Drawdown Funds”) managing $7 billion in investable assets,  (3) a performing middle market lending strategy (our “Direct Lending Strategy”) managing $17 billion in investable assets; and (4) a liquid performing credit business managing approximately $8 billion.
strategy_description:
Distressed Opportunity Institutional Partners II (the “Fund”) seeks to achieve superior risk-adjusted returns by investing opportunistically in debt, equity and other financial obligations and assets, with a particular focus on companies and/or instruments that are mispriced, stressed, distressed, overleveraged and/or going through restructurings, bankruptcies or other complex situations in which the Fund can play an active role in driving events. The longer-locked structure will allow us to maximize value by (i) being more concentrated in highly attractive process-oriented investments; and (ii) capitalizing on illiquid investments that offer attractive absolute and risk-adjusted returns.

The Fund seeks to capitalize on market inefficiencies that arise in the credit markets due to (i) forced sell-offs and dislocations that result from market re-pricings; (ii) process complexities; (iii) the opacity of stressed, distressed, or bankrupt businesses; and (iv) the resource intensity required to navigate complicated capital structures, creditor laws, and credit documentation. As a large and experienced credit manager with a 22+ year track record in the strategy, Silver Point is well positioned to take advantage of the opportunities that persist during and following a market dislocation. This opportunity set includes both the initial liquid, stressed opportunity that arises from a market disruption, as well as the event-driven, complex distressed and turnaround opportunities that we drive given our experienced team, depth of resources, and expertise in the space.
       
Please note we are open to discussion around strategic partnerships at certain size minimums. Additionally, Silver Point offers both offshore and onshore fund offerings for investors.
region_exposure_description: The Funds have a global mandate. While Silver Point has experience pursuing investment and restructuring processes in over 50 jurisdictions globally, the majority of the portfolio tends to be in North America, given North America has the largest leveraged credit markets and the strongest debtor / creditor laws. We also have significant exposure to Western Europe and have historically had exposure to other regions including Europe, Asia, South America and others. The strength of creditor laws, process risks, and jurisdictional risks will all impact both risk adjusted and relative returns and will be taken into account when evaluating positions. Ultimately, the geographic breakdown of the Fund will be purely opportunistic and will leverage our experience and expertise in global distressed investing.

We raised Specialty Credit Fund III to continue the successful track record of our direct lending strategy. SCF III, which had its final close in November 2024, focuses primarily on originating floating rate, first lien senior secured performing loans to both sponsor-backed and non-sponsored middle-market companies generating $75-125 million of EBITDA. The Fund’s objective is to generate superior risk-adjusted returns by directly originating loans to cash flowing companies with strong credit profiles, and by negotiating upfront robust structural protections in credit documents to mitigate downside risk. 

Consistent with Silver Point’s investment focus since inception, the Fund targets what we believe are less competitive direct lending opportunities in the middle-market, typically because they require differentiated sourcing, in-depth due diligence, independent valuation and/or collateral analyses, involve complexity, and/or reward speed and certainty of execution or confidentiality. management_company_description:
Silver Point Capital, L.P. (“Silver Point”, the “Firm”, "we") was founded in 2002 by Edward Mulé and Robert O’Shea, both previously partners at Goldman Sachs (“Goldman”), where together they built and co-headed numerous global credit businesses for the firm. 

Upon departing from Goldman, Mr. Mulé and Mr. O’Shea partnered to establish Silver Point in 2002 to replicate the credit businesses that they had built and managed while at Goldman. The Founders’ vision for Silver Point was to build a world-class private investment firm that would specialize in investing in credit and special situations opportunities.  They believed that they could leverage their experience and expertise to build a global credit investing business that would seek to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns across credit cycles for its investors.

Today, the Firm manages approximately $45 billion in investable assets across synergistic credit strategies, comprising (1) opportunistic credit and special situations funds, which include an evergreen global special situations investing strategy focused on publicly traded credit markets (the “Flagship Hedge Funds”) managing $13 billion in investable assets, (2) a dislocation drawdown strategy (the “Dislocation Drawdown Funds”) managing $7 billion in investable assets,  (3) a performing middle market lending strategy (our “Direct Lending Strategy”) managing $17 billion in investable assets; and (4) a liquid performing credit business managing approximately $8 billion.
strategy_description:
We are raising Specialty Credit Fund (U) III, an unlevered fund, to continue the successful track record of our direct lending strategy. SCF (U) III will focus primarily on originating floating rate, first lien senior secured performing loans to both sponsor-backed and non-sponsored middle-market companies generating $75-125 million of EBITDA. The Fund’s objective is to generate superior risk-adjusted returns by directly originating loans to cash flowing companies with strong credit profiles, and by negotiating upfront robust structural protections in credit documents to mitigate downside risk. 

Consistent with Silver Point’s investment focus since inception, the Fund targets what we believe are less competitive direct lending opportunities in the middle-market, typically because they require differentiated sourcing, in-depth due diligence, independent valuation and/or collateral analyses, involve complexity, and/or reward speed and certainty of execution or confidentiality. These transactions may also include a level of process inefficiency on the side of the borrower, which allows us to drive what we believe are premium terms relative to comparable transactions in the direct lending market.
region_exposure_description: In terms of geographic focus, although the Fund has a global mandate, we predominantly target issuers domiciled in the United States. When we do opportunistically invest outside of the United States, we prioritize jurisdictions that we believe have strong and tested debtor/creditor laws, such as the United Kingdom, Canada, and Australia.

management_company_description: Parkman Healthcare Partners is primarily focused on global, small and mid-cap public healthcare equities across the various healthcare subsectors, including biotechnology, medical technology, pharmaceuticals, healthcare services and life science tools. Parkman seeks to protect and grow capital over the long term. The firm hopes to achieve this objective by employing a long/short equity strategy focused on the healthcare sector. The experienced investment team, led by Greg Martinez, has been together since 2014 and has over 100 years of combined healthcare investment experience.  The team utilizes a rigorous and repeatable research process to identify high quality products and businesses that have the potential to create lasting value for shareholders. Parkman Healthcare Partners is an SEC-registered investment adviser that was founded in 2019 and is headquartered in Stamford, CT.
strategy_description:
Parkman believes that there are significant benefits to focusing on one sector and developing expertise in that domain.  The firm believes that the healthcare sector is large, dynamic and complex, and therefore is ideally suited to a focused strategy.  In addition, Parkman believes that complex science, rapid technological change, and a complicated regulatory and reimbursement process all offer opportunities for the team to gain unique insights into value-creating investment opportunities. The rigorourous research and investment process enables our team to identify exciting innovations in healthcare and capture value. In addition, our strategy tends to be uncorrelated to both the market and our peers. 
Parkman seeks to pursue investment opportunities that appropriately balance risk and reward. As such, Parkman believes that a diversified healthcare portfolio, across multiple subsectors and geographies, provides the best opportunity for higher risk-adjusted returns over time. Where possible, Parkman seeks to minimize risk by investing in products and technologies that are sufficiently mature that a reasonable judgement about their commercial prospects can be made. Parkman generally seeks to avoid binary clinical events given their broadly unattractive risk-reward and their inherent lack of predictability. We participate in binary events on a selective basis and maintain a diversified portfolio that is balanced across all subsectors of healthcare.

management_company_description: BlackRock is a provider of global investment management services. As of December 2024, BlackRock managed $11.60 trillion across equity, fixed income, alternatives, multi-asset, and cash management strategies for institutional and retail clients. strategy_description:
The Fund is a long/short UK equity hedge fund focusing on all cap equities, investing in long and short positions. The Fund’s investment objective is to maximise total returns, whilst limiting correlation with the UK equity market. 

We look to uncover investment opportunities that align with our investment philosophy based on quality differentials and industry change and combine them in a portfolio which seeks to deliver positive absolute returns irrespective of market conditions.

We seek to own differentiated companies often with low market share in global markets, and/or the companies driving industry change. We look to short the ‘legacy incumbents’, the companies and industries that are left behind or being actively disrupted.
